Ternyata wisata yang dimaksud adalah toko kecil yang menjual kain dan lukisan. Dan kami dipaksa untuk membeli.

Berbeda dengan keraton bagian belakang, wisatawan dibiarkan memilih mau pakai guide atau tidak.
Faktor Penarik: Ketertarikan Budaya, Ketertarikan Fasilitas, Ketertarikan Suasana
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Ce palais ne vaut pas franchement le détour. Les expositions d'objets ne sont pas commentées en Anglais ou dans d'autres langues que l'Indonésien. Le parc est joli et la petite représentation musicale est très sympa aussi mais ça ne vaut pas le prix de l'entrée ni le temps passé à l’intérieur.
Bagus juga tempat ini utk belajar sejarah ttg kerajaan jawa yg tekenal pada jamannya. Pada hari minggu anda dapat melihat pertunjukan seni tari dan pertunjukan lainnya.

So much history and culture/tradition. There was a 10am live performance of traditional Wayang Kulit (theater puppets). Live singing sent chills down my spine! Usually we only witnessed such on TV or the web but to experience the performance live was such an amazing experience. The royal servants remained loyal in Kraton and extend guide services in English, Dutch and Japanese with a fee.

Intéressant si vous rêver de tout savoir sur la vie de l'empereur qui habite toujours le Kraton. Le lieux offre un grand moment de calme au centre de la très animée Yogyakarta. Si vous faites la visite un  samedi vous pourrez écouter mais surtout regarder un spectacle de marionnette en ombre chinoise avec tout le instrument de musique traditionnelle, c'est exceptionnel.

kraton jogja selalu jadi pilihan pas , untuk menikmati bangunan sejarah dan cerita sejarah . 
buat yang belum pernah kesini , 
atau yang kesini tanpa tour guide lokal, 
pasti enggak menarik . 
karena hanya berupa bangunan semata. 

tour guide disini , berguna sekali untuk mengilas balik sejarah . atau menambah ilmu pengetahuan .
karena setiap hal disini , mgkn butuh petua untuk menceritakan perjalanan panjang kerajaan keraton . 

happy holiday!

Interesting to see the pictures and displays of personal belongings of the royal family. Best to have a tour guide as nothing would make much sense without one. Also, do your research and find out the days and times of their traditional dance performances as it will make the trip much more worthwhile!
Kurang bisa menikmati wisata ini karena membawa anak kecil. Tempatnya cukup luas dan bersih, dengan tiket yang sangat murah.
Get the tour guide to know and understand the history of the palace. Interesting history of the rulers and their families.

Together with family going to kraton yogjakarta, there is excellent place. My family is enjoy and very excited.
We go around to kraton. The location of kraton near to the jalan malioboro ( malioboro street). and there is a lot of reataurant near the kraton. You can easy dind everything that what you want.
Faktor Penarik: Ketertarikan Budaya, Ketertarikan Fasilitas, Ketertarikan Suasana

Review Text:
Mendapatkan pengalaman yang berkesan saat melihat kegiatan di dalam Kraton.
Sangat banyak pengetahuan yang didapat mengenai Raja dan sejarahnya terdahulu lengkap dengan peninggalan-peninggalan yg bernilai historis.
Bangunan indah khas nuansa kraton. Cocok untuk foto-foto.
Disarankan menggunakan pakaian yg sopan saat masuk area kraton :)
IMO, not worth the visit except if there is any traditional activity like dance or special event or ritual. Otherwise not much to see

tempat yang dapat dikunjungi atau dbuka setiap wekend cukup menarik didalamnya dapat melihat sejarah sejarah nya, tempatnya sangat bersih dan terawat
keren sih :D
Faktor Penarik: Ketertarikan Budaya, Ketertarikan Fasilitas, Ketertarikan Suasana

Review Text: De Kraton was deels te bezichtigen. Datgene wat in het paleis te zien was, is vrij sober. Veel familie portretten. Alle wachters geheel volgens traditie gekleed., met kris.

The ticket was 12.500 per person BUT they ask you for 13.500 because you have to pay additional tax for taking pictures inside. Actually you don’t have a choice not to pay this 1000  . you have to be very CAREFUL with your change  because the lady tried to lie us twice in one transaction  I think this is very common here, it happened also in tirta gangga, Borobudur and Ratu Boko. You have to keep in mind that the palace is closing in 13:30pm, you need at least 1 hour to look around.  A lot of people were stopping us and telling us that we won’t make it in time, so we better go and see something else – don’t believe them, they just want you to buy something from them  Also, you can take a ride from Taman sari to the sultan palace for not more that 20.000k.  The palace It is interesting and beautiful. Go and see it if you are in Jogjakarta.

Yogyakarta khususnya kraton Yogyakarta membawa kita ke masa lalu. Indahnya bangunan istana yang ada sampai saat ini meskipun ada beberapa bagian yang sudah mengalami kerusakan akibat bencana dan ulah manusia tidak berkurang. Kita akan terbawa ke masa lalu, dan kita akan membayangkan bagaimana kehidupan raja-raja Yogyakarta beserta keluarga dan abdi dalemnya yang sampai saat ini masih dijaga. Kunjungan ini juga cukup berguna untuk menambah wawasan sejarah kita, mengagumkan dan membanggakan.

We engage the service of a local guide at the entrance of the Kraton which was definitely useful as he had many stories to tell as he guided us around this beautiful palace. 
It cost us IDR 40,000 for his 45 minutes  for his services.

It's always interesting to learn about the history of Sri Sultan Hamengku Buwono's family. Here, they showcased the history from the very 1st Sultan until the 9th. One thing that I guess should be improved by the management is to provide the English translations on each and every signages. At the moment they are in Indonesian language only. Overall, it was a great experience, I wish I could spend time longer to admire the paintings but it was quite crowded with people taking selfies lol.

It's nice to walk around. You can see some royal photos, traditional royal batik clothes, etc. However, the place is not very well maintained and there are no interactive elements. I went there in the afternoon and there was a puppet show with nice music in the garden.

Wij hebben het Kraton s ochtends bezocht. Het was er niet druk. Naast de entree betaal je een bedrag voor het fotograferen. 
Bij de uitgestalde bezienswaardigheden staat weinig vermeld maar het is toch mooi om te zien. 
Binnen kun je ook iets drinken.
Op verschillende tijdstippen wordt er muziek gemaakt waar je op je gemak van kunt genieten. 
Naast het Kraton is een kleine markt.
Faktor Penarik: Ketertarikan Budaya, Ketertarikan Fasilitas, Ketertarikan Suasana
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Ya no vale visitar el keraton, ya no te encontrarás con el palacio del sultan y su entorno.  Hace 4 años te encontrabas aun con los guardianes en persona,la orquesta gamelan de la corte y todos los carruajes, y piezas de arte. Está vacio y la v ida del palacio se refleja con fotos y manequis.. Para ver algo de lo anterior hay que visitar el museo fuera del recinto.

The palace area which was opened to public access is very simple and spacious, there are two exhibition halls explaining the history and showing some old photos to give you some ideas of how the place worked in the past. The video hall is playing a video of the festival and parade related to the palace and the king. Entrance fee for foreigner is 7k rph and you need to pay 2k extra for camera. You can ask for a guide if you are interested to know more, but the guide might bring you to local batik shop to buy batik in their neighbourhood, the people are friendly so just be persistent if you don't want to buy.
苏丹皇宫就在苏丹水宫附近  里面其实不大 ！  我进去之后还有一些歌曲表演  听了一会儿 ！  然后参观了一下宫殿 其实不是很辉煌  非常普通就像中国公园一样样！  看一些古时候用的器具  生活的模式这样 ！

Nous avons visités le quartier mais sans être charmés par les lieux. Seul le water palace vaut la peine. A noter qu'il ne faut surtout pas écouter les gens dans la rue, même si ils sont très sympa.. Pourtant très vigilants, nous avons cru un soit disant musicien du sultan palace qui nous a dit que c'était fermé exceptionnellement le matin pour cause de cérémonie et que c'était ouvert à la place l'après midi, le pensant de bonne foie nous avons pris un betchak qu'il nous a aidé à prendre et on a fini dans un atelier à batik !!! La seule chose est que la balade était sympa en touk touk pour 1,5€ lol. Bien évidemment il nous avez menti l'ayant vite su on y est allé 1h apres sans avoir vu aucune soit disante cérémonie ..
There was nothing when I went in there except people are renovating that place. Some pictures of sultans and that's it......
Obligatory (good) guide. Only one hall was really impressive. Dusty museum with some interesting objects.
Prachtig paleis middenin de stad. Neem vooral wel een gids mee om jou alles over het paleis te vertellen dan wordt het nog interessanter.

C'est l'un des derniers sites que nous avons visité à Jodja. Utile pour connaître les Sultants passés et actuel qui ont dirigés cette ville depuis bien longtemps. Quelques beaux bâtiments, des salles de musée malheureusement mal éclairées,  mais aucune explication sauf à prendre un guide sur place si vous n'avez pas déjà le vôtre.
On ressort un peu sur sa faim.

Suka banget ama keraton yogyakarta. Masih terawat dengan baik. Asri. Bersih jg. Pemandu kraton jg memberikan penjelasan yang detail. Klo ke sana mending pagi saja. Karena jam 2 sudah di tutup wisata ke keraton nya.

The heritage from Jogjakarta Kingdom that already exist until now. This place offer many unique attraction from the building, culture, food, music and many more. Just come here and experience it yourself!
Faktor Penarik: Ketertarikan Budaya, Ketertarikan Fasilitas, Ketertarikan Suasana
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
Eins vorweg: Vorsicht beim Eingang. Es gibt, wenn man über den Platz von Norden her kommt, einen "falschen" Eingang. Dieser fordert ca. 7.500 Rupieh. Für nichts. Hier unbedingt rechts (westlich) am Kraton die Straße weiterlaufen, bis man zum richtigen Eingang (12.500 Rupieh + 1.000 Kamera) kommt! Alles andere ist Fake! 

Der Palast ist an sich nicht sonderlich spektakulär. Mittwochs sind Puppentheatervorführungen, da kann man mal 10 Minuten zusehen, dann wird es langweilig, wenn man die Story nicht kennt. 

Zu sehen gibt es viel aus dem Leben des Sultans, unter anderem dessen Reitsattel, Schüsseln und Besteck --> Wuhuu! 

Man kann sich das schon mal ansehen, aber so richtig sehenswert ist das nicht...

I think the Sultan must have been proud of his palace. The palace doesn't make you feel like the place where the powerful rich man lives but instead it feels like the place full of cultural meanings. It houses many beautiful gifts and a texts.

We pay only 5000 to enter this place, but it is a bit difficult to get a guide during the holiday season since it is really crowded. For the collections and the things in this place, I think they are really good.

My son was very interested with this place because h just know my story telling ( I was born in jogja),, so he listened all explanation with well. For your info because can not use hat or cap so better morning Or afternoon after 3 pm.

I dont understand how is this an attraction when it is so empty with minimal (close to none) of the items described in English.Should include the history/stories of their royals etc - but there isnt one.

Architecture is old, but nothing fancy or grand. 
It is rather run dow and poorly maintained palace. 
(No it is not closed for cleaning etc, it is what it is)
There are some areas that are not open to the public
 
 
Felt more like an education trip for their local students.

Would skip this place if you do not have the extra time. The water castle (taman sari) is way worthwhile than this.

Der Besuch des Palastes war dank der Führung etwas einmaliges. Die Familie des Sultans, die Batikarbeiten und der Stammbaum der Familie wurden uns sehr eindrücklich und sozusagen aus erster Hand erklärt, da die Verwandten unserer Guide im Sultanspalast gearbeitet haben. Eindrücklich.
The visit was interesting nad the guide that showed us round obviously a love for the Sultan and family. The tour focus on the previous Sultan and is interesting but sparse. But worth the visit

It was a very interesting assortment of structures. The present sultan, who is also the state governor, lives in another palace nearby. We were told his eldest son would have lived here, but he only had daughters. It is still used for official occasions and a large retinue of older courtiers were still employed at the palace. The day we visited, the sultan's gamelan band(100 musicians) was playing and singing in one of several large open air halls. We could not see the private living quarters but there was a small museum, rooms,halls, a royal batik display, … it was well worth a visit.

The Sultan is a sort of King and the Kraton is his palace. You can enter it, just make sure it is open when you want to  visit. The Kraton has lots of interesting things to see, you may see a gamelan (percussion) orchestra practising, or see a traditional dancer rehearsing. You probably won't see the Sultan, though. I have visited the Kraton several times, ythere is always something new to see...
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: menceritakan sejarah hamengkubuwono dari pertama sampai sekarang. sangat disayangkan tidak ada AC sehingga cukup panas di dalam ruangan

We payed for the entrance and discovered that the place was almost empty. I don't know if it was a special day (cleaning day ??) but there was almost nothing to see except some pictures with explanations in Bahasa. The architecture is ancient but not special at all. I don't understand how this can be labelled as an attraction. This is the most confusing and one of the shortest visits I did during my trip to Indonesia.

Nice place, easy to reach. This palace have five area, but please do not visit it on Friday as I did because it will only open until 12.00, after Sholat jumat, you will only able to visit one of the palace area.

Tempat yang memiliki nilai sejarah ini sangat baik untuk belajar tentang masa lalu kota yogyakarta, banyak relief ukiran yang bercerita perjuangan rakya yogyakarta zaman dahulu kala, sampai sekarang tempat ini masih digunakan untuk acara tertentu setiap tahunnya.

Met hoge verwachtingen deze tempel bezocht, helaas mag je niet in de daadwerkelijke tempel. Daarnaast een soort opstelling met allerlei kleding gedragen door bewoners van de tempel. Muziekinstrumenten gebruikt bij ceremonies e.d. Helaas vrijwel alles met een begeleidende tekst in het Indonesisch. Gidsen zijn wel beschikbaar, maar heb hier zelf geen gebruik van gemaakt.

The place is good, but they divided into several location, so you must buy several ticket in the several different place. The first place near "Alun-Alun", the second place behind it. The ticket was cheap for local people, better you rent the guide to know better the information, especially the second place which bigger and a lot of object to see/know.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Per avere un'idea di come vivono i Sultani!!! È una curiosità che comunque merita una visita. Ovviamente la parte dove vive il Sultano con la famiglia non  è visitabile,ma il resto è carino con padiglioni e alcune sale dove si possono vedere foto e cimeli vari.Si deve pagare un extra per la macchina fotografica oltre al biglietto di ingresso.

Love to sightseeing here. Very peaceful here. Ada museum batik jg d dalam area kraton. Suasana tenang dan adem. 
Loket tiket hari biasa tutup jam 14.00. 
Hati2 sama tawaran tukang becak. Biasanya menawarkan tour keraton tp ternyata d luar keraton dan diajak keliling ke toko bakpia- dagadu. Kalau mau beli gpp tp hati2. Tanya harga dl ya.
This is part of the palace. Recommend to hire a guide so that will know more about this place. There is also so performance near the entrance.

Tujuan utama ke Jogja yaa Keraton.. Tempatnya bersih, tersedia free guide yang jelasin sekilas tentang Keraton Yogyakarta.
Pokoknya manteb.. Apalagi coba jalan merem di pohon beringin.. Nyaris berhasil..
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Se supone que es de las visitas obligadas en Yogyakarta, pero en realidad no tiene mucho que ver. Te cobran para poder sacar fotos, y tampoco tiene tanto... al menos el precio es igual para los oriundos y los extrangeros.

ジョグジャカルタの市内観光では必ず訪れる場所。
市内の中心部に広いエリアを占めています。南国らしくオープン。お堀や高い塀に囲まれているわけでもなく、とても親近感が湧きます。
王宮内では、毎日ガムランや踊りかわ上映されています。
建物を見て回り、その上伝統文化に触れることも出来る場所です。
王宮を守る伝統衣装に身を包んでいる方々も、王宮の雰囲気を盛り上げてくれます。
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Hoort gewoon bij een bezoek aan Yogja! Je mag er zelf rondlopen maar met een gids is het interessanter omdat je dan meer (historische) informatie krijgt.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: good place for exploring the Javanese culture in modern time. The architecture is old and antique as well. You will be lucky if there are not many visitors because can roam with explanation by a guide but when crowded situation it definitely hard to follow the guide. I really wanted to sit down for a moment but unfortunately no space to do it.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: There isnt really much to see in terms of artifacts nor of the structure which was very modest for a palace but perhaps that was the intention of the kings then who eschew ostentatious living that seperates the royalty from the commoners.

Ne pas s'attendre à un palais magnifique de beauté et de verdure! Franchement le lieu est sans grand intérêt, on ne comprends pas grand chose de ce qui y est exposé car rien n'est fait pour les touristes étrangers étant donné que rien n'est traduit! 
Nous avons quand même pu y voir des râpe pour la cuisine, une gaziniere ainsi que des spatules pour cuisiner!

Very welcome city for backpackers.
I like to spend my time in this city. Lots of tourist attractions. Malioboro street, tamansari water castle, prawirotaman as backpacker area. Sosrowijayan close to tugu train station.
Faktor Penarik: Ketertarikan Budaya, Ketertarikan Fasilitas, Ketertarikan Suasana

Review Text: There is not much to see but if you are lucky you get to hear interesting stories from your guide and learn more about java and its people
Menurut saya jam operasional nya kurang lama, cuma sampe jam 3 sore. Jam 5 mungkin bisa ya, karena suasana sore lebih enak utk jalan2 disini
Leuk om te zien hoe deze man leeft en zijn voorgangers hebben geleefd. Alleen al de 2000 bewakers die er rondlopen. Even werd er een stukje muziek gespeeld.
Pusat budaya Jogya dengan berbagai koleksi yang menakjubkan. Abdi dalam yang ramah dan dengan senang hati membantu dan memberikan informasi.

Jika anda ingin engunjungi jogja, dan ingin mengetahui tentang kebudayaan dan nilais ejarah dari kota ini, maka tempat ini wajib untuk dikunjungi.
Tempat ini sangat strategis dan mudah untuk ditemukan

Kembali mengunjungi keraton Jogja untuk kesekian kalinya , terahir 10 thn lalu. Saya membawa keluarga yg kebetulan blm pernah mengunjungi keraton Jogja ini. Kecewa karena Keraton kebangaan bukan hanya warga Yoga tp Indonesia ini sekarang terlihat kumuh, suram, kaca display ditambal krn pecah , halaman kotor berdebu pdhl sedang musim hujan. Ruang yg dibuka sedikit sekali tidak ada yg bs dilihat selain gambar2 tua yg sdh usang, tidak ada lg display kereta kencana, jg pernak pernik keraton yg indah skrg diganti hanya gambar2 tua yg kusam. Harga tiket sangat murah mungkin  karena hal itu sehingga perawatan kurang maksimal, sangat disayangkan. Mungkin saya juga  tidak akan dtg kembali dan tidak merekomendasikan kepada teman dan keluarga yg  blm pernah datang.

This royal palace is very close to Malioboro shopping street. Very decently maintained property, the museuam and the artifacts from the period of mid 18th century. It's direction of buildings and the architecture represents the mythological values of the Javanese.
Penting memerlajari sejarah bangsa ini salah satunya melalui datang ke Keraton Yogyakarta. Lokasinya bersebelahan dengan Aloon aloon, Sewa aja tour guide biar main tahu sejarah.

Keraton kasultanan Yogyakarta ini terletak di sebelah Selatan Malioboro, bisa ditempuh dengan jalan kaki kurang lebih 10 menit dari malioboro. Keraton ini dipimpin oleh Sri Sultan Hamangkubuwono X. Tempat ini merupakan destinasi favorit wisatawan saat berkunjung ke Jogja, di depan keraton terdapat alun-alun yang luas serta masjid.
Faktor Penarik: Ketertarikan Budaya, Ketertarikan Fasilitas, Ketertarikan Suasana
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Mooie plek die in de loop van de jaren steeds beter onderhouden is. Kan na vele beaoeken vanaf 1982 zeggen dat de collectie steeds beter wordt gepresenteerd. Blijt een omgeving waar je on alle rust kennis kan maken met dit verblijf van de sultan.
If we like to know about jogjakarta more this is the right places to visit. All about the places and historical thing we can find here.
Senang karena kebagian ada pementasan tari dan sempat lihat yang lagi latihan menari. Hanya saja cuacanya panas bener jadi kurang nyaman aja jalan2nya.

setelah bertahun tahun di jogja akhirnya baru bs mengunjungi keraton jogja yg ternyata sangat indah, mulai dr area pagelaran kemudian masuk ke area keraton, ada banyak yg bisa ditemukan didalam, pertunjukan sendratari, kelas menari yg diikuti oleh berbagai bangsa, museum batik, lukisan dan barang kuno juga aneka barang pribadi sultan ke ix...suasana keraton yg njawani sangat menyejukkan hati
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Little to recommend here. I did not find the architecture particularly unique or interesting and the museum exhibits on the royal family did not capture the imagination. The sultan still retains (I choose the word deliberately over employed, as they are paid a pittance) a large staff and you see a large gamelan orchestra performing in the grounds. Not to my personal musical taste and I felt sorry for the (mostly frail and elderly) players.

The visit to this place is a must! The palace of the Sri Sultan His Highness Sultan Hamengkubuwono X.  Rich historically and culturally enriching! Ask for Ibu Endan as your guide - lovely, humorous and full of life lady!

Permet de se faire une idée de la province de yogyakarta et de son sultan, encore en fonction, système qui n'existe qu'ici.
Dommage que presque la totalité des explications soient en indonesie et non traduites en anglais

berkunjung ke jogjakarta ga apdol kalo tidak mengunjungi keraton yogyakarta disana kita bisa melihat kearipan lokal keraton yang masih terjaga dan di lestarikan hingga saat ini.semua abdi dalem/penghuni keraton memakai pakaian adat tradisioal yogyakarta yang seakan membawa kita ke abad jaman dulu.keraton yogyakarta yang ga akan hilang di telan zaman.

Sekali lagi, saran untuk Anda untuk menggunakan jasa pemandu museum, agar bisa memahami dengan jelas tentang kraton, karena banyak ruang-ruangan mulai dari batik, peralatan yang digunakan sehari-hari oleh keluarga keraton
Niente di eccezionale, ha veramente poco di un palazzo reale. Anche la guida parlava un inglese stentato.

ach je moet het gezien hebben . het verhaal van de Kraton is wel interessant .
je moet wel een oude gids hebben om je rond te leiden. mensen moeten ook wat verdienen en dus geeft hun geld.

beside there are a old kingdom of ancient governance (still until now) but they also have a restaurant owned by sultan daughter. they serve a traditional and also a food that sultan used to eat. they started to introduce us the food for the highest in keraton to public.

Kraton might be boring for certain people but to have a better appreciation of this region, one only need to come here to realise that the Palace is a melting pot of different influences.  To these days, Yogyakarta is a self-governing district and it reports directly to Jakarta for the fact that its Sultan plays a pivotal role in the independence of Indonesia, by standing in solidarity with Sukarno at the time when he had a stand off against its Dutch colonial master.  Local people is very proud of this fact, and that Sultan and its family is very much loved.  There are highlights here such as listening to a full 2 hours of Gamelang music (on different days, you might get to see shadow puppet performance instead).  By visiting different parts of the Palace ground, you would get to see what tickled the fancies of the Sultan, his allies and their gifts, and so forth.  The highlight here would be to see the elderly retainers in their regal costumes hosting guests and to showcase their proud traditions and culture to us.  Visitors should be mindful that places of interest are exactly that, places to educate and to inform, and NOT to entertain you and to give you a reason to take selfies.  If entertainment is what you look for, I do suggest you to visit amusement parks and entertainment centres, and not Kraton, which happened to these days is still the living residence of the Sultan and his family.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

For first time visitor, if you are not getting a driver or following a tour group, do make sure that you go to the correct Keraton entrance.  The real Keraton (Keraton Ngayogyakarta Hadiningrat), where the Sultan live, charges Rp12,500 for entrance and there is no ticket booth. There is another Keraton Yogyakarta which the entrance is located on Tepas Keprajuritan, after the big green field (Alun Alun Utara) if walking from Malioboro, charges only Rp7,000 for entrance.  The latter was operated by the Sultan's relative and only allow access to just one wing of the palace.  It is easily been mistaken as the real keraton because the entrance is very obvious from main view with a ticket booth.  Just walk past the ticket booth then turn left and walk around 100m and you will see a lot of tour buses, that's where the real entrance is.  Another obvious difference is the latter Keraton have some birds kept in cages near the entrance.  Do look at google map if unsure.  For the entrance fee of Rp12,500 at the real palace, you can request for a free guide - the guides are the palace staff.   Just ask the man when buying the entrance ticket and he will arrange a guide.  As I was alone, I got a free English speaking guide on 1-to-1 basis.

Review Text:
An extremely popular destination for locals, westerners would probably appreciate more English language signs. The cost of admission is very low 12500 IRH and includes a guide who you are expected to tip. Many of the guides are retired members of the Sultans staff.

Jika anda traveler yang menyukai atau tertarik dengan kebudayaan khususnya kebudayaan Jawa, so this is the best place for you.

First of all,  let's talk about the location and how to get there.  The location is in the Centre of Yogyakarta city. It's easy to get there, you can go there by modern public transportation, or traditional public transportation or becak.

Dulu, Kraton ini digunakan sebagai tempat tinggal dan pemerintahan Daerah Istimewa Yogyakarta,  tetapi sekarang tidak dipergunakan sepenuhnya untuk tempat tinggal dan pemerintahan,  meskipun masih ada kegiatan untuk menjalankan tradisi kesultanan.

Review Text:
Kraton is the palace of the Sultan of Yogyakarta. The royal family still occupies parts of the palace. The rest of the palace is open to the public. Tour guides are also available at the entrance to the palace.

The palace itself is huge with various buildings like a dining hall, school and pavilions strewn amidst extensive grounds. A lot of the buildings have been converted into museums providing a glimpse into the royal lifestyle and traditions of the old days.

The pavilion next to the entrance holds regular performances of Javanese classical arts like shadow puppet dance, gamelan music etc.

The road leading to the palace is flanked by the usual souvenir shops. The area around the royal palace also has a lot of shops displaying traditional Javanese crafts like Batik, leather puppet etc. and is worth a tour if you are interested.

The palace and the area around it takes you back into traditional Javanese history and provides a glimpse into the era of royalty.

Whether you are interested in Javanese royal history and culture or just looking to pass some time, this area is definitely worth a visit.
Faktor Penarik: Ketertarikan Budaya, Ketertarikan Fasilitas, Ketertarikan Suasana
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Kraton Yogyakarta is a very old palace and is situated somewhere near the end of Malioboro Street. It can be easily accessed by the pedal-power or motorised Becak (trishaw), by Horse-cart or even by taxi.

Entrance was IDR7000 per person and a minimal IDR1000 per camera for those who would like to use their cameras or mobile phones within the palace compound. 

The whole palace complex was not very big with a central, main open-sided building holding the royal dais and surrounded by a few outbuildings which were filled with ancient exhibits, pictures, artifacts, etc showing mostly the royal lineage of Sultan Hamengku Buwono heirarchy. Guides are available near the entrance at an additional fee for those who prefer a running commentary as they view the exhibits there.

The history buff may find this visit to the Kraton to be of great interest but to the ordinary tourist it may be just another tourist attraction.

Hire a tuk tuk driver for the day, and ask them to take you around Yogya- if give the locals an income and it takes the stress off you trying to navigate your way around with a map. Plus, if you treat them nicely, they can become a tour guide of sorts and take you to the best lunch warungs and give you private tips about the attractions.

The Kraton is no exception. I walked around the Kraton at my own pace, although there is the option to take a palace tour guide. I just walked around and followed the paths myself, listening in on the tour guides whenever I was near one. I got a lot out of it. The Palace Museum preserves everything really well and is quite educational and informative about the Dutch colonisation. It's a beautiful palace and the museum aspects; costumes, historic images, sculptures and art, make this place very cultural and worth the visit. I really enjoyed myself there, but then again, I like following my nose around museums.

Tip: take the time to have a wander though the palace town as well. Within the palace walls live all the people who keep the palace and the local economy running. There you will find authentic food and handicrafts.

Tip: watch the local tv when you're just messing around in your room. In doing so, I stumbled upon advertising for a nightly traditional shadow puppet event (although check with hotel staff to confirm) at the Kraton. It was spectacular, cultural and traditional, and was an accidental highlight of my trip to the Kraton at night.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Sultan Hamengkubuwono IX memprakarsai agar Kediamannya dapat dinikmati oleh orang luar yang mau mengetahui sisi dalam kehidupan Keraton berikut sejarahnya. Oleh karena itu, beberapa bangunan di dalam Keraton disulap menjadi semacam museum-museum mini yang menceritakan sejarah Kerajaan Mataram (Islam) Modern dan bagaimana terjadi perseteruan antara Kesultanan Mataram dengan Pemerintah Kolonial Belanda. Museum juga berisi lukisan para Sultan Mataram dari Sultan Pertama hingga Sultan yang sekarang. Museum juga berisi koleksi barang-barang Keraton. Terdapat pemandu atau tour guide yang dapat menceritakan sisi-sisi kehidupan Keraton berikut sejarahnya. Tour Guide ada yang berbahasa Inggris, Perancis, Jepang, Mandarin, dan Penutur Lokal (Bahasa Indonesia).

Take a guide!!!  They will tell you all you want to know. Without a guide you don't get as much out of your visit as with a guide. Our guide told a lot about the history if the sultan dynasty, history of Java and culture of Java.

Tidak sulit mencari lokasi kraton ini, di pusat kota Yogya tepatnya di km-0 (kilometer-Nol)  yaitu di perempatan Monumen Serangan Oemoem/Benteng Vredebrug - Gedung Agung - gedung Bank Indonesia/kantor Pos & kantor BNI, terpampang lokasi Kraton hanya berjarak 400 meter kearah selatan.
Bertepatan dengan pasar malam Sekaten pasca upacara Grebeg Mulud, kami sekeluarga singgah semalam di 'kota gudeg' ini menyempatkan diri mampir lokasi sambil menikmati sensasi ramainya pasar malam dan macetnya jalanan

Kraton Yogyakarta adalah sentral dari Daerah Istimewa Yogyakarta. Letaknya berapa di pusat Kota Yogyakarta. Secara filosofis Kraton Yogyakarta merupakan pusat dari sumbu Utara Selatan Daerah Istimewa Yogyakarta. Sumbu utara selatan tersebut mudah dikenali oleh awam dengan memperhatikan letak bangunan Kraton terhadap Alun-alun Utara, Alun-alun Selatan, dan posisi Jalan Malioboro. Bagi anda yang masih awan dengan kebudayaan Jawa, datanglah ke Kraton Yogyakarta pada saat berlangsungnya upacara adat, dan rasakan rakyat setempat memaknai upacara adat tersebut. Carilah informasi jadwal upacara adat yang dapat disaksikan oleh publik sebelum mengunjungi Kraton Yogyakarta. Jika anda menyimak penjelasan pembawa acara, juga turut aktif bergerak dan berjalan kaki mengikuti arah gerakan di jalur-jalur yang dilintasi Pasukan Kraton dalam pelaksanaan upacara adat, dengan sendirinya anda akan terlibat, aktif dan merasakan makna simbolik dari upacara adatnya sebagaimana warga setempat.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: There is an entry fee, plus a fee for taking photos.  It is quite extensive, and the throne room is beautiful, but the artifacts used by the Sultan are rather mundane.  No Gold, no silver and no jewels.  It is an interesting 45 minutes

Si vas en fin de semana podrás ver algunas danzas y música en directo del palacio del sultán, que le dan alguna chispa a la visita. Intenta alquilar motocicleta para visitar la ciudad.

Kalo mau dateng jangan siang2, usahain sebelum jam 1 siang, karena akan istirahat dan buka kembali jam 5.

Belum ke Jogja kalau belum ke Kraton sih namanya. Apalagi saat malam-malam, sambil dengar pengamen membawakan lagunya KLa, makan gudeg, atau sekedar nongkrong liatin turis yang matanya ditutup dan mencoba peruntungannya. Good fun
A guided tour is highly recommended. We had a guide who can speak and explained every thing to us in English. I have to classified this place as a must to be visited.

However, when you're walking in Malioboro area when a lot of becak driver offer you a becak-tour with IDR 10,000, I suggest you not to take it, because the price did not make sense. Review Text: The Javanese sultanate palace of Yogyakarta is a must see if you happen to be in Yogyakarta. It's an old palace but relatively well maintained, in a much better shape than its older "brotherly" palace of Surakarta in Solo. You also get to see a lot more of the parts of the palace relative to the one in Solo (which is reality is a bigger palace but most of it is off limits for tourists). There are plenty of display rooms to see, including the museum where they keep the sultan's collection of historical carriages. Indeed a journey into the past glory with a taste of present time majestic Javanese tradition.
Faktor Penarik: Ketertarikan Budaya, Ketertarikan Fasilitas, Ketertarikan Suasana
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: The Kraton Jogjakarta is the residence of the Sultan of Jogjakarta. Sultan could be translated as "king" or "prince." "Kraton" means palace. Sultan Hamenkubuwono X lives in his private quarters. Otherwise, there is a lot to see. The kraton is fairly well maintained but is a trifle shop soiled. Look out for cultural performances such as gamelan (percussion orchestra), wayang golek (marionettes), classical dance and Javanese poetry reading. Javanese is a notoriously difficult language to learn, so you are unlikely to understand much. The kraton is more like a small town than a European palace. No one seems to mind much if you wander around. The Sultans of Jogya have been prominent in Indonesia's democratisation movement and are traditionally governors of the Special Administrative Region of Jogjakarta due to this. Jogya is called the "New York of Central Java" and has many sights worth seeing in addition to the kraton. .
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Dari semua kraton kesultanan yang ada di Indonesia yang masih ada dan berdiri lestari , terawat dengan semua kegiatan keluarga sultan masih berlangsung di dalamnya hingga saat ini, hanya kraton Yogyakarta lah yang paling besar, luas dan memiliki abdi dalem yang masih cukup banyak. Kraton terbagi dua area yakni area terbuka bagi wisatawan dan area tertutup yang masih dihuni oleh keluarga sultan. Berbagai peninggalan bersejarah dipamerkan...mulai tandu, kereta kuda, mobil, hingga keris dan wayang.

Lemah, lembut, dan murah senyum dengan bahasa jawa yang sopan dan halus sekali. Unsur mistis keraton jadi hilang melihat senyum mereka.

ジョグジャカルタ王朝の初代スルタン、ハメンクブオノ1世の居城として、1756年に建てられた王宮。現在も第10代スルタン、ハメンクブオノ10世が暮らしています。伝統的なジャワ建築様式ですが、ヨーロッパ文化が混ざり合うことの相乗効果で、華やかさがあり素敵でした。歴代スルタンが使用した家具調度品やクリスと呼ばれるジャワ独特の短刀、衣装、乗り物などが展示されています。ちょうど日曜の午前中に行けたので、11時からのジャワ舞踊の公演を鑑賞できました。他の曜日は見ていないので分かりませんが、写真も撮れますし、時間を合わせて訪れるのがお薦めです。日本語ガイドと同行していましたので、入場する際のガイドの話しはありませんでした。今も生き続ける王宮文化を感じ、とても良い思い出になりました。
Faktor Penarik: Ketertarikan Budaya, Ketertarikan Fasilitas, Ketertarikan Suasana
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Keraton Yogyakarta merupakan ibukota dari kesultanan mataram di masa lalu, di tempat ini kita dapat menemukan tradisi yang masih terjaga dengan baik, sultan, abdi dalem, permaisuri hidup saling menghormati dan menghormati. Karakter gotong royong akan kita temukan di tempat ini. Hal yang paling terkesan di benak saya ialah koleksi-koleksi lencana dan lambang, kereta kencana, payung serta alat-alat makan yang sengaja dibuat berbeda dari kebanyakan rakyat. Voor de tweede keer hier geweest en ook dit keer heb ik van mijn bezoek genoten. Interessant om te zien hoe de Sultans toen en nu leefden en leven. Belangrijk stukje geschiedenis.

Jeden Sonntag ab zehn Uhr findet im grossen Pendopo eine Übungssession der Tänzer und des Gamlans statt. Wenn man das immens rhythmische balinesische oder das melodisch gefällige Sunda-Gamelan kennt, ist die javanische Version dieser Musik zunächst gewöhnungsbedürftig. 
Wenn man traditionelle balinesische Tänze kennt, muss man eine Weile genau hinschauen, weil bei flüchtigem Zuschauen wenig Beobachtbares passiert. Lässt man sich aber auf diese Fremdheit ein und konzentriert sich auf die fast dekadent überdehnten Bewegungs- und Musikminiaturen, dann wird es plötzlich sehr faszinierend und spannend, und man sitzt völlig versunken zwei Stunden auf den Stufen des Pendopo und vergisst die Zeit ... Der Rest vom Kraton ist für westliche Besucher wenig interessant, doch diese Übungsstunden sollte man nicht verpassen.

We visited the Kraton in a bad season: rainy. It was raining cats and dogs when we were there. 

Nevertheless, the weather didn't seem to dampen our guide's mood. She explained the history and spirit of the Kraton very well.

This is a good place to bring kids to learn about Javanese culture.

saya selalu berasa masuk rumah sendiri saat mengunjungi kraton, hanya saja nampaknya kurang perawatan, haruus lebi meanampilkan pertunjukan seni khas jogja yang lebih banyak lagi biar menarik

Le lieu en lui même est vaste et reposant.
un beau lieu pour se balader, surtout vu le prix dérisoire de l'entrée (dans les 1€ par personne).

Le musée est plus une sorte d'exposition de divers objets amassé par le sultan au fil des années. Des cadeaux diplomatiques (vases chinois, porcelaine, etc.) aux objets de la famille... mais ça manque de fil rouge : on n'a pas vraiment d'histoire ni de motivation pour rentrer dans les différentes pièces et découvrir ce qui s'y trouve.

La bonne surprise venait surtout de la représentation de danse Javanaise classique, avec un orchestre : majestueux !

ATTENTION : il y a deux entrées distinctes, mais une seule donne vraiment l'accès à l'intérieur du palais. Il faut passer par l'entrée située plein ouest, reconnaissable à l'horloge au milieu d'un petit rond point.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: I arrived to catch the musical and dance performance which was my primary intention. It was worth the time. I began to walk through the Kraton on my own and was rather underwhelmed. Then I went back to the entrance and got a good English speaking guide. She was able to provide a narrative for everything on display, which increased my appreciation. Go in with proper expectations - this will not be the impressive oppulence of Versaille or other European palaces. The style is much more understated and minimalist - the more impressive story is the function of the Kraton for the larger community. It is a good opportunity to see Javanese culture & dress in everyay life.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
Oubliez cette visite et achetez un billet pour l'Inde (là, vous allez voir des palais de sultans dignes de ce nom). Cette visite est ennuyeuse à mourir. On cherche vainement ce qu'il y à voir et on ne voit que de vieilles photos pourries de choses qui pourraient être intéressantes à voir en vrai : trône, calèches, salles de cérémonies. Tout ce qui doit être bien est derrière le mur infranchissable au fond du "musée".
Loin de tout (marche sous le cagnard obligée).
Malhonnête (on vous fait miroiter des choses, mais... rien).
Si le sultan veut préserver sa vie privée, pas de problème ! Mais arnaquer les touristes pour visiter son local poubelle : NON !

Saya menyukai keraton ini, tetapi banyak ruangan yang tidak boleh diakses karena Sultan masih menempati kraton ini. Saya sangat menyukai ornamennya, terutama ruangan museum yang baru dibangun Sri Sultan Hamengkubuwono X.

Le Kraton de Yokjakarta ou ancien palais des sultans du lieu est un ensemble dont certaines parties sont intéressantes à visiter, mais on s'y perd à trouver une unicité de style. Les jardins de Taman Sari à proximité qui dépendent du kraton sont du même cabit.
Great place to learn a bit more of the history and culture of Yogyakarta and Indonesia and of its traditions.
Is de wandeling ernaar toe nauwelijks waard, er is erg weinig te zien, wat te zien is wordt slecht onderhouden.

se volete passare un paio d'ore per osservare il cerimoniale del cambio della guardia e tutti i cimeli della famiglia reale, questo è il posto, se volete spendere meglio il vostro tempo, proseguite per la città

It is always beautiful to know who we are and what has made us today, and one way of doing that is to go to the time-tunnel by visiting the old places. The stories are always amazing and we could learn a lot. From the ticket booth, there will always be a guide, they never put a price for their service, it is based upon how good they telling stories and how satisfied we are. Our guide is 82 years old but he seemed so energetic and tells us many stories. Overall, trip to Kraton is unforgettable!

Let me start by saying I am not a monarchist. 
That being said, the insight into the history and live in the Royal Palace of the Sultan and ruler of the Special Region of Yogyakarta is truly unique. 
From the dancers and musicians practicing the gamelan, to the museums with the amazing artifacts of the generations of rulers, it is an amazing insight into the workings of the seat of power for the area. 
The only thing I would strongly suggest is - please show the due respect - some tourists while we were there apparently didn't understand how important the palace is and were truly appalling in behaviour.   
The other thing is, be mindful of the hawkers immediately outside - whilst it is always good-natured - the prices are definitely ratcheted up to international tourist level. To haggle always smile and be happy but start at around 30-50% of the initial price and work up from there. You'll still pay more than a local but remember - the sellers appreciate and need the money more than you. 
Other than that - enjoy.

Coming from India, a land of enough palaces, I've been to several "museums" that suffer from the same affliction. I imagine the conversation goes as follows :

Queen: I don't want a single piece of your mother's crockery in my Palace you hear! 
King/Sultan: but their heirlooms my dear :( we can't just throw them away. 
Queen: I don't care. Just put them away someplace! 
King/Sultan: Put. Them. Away. Someplace. Hmmm. There's an idea there. 

The Kraton is a lot like that. Room after room of what boils down to the Sultans junk, especially as none of it comes with any English description to set the context. So there is one room full of crockery, another full of his medals and so on so forth. The only part of this entire complex that had the potential to be interesting is the Batik room. Sadly, not a shred of explanation in English anywhere in this room. Really hope they'll get someone from a place like the V&A to properly curate this because the usage of symbols and iconography in batik can be so deep. 

Anyways, the other redeeming factor is that the complex sometimes has a Gamelan orchestra playing which u found absolutely mesmerising. Avant-garde before the term was even known. 

So do drop in to the Kraton but keep your expectations low and you might find it interesting. Whatever you do don't, and I repeat, don't visit a separate paid wing of the Complex, called the Pagelaran. It's an absolute disgrace that they even try to charge for it

Review Text: We were met by a very courteous and well informed guide who took us around providing a wealth of information and intrigue. The entrance hallways are wonderfully preserved and demonstrate the regal prowess of the Sultan line.  We can't praise our guide enough for providing such an enjoyable experience that included a visit to a Batik gallery where we purchased some fantastic Batik paintings as mementos.

Merece la pena cogerlo porque te va explicando cosas que de otra manera no sabrías. Hay retratos y objetos de sultanes anteriores y también del sultán actual, que aún vive en ese palacio pero en una zona que no se visita. Desde aquí puedes ir al Castillo del Agua caminando o en tuk tuk, que es más cómodo y más típico por tan solo 10.000 IDR, 0,70€

Review Text: Кусочек истории, дворец султана. А раз уже находишься в Джогдже, то конечно надо и в Кратон заглянуть. Интересная архитектура и подборка музыкальных инструментов. Впечатлил рассказ гида о придворных порядках, кто где стоит и какую функцию исполняет. Но большого восторга не ждите, так, для общего развития. И без гида делать нечего (англоговорящий, конечно). Кстати, после экскурсии неизбежен поход в очередную Академию Батика, именно так, с большой буквы, и рассказ про то, что вот эта академия батика единственная настоящая на всей Яве :) Заранее скажу - да везде этот батик одинаковый, и сюжеты пуля в пулю, те, которые с лодочками и пальмами)))

Die Palastanlage ist noch nicht besonders alt (18./19. Jhd.) und besteht zum überwiegenden Teil aus offenen Holzgebäuden. Die Anlage ist nicht allzu groß, bietet aber neben den teiweise sehr schön gestalteten Gebäuden diverse Kunst-, Gebrauchs- und Hobbygegenstände der Sultansfamilie, Gemälde, Fotos und Dokumente (alles also Klassiker von Palästen auf der ganzen Welt). Ein paar besondere Exponate wie z.B. Lampen aus Büffelhorn lassen sich entdecken. Wir hatten sehr viel Glück mit unserer lokalen Führerin, die nicht nur gut Deutsch konnte, sondern mit viel Humor und Ironie uns über den Palast und die Sultansfamilie erzählte (sie zeigte uns z.B. eine Marmorplatte, die angeblich Helmut Kohl aufgrund seines Körpergewichtes zerbrochen haben soll). Man kann überall Palastpersonal/-wachen bei ihren Tätigkeiten beobachten, was neben Instandhaltungsarbeiten z.B. der Schattenspielfiguren häufig nur aus Rumsitzen und Quatschen besteht, was unsere Führerin auch entsprechend kommentierte. Wenn man Glück hat, dann kann man einer Probe des Gamelan-Orchesters beiwohnen. Man kann sich mit den Palastwachen fotografieren lassen und unsere Führerin hat uns auch gerne mit unserer Kamera aufgenommen. Die öffentlichen Toilettenanlagen sind allerdings mal wieder etwas peinlich für einen solchen Palast, ansonsten können wir aber auf einen unterhaltsamen Besuch zurückblicken.

The Kraton, or Sultan's Palace in Yogyakarta, should be on every foreign visitor's list of must-see things in this amazing city on the island of Java, Indonesia.  The fact that there is still a real, functioning sultan ruling this "special province" of Indonesia is, by itself, incredible.  This is because of the crucial assistance given by the sultan who was ruling at the time to the Indonesian Revolution in the late 1940's.  In gratitude for this assistance, the subsequent indigenous free government of Indonesia granted Yogyakarta special quasi-independent status, and allowed the sultan to retain his power as hereditary ruler thereof.  To this date, the sultan is the actual governor of Yogyakarta City and Province.  The palace is open to the public, and well worth visiting.  Built in the 18th and 19th centuries, it is a beautiful example of Indonesian architecture of the period.  There are many interesting exhibits, and an open air stage on which indigenous music is performed by the royal gamelan orchestra.  We thoroughly enjoyed our one-hour visit, and would recommend this to any foreign visitor to Yogyakarta.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah
