Review Text: There are guides to take tourist through in the various languages. It is not large and the exhibits are not substantial. So, an hour would be more than enough here.

Just back after 45 minutes inside.
Was "empty" compared with the Solo counterparts.
Few structures probably for ceremony during ancient time. A model display of a bigger Palace compound! That means the area open to public is Just the front portion of the Palace complex.
Rather disappointed.
The guard cum guide demanded a few of 50k Rupiah which I refused. I could not understand Indonesian anyway.
Entrance fee fo foreigner is 7000rp.

bel palazzo, preceduto da un ampio mercato, tuttavia una volta all'interno non c'è molto da visitare poiché esso è ancora abitato dal sultano di Java, da vedere ma solo se si ha tempo, si trova alla fine di Jalan Malioboro. Attenzione alle solite persone che approfittano dei turisti per offrire passaggi in risciò in posti da loro sponsorizzati.

The palace is interesting to see and there are many exibits as well. However, nothing is written in English which makes it difficult to grasp the meaning of certain things. So it's good to browse around but I feel I would have benefitted from some English signs. I think there are English-speaking guides though...
Be sure you make it to the right entrance. There's a large clock there. The other entrance only gives you access to a smaller part of the palace. Also don't be put off by people trying to convince you the palace is "closed today" and want to show you an art exhibition/batik museum etc instead...
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Ngayogyakarta Palace or Sultan Palace is the official palace of Yogyakarta Sultanate which is now located in the city of Yogyakarta, Yogyakarta, Indonesia. The palace still serves as the residence of the Sultan and his court of households who are still running tradition of the empire to the present. This palace is now also one of the attractions in the city of Yogyakarta. This palace is one example of Javanese palace architecture at its best, has a luxurious halls and grounds as well as extensive pavilion
Faktor Penarik: Ketertarikan Budaya, Ketertarikan Fasilitas, Ketertarikan Suasana
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
We visited today and spent approximately 1 hour inside. Beware there are two entrances!! Entering through one exit means you must pay twice! The entrance with the white clock is the one you need to go through. Fee is 12,500. Men also beware, shoulders must be covered no vests (my boyfriend had to wear my kimono, very funny!) 

Pros: beautiful paintings and artefacts. Very cultural. Present guards all over the palace will sometimes make conversation. Stunning bulging work, worth taking pictures.

Cons: Little shade once inside the complex. Confusing to get around. No description of items in anything other than Indonesian. Some items in dusty cabinets, obviously been there for years (as in not well cared for). No sunhats allowed despite the heat. You do not actually enter the palace, just the grounds.

Although we were aware of guides which will offer (i believe free guiding around the palace) we did not see any and so went around ourselves. 

Overall, it was an interesting visit and fir the price a worthwhile trip but do not expect to be astounded by beauty as this is just an average place to see.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Probabilmente i visitatori leggendo che si tratta del palazzo dei sultani hanno aspettative molto alte e da qui la delusione che si legge in molte recensioni. In realtà si tratta di un insieme non privo di un suo fascino. Il vasto complesso di semplici e bassi edifici, cortili e tettoie è costruito secondo la tradizione indonesiana e ospita alcune collezioni di fotografie, oggetti e una interessante esposizione di tradizionali tessuti batik utilizzati dalla famiglia del sultano. L'atmosfera decadente è forse accentuata dalla presenza del numeroso personale -in maggioranza anziani - vestiti nell'abito tradizionale e collocati qua e là non si capisce bene se solo ad uso e consumo delle fotografie dei turisti. Alle dieci, compreso nel costo del biglietto (12.500 rp più 1000 per ogni macchina fotografica), è possibile assistere ad uno spettacolo di canto e danza, che ho trovato abbastanza deprimente ma forse sono io che non capisco la musica tradizionale.

It's a walk through history of Javanese Royalty. Guides is a must as it helps make the visit more meaningful.  I only wish that the displays were better lighted and and information a lot more descriptive. The place needs an Overall revamp and it deserves it as its quite special.
ジョグジャにある王宮です。他のかたの口コミにもあるとおり、南北分かれていて「北側」に行ってしまいました。（北に町の中心街があり、そこから歩いて行ったので、近い方に入ってしまいました。。）基本的に北側には特に見どころもない（ですが有料）ですので、南側に行くことをおすすめします。

Per fortuna costa pochissimo perché saremmo usciti in un minuto, se non fosse stato per la moltitudine di persone del luogo che ci chiedevano di farsi foto con noi come fossimo divi di Hollywood...e non sto esagerando! Simpatico finché dura poco...comunque non c'è veramente niente da vedere, però lì abbiamo trovato una guida improvvisata che ci ha portati tra le case che conducono al water palace e ci ha fatto respirare l'aria caratteristica del luogo.
Sinceramente non vale la pena. Il biglietto costa poco ma non c'è nulla da vedere, il palazzo non ha molto da offrire, meglio curiosare nel mercato alle spalle del palazzo!
Visite à faire si vous vous trouvez ds les alentours. Il n y a rien d exceptionnel mais a visiter par curiosité !

The front complex is just a big hall with very few exhibits. On both sides are two small buildings with glass wall to separate the mannequins dressed in old-time traditional wear. Besides that, there's nothing much to see.

The inner complex was locked due to preparation for some kind of ceremony. Quite disappointed really as I'd read the second one has more things to see.

Learned so much from the guide who was supplied free - as with Borobudur I found the guide to be quite passionate about the history which made the place come alive .  Of particular interest was that not all the Sultans have been Muslim,  one particular Sultan had 20 wives and 70 children and had a rather unique way of deciding which wife would be spending quality time with him! Thee pools, one for the wives, one for the children and a personal one for the sultan During restoration they have tried to keep to the original materials - this meant that restoration of the walls around the pool areas required 11,000 ltrs of egg white to be useed as a binding agent for the materials ised to cover the walls!  I could keep going - obviously I enjoyed it very much - but if you are interested in history then it really is worth a visit although I could understand how it could become a little boring for younger children

"LA" visite de Yogyakarta.... moui, ça n'a rien de fou, si ce n'est le spectacle organisé chaque jour entre 10h et 12h (en particulier le dimanche la danse !). Attention aux rabatteurs qui vous disent que c'est fermé, c'est faux.
Prendre l'entrée Nord Ouest.
Zonder gids is er hier weinig te zien. Engelse displays ontbreken en het geheel doet zeer kaal aan. Het kost ook vrijwel niets aan geld en tijd, dus je kunt je er geen buil aan vallen.

The Sultan residence is of interest for people lo ing hitorical sites. I was ther with my fmily and my kids got bored pretty soon. Only looking at the " knives" worn on the backs of ancinet guards walking around the place made them a little more curious about it. We had the only italian speking guide, a lady, almost 70 years old, that did her best with her self-learnt italian, just what she needs for her job. We all got the feelings of the importance and respects the locals have for their sultns, even with the new nd different behviour they have been seeing recently. 
A easy to reach place, worth a visit to get an insight.
passage 'obligé' à Yogya, pas bien mis en valeur. C'était très décevant. Pas beaucoup d'explications, malgré le guide qui fait de son mieux...

Rekomended karena blm lengkap wisata ke jogja kalau blm mengunjungi kraton jogja. Pemandunya sangat ramah dan sangat menguasai sejarah jogja. Tidak ada tarif khusus terswrah kita mau memberi tips berapa.
私はおそらくつまらない方に行ってしまったのでしょう。北の方に入場しました。ほとんど見るものはなかったです。というより、驚くほどなにもなかったです。南の方はガイドブックによればステンドグラスがあるとか…。失敗しました。

Si vous etes dans le coin, il vaut mieux le voir meme si rien d exceptionnel. Ce n est pas une perte si vous ne le voyez pas. Pour 12500 idr et 1000 en plus si vous avez un appareil photo cela ne va pas vous ruinez = 1 eur !

Erg veel van het paleis krijg je als bezoeker niet te zien. De buitenplaatsen zijn mooi maar niet indrukwekkend. Het is met name leuk om de rustige sfeer in  het verder hectische Jogjakarta te beleven. 
Wat heel erg jammer is, is dat het Waterpaleis erg is aangetast door de aardbeving.

Jeden Sonntag um 11 Uhr wird eine traditionelle Performance vorgeführt, die die Geschichte der Könige und Götter erzählen soll. Dabei wird getanzt und gesungen. Das traditionelle Orchester begleitet dieses sehenswerte Spektakel. sehr empfehlenswert!

Für 50.000 Rp könnt ihr eine Führung haben. Nehmt sie!  Sehr spannende und faszinierende Informationen

Berkunjung ke keraton Jogja tak pernah membosankan. Selalu ada yang menarik. Karena luasnya maka tiap kunjungan hanya mampu mengeksplor sebagian kecil keraton.

Yang menarik dari Keraton ini adalah arsitektur klasiknya yang keren dan membuat pengunjung berdecak kagum. Usianya yang sudah ratusan tahun namun bangunan keraton tetap terjaga dengan baik. 

Selain itu yang menarik adalah koleksi seperti kereta kencana, keris, maupun lukisan kerabat keraton. Entah mengapa seperti melihat sebuah jendela sejarah masa lampau.

Jika kita beruntung di hari tertentu ada prosesi pergantian petugas jaga keraton yang menarik. Prajurit keraton berusia tua berbaris rapi dengan mengenakan pakaian kebesaran mereka. Seperti di sebuah kerajaan antah berantah.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Ho dovuto fermarmi più volte, guardarmi intorno e smettere di ridere vistosamente del fatto che fossimo qui, che avessimo pagato un biglietto e anche una tassa per la fotocamera a cui non ho tolto neanche il tappo. Non ci sono parole, perché non ho proprio capito il senso e il valore di questo posto e delle cianfrusaglie esposte nei vari padiglioni, alcuni dei quali hanno sulle pareti le piastrelle da bagno. Molto lontano dall'idea di museo e monumento. Una nota divertente è la curiosità che si suscita nei locali e la richiesta continua di essere fotografati. Da evitare.
Le palais du Sultan n'est qu'une succession de cours avec un petit musée sans explications. Seul le pavillon doré mérite le détour.
Davvero grande, ricco di oggetti e testimonianze,tutto ben tenuto...Se avete tempo potete anche visitarlo, ma non è nulla di spettacolare!

王宮就是蘇丹王居住的地方，現在還有蘇丹住在這裏。所以王宮隻開放了前麵博物館和廣場的位置，展示了各代蘇丹的照片，用過的物件，還有就是穿著的服裝之類的！！ 
各人感觉很无聊，不过就是便宜！！

It's a big place. .. but due to me and my mom  not  "history " lover..  so we don't really enjoy our visit there.  My mom bored till escape from the side entrance besides the kitchen and we get lost from our driver.  But just near to this palace there is a nice traditional food store our driver brought us turn out to be a nice experience for us to enjoy their local meal. Can't tag location as I don't have Internet access there.  Sharing the shop photo here.   Tea with little sugar is nice!

Una visita al palazzo del sultano di Yogyakarta (Kraton) si può fare non dovendo portare via tempo ad altre escursioni. Il costo del biglietto d'ingresso è irrisorio. La visita è consentita solo in alcune parti della "cittadella" e comprensiva di uno spettacolo di suonatori di Gamelan e marionette.

Kraton yogyakarta memang tidak pernah sepi pengunjung ini kali kedua saya kesini namun suasana masih ramai bahkan lebih ramai lagi,belum lagi letaknya ditengah kota dan bisa diakses dengan semua transportasi. Banyak penjual souvenir dan kuliner diaekitarnya jadi bisa sekalian berwisata sambil kuliner dan tak lupa souvenir khas jogja

many people are quite unhappy about this palace, bear in mind this is a very old and sacred place in Yogya, we need to preserve it that way. I love how vintage and unique this palace is. My grandma is originally from Yogya so when we were little, she took us to come visit to remind us how beautiful our culture is. I have nothing to complaint since my sole purpose to visit this place is to reminiscence the old memories.

Unfortunately, our online maps led us to the exit of the Kraton where we were welcomed by locals who nagged us their tour offer to Kraton including buying souvenirs and impolitely turned their back away when we refused to do shopping but only visiting Kraton, they are making money on it, I guess. And they're quite smart to provide you a parking lot cost IDR 10k firstly for an unfavorable offer (which parking usually only cost IDR 1-2K around Indonesia). Use the guide service if you're interested with Kraton history, but what we did is just skip this site since it is not well maintained and doesn't seem to support any chance to go through the history by not providing signage or any information of the historical site, we were walking back and forth without seeing anything.
Het zal ooit mooi geweest zijn,  nu is er niets meer van over.  Achterstallig onderhoud, erg vies. De entree is goedkoop maar het is zonde van je tijd.

If you do not have much time, skip it... I believe the palace has an importance in Indonesian history, but there is not much to see inside. Couple of paintings, some cages, cravings, but not anything u would have to see... Try to check the small streets around, there is a mosque behind the palace and taman sari is not far away, which is much better.

어찌보면 엉성하고 볼것이 없는 것 처럼 느낄 수 있지만 족자 사람들의 자긍심을 볼 수 있는 장소 입니다.
족자인들이 왕에 대한 존경심이 대단하여 자원봉사를 하며 가이드 역활을 하는 할머니 할아버지등이 관광객을 안내하며 설명을 하기도 하고 금기 사항등을 알려줍니다. 선그라스, 안경,모자, 양산,우산들을 사용 할 수 없으며, 너무 짧은 바지나,치마,슬리퍼등도 착용할 수 없고, 지정된고 이외에는 올라서지 못하게 하는 등 관리와 에절을 강조합니다.
Salah satu tempat wisata murah meriah di Yogyakarta. Tiket masuk hanya Rp.5000. Dapat menambah pengetahuan tentang sejarah dan silsilah keluarga Kraton Yogyakarta.

Make sure you see the danse. There is a show every day.
The palace is amazing. A must see. Too bad there are no explanations in English, we don't know what we are looking at.
There are 2 entrances. Be aware that if you go to the small one first you will have to pay twice. Go to the main entrance, with this fee you will be allowed to both entrance.

When you exit the palace you will be harassed to go to some shops. The men pretend to be tour guide and present fake ideas. In fact they take you to some friends shop.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Mengunjungi kraton yogya memiliki sensasi tersendiri...apalagi jika membawa anak2 kesini...memberikan pelajaran sejarah tersendiri buat anak2... liburan plus ilmu yang bermanfaat

I read a fair bit about this place prior to my visit, which piqued my interest, and it surely did not disappoint. 

I should first caution that there are apparently TWO Kraton complexes - the first, which entrance is by the square immediately at the end of Jalan Malioboro, is the relatively smaller complex with not too much to see by way of exhibits and structures; and the second, which is about another 400m or so further away from the first complex, has more to offer. This review is for the second complex. (The first is not really worth your time so skip it.)

The second complex had various ornately decorated buildings housing numerous exhibits ranging from the king's personal effects, his military decorations, collections from his travels, to old pottery and stunning artworks depicting the king's ancestry and various scenes from Jogja's history. The complex is huge, and many exhibits had accompanying English signs, but by and large the depth of explanation is not as sufficient as those you may find in other museums. Still, it was enough to give one a basic understanding of the exhibits on display.

The architectural styles employed in the buildings within the complex also merit special mention as they comprised various styles. A wonderful place to spend a good 2 hours or so exploring. Highly recommended especially since the entrance ticket costs only 7000Rp for foreigners (and an additional 1000Rp for a camera permit).
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Peu ou pas d explication sur place. Sans véritable charme. Objets désuets exposés (vieilles photos politiques, objets de cuisines...)

Der Palast kann nur teilweise besucht werden, es gibt einen öffentlichen und einen privaten Teil. Für Freunde von vergilbten Bildern und Verehrungen der ehemaligen Führer ist das sicher ein schöner Ort. Die meisten Touristen verlassen enttäuscht die renovierungsbedürftige Anlage.
Leuk om de sultan geschiedenis van Yogjakarta te zien. Mooie authentieke muziek en poppenspel. Zeker de moeite waard. Als je een gids wilt, zoek die dan binnen (dames met rood witte blouse)
Tempel mit kleiner Ausstellung, bei der alles auf Indonesisch beschrieben ist. Somit für Touristen unlesbar. Anlage nicht der Wahnsinn, kann man sich auch sparen.

Palais assez modeste et pas d'explications en anglais. Peut être aurait-il fallu un guide mais on ne nous l'a pas proposé. Spectacle de marionnettes assez sympa. A voir si vous avez du temps, sinon n'ayez pas de regrets.
Entree 12500 rp + 1000 pour l'appareil photo. Pas de mini short, ni de marcel autorisés pour les hommes. Ferme à 14h.

The palace of the king is a nice sight but unfortunately most of the place is simply a museum for the previous kings and Indonesia's customs in general. Was nice but the sight is easily seen in just over 30 minutes. 
Tamensari is much nicer and should be prioritized higher.

Don't mention that the palace itself was not so grand. The place was low maintained. Stuff in the buildings which were supposed to serve as a museum, ex. old Europian style vases, was poorly displayed.

It was cheap, only 7,500 each for entry but we still felt ripped off. We paid the extra 2,000 to use our camera too but didn't even take any pictures! The only thing you can really see here is some crumbling mannequins wearing some clothes. Dusty, dirty save your time and money. May have been better if there were signs in English, but we couldn't understand any of the Indonesian signs. The only English sign I saw was "DON'T TOUCH"

Main halls are great (and worth a visit), nice (and big) wayang and gamelan performance, but the surrounding buildings containing the museums are somewhat disappointing.

Overall, maintenance needs to be done on the paintwork badly and better conservation (and cleaning) of museum pieces would be in place. Flags rotting and paintings hanging in moist rooms won't survive long. 

I feel if the many people sitting around doing nothing picked up a brush the place would look happy in no time.

There's the Sultant Palace.  We visited at 10am and there's a dance at 11am.  The visit was quite refreshing and I highly recommend it.  You get access to only some parts of the palace.  You get lots of sellers who wants to sell you souvenirs however negotiate hard.  A pack of 10 postcards does not cost 100k IDR.  It cost 3k IDR per piece elsewhere.  So the most it should cost only 30k IDR.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: It is touted as the best example of a Javanese palace...it looked more like a run down tropical resort and not very "grand" for a palace. Staff looked bored, no map, poor signage, no English information, a lot of poorly displayed items in dusty cabinets. Luckily it's cheap and takes about an hour to walk around. It's something to fill in a morning but don't come to Yogyakarta for just this.

Visit if you want to know more about the Sultan. Worth a visit once! 

Entrance fee per pax: IDR 12,500
For camera taking: IDR 1,000

Een bezoekje aan het Kraton wekt grote nieuwsgierigheid, maar wat je eigenlijk wil zien, is niet voor publiek toegankelijk. De gidsen zijn langdradig. Toch kun je een bezoek aan het Kraton niet overslaan.

You must visit the Kraton if you visit Jogja. This is the palace of the royal household of Jogjakarta. I was informed that the current Sultan and his family still live within this complex. There was a Gamelan orchestra playing when we visited. We sat through the performance and it was mesmerising. Beautiful melody from the gamelan instrumants accompanied by singing by a gamelan diva. Its interesting to see the way the structures within trhe palace have been positioned in construction. There are different wings for prines and princesses. The palace guards still wear the traditional guards' uniform. Most structures are pavillion-like in nature and this gives the feeling of serenity within this walled complex. Get the services of an official guide. It isnt expensive and its worth it.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: 크게 볼 거리는 없는데 그래도 인도네시아 왕궁은 어떤가 싶어 가 봤어요. 입구에서 자원봉사 가이드분이 따라 붙으셔서 설명해 주시는데 나중에 팁으로 돈을 조금 드려야한답니다. 저희는 엄마랑 동갑이신 할머니가 설명해주셔서 음료수도 사 드렸네요. 족자를 지배한 왕의 역사와 유물 등을 볼 수 있고 건물구경 할 수 있어요. 크게 볼 거리는 없지만 지나가는 길에 들릴만은 합니다.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
Este sitio no merece nada la pena. Las visitas son guiadas pero se trata de culto a la personalidad del sultán...... Que si las zapatillas del sultan, su pijama, sus manoplas de la cocina...... Muy surrealista. 

No lo recomiendo para nada, vaya timo.
Yes I liked the attraction but want English audio or English on the signs on the items displayed. Overall a good effort

Lieu plein d'histoire, où une partie importante de l'indépendance indonésienne s'est jouée. Les gardes du palais sont nommés à vie, ce qui permet de rencontrer des gardes septagénaires-octagénaires en uniforme et avec kriss qui aident les touristes et font faire des tours commentés. Extrêmement intéressant et riche sur le plan culturel. Visite du Taman Sari s'impose (bains du sultan).
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Uno de los principales monumentos de la ciudad de Yogyakarta.Kraton significa Palacio Real en Javanes.Alberga algunas salas,en una de ellas puedes ver las fotos de antiguos sultanes entre otros.La entrada me costo 7.000 rupias,no es un lugar desde mi humilde opinion que me dejara impactada,pero si tienes tiempo visitalo

Abbiamo deciso di visitarlo per capire ancora di più la storia di Giava. Il biglietto d'entrata costa molto poco: RP 12.500 a persona più RP 2.000 per poter utilizzare la macchina fotografica. All'entrata abbiamo trovato una guida che parlava italiano quindi per poche RP ci ha spiegato la storia dei sultani di Giava. Visita veloce, non troppo interessante, poche cose da vedere: solo la struttura dove fanno le varie celebrazioni e qualche foto dei sultani.

Memasuki Kraton berarti belajar mengenai sejarah Yogyakarta dan kerajaan Islam di Indonesia yang masih bertahan sampai saat ini. Biaya masuk sangat murah.

Tips: Bila anda menggunakan becak ke lokasi harap hati-hati agar anda tidak dibawa berkeliling dahulu ke tempat-tempat yang lain terutama tempat belanja oleh-oleh. Harap perhatikan juga bahwa kraton ada jam buka dan tutup (sore hari). Anda bias meminta guide dari pintu utama (lokasi tiket) untuk menjelaskan apa isi dan sejarah di dalam kraton.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Kraton jogja memiliki banyak koleksi bernilai sejarah, tempat yg khas dan teduh. Namun perawatannya kurang sehingga beberapa koleksi tampak kurang menarik dan rusak.

Keraton is yogyakarta palace where sultan live. From the begining the tour guide (which is the abdi dalam for keraton) said that the palace is near but after a few hour walk , we realize it took too many time to explore all place. the guide always stop at shop across the site which is really wasting our time whereas we only want to see the keraton complex to learn about yogyakarta culture. We halt at middle of tour  because we need to go to other place again, after 3 hours wondering along the keraton complex .
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Tijdens een bezoek aan yogyakarta  kom je meestal wel uit bij de kraton.     Het paleis van de sultan is echter weinig bijzonders. De bewegwijzering is minimaal, de Engelse uitleg op de borden ontbreekt regelmatig, het tentoongestelde is behoorlijk gedateerd en het personeel was er verre van vriendelijk. Als je er tijdens je bezoek aan yogyakarta niet geweest bent heb je weinig gemist.
a visiter si vous avez trop de temps, mais palais et musée assez vieillots. Par contre très bon guide (une dame parlant très bien français et avec beaucoup d'humour)
Mal entretenu, difficile à comprendre sans guide et certainement plus adapté à des férus d'histoire que de simples touristes

Je ne vais pas garder un souvenir impérissable de la visite du palais du Sultan. Le lieu n'est pas spécialement beau, et il n'y a pas grand chose à voir ... des tenues traditionnelles portées par le sultan, sa femme, sa fille, les serviteurs ..., des instruments de musique, des photos des 10 sultans....
La seule chose que j'ai trouvé sympathique lors de cette visite c'est notre guide - non seulement il avait une tablette pour nous montrer les différentes cérémonies qui ont lieu dans ce palais, mais le plus improbable c'est qu'il a sorti une vidéo de Christophe chantant "Aline" .... c'est mon prénom. Alors là je dis chapeau ! Je me souviendrais de la visite grâce à cela.
Après la visite, qui est plutôt rapide, on nous a proposé une visite des ateliers de batik dans les petites ruelles alentours. Ce fut rapide, et nous avons atterri dans une boutique. Mais franchement, ils ne sont pas insistants et nous sommes repartis aussitôt.

Francamente solo he visto el palacio por fuera ya que los horarios de apertura son muy cortos aunque parecía haber escolares dentro. En todo caso el complejo es decepcionante, esta abandonado y totalmente seco. Una lastima que con las posibilidades que podría tener toda esa zona no le saquen partido, realmente le pondría un 2 pero me parece injusto sin haber visto el palacio por dentro.

Nous n'avons pas ete conquis par la visite du palais, que nous avons trouvee sans interet. Comble de malchance, aucun spectacle n'etait propose ce jour la. Une visite que vous pouvez largement rayer de votre liste.

Kraton terletak di dekat Malioboro. Untuk sampai di tempat ini, kita bisa berjalan kaki atau naik becak dayung dari Malioboro. Kraton buka sampai pukul 15.00 WIB. 
Kraton tempatnya bersih, dan nyaman. Sebuah wisata budaya yg tidak boleh dilewatkan.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Lo que queda de esta palacio real esta bastante descuidado, por lo que no se ve nada espectacular. En unas pocas salas se muestran fotos de como era el palacio, y piezas y elementos de la cultura javanesa, pero todo muy descuidado y sucio

The Sultan's Palace or also known as Keraton Ngayogyakarta Hadiningrat is located in the city of Yogjakarta. It serves as a cultural center and has a museum displaying some artifacts of the Sultanate.

Opening hours : 08:30 hrs to 12:30 hrs except for Fri and Sat closed at 11:00 hrs.
It is closed in the afternoon. So do check your timing.
Entrance ticket for foreigner is Rp 12,500 ( inclusive of English speaking tour guide )
Also you have to pay Rp 1,000 per Camera / Video cam.

This place is consider a sacred place, hence proper and respectful dressing is required.

The kraton is the one of remain kingdom in Indonesia, where the king and royal family stay. The compound including museum, balairung, gamelan performance stage, royal mosque, and royal bathing place. Chariot museum, arsenal museum and water palace also located in the nearby area.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: This urban complex is a city inside a city. When you enter the walls you take a time tunnel and see how it was the life of the sultan and his servants in past times. Architecture is very well preserved, there are very nice houses and, of course, the sultan's palace.  IMPORTANT: When you get to what seems the main entrance, don't go in there, that's a fake one. You have to walk a little more and you enter the real palace.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Kehidupan Kraton memang susah dibayangkan oleh orang biasa, seperti saya. Pasti kita semua pernah bertanya-tanya, kayak apa sih rasanya jadi raja, enak nggak sih jadi pangeran dan puteri, coba deh kunjungi kraton jogja. Walaupun Jogja ini masih ada raja dan masyaratnya masih hormat betul pada sang raja, kita sekarang bisa berkunjung ke Kraton tempat tinggal para keluarga bangsawan di masa lampau. Kita bisa melihat barang2 peninggalan kraton, dan cerita2 yg menunjukkan perjalanan hidup keluarga kraton. Bakal ada tour guide dan bagi yg kepengen tau lebih dalam, disarankan banget untuk menyewa salah satu tour guide ini. Tour guidenya adalah salah satu abdi dalem Kraton. Keluarga abdi dalem ini, sudah dari nenek moyangnya selalu mengabdi kepada keraton, walaupun mereka tau upahnya juga sangat sederhana. Pembiayaan untuk maintenance kraton ini sangat besar, namun menurut saya kondisinya terawat baik. Pokoknya kalo mampir ke Jogja, sempetin deh ke Kraton. Lebih bagus lagi kalo bisa datang waktu ada performance tarian tradisional jawa. Lebih krasa Jogjanya. Selamat jalan-jalan!
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Kraton is in the middle of Jogja city. On January,24, there is a great ceremony for Muslim. The guard of the palace and also some local residents well dress formally in army suit and walk out from palace. There are crowded everywhere. Watch out your personal belongings. My bag was cut and my smartphone was stolen. Still, it was a pleasant trip.

Avevamo tempo da spendere in giro per Yogya e visto l'economicissimo biglietto di ingresso del Kraton abbiam deciso di visitarlo.
Il palazzo è una zona centrale ai piedi della via principale del turismo!

Devo dire che non mi ha trasmesso molto, è poco curato e sembra che venga aperto al pubblico tanto per dar da fare qualcosa ai turisti che girano per il centro!
Da visitare sicuramente dopo i principali siti di interesse.

Onestamente ho trovato molto più belle e interessanti alcune abitazioni reali sull'isola di Bali.

Честно, ожидала намного большего от посещения. Как звучит - дворец султана! А по факту симпатично только пара мест, да и то крыши у павильонов. Но посетить всё-таки стоит для общего развития. Вход дешёвый, а разрешение на фотосъёмку стоит смешные деньги 1 000 рупии (4 рубля по курсу:)) Для обзора фотографии, картины, посуда, одежда. Много пыли и паутины, но в Индонезии это почти во всех музеях - тут это нормально. Так что не стоит особо на это обращать внимание и искать злой умысел. Дворец султана открыт до 15.00, а в дни национальных праздников до 12.00. После дворца лучше потом посетить ещё водный дворец в Taman Sari. Дорогу до него спрашивать у местных.

Liburan bersama keluarga kali ini tentunya tidak melewatkan ke Kraton Yogyakarta, kondisi yang tidak ada perubahan dan tetap masih terawat dan kondisi yang sangat ramai pengunjung, toilet yang bersih, namun semakin banyak pedagang yg berjualan di lingkungan keraton.
Faktor Penarik: Ketertarikan Budaya, Ketertarikan Fasilitas, Ketertarikan Suasana
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Bagi kami, wisata ke keraton adalah salah satu cara untuk memperkenalkan sejarah kepada anak-anak. Tiket masuknya pun sangat murah, hanya 5 ribu rupiah saja. Di dalam kita bisa berkeliling, ditemani guide dengan biaya yang terjangkau.

We had an Abdi Dalem (roughly, servant of the Sultan -- king) guiding us around. It's fascinating to learn about the history of how the palace used to look like, the Hindu, Chinese, and Islam influence on the building, the "zero point" (Titik Nol), past sultans, and people's view on the current intrigue in the kingdom. The building itself is not particularly impressive, and I imagined someone walking around without a guide would not find much to appreciate.
Kraton Jogja merupakan tempat yang wajib dikunjungi jika kita ke Jogja, karena merupakan peninggalan kebanggaan Indonesia dengan tradisi yang masih terjaga sampai sekarang

Dentro del día que dedicamos a Yogyakarta desde Bali nos llevaron (como a casi todos) al Palacio del Sultán. No es un sitio espectacular pero tiene su atractivo. la visita es guiada y al final se le da una pequeña propina a la guia. Algunos pequeños pabellones museo de interés relativo. Dde todos modos no me desagradó su visita.

The sultan's palace which is still in use for special occasions. It is essential to have a guide here as all the rooms look very similar and the little that is labelled is written in Indonesian. Once you've paid for your ticket, the uniformed guides of varying languages  are waiting and operate on a donation/tip service. 
It's not spectacular but fascinating all the same.

Whilst In Yogya, we had planned a day to go and see all the usual sights. First stop was the Kraton. Maybe I had too high an expectation, as I was slightly underwhelmed by the whole experience.

We took one of the guides allocated and she did her best to try and make it interesting, but it's quite difficult once you have seen the main palace from the cordoned off point. From then on it's just a procession of one room displaying gloomy exhibits after another.

There was a dance show in traditional costumes taking place when we first entered which was quite interesting and another pavilion opposite displaying  instruments.

If you have time, then visit - if not, don't feel like you missed much.

Wat een oude troep is het daar zeg.. Geen bezoek waardig. Ga dan naar de oude binnenstad en ga onder begeleiding van een lokale gids (biedt zich vanzelf aan) een bezoek brengen aan bv de ondergrondse moskee en loop heerlijk door alle steegjes in de buurt. Vergeet niet de gids een tip te geven, daarna kun je via hem nog veel meer trips goed en prijswaardig ondernemen.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
Don't believe the hyperbole of Lonely Planet and other travel guides – the Kraton in Yogyakarta is an interesting place to visit, but isn't the opulent experience you'll be expecting.

While the buildings and gardens are interesting and often beautiful, the collection of 'treasures' owned by former sultans is shockingly poor, and displayed in dusty cabinets that make the palace feel more like a thrift store than a royal residence.

Worst of all is the collection of items that once belonged to the sultan Hamengkubuwono IX, which includes his excellency's broken bathroom scales, a half-used jar of sugar, a bunch of plastic takeaway spoons, and two soiled dishcloths pinned to the wall with rusted thumb tacks.

We visited the Kraton on Saturday, which meant we were also treated to a shadow puppet show in the main performance area. However, as the white sheet on which the shadows were cast was covered in unsightly yellow stains – and we could see the bored-looking musicians regularly stopping for cigarette breaks – the magic was shattered.

We thoroughly enjoyed visiting the Kraton, but for all the wrong reasons. If you have time to kill in Yogyakarta, don't miss it... just try not to giggle and look disrespectful in front of the grim-faced royal guards.

Kraton Yogyakarta ini lokasinya tepat di jantung kota Jogja.
Kraton ini merupakan istana raja Jogja. Namun telah dijadikan tempat wisata jika tidak ada kegiatan keraton. Kraton ini sangat ramai dikunjungi wisatawan, terutama wisatawan domestik, apalagi saat periode liburan anak sekolah. Hal ini membuat nuansa kraton menjadi tidak terlihat kental karena semua wisatawan, sebanyak apapun itu bisa masuk, jadi di dalamnya terlihat sangat crowded sehingga saya tidak bisa melihat-lihat isi keraton dengan seksama.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: terletak ditengah kota jogja gampang buat buat diakses, cukup tour dengan becak maka itu sudah termasuk ke keraton, Didalmnya hanya sebatas bagian luar saja yang bisa dimasuki tidak untuk dibagian dalam. Jadi penasaran apa saja isi dalam keraton
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: the Kraton means in english is Palace. The palace is full of historical meaning, and also the place of big event for the Sultan. You can also see many heritage from the first Sultan of Jogjakarta. the story of Indonesian fight to freedom, the Jogjakarta culture. They also provide guide to explain about this Keraton and the Sultan with his families
Bagus untuk liburan keluarga menambah pengetahuan dan sejarah....letaknya strategis,keraton jogja adalah salah satu situs kerajaan tertua yang masih ada, hingga 9 generasi keturunan sultan

If you visit this place after dark, you can get a whole new experience. since people still live in there, so i guess u can't unless you have special pass. even under broad daylight, i can feel eery feeling creeping on me. some people believe that some spirits are there. so come and enjoy all the history and culture they offer.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: So I go there without expecting much. After Solo,'s prince palace also not much, that was worst. Without a guide forget about it. The guide gives it life and he also used videos on his Samsung Pad, that was a great idea.For historical purposes it was worth it, not unlike my Solo experience. I do not know if all guides are the same but Nur was good. I gave hime 50,000 and he was happy and worth it. The surrounding was more interesting. Ok it could be missed or not, no matter unless you're around and want to do the things to do. Enjoy anyhow, we are traveling, not to be forgotten and through this we get to meet locals, isn't it what counts.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
Our guide/driver brought us here during a private tour of Java. Then he arranged for a docent (local guide) to take us around the Kraton. Without this person, my spouse and I would have had no idea what we were viewing or where to go.

The palace is a series of open air pavilions within a very large compound. It is effectively a walled city. Most noteworthy is the Golden Throne Pavilion with its marble floor and ornate roof.

Many of the pavilions are used as museums. And many are VERY boring: one houses an extensive collection of gifts from European nations; another contains the royal family tree and old photos and portraits. 

As a whole, the sultan's palace is just an okay place to visit.

Our guide was very thorough to the point of being extremely tiring. My spouse and I were relieved to finally escape the palace environment
nice palace. the information is in indonesian only. do avoid the becak drivers in the neighbourhood. Most of them are frauds.

Dengan adanya pemandu,..bisa lebih mengerti. Kunjungan saya yang lalu tidak menggunakan pemandu,..kita hanya bisa membaca apa yang tertulis saja,..bila menggunakan pemandu,..bisa mengerti hal-hal yang tidak tertulis tentang sejarah kraton Jogjakarta, karena hal kesejarahan ada hal-hal tertentu yang bisa lebih baik bila dijelaskan secara lisan, misalnya dalam hal yang mistis tentang keraton Jogja. Perawatan keraton perlu ditingkatkan. Pemandu bisa membantu memfotokan para tamu sehingga dokumentasi kunjungan saya lebih bagus. Tiket masuk murah , ada tambahan biaya untuk yang membawa kamera, Rp. 1.000,-

Our visit to the Kraton was made better by a delightful guide whose knowledge and ability to answer our questions in an interesting way really made the visit. The buildings have significance and the lives of the sultans were worth investigating. It helps a non Indonesian to understand more of the life and history of the people of Yogyakarta and surrounds. Our guide had excellent English!  Watch the steps here and there and bathroom facilities.

Every Sunday at 11.00  am is a practice of kraton dances with live orchestra and kraton singers. Every week from a different school of dance. At every age and level. Most of the times 3 or 4 dances are performed. The costumes are wonderful in colour and detail, and the dancers immaculate make ups. De dances are very refined. So not to miss. If you want to sit on a chair be there at 10.30!

I think most visitors will be disappointed with this visit. Unless you have a special desire to see a range of framed photos of old sultans in badly presented rooms, I would suggest you use your time in yogya to greater advantage.

Toured the Kraton today. Travelled from our hotel by becak which is always an interesting challenge. The Palace itself though interesting is quite restricted. There are many bale pavillions which you cannot enter and as these seem to have the greatest decoration it is a little dissaponting. The guide (13,000rp 'donation') explained things well however there were no explanations in other than Indonesian so if you say "no" to a guide, you will have no idea what you are looking at.

We enjoy learning the history of the ountries we visit so a bit underwhelmed by this site.

This is the palace of the Sultan and is not something not to be missed. It is a letdown for those who have visited castles and palaces elsewhere. This is a very simple place with of course some history attached. Hiring a guide is a must who can at least tell some stories as otherwise it's pretty dull.
There are certain interesting aspects like the old folks being appointed as security guards - keeping alive the culture Jogja is known for. Locals take this as a matter of pride to be appointed a guard in the palace

Final Say : Include if you have spare time. Hire a Becak from outside your hotel and enjoy the surroundings also
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
Der Sultanspalast besteht aus einem öffentlichen Teil und einem Bereich, der noch vom aktuellen Sultan bewohnt wird. 
Mit einem Führer, die auch in deutsch kommentieren, begibt man sich auf einen Spaziergang durch die Anlage. Man bekommt den Hof zu sehen oder auch diverse Instrumente und eine Kammer mit vielen Gastgeschenken ausländischer Würdenträger, die mal zu Besuch waren. 
Leider ist das alles irgendwie nicht so richtig fesselnd und so ist man am Ende froh, dass man nach etwa einer Std fertig ist.
Siehe auch: http://joinourjourneys.blogspot.com

Sebenarnya saya sudah sering berkunjung ke Kraton yogya ini, namun baru kali ini memakai kasa pemandu. Ini pun karena kali ini sayap membawa teman yang kebetulan orang asing dari Hongkong.

Tentunya harus pakai pemandu yang bisa Bhs Inggris .. Seorang ibu yg usianya lebih dari 50 tahun menyambut kami dan kemudian menjelaskan dengan rinci semua bangunan, dan juga benda2 yang ada di dalam kompleks istana sultan Yogya ini.

Kunjungan yang berkesan dalam waktu lebih dari 1 jam. Salut dan salam hormat untuk ibu guide yang luar biasa!

We used one of the offered guides for a tour of the palace and I can imagine that without her we would have lost interest much quicker than we did - which was still pretty quickly. I personally found the surrounding city much more interesting and would recommend getting lost (temporarily) in the alleys.

Con il biglietto che pagate avete automaticamente una guida al seguito, che vi spiegherà tutta la storia e le diverse usanze, le guide sono molto disponibili, come un po' tutta la popolazione indinesiana.
Il palazzo è carino, ma niente di speciale. La guida vi porterà in un atelier, dove vedfete favolosi dipinti in tecninca batik, ATENZIONE, acquistate le opere direttamente all'accademia dell'arte dove avrete più scelta e i prezzi sono decisamente migliori.

Liburan thn 2015 ini kami mengunjungi Keraton Yogya. Saya dan suami bersama 2 orang anak kami yg sudah remaja. Ini kali pertama mereka mengunjungi keraton. Mereka sangat "bersemangat" melihat2 isi dari Keraton, terutama lukisan 3 dimensinya. Tujuan saya mengajak mereka ke tempat2 bersejarah ini supaya mereka tidak hanya mempelajari sejarah melalui buku/sekolah, tetapi terutama mereka bisa melihat langsung apa yg dipelajari tsb. Sebab biasanya yg dipelajari melalui visual itu lebih lama tinggal dlm ingatan. Saya rekomendasikan tempat ini unuk dikunjungi, selain utk menambah wawasan pengetahuan anak2 kita, juga utk melestarikan budaya Indonesia kita.
They have really friendly staffs here and you should definitely visit the place if you want to learn about their history
we had a free tour organized by the hostel who provided us an undergraduate in tourism. we had good knowledge of history background about this palace that made our trip interesting.

especially because it shows the culture of the people. Most of the place is about the Sultans over the years. You will see their socks, clothes, shoes, camping gear, flash lights etc..

Besides this insight to the local culture, this is a nice building group. You should visit when there is a show ( almost every day something is happening). It's nice to see the traditional music and dancing in a place like this. 

PS. People are very annoying on the way there and back. You will be THE tourist and will be seen as walking money. Try to ignore them:) 

PS2. do not fall for the "original" batik that the guides will try to sell you. It's obviously not any different than the one in the stores.
Faktor Penarik: Ketertarikan Budaya, Ketertarikan Fasilitas, Ketertarikan Suasana
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: banyak yang boleh dipelajari untuk sejarah raja - raja di jogja. ada quote quote menarik boleh diambil dari ungkapan raja dipamerkan di kraton ini. bapak bapak dan ibu yang berpakaian tradisional jawa juga memberikan impak pembelajaran budaya serta tradisi istana jawa. juga elemen baik sekali untuk bergambar! awas tiketnya kerana aku terkeliru dengan tiket masuk ke satu tempat lawatan di hadapan kraton itu.

If you love history, its good to visit here as there will be tour guides waiting for you outside to bring you in. It get bored if you do not love history as the palace is quite 'old look' be it inside and outside.  Nothing much to admire about, except the feeling of warm inside.

Ons bezoek aan het Kraton, zal niet de mooiste herinnering aan onze reis naar Indonesië worden. Erg veel opdringerige becak-rijders die ons naar het Kraton wilde brengen. Veel opdringerige verkopers/sters voor de deur. Eén maal binnen werden we rond geleid door een moeilijk verstaanbare gids die een enorme haat koesterde tegen oud president Soeharto en dit heel duidelijk liet merken. In het kraton zijn wat foto's, kleding en andere voorwerpen te bezichtigen van de Sultan. Ook is het paleis aan de buitenzijde te bewonderen. Aardig on te zien, maar niet meer dan dat. Kost nog geen euro per persoon.

Tidak akan pernah bosan mengunjungi salah satu peninggalan sejarah masa lampau. Setiap berkunjung rasanya saya ikut masuk ke dalam cerita atau pun kisah yang merupakan penjelasan atau keterangan dari setiap koleksi keraton yang dipajang.  Yang saya suka adalah pementasan tari penyambutan yang biasa ditampilkan di pendopo.
Don't mean too be rude, but saw a lot of staffs working in the palace, however,  i think they lack a cleaning contract or simple repair works like electrical contractors, if u know what i mean....

Kraton ini memiliki wilayah yang sangat luas tetapi sayang sebagian besar lahannya sudah di bangun rumah rumah baru tempat keturunan abdi dalam kraton dan anak cucu keturunan raja dari selir .
Tetapi tampak kejayaan dan kemegahannya masih terlihat dengan bangunan bangunan kuno dan dinding tembok yang sangat tebal .
saya lihat cukup terawat baik semuanya , bahkan seperangkap gamelan dengan perlengkapannya masih bagus.
suasana di dalam kraton yang selalu terdengar gamelan gamelan bersenandung enak sekali di dengar seolah olah hidup pada jamannya.
maka kalau ke yogyakarta wajib datang
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Как ни странно, ничего особенного... Да, дворец, но, если честно, не очень впечатлилась. В общем-то интересно было посмотреть сквозь стекло на фигуры в национальной одежде в двух павильонах, но стекла поставлены с наклоном и отражают тебя саму, чтобы рассмотреть то, что за стеклом, надо напрягать зрение. А вообще, если хотите тишины и какого то стародавнего покоя, сходите... Посидите в тени на ступенях, посозерцайте стену с барельефами, отражающими значимые моменты истории, прикройте глаза, послушайте ветер... Возможно из тишины вы увидите больше, чем просто глазами...

Zo onder de indruk was ik niet. Het paleis wordt nog bewoont en er zijn zeker plekken die erg mooi zijn. De bewakers in klassieke kleding zijn fraai om te zien. En het museum heeft veel te bieden. Daarbij is jammer dat het slecht onderhouden wordt.

Avevo letto pareri non molto lusinghieri prima di andare e invece è stato piacevole ed interessante.  E' chiaro che ognuno ha il proprio bagaglio e modo di percepire le cose, ma io consiglio questa visita, invito ad utilizzare un paio d'ore della propria vacanza in questo luogo. Il prezzo di ingresso è di circa 2 euro e  inoltre, uscendo, si può seguire un percorso tra botteghe artigianali fino alla moschea sotterranea e al water castle. Si può essere guidati da utilissimi cittadini di Yogya che incontri proprio all'uscita e che, pur portandoti presso i propri amici/riferimenti,  non ti obbligano a comprare nulla e ti danno tantissime buone indicazioni. Se fai acquisti inoltre, puoi verificare successivamente di aver fatto anche buoni affari. La nostra "guida" ci ha portato anche ad un matrimonio dove siamo stati accolti come gente di famiglia: fantastico!
Faktor Penarik: Ketertarikan Budaya, Ketertarikan Fasilitas, Ketertarikan Suasana
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: When you come to the Kraton you just have to see the show. Every single dance move had a meaning. Most people don't notice the museum at the back since it's not shown on any signs.

Have strong history around the place, can visit alot of places inside the Kraton including access all information that relate to Kraton living aspects . but then remember to have a guide with you to explain about the history and the meaning of all stuffs inside the Kraton . if u dont have it your trip here will be confusing , long and boring. *so many stuffs , places , information , culture , etc inside this place, mostly relate to Kraton or Jogja's history*
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: I have taken many friends on their first visits to Jogjakarta.This is very interesting going back through the royalty in the area being self governed but the building and the display is very unruelly and untidy . Really need a good clean up and tender loving care... Right at the end of the city and some really great local street food surround the location..hope you like spicey food.

Non seulement le palais du sultan est magnifique mais il faut aussi faire les petites ruelles avec les maisons basses réserves aux serviteurs et employés du palais. Vous serez accueilli toujours avec le sourire et de plus on souhaite aussi vous prendre en photo avec toute la famille.

Kraton Yogyakarta sangat terkenal, selalu menjadi tujuan wisata study tour anak sekolah hingga dewasa, sebaiknya tidak ke sini pada masa liburan sekolah, karena pasti sangat padat. Sebaiknya mengajak guide supaya kita mengerti sejarahnya. Sayang benda2 bersejarah dan bangunan kurang terawat baik, mestinya ada dana khusus untuk perawatan, karena barangnya sangat berharga.

Merupakan komplek lokasi tempat tinggal Sultan Hamengkubuwono di Yogyakarta. Lokasi yang bagus untuk mempelajari sejarah kesultanan di Jogja sekaligus melihat benda-benda seni di Keraton. Di waktu-waktu tertentu dapat menyaksikan event pertunjukan tarian.

Vintage 😉😉

Kota yg akan selalu di Rindu kan dan di Rindu kan lagi. Tempat bersejarah yg sangat kaya akan budaya dengan bangunan yg indah serta menjadi salah satu magnet dan daya tarik wisatawan domestik maupun luar negeri.

Sangat mengundang rasa ingin tau untuk jauh lebih dalam melihat segala bentuk tekstur bangunan dan budaya yg terdapat di dalam nya.

Terimakasih Yogyakarta, ak akan selalu Rindu ingin berkunjung ke Kota nan Indah dan penuh dengan warisan budaya nya.

Love u Kota Yogyakarta 😘😘
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Die Anlage ist tatsächlich in die Jahre gekommen und dürfte sicherlich Investitionen in Renovierungsarbeiten verdient haben. Aber um das Land, die Stadt und die Geschichte zu verstehen, der sollte dieser besonderen Anlage seine Aufmerksamkeit und seinen Besuch widmen. Es liegt in unmittelbarer Nähe des Stadtzentrum und nicht zu weilt entfernt. Die ausgestellten Fotoaufnahmen und das Videocenter vermitteln einen sehr guten Eindruck von der Geschichte und der aktuellen Lage. Am Eingang gibt es Guides, die gegen eine kleine Bezahlung einen Rundgang angenehm organisieren. Der Besuch selbst dürfte eine Stunde betragen, dann haben Sie alles gesehen.

Tempat sangat bersejarah, minta guide biar lebih afdol ceritanya dari a sampai z, bisa lebih terperinci ceritanya, ada toko souvenir nya juga untuk dilihat lihat, bawa hp yg ada kameranya atau kamera harus bayar, tidak mahal kok hanya IDR. 1.000 saja per buah kok

Opzich wel leuk om te zien, maar niet echt bijzonder. Weinig tekst en uitleg als je zonder gids de kraton bezoekt. veel van hetzelfde en erg toeristisch.. Schilderijen van de sultanfamilies vond ik wel mooi.

Keraton Jogja jadi destinasi wajib tiap wisatawan yang ke Jogja. Tapi kebanyakan orang keliru dengan Museum Keraton Jogja, padahal sudah bayar tiket masuk, sayangnya banyak yang tidak diberitahu.

Untuk ke Keraton Jogja memang agak perjuangan karena becak lumayan mahal karena banyaknya wisatawan yang kesana. Kita diwajibkan membayar tiket masuk dan setiap kamera yang kita bawa kedalam. Untuk Guide harus membayar lagi, padahal seharusnya sudah termasuk.

Didalam keraton, banyak sekali sejarah tersimpan mulai dari kereta tua yang pernah dipakai Sultan pertama sampai baju dan alat-alat dapurnya. Betul-betul mengesankan. Tempatnya bersih dan terawat.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Kraton Yogyakarta ini sangat mudah dijumpai karena terletak di tengah kota. Saya ke sini pagi hari karena Yogya mulai terik setelah pukul 10 pagi. Meski bangunan kraton ini telah berusia cukup tua, namun bangunannya tetap kokoh. Sembari ke kraton bisa membayangkan bagaimana Yogya masa lampau.

The Kraton was a nice place to see considering its history. I enjoyed seeing the Kraton men and women (locals who work there) who have kept the traditions and still wear the same thing as their predecessors did back in the day. That made the experience feel more exciting. There was also a gamelan & singing performance when we were there. Much of the museum displays however were just dusty and not well presented.

Le palais du sultan est un site historique  à voir  lors de la visite de Yogyakarta.Des concerts de gamelan sont  organisés dans la cour principale du palais ainsi que des visites guidées très instructives et indispensables pour mieux comprendre l'histoire du kraton .Cependant,les collections ne sont pas exceptionnelles et ne présentent pas un grand intérêt.Nous n'en garderons pas un souvenir très mémorable.

Apart from my kind, humorous, elderly guide, this place really doesn't offer much. Not big enough to inspire awe and not well maintained to keep up with the times. Architecture is pedestrian and displays a little sad. If you're visiting Yogyakarta, this can be at the bottom of the to-see list.

Anda pertama kali berkunjung ke Yogyakarta? Tempat ini merupakan kewajiban. Kraton Yogyakarta mudah dicapai baik dengan berjalan kaki maupun moda transportasi umum. Dengan membayar 5 ribu/org aku berkeliling disini. Sayangnya tidak ada pemandu yang menemani sehingga aku tidak tahu sejarahnya. Oya, dianjurkan untuk menggunakan pakaian sopan dan tidak memakai topi pada saat memasuki kawasan ini, topiku harus dibuka. Hanya berfoto saja aktivitas yang kulakukan. Selebihnya hanya menikmati suasana saja karena Jogja identik dengan Kraton.

The tour can be done in 15 mins - the guide is good but not terribly well informed and the  exhibits are nothing particularly interesting. We were there on Sunday and managed to catch the weekly traditional dance performances at 11am .

Une visite instructive sur l'histoire de Java
Un cadre agreable au calme apprécié
Un guide est necessaire pour profiter pleinement de l'endroit
La dynastie des sultans n'aura plus de secrets pour vous !
Un incontournable de Jogya

Het was lekker rustig, en de gebouwen zijn mooi bewaard gebleven, er speelt een orkesten, en de mensen lopen in Javaanse kledij. Het is relaxed rondslenteren, met in diversen paviljoens gebruiksvoorwerpen en kledij uit vroegere tijden.  Niet echt spectaculair maar een leuke afwisseling.
kayak balik dizaman raja2 tempoe doeloe... bangunannya bersejarah banget... disini kita bisa tau dan belajar mengenai keturunan keluarga kerajaan Jogjakarta... sayang kurang terawat,...
When ranking with other palaces around the world, Kraton is just okay. Not a must see destination but more like a place you should visit for the sake of visiting, if you have time.

The entrance fee is 12.500 rupiah per person and at the gate we were greeted by a woman who is actually part of the abdi dalem & is also the Kraton's official tourguide. She was telling us all the interesting stories from the start of Sultan Hamengkubuwono the 1st till the current one the 10th. It's more a place if u really like to know the history of Jogjakarta, because there isn't something specific u could see. But I still think it's a place u have to visit if u ever come to Jogja.
The place is tiny as compared to many other palaces around the world. Nevertheless it's informative to understand the history of the royal family in Yogja.

We only understood what was happening because we had engaged one of the guides on site - he spoke multiple languages and was very knowledgeable about the history of the palace. Otherwise, everything else was in Bahasa Indonesia. We were taken to see a variety of costumes, the coronation hall and several photos/portraits of the sultan, but that was it. We were taken afterward to a batik art gallery where there were many batik art pieces on sale - it's free and completely up to you if you want to buy one.

Wij vonden het wat tegenvallen en misschien waren onze verwachtingen wel te hoog. We mochten eigenlijk niets binnen bekijken. De Gids deed wel heel erg zijn best. Alle gebouwen aan de buitenzijde wel gezien maar de binnenkant van het paleis was niet te bezoeken!!!

We visited this still used royal palace on a day where lots of school groups were there as well and sometimes we felt more sensational than our surrounding. As we are both tall and white haired we were surrounded by dozens of teenangers who wanted to take their selfies with us. It was fun, if a bit embarassing (we are no film stars!). The buildings were beautiful, the exhibition was not so interesting as it consisted mainly of photos of the Sultan's family. Our femal guide was lovely and we had lots of fun together.

Today is the second day of jogja tour after visiting Borobudur, lava kali tour, prambanan tour on the first day. We continue to visit sultan palace, taman sari west castle, ngasem bird market, bringharjo market for one day visit. And in the night we watch Ramayana dance.

Interesting place. It is Sultan palace, maintained very well. Everything is still original. 
To enter this palace, you must buy a ticket that available at the entrance. If required, there are officers who can guide you there. they explain in detail about this place to you. but of course with a little fee.
But what bothers me is the pedicab driver, at a low price to certain places they offer.
Zeer sterk vervallen. Weinig te zien, vooral veel van hetzelfde: de spullen van de sultans. Verhaal achter de spullen is niet echt duidelijk.

debu tebal di seluruh gedung. Sayang sekali. Yang menarik jika didampingi oleh pemandu wisata yang bisa menjelaskan tentang sejarah Keraton ini. Jika tidak, Anda hanya akan melihat barang-barang tua yang kurang menarik saja.

Une visite sans grand intérêt. On traverse des salles, avec des objets divers sous vitrine ( appareil photo, couverts, théières etc)... On y voit des portrait d'anciens sultans...
J'en garderai pas un souvenir impérissable....

As the Sultan still lives there you can't see too much. A guide will make it more interesting but will overcharge you and take you to his mate's Batik shop where you will be pressured into buying Batik.

A lot of people have said to get a guide to make it more interesting, just make sure you get a good price and aren't taken to the Batik shop.

It is not a typical palace one would imagine. However, a guided tour might make it a ted interesting as he will be able to explain the details that will otherwise be left unoticed (not that it is significant, but every bit will help make it interesting.) After the guided tour in the palace, the tour guide will take you to the exteriors to some batik shop. I thought that was MORE INTERESTING. The land belongs to the Sultan, and therefore, many dwellers still respect him for giving them "an opportunity" to live comfortably* By local standards. The batik shop is inexpansive and there are some arts pieces worthy of purchase. Not heftily overpriced. I bought some without even bargaining.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: This place is the Jogjakarta Sultan palace who is presently living in. Therefore only part of it is accessible so the visit can be done in 15minutes only if you do not take a guide. The place is surprisingly very simple for a "palace" and I guess that's why quite some people are disappointed... However, we took a guide who was very interesting and told us a lot of stories about the Sultan life, the use of the various areas of the palace, etc and believe me or not but we spent there 1.30 hour ! And my kids of 11 years old where very pleased by the visit... So I can only recommend you to go there but indeed get a guide and get interested...

Nous avons visité le kraton 1 matin (prendre l'entrée à l'ouest pour y entrer et non celle au nord qui est une fausse), nous avons eu le droit à 10h à l'orchestre qui jouait... Nous sommes resté 15 minutes (musique un peu répétitive) et après nous avons continué la visite.  L'archeticture du lieu n'a rien d'exceptionnelle et dans les salles d'exposition rien n'est traduit en anglais donc on ne comprend rien... C'est domage! Un petit effort de traduction pour que les touristes puisse se plonger dans l'histoire serait pas mal!
マリオボロ通りからベチャで向かいました。舞踊を観たかったので、「南側宮殿へ」と言ったのに、北側に連れていかれました。仕方が無いので北側に入り、後で南側を訪問しましたが、やはり南側王宮の方が、展示物も博物館並みで、見ごたえが有り、良かったです。ジョグジャに来ると、必ず訪れる事をお勧めします。
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
Ne pas s'attendre à visiter un palace.
Malheureusement nous ne voyons pas grand chose, le roi habitant encore les lieux ...avec un guide on a quelques explications mais la visite reste tout de même sans grand interet.
Le palais en lui même ne se visite pas mais les annexes oui mais rien à voir avec le genre de palais ou château en Europe

Geweldig om te zien, het paleis van de sultan. Deze woont er nog steeds maar je ziet veel over de geschiedenis. Absolute aanrader, neem wel een gids, dan krijg je een hoop meer informatie en achtergrond verhalen. Must see in Jogya
Simplemente NADA que ver. No pierdas el tiempo ahí. El lugar es feo, poco interesante y con tierra. :/

Difficile de plonger dans le passé tant les explications manquent (aucune traduction en anglais). Succession de salles / lieux sans grand intérêt quand on ne visite pas à l'heure du spectacle du jour qui doit, lui, être un gros plus pour la visite. Nous avons été très frustrés de ne rien apprendre ou découvrir, ce lieu nous a vraiment déçu et pourrait être bien plus attractif. Certes, ce n'est pas cher mais cela ne justifie pas une visite incontournable pour autant !

Tempat ini wajib dikunjungi jika kita berkunjung ke Yogyakarta, selain tempatnya yang "Jawa" banget disini juga kita bisa belajar mengenai silsilah keluarga kraton yang memerintahkan Yogyakarta. Harga masuk kesini pun murah hanya 7000 buka dari jam 09.00-14.00. Di kraton ini juga merupakan tempat tinggal raja yang memerintahkan Yogya.
There's nothing much about the palace. It was a bit of a waste of time. Get a guide for IDR30,000 which makes it more informative than walking around clueless.

From its outlook, you cannot imagine that it is a palace . No luxurious surroundings, it seems to be more plain than Ubud palace, ordinary as a local school site. I was told by my hired driver that a performance will be held on 10 a.m; after my arrival, I found it was overcrowded with school kids for outing. Many of them like to take photos with two aged-guards, of course just like a backdrop. The puppet performance is held under a well-decorated pavilion ( no steps allowed inside) with a matched background music play by court musicians,unfortunately, the story seems to be all Greek to me. After fifteen minutes, I finally gave it up.There are also rooms for displaying the batiks of Sultans as well as some photographs taken for the royal families. Without a permission, you are not allowed to take any picture inside the exhibition halls.Besides, the Sultan is still living with his family members inside the palace, therefore some parts of the compound are not allowed to enter .

Sebagai warisan leluhur, tempat ini sangat cocok dijadikan sarana pembelajaran sejarah, sebab selama mengunjungi kraton akan ada guide yg menjelaskan asal muasal atau kegunaan tempat itu pada jaman dulu. Jangan datang kesini saat tahun baru, sebab kraton tutup.
erge leuke rondleiding met een objectieve kijk op de geschiedenis van de sultan en zijn rol in de ontwikkeling van Yogja
It is nice to know that the King and Queen so live there and it is a working Palace.  what always gets to me is everyone serving the King is a volunteer.
Incontournable visite du palais du sultan de Yogyakarta qui peut se terminer par l'écoute de chants et de musique javanaise, donnés par un ensemble choral qui à lieu vers 10 heures le matin.

Interesting place to go and get a bit lost. It is filled with winding streets and feels like a little village within Yogya. 

You can find workshops making puppets and Batik. They do try to sell you stuff but it's not a hard sell. We just watched and asked a few questions before politely leaving. 

You have to pay to go to the water palace but if you weave up the side streets you stumble across it for free... But the tickets are only around 12000Rp anyway!

Definitely worth a wonder around and in the morning before noon you catch a free dance or puppet performance which is cool.

This is the Palace of the Sultan, who has a double duty as the governor of the Yogyakarta special province. You can visit the Palace grounds and the reception pavilion as well as several exhibitions on the Sultan's family. It is a very interesting place where you can learn something about the modern history of this country and the region. The English-speaking guide was friendly and informative. The exhibition on royal Batik cloth was also interesting. You have to buy a permit to take pictures inside the palace, but it was not expensive. The dancers and musicians perform periodically in the pavilion immediatlely inside the main gate.
Interessante a visita ao Palácio para conhecer um pouco da vida do sultão, no dia que visitei em alguns momentos havia apresentação de música e danças tradicionais.

I don't think we would have gotten much out of the Kratonw ithout a guide, so I would highly recommend saying yes to one when the ticket people offer you one. There is no charge - donation only. We learned alot about the Sultan and his family history from our guide, who spoke excellent English. The sights are pretty, but wouldn't be very interesting to see without the context.

It was raining at the time I went, so it made for a bit more interesting experience with crowds hovering under shelters and making it seem a bit more crowded than maybe the norm. 
There are many different rooms and sections to see stuff, but I ended up viewing them quite quickly as compared to the groups that I witnessed around me. 

The staff were around but not really attentive.  The hours it is open is minimal and it closes in early afternoon.  I'd suggest seeing it as it doesn't take too much time and it is worth the experience to see the history of the royal courts.

I can imagine that in its heyday, The Kraton would have been a bustling, interesting, beautiful place. Not so much now..... We were there on a Saturday and arrived just in time to see the Wayang Kulit (shadow puppet) show. It started later than it's 10:00am starting time and we persevered through the first 20 minutes, but nothing much happened. They moved the puppets a couple of times behind the screen and there was a lot of talking in Javanese? (don't think it was Bahasa Indonesia as neither my husband or I could recognise anything and we speak a decent amount of Indonesian).....although the PA system was so muffled that I'm not sure anyone would have understood it. The gamelan orchestra was nice though. 

The palace itself seems to have some interesting things, but nothing has signs so you don't really know what you're looking at. We were chatting to another tourist who did a guided tour and she said that she didn't really learn much either.

I think if a bit of money was put into the palace and it was made more tourist friendly (with the use of signs, booklets etc) it would be much more interesting for the visitor. In my opinion, you're better to spend your time visiting the other tourist sites which are well done and so impressive.

Braucht man nicht gesehen haben - ist schön, kulturell und architektonisch , aber eher ein Zeitvertreib !!!

Man hat kein Museum oder Fotomotive - ist nicht lohnenswert, aber südlich davon ist noch ein schöner Kraton & dort auch das ominöse Café mit aus den Katze Po Bohnen :0)
Music, costume, pavilions, and batik museum are the core value of Jogja kraton remained today. Don't miss.

The Kraton attraction divided into two sections. North wing display the Sultan Throne Area, traditional clothes and ceremonial of Java.   The tour guide will explain about the architecture of Kraton also. South wing displays batik textile, royal photos and utensils (plates,cups,chairs, etc.). Overall, it is interesting place to visit for the first time. But, looks like there's no new collection for years. The only section that looks like new for me is Sultan HB IX wing, a glass-wall room with memories of Sultan HB IX.

Wanted so much to really enjoy this visit but it was less interesting than I thought and I particularly appreciate history and culture. Our assigned English guide was rather strict with us and what we needed to see, know, take pictures of -- struck me as more Soviet than Indonesian, completely lacking friendliness. 

Of interest is the architecture of the traditional Joglo structure and perhaps you might be fortunate enough to wander upon a wayang or dance performance.

Lovely palace where the sultan still lives with his (only one) wife. Side rooms with artifacts from previous sultans, carriages, gifts, etc. But overall, meh.

Sad to say but this palace needs some investment or more atention from local government. The building itself looked old and abandoned...such a pity. The big grass field (supposed to have green grass) and landscape in front of the palace looked dull and dry, not attractive at all and it killed our mood as we were heading to the palace. They should come up with smth good to make this historical place shine again.
Faktor Penarik: Ketertarikan Budaya, Ketertarikan Fasilitas, Ketertarikan Suasana

Review Text: Keraton, tempat yang sangat wajib dikunjungi, kita bisa tahu sejarah mengenai keraton, silsilah keluarga keraton, benda benda peninggalan dan lain lain.

크라톤을 가기 위해 발걸음을 옮겼을 때 가장 놀라웠던 것은 크라톤 앞에 형성된 노점들이었습니다. 여전히 왕이 살고 있다는 왕궁 앞에 일반 서민들이 이렇게 자리를 잡고 생계를 위한 활동을 할 수 있다는 것 자체가 저에게는 엄청난 충격이었습니다. 왠만한 나라에서는 보안과 소음 등 여러 이유로 이를 못하게 규제했을 터인데 이곳의 국왕은 정말 백성을 사랑한다는 느낌을 받았습니다. 그 노점들은 정말 없는게 없을 정도로 다양한 음식과 물건들에 어린이들을 위한 작은 놀이동산까지 갖추고 있었기에 그 모습은 매우 신선하고 부럽기도 했습니다. 크라톤 내부에서는 수시로 전통 공연이 펼쳐지는 듯 하니 시간이 충분하시고 더위에 지치시면 그 앞에 앉아 전통 공연을 감상하시는 것도 좋을 것 같습니다.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Palacio del Sultán. De barato acceso, invertir solo la 1h30 que se necesita praa recorrerlo si se tiene tiempo, si no, dedicarlo mejor a ver los templos de Borobudur y Prambanan

Kral gitmiş ama sarayındaki eskiler içeride duruyor. Genelde tüm eski  çatal , bıçak , metal aksamlar  İngiliz ve U.S. menşeyli . Geniş bir alan gezmemekle bir şey kaybetmiş olmazsınız . Yogyakarta nın içinde  bu yapıdan başka görülecek bir şey yok denebilir.

Memasuki kraton yogyakarta sangat terasa nuansa tradisional dan sejarahnya. Dapat dilihat bangunan tradisional, benda-benda unik dan bernilai sejarah. Di kota yang modern tapi masih berdiri kraton bernuansa tradisional. Sangat direkomendasikan untuk pelancong yang menyukai tempat tradisional dan sejarah.
Die herrliche Anlage, die nach wie vor von der Familie des Sultans bewohnt wird, vermittelt einen guten Eindruck des höfischen Lebens.

К большому нашему сожалению, мы не смогли осмотреть дворец изнутри. В город приехал президент, и дворец был закрыт для официального приема. Но мы смогли походить вокруг. Нас даже пустили во внутренние дворики. Очень вежливая охрана с пониманием отнеслась к приезжим из такой далекой страны, как Россия! Все без блеска и роскоши, сдержанно и мило. Особенно чудесны малюсенькие улочки, на которых раньше жила дворцовая прислуга.

Saya baru saja mengunjungi Keraton Yogyakarta setelah bertahun - tahun tidak mengunjunginya. Tampilannya masih sama tentu saja, sayangnya pengelola keraton tidak membersihkan dengan baik tempat wisata ini, sehingga terdapat sampah yang berceceran. Informasi wisata pun tidak diperbaharui sehingga terlihat kusam karena sudah di pakai bertahun - tahun.
Untuk menambah pengetahuan, sebaiknya anda menyewa guide yang akan menjelaskan berbagai sejarah keraton Yogyakarta yang menarik.

Bagi Wisatawan yang suka dengan tempat bersejarah, saya rekomendasikan untuk mampir Keraton Yogyakarta (Keraton Ngayogyakarta Hadiningrat). Selain ada Museum, Keraton ini masih menjadi tempat tinggal Sultan (rumah tangga istana).

Museum ini banyak menyimpan berbagai koleksi milik kesultanan, termasuk berbagai pemberian dari raja-raja Eropa, replika pusaka keraton, dan gamelan. Malah bisa mendengarkan Live Music Gamelan. Dan kalau lagi beruntung, bisa melihat tarian jawa.

Untuk melihat di dalam Keraton ini, saya sarankan menggunakan Pemandu, karena Pemandu nya sangat sopan dan lemah lembut. Pemandu nya gratis, tapi saya sarankan diberikan Uang Tip ya. :)

Tempat sangat luas sekali, jadi butuh waktu sekitar 1 - 2 jam untuk berkeliling di dalam Keraton ini. Tempatnya bagus untuk menjadi Photo Spot atau Selfie. :)

Untuk menuju lokasi ini, lebih baik naik Becak atau Dokar (Kereta Kuda) dari Malioboro, jadi bisa lihat pemandangan selama perjalanan ke Keraton Yogya ini.
Faktor Penarik: Ketertarikan Budaya, Ketertarikan Fasilitas, Ketertarikan Suasana
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: must take a guide to explain you the delicate details of this wonderful landmark. the children especially loved the stories and details about the royal family "normal" day lives. wonderful experience!
Enjoy to visit this beautiful palace. Near the famous Malioboro street too. You should go here for the classical feeling.

I visited the Kraton with my (Indonesian) family in March 2015. As a museum professional I found the Kraton very interesting, and there was plenty to intrigue the grand kids :)

How much you get out of your visit depends on the quality of the guide assigned to you. While my guide was a lovely lady I felt the tour was a bit rushed. The reason for this became clear at the end of the tour when the guide told me her son was an English language tutor and would I spend some time talking with his students.  

While my family had warned me that individual school children might approach me and I'd said I was fine with that, neither they nor I were prepared when we were confronted by an entire class wanting one on one time from me. The fact the students were literally already there, all waiting for me at the end of our tour, put me in a position where I couldn't politely refuse.  

I stayed with the students while my family went to watch the trainee Javanese classical dancers practicing, something I'd been looking forward to seeing. 

I spent one on one time with three students. Each student had about 30 questions, which is way too many, and they all had exactly the same list, which gets a bit boring for the English language speaker (me). Also, if you are going to do this kind of thing properly you really need to get a discussion going with each student, you need to ask them questions as well.  Just replying to their questions doesn't teach them anything.

While I didn't mind doing this - they were nice students - it was very time consuming and by the time I rejoined my family they'd had quite enough time watching the dance practice and wanted to move along.  

I'm not saying don't do this if you are approached by English language students. Not at all.  But learn from my mistakes: 

1) set a time limit -10 minutes per student would be good, no matter how many questions they have on their list.  Make sure the tutor times it.

2) ask to see the tutor's list of questions before you agree.  If it's long get the tutor to choose ten from the list, or select questions yourself that make a foundation for good discussion. 

Have fun :)

Review Text:
Beautiful Java palace that is more than one complex, very luck visited with Indonesian friend born and lived in Jogja all her life so had probably better insight than other reviews. 
Better to go early (when it opens), we visited 3rd and 4th March and very quite.  
Try Bale Raos in one of the outer courtyards for a lunch snack and drink, very beautiful, cool setting serving food and drinks that (apparently)  favorites of Sultans past and present.
The presentation of the museum collection, information, labeling and the level of access is typical Indonesian, a mix of good and bad, but well worth a visit.
We visited twice during our 5 day stay and would still return again.
