El palacio es curioso, y agradable de visitar, pero no ofrece nada realmente interesante, ni lujoso, ni demasiado exótico. Si alguien espera encontrarse un palacio como los de los reyes de Tailandia, por ejemplo, se equivoca. Nada más lejos de la realidad.
El edificio poco tiene de espectacular. Es algo pintoresco, pero no tiene demasiado valor arquitectónico. Y el paseo por los patios resulta agradable, pero nada más.
En las salas del palacio se exhibe una colección de objetos pertenecientes a los sultanes de Yogyakarta. Objetos de lo más variopinto: desde esculturas y otros regalos de gobernantes extranjeros, hasta utensilios de cocina de lo más vulgar, cutre y simple, como ralladores, espumaderas y cucharas de los que puede haber en cualquier casa, y que no se comprende muy bien por qué forman parte de una exhibición de objetos supuestamente artísticos, valiosos o de valor histórico.
La historia del palacio y su entorno son interesantes, pero, hablando con franqueza, aquí  hay poco que ver.
Ojo con las tiendas de supuestos  "artesanos" del batik y la seda situadas en el entorno del palacio. En un altísimo porcentaje, se trata de trampas para turistas, que ofrecen productos muy caros y de no muy buena calidad en relación con su precio, además de no ser especialmente bonitos.
En resumen: si no tenéis nada mejor que hacer en Yogyakarta, y os apetece resguardaros del calor o de la lluvia tropical, podéis visitar el palacio. En cualquier otro caso, no os recomiendo la visita. Hay muchas otras cosas que disfrutar en la ciudad y en su entorno, y también se puede aprovechar mejor el tiempo descansando o en la piscina del hotel.

Ada dua tipe pemandu wisata, ada yang resmi berseragam dan duduk berjajar ketika kita masuk pintu dekat loket tiket dan ada abdi dalem yang juga bisa menjelaskan sejarah dan filosofi keraton tapi bukan pemandu resmi. Semua detail di keraton bahkan di ukiran ada artinya. Ada titik yang katanya pusat kota yang persis di tengah-tengah antara Gunung Merapi dan Pantai Selatan. Di titik itu kalau kita teriak akan bergema, tapi kalau bergeser 1-2 m saja dari titik itu sudah tidak bergema lagi. Sayangnya agak kurang terawat, banyak yang pudar dan berlumut.

When we left the hotel on a taxi, it was nice and bright.  However, when we got there, it rained very hard towards the middle of our tour. We were soaked before we got back to the hotel. It was crowded.   We had no guide so we just walked aimlessly and tried to see as much as we could.  There were a lot of pictures of the sultan and his family.  There were displays of his certificates, household furniture, China and kitchen utensils.

A collection of the Sultan's families pictures, paintings, furniture, batik, dishes, crystal, costumes, and gifts received from visiting dignataries are displayed. There are also several large areas where traditional dance and music are presented on Sundays. The Sultan no longer resides here, but has moved into a more modern residence on Malioboro Street.

Understand the Kraton would like to maintain it's surrounding as closed as possible to it's original state. However, trust the Kraton administrative can further enhance and change the indoor area into perhaps to a more royalty looks, planted more trees, water fountains to cool down visitors during hot/warm weather season.

Also, take the time to look at the Sultan's name at one of the Kraton's area and see if you can remember it
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: See one of Indonesia's remaining monarchs in Central Java. By the time I visited Kraton, there was an exhibition from the museums near Kraton. It was worth it, entrance fee was for only $0.4 and the permit for taking pics was only $0.2.

Qualche spoglio padiglione aperto, tra cui la sala del trono; qualcuno chiuso e vuoto, salvo qualche foto d'epoca alle pareti e... lavabi pure d'epoca scrostati e scollegati; una galleria di costumi inaccessibile, visibile solo attraverso i vetri di un altro padiglione; grandi gabbie con galli da combattimento... sembra che anche il sultano abbia deciso di snobbare il palazzo andando ad abitare nei vicoletti che lo circondano. Vicoletti senz'altro più interessanti, con le case basse, le gabbie degli uccellini appese alla porta, la gente che sorride, gli artigiani del batik e delle marionette wayang.

Got the news that the Jogja King Palace was opened to the public. So do not want to lose the opportunity we immediately took the time to visit there. Moreover, seem that the God of Rain in the morning was quite friendly as it gives the opportunity to the God of Sun to warm the earth's that have been watered by non-stop of rain for the last few days.

The Jogja King Palace is just close from where we were staying at the Ceria Hotel in Judoningratan as known as Jalan Ibu Ruswo. A few time of walk while enjoying the warmth of the sun, we get to the North Square that looks full of entertainment stand because there was “Sekaten”, a week long Javanese traditional ceremony, festival, fair and  night market commemorating the birthday of prophet Muhammad. But seem the booths were out-of-duty because the night market would be opened from 4.00-12.00 PM. Only food and clothing booths seemed get ready to start selling their merchandise.

There are some places in the palace complex which can be visited. The first is the Ward called “Mangunturtangkil”, the second were the Museum of Royal Carriages, and the third was the Palace itself. To visit to the three places, for each place we must pay 5 KRup (kilo, thousand rupiah, about 40 cens dollar) per person with a permit photographing 1 KRup (8 cen dollar).

The Ward “Mangunturtangkil” was last used at March 7, 1989 when the coronation of Hamengku Buwono X becomes the King, replaced the Hamengku Buwono IX who famous in its struggle for independence, and had served as Vice President accompanied President Soeharto, The Smiling General. As a king, Hamengku Bowono IX was very famous with his word "Tahta untuk Rakyat" (Throne for the people). From the ward is reportedly able to see the “Tugu” monument at the intersection of street of Malioboro-Margomulyo-AMSangaji, and street of Sudirman-Kiai Mojo. Leaving the ward, we were going to the Museum.

In the Museum of Royal Carriages, lined standing carriages that operationally be pulled by horses, including the hearse to carry away the nobles to their final rest. The carriages are still be used depending on the needs, such as for the procession, royal wedding, or funeral ceremony. We were then going to the Palace.

At the entrance to the palace complex was seen Kencana ward in where ongoing “Wayang Kulit” (shadow puppet) performances.  At the ward, we also had met Rizki Kuncoro Manik the youngest courtiers of Jogya King Palace which last night was seen on Local TV Yogyakarta. Seem many visitors at that time, especially school children from various cities in Indonesia, and the atmosphere is quite crowded. Foreign tourists were also seen but only a few people.

We were observed several rooms containing the relics of the inscription, “gamelan” (Javanese music instruments), antiquities, furniture, sculpture, portrait, painting, and batiks of special royal motives (not permitted to take pictures). 

And the observation was stopped after a long time walk in the building and the foot was felt stiff and heavy to be ordered to move. Then slowly we were back again to the Ward Kencana, took a rest while watching performances of Wayang Kulit. The show evocative back memories of watching the shadow-puppet when we were child. After a while, we took off back to the inn. On the way, we bought a special local drink called “dawet ayu” and lunch consist of Javanese salad rice and coconut ice with palm sugar at roadside stalls. It was enough to energized us to get home.
Faktor Penarik: Ketertarikan Budaya, Ketertarikan Fasilitas, Ketertarikan Suasana
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
他の方も書かれていますが、王宮というよりは博物館といった感じでした。

また、入場券（5,000rp）とは別に撮影するために（3,000rp）を別に徴収されました・・初めから撮らないところが面白い。

ただし、展示内容自体は非常に多い感じがしました。

ちなみに、朝は9時（2014年12月末）からOPENしています。

＜補足＞
年末なのかもしれませんが、目の前の「王宮北広場」が移動遊園地化されていました・・面白かったです。

This site has a great deal of significance locally and is crowded with local visitors.  Driving along Jalan Malioboro and entering the Kraton itself you are transported into the last century, if you ignore the roaring traffic.  The Kraton has not been spruced up for visitors and consists of a number of rooms with display cabinets holding artifacts belonging to the father of the present Sultan.  The guide will take you through dusty courtyards filled with visiting school groups and other tourists and expects a tip at the end of the tour.  The toilet facilities here are very basic.
If you have a chance drive past the rear of the complex to view the entrance used by another branch of the family, which overlooks a deserted town square.  The narrow streets laid out in a grid-pattern with colourful houses probably offer many interesting photo opportunities.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Meski telah berusia ratusan tahun, namun Keraton Yogyakarta beserta isinya masih sangat terawat, bersih dan suasana sakral masih menyelimuti di beberapa area. Berada di dalam keraton harus berhati-hati dalam tindakan maupun dalam berkata-kata. Apalagi saat berada di bagian museum kereta. kadang tanpa ada sebab, bisa merinding.

Enteuscht und sauer. Enteuscht darüber wie klein, heruntergekommen, ungepflegt und dreckig es war. Sauer auf die abzocke mit dem Eintritt und den 3000rupi die später noch verlangt wurden um Fotos von dem bisschen schlecht gepflegten Plunder machen zu dürfen. Noch dazu kommen die ständig nervigen Schlepper bzw. Guids. Wir sind ja schon viel von SOAsien gewohnt, aber Yogyakarta mit dem "Palast" und alles drumherum war eine bittere Enteuschung. 
Persönlich kann ich nur dringend davon abraten.

Sangat bagus sebagai tempat untuk menambah wawasan, membandingkan suatu kerajaan dengan kerajaan lainnya, hubungan antar negara, penghargaan yang diterima dll.
Tempatnya bersih, rimbun, sejuk.

Wir waren geschockt über die abzocke am Palast. Erstmal 5000rp. "Eintritt" und dann musste man, wenn man bilder machen wollte pro kamera auch nochmal 3000rp. zahlen...  ganze 3 fotos haben wir gemacht.. das war. Ich würde nicht nochmal dahin fahren. Überall wir man angesprochen angesprochen und das wirklich dauernd.  

Was gab es zu sehen? - nichts. . Außer ein paar Hähne die eingesperrt waren und ein bisschen Gerümpel.  Nichts prunkvolles, was man normalerweise von einem Palast erwartet.  

Wir sind super enttäuscht..

een attractie die in mijn de moeite waard is om te bezoeken. ga niet vergelijken met de huidige paleizen of zo. historisch gezien een plek die je gezien moet hebben als je Yogyakarta bezoekt.
de welkomstceremonie op de maandag was een lichte teleurstelling, maar daar kan ik mee leven.

If you want to learn about the history of Yogyakarta kingdom or "kesultanan Yogyakarta",come to this place.You will learn about  the kingdom in a real palace.This is the part of yogya's palace which is open for public.
You will find a real yogya's palace architecture now and then,complete with the collection of royal palace.You will see The history of the kings,pictures of royal family,and also their outfits .You can also find some real "abdi dalem" (the servants of king and his family).There are also some tourist guides who fluently speak in different language:english,french,dutch,etc.This place is absolutely unique and a must visit place if you come to Yogyakarta.

Although the building is not so spectacular. i would still say its a interesting place to visit. Please do note the opening hour. 

The Palace Guard and palaceTour Guard  is Voluntary but i was advise to give small token (which i did it willingly).

Do try the food in the restraurant surrounding the palace...

it was a nice trip to this historical site, unfortunately they closed at 2 pm. when we came, some palace tour guide come to us and show us around keraton, there's great history behind this old palace. and he lead us to "Museum Kereta" and to Batik Tulis market wher my parents bought some batiks there. our guide was nice and funny so we didn't even realize we have been there for 2 hours. a recommended sightseeing for any tourist.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Incontournable, mais pas exceptionnel, il faut juste se méfier de tous ceux qui vous proposent de voir du batik toute la journée mais sinon visite intéressante à faire, en plus nous avons eu un guide qui parlait français et nous a très bien renseigné.

The architecture is less stunning that the various temples travellers come to Yogyakarta to visit (Borobudur, Prambanan), but the Sultan's Palace is worth and hour or two or your time. Built in the Javanese style as a series of open rooms in extensive gardens, it is a fascinating insight into the history of what was once a kingdom, through the Dutch colonial period and to the present day. The rooms containing  artefacts are poorly lit and signage is entirely in bahasa Indonesia, but entry includes a free, well-informed guide.

The palace is still in use by the Sultan and his family, and much of the grounds were, therefore, closed to the public.  The demonstration of shadow puppetry, and the large gamelin orchestra behind it were very interesting.  The rest - not so much.  There was a minimal fee to take pictures inside.

De vorige keer dat we er waren was het gesloten. Dit maal nog een keer heen, maar wat een tegenvaller. Weinig te zien, een paar gebouwen, niet veel bijzonders. Speciaal hier op zondagochtend naar toe gegaan omdat er om 11 uur een dansoptreden zou zijn. Om een of andere reden ging dit deze zondag niet door.
Good place for educational trip and include culture and historical tour. The explanation of guidance was good when i came here last time

Borubadour and Prambanan are the main draw cards for Yogyakarta...but once you're done checking out those main sights, it's worthwhile to check out stuff in town..and Kraton should be the first stop...enough to keep you interested for a few hours

Voor het belangrijkste paleis vond ik dit tegenvallen; het water paleis iets verderop is veel mooier. Het Kraton is niet groot, een entreezaal, daarna de trap op en je staat in de belangrijkste zaal. Binnen 30 minuten heb je dit wel gezien, inclusief de foto's in de achterliggende gebouwen.

Definitely schedule a visit to this palace complex. It is worth going with a guide who can explain what different buildings etc. signify. Also very interesting to be there when the musicians are playing the traditional instruments. If you know South Asia this type of complex will be familiar but still it is worth the trip for all the royal paintings, architecture, furniture, memorabilia, artefacts etc. - we visited in Jan 2013 (ignore date below) and took a good few hours inside the complex and then a few more walking around In the area surrounding the complex which is full of cool shops etc.
Faktor Penarik: Ketertarikan Budaya, Ketertarikan Fasilitas, Ketertarikan Suasana
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
Just hope that you get a good guide to take you around the Kraton. We were blessed to get one. The guide comes with the ticket that you pay. It's just a small token sum that should not stop you from tipping the guides after they bring you around for a tour. You'll enjoy the gamelan performance, it usually goes on for hours. If you are in a hurry, you may want to spend 10-15 minutes to appreciate the traditional music. You may want to check the schedule of the different performances to maximize your experience at the Kraton. 

You'll get to see some of the palace staff (abdi dalem) who volunteered their service to the Sultan. They'll be seated around the palace grounds. Do ask politely before taking their photos and do ensure that you do not show your backs to them in your excitement to capture the moment with the palace staff in their traditional attire. 

As you go around, you will notice that the exhibits and artifacts are not displayed in the most desirable environment. You wished that they are kept properly so that such valuable pieces of history are preserved well for longevity sake. Hence, it's good to visit as soon as you can, while they are still in their best condition. 

I do recommend that you go around with a guide to really appreciate the significance of Kraton Yogyakarta.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
綺麗な入口を入ると、広大な空間に数多くの建物があります。
その建物の中には、当時使用していた道具類や歴史資料が展示してあり、
荘厳な王宮というよりは博物館のような雰囲気でした。
多くの観光客が訪れるため、王宮前はバスや車で大渋滞です。。。

I didn't see much that was exciting and the things that were were not labeled in English well.  The "English" tour guide could barely speak English and she was, at best, annoying because she kept talking and was completely not understandable.  The only thing I'm sure I learned is that there are a lot of folks in the city that mostly sit around and do nothing and are on the Sultan's payroll.  Don't bother wasting your time going here.  And, before you go in you will be directed by "helpful" folks in a direction away from the Kraton - clearly looking to sell something, probably Batik.

Last time I went to Kraton when junior high school (yes, 10 years ago)
When you enter to this place, you can feel the magic so strong.
But yet I so surprise this visit (Nov 2014) this place untreated well. Dust everywhere. Mock-up glass broken and yet there's a warning but why management doesn't try to fix it?
Messed up overall.

The overall condition of the building and exhibits is quite poor. The information for the exhibits is mostly in Indonesian and there seems to be a focus on quantity rather than quality of artefacts. Best part was the guide who told lots of stories and talked about the philosophy of certain aspects of the building and the history of Yogyakarta.

Went here on our last day.The building itself was just OK, not that interesting but we enjoy the history behind it.Thanks to our competent guide who did an excellent job explaining every little anecdotes of the kings.It was crowded when we visited maybe because it was on the weekend.

Setiap ke Jogja selalu tdk lupa berkunjung ke Keraton.
Tidak pernah ada bosannya. Suasana keraton yg dingin dan bersih, sejarahnya dan abdi dalem yg sopan dan berwibawa jd kelengkapan keraton yg selalu membuat kita selalu ingin kembali kesana.
Lingkungannya sejuk dan berkharisma.
Kalo berkunjung kesini harus mampir ke keraton.

Had a great guide who was very pasionate about the history of Yogyarta and the Sultan. We learned a lot about the culture and were amazed to hear how many volunteers were involved in keeping  the Sultan still resides in going

Кратон - дворец местной султанской династии. Довольно скромный, между прочим. Понравились красочные костюмы охраны и музыкантов - во дворе показывали что-то вроде кукольного театра теней. Обязательно зайдите в султанский музей - там даже султанские носки лежат под стеклом в качестве экспоната - хорошее настроение гарантировано))

Review Text: Sultanspalace In Yogyakarta vond ik niet boeiend, maar dat is persoonlijk. In een uur heb je het gezien. Entree is incl gids. Maar als je toch in de stad bent kun je voor die paar cent niet overslaan.

Having read about the touts and false guides in our guide book we made our way to the correct entrance early in the morning as they have traditional dances on some days. We had no bother getting entrance tickets at the ticket booth and proceeded in to visit the Kraton. Unfortunately there was no dancing on that day but we listened to elders reciting Indonesian poetry which was great too. 

The visit of the Kraton will show you items from the Sultan's collection and some real antique batik which are on display there, though the main display are the grounds, houses and rooms within the palace. You will learn about the history of the area and how dutch rule affected the Indonesia and how the sultan cooperated with them and how the Kraton still plays an important part in governing post independence. 

It takes a good two or so hours to visit so set aside a morning to visit.

as it was Sunday , their where the Dances too, very nice and so slow dancing,
historical info from a incl. guide , very good, , and you see the influence of trade, religions and lifestyle and totally very cheap trip

Di dalam kraton ini kita bisa mengunjungi beberapa peninggalan kerajaan di masa lampau. Seperti tandu raja, pakaian raja, gambar kegiatan raja dsb. Dalam kunjungan berkelompok kita akan dipandu oleh seorang guide yg sangat atrakrif. Terdapat pula area terlarang yg hanya boleh dilihat dr kejauh an. Tempat ini rupanya bisa menggambarkan lebih jelas bagaimana zaman dahulu kala kehidupan keluarga kerajaan begitu wah dan luar biasa.
Students like the Sultan's palace but again said that you really needed a guide to appreciate it and understand it. My students really liked the family trees.

Tempat yang bersejarah, namun saat berkunjung ke sini saya kurang terkesan.  Suasana dan aura kuno atau aura jaman kerajaan kurang terpancar.  Di sini kita bisa melihat diorama dan beberapa bangunan kuno.  Kamar mandi dan toilet sangat kotor, tidak dikelola dengan baik.
Faktor Penarik: Ketertarikan Budaya, Ketertarikan Fasilitas, Ketertarikan Suasana

Review Text: Nothing word could say and express to describes the best Indonesian heritages, all collection was in pretty good condition.

We visited this place last after we take a long walk trip around Malioboro street. I'm suprised how Yogya's netizen able to preserve well this place. There are some guide present right infront of the gate entrance. The guide will explain for us about all the Keraton Hall function and history also. I find one hall is very amusing which is the "Calling Hall" (hope it was right), which is the function for Sultan's right man to call the person prior meeting Sultan by clapping his hand. The clapping sound was able to hear until far away. This is one secret that our guide told us and we try at that time. We were not allowed to see the whole keraton (we only able to visit front side) for another side was prohibited, but if you were able to pay attention you will saw the corner of the Keraton in some street. If you are history people, you are very much invited here.

The Keraton is the palace of the Sultan of Yogyakarta. It is a touristic attraction in the morning and people can visit it. It is also an official palace of the government, since the sultan is also the governor of Yogyakarta.

Kraton means Palace.  This is the palace where the Royal Family (Sultan) lives with the whole family and staffs.  This is the must-visit place in Yogyakarta, but dont expect too much since the condition is now not really shows its beauty and grandeur.

We spent a few hours here, trying to gain some insight into the culture and history of this part of Java. Unfortunately, we had done little homework as we hoped that the vast royal palace compound might in some way be guided or self explanatory. Unlike others, we were not able to find a palace guide. 
We knew that we needed to take our time, and we wandered slowly through the many royal pavilions that house the multitude of brilliant artefacts on display, trying to absorb their meaning. We gained some understanding of a royal family that has endured the political changes that have shaped Indonesia. We could not, however put the pieces together easily, most probably because we were underprepared and unguided. My basic Indonesian helped a bit, but was not enough to convert a multifaceted visual display into a cultural experience.
If you plan to visit the Kraton, do your homework, make sure you get a guide and do take your time. This place is steeped in history but it requires work to scratch the surface.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
It is worth a visit thou this palace is not as 'grand' by any 'palace standard'! However, it is preserved well. Get a guide by the entrance, and he/she will be able to explain to you the history of the Sultan and the palace.
A pleasant walk around the vicinity - especially the surrounding 'Kampong' where most residents actually work for the Sultan.
The main hall (ceremonial hall) could get a better refurbish as we saw a lot of birds actually making their nest there, and it mess the place.
Overall, not a bad experience - worth visit at least once.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Jogja adalah kota yang masih menyimpan banyak nilai sejarah.yg begitu lekat dengan bangunan-bangunan yg masih bediri kokoh macam2 candi,dan yg utama adalah keraton jogja yg masih aktif dengan kegiatan nya.

Devo dire che, sebbene il posto non si stupendo, non ritengo sia del tutto evitabile! La strada da percorrere per arrivarci (Jl Malioboro) è a dir poco caratteristica, l'architettura del luogo è tipicamente orientale e per chi non fosse mai stato in Asia ha un sapore molto Cinese. Detto ciò una volta che si va a Yogya è un peccato non passarci due ore, farsi la camminata per raggiungerlo e magari poi girare a piedi nei dintorni dove per caso sono incappata in un bellissimo laboratorio tradizionale di marionette.

The tour of the Kraton (Sultan's palace) with a mandatory appointed guide, was a pleasant surprise. While the Kraton itself is not really an ancient monument, the grounds are well preserved, and the guide did a really good job of walking us through all the exhibit rooms, pointing out the stories and anecdotes. Seeing the batik weavers, and the music performers live, was a bonus in the morning. If you have 90 min, it's a good tour (not expensive) and gives you a flavour/perspective of a closer-to-present-day Java than the other sights around Jogja.

The Sultan's Palace is one of a handful of actual sites in Yogya to visit. It doesn't require a lot of time, and there are guides to whisk you around it. The collection of instruments and porcelain/glassware are about the highlights of the exhibits, but the real treat are the aging gentlemen who comprise the Sultan's Guard.

Keraton Yogyakarta merupakan salah satu dari sedikit peninggalan kerajaan di Indonesia yang masih terjaga. Terdapat beberapa ruangan yang bisa dilihat, diantaranya koleksi foto dan koleksi batik. Masih terdapat beberapa aturan yang tidak bisa dilanggar, misalnya untuk tidak menapak ke lantai tempat menyimpan benda-benda yang dianggap keramat. Selain itu terdapat pagelaran kesenian khas Jawa pada jam-jam tertentu yang banyak diminati wisatawan mancanegara. Waktu saya kesana, ada wisatawan asing yang menunggu pagelaran tersebut setelah terlambat mengikuti jadwal sebelumnya. Sayang, beberapa tempat masih kurang terawat. Diperlukan komitmen dari pemerintah untuk melestarikan warisan budaya yang bernilai tinggi ini.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: My visit here would have been much more enjoyable without the approaches of the fake guides. I enjoyed many of the exhibits and performances but found I was having to try and fend off the fake guides and other hustlers too often which was as exhausting as walking down Malioboro Road.

With cheap entrance fee we can see this historical palace of Jogja. But you won't get nothing if you just walk and see... so better take a guide (for free or you can give a small tip) that will tell you everything about its history, mystic story of the palace and family tree of the sultans. The guide will approach you once you enter the palace, almost all of them are old but they can speak in many languages. But be aware, after exit the palace they will lead you to batik shop or painting shop. It's okay if you interested (I bought batik painting of Ramayana story for IDR100.000), but if not you can refuse it politely.

ジャワ島の古都ジョグジャカルタは、郊外に大きな遺跡があるけど、街中にはあまりみるところは多くはないようでした。その中で、王宮は大きくはないけど雰囲気がよく２回訪れました。　緑が多いし、展示物も豊富です。　また、伝統芸能をやっていて、火曜日のジャワの伝統唄と木曜日のガムラン演奏を聴きました。　最初は椅子がいっぱいになるほど観客がいるけど、１時間半ぐらい演奏がつづくし、割と単調なせいかだんだん聴衆が減っていきました。　最後は拍手するひともまばらでした。

The Kraton is nice to visit for a few hours, especially to hear the live traditional music and signing. Make sure to find the main entrance beside the big clock, and not be distracted by some of the hustlers who will bring you to a very small museum
この王宮はまだ現役で、王様もおられるそうだ。勿論、国の政治は大統領制で行われてるけど、ある種の役割を持って賓客の接待やら儀礼的な仕事をされる場所になっていると聞いた。ここには伝統の民族衣装を着た警備兵がいて、威厳のある佇まいでみじろぎもしないでじっとしている。すべてボランティアなのだそうだ。代々の王家に伝わる家具、調度品などが見られ、運がよければ伝統舞踊も見学することができる。
Faktor Penarik: Ketertarikan Budaya, Ketertarikan Fasilitas, Ketertarikan Suasana
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Kita sering mengagumi suatu objek wisata karena sisi fisik gedung artau bangunannya padahal dibalik kemegahan itu ada kesejarahan panjang tentang Indonesia hingga mencapai kemerdekaan, peran dan fungsi Kota dan kraton Jogjakarta menyimpan banyak kisah yang patut untuk ditemu-kenali sebagai bagian dari perjalanan bangsa Indonesia.
Saai, niet veel te zien en niet erg mooi. Kan niemand aanraden er heen te gaan. Entree is wel erg goedkoop.

Je kan dit paleis niet vergelijken met een Europees paleis. De gebouwen zijn  nog wel waard om te bekijken (zeker bij het begin van je reis door Java) maar de inboedel en de zaal met geschenken is heel povertjes voor onze normen. Ik zou er niet voorbij lopen als ik de omgeving ben maar ik zou er niet speciaal heengaan vanuit een andere stad.

A very good value for money attraction. Only costs about 7000rp to get in, but there is a lot to see. We didn't get a guide but there are many available (just make sure they don't take you to a batik shop at the end of it).

Make sure to check the performance schedule. Most mornings, there will be some type of free performance - we saw a gamelan orchestra who were pretty good!
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
Très décevant et une orde de guidon qui vous agresse presque. Ces guides veulent souvent vous suivre après votre visite. Je vous conseille de refuser. 

C'est très endommagé et peu intéressant mais pratiquement gratuit alors si vous êtes en surplus de temps c'est ok mais encore je vous suggère plutôt le musée Budoyo juste en face.

Rien de transcendant dans la visite du kraton mais c'est a voir quand même.
De toute façon j'été venu la pour voir pranbanan et borobudur .

A palace guide is inclusive with the entrance ticket.Most of the guides are old .We had a nice lady who speaks good English.She took us around the palace giving us good explanation.
The architecture is nothing spectacular and a bit run down but the guide made up for that.
There's a fine-dining restaurant just behind the Kraton.Don't order the pasta there as they really don't know how to prepare western food.The fresh juices are nice.Food quite costly for Jogja standard.

Kraton yang benar-benar budaya totokromonya itu diterapkan sekali. Sampai abdi dalemnyapun sangat setia, rata-rata sudah berumur lanjut usia. Di dalam kraton kita bisa melihat banyak sekali   peninggalan-peninggalan zaman dulu. Dari lukisan-lukisan, kereta kuda, dll. Kraton ini di buka untuk umum pada jam-jam yang ditentukan, dan bila tidak ada kegiatan atau acara khusus di keratonan. Untuk wisatawan mancanegara ada tur gaide-nya sebagai penerjemah. Bila kita ingin tau lebih lagi tentang kraton, kita juga bisa bertanya dengan pemandunya.

Echt saai. Iets anders kan ik er niet van maken. Naast het feit dat de helft gesloten was, was de rest oud en vervallen. Zonde van je geld. Gewoon links laten liggen en kiezen voor de Prembanan tempel of de Borobodur

Entree + extra betalen voor het maken van foto's. Prima als het echt de moeite waard is. Paleis is niet bijgehouden en heel vies. Binnen 5 minuten sta je weer op straat. Jammer van dit stukje cultuur wat vervalt.
Non ha nessun fascino. Non ha niente di particolare ne dal punto di vista architettonico, ne dal punto di vista culturale. Ci aspettavamo di più.

I would not be giving a fair review so I just want to share my experience visiting this attraction. The whole walk ends in 15 min which was a let down for me.. this was suppose to be a main attractions  in the city. After I paid for the ticket the entrance, this supposedly tour guide take the ticket and follows in withe starting explanation. I clarify is he tour guide? he says he is the palace tour guide, he was helpful with taking picture but very brief in explanation, after circling the main hall and the small hall near the palace in house classroom, he guide us out the gate. I was disappointed the palace is only of 2 halls. when we says thanks at the gate, He says the tour is not finish and continue to lead us across the road through the small maze to end up in the batik shop.!! I felt cheated and decided to move on. Only in the next day do I realise from other pictures posted that I have missed the other part of the palace!! This unscrupulous so called guide steer us away to the exit to fill his pocket. What a cheat and a scam! I don't mind to pay for a guide because I believe to help the local tourism but I don't want to be cheated.  this is really scam! My advice, don't trust any of the guide at the entrance. and now I discovered the taxi had drop me at the side entrance and not the front hence I never realised there is another part of the palace!!

Si uno acude a esta palacio esperando encontrar un ejemplo del lujo asiático e otros sultanes, como fue nuestro caso, se va a llevar una decepción.
     Si ya se han hecho antes de ésta otras visitas a recintos en Indonesia, el viajero ya puede haber ido reduciendo sus expectativas, pero aún así, lo que queda de este palacio real no hace honor a esta calificativo ("real").
     solo unas pocas dependencias conservan algo de su posible esplendor pasado. Los holandeses y los japoneses lo han esquilmado a conciencia, y ls piezas que se exhiben son escasas y de muy poco valor. Las más llamativas hay que contentarse con contemplarlas en fotografías, muchas de ellas, bastante antiguas.
    La visita, como en casi todos los recintos históricos, deben realizarse acompañados obligatoriamente por un guía del lugar de que se trate, lo cual conlleva una elevada indolencia en las explicaciones, actitud que nada colabora a hacer más atractiva la visita.

si potrebbe tranquillamente evitare di visitare questo palazzo del sultano che davvero non ha nulla di interessante, qualche porcellana e qualche sarong ma rispetto ai palazzi a cui siamo abituati in Europa proprio non ci siamo. Diciamo che dato che l'ingresso costa poco e che a Yogyakarta non c'è molto altro da vedere fateci un giro così giudicate coi vostri occhi.

We went to see the Kraton and were forewarned not to expect too much. Actually, we still expected too much. While the history of the place might be impressive, the architecture is far from breathtaking. Still this was one of the most enjoyable experiences of our entire holiday, thanks to an extremely friendly lady who took it upon herself to guide us through the entire area surrounding the Kraton and the Water Palace (without expecting a tip, which was a wonderful change from what we had grown used to over the previous weeks). Hence, we found this to be an amazing day, but since that was a unique experience and not the typical visit to the Kraton, I cannot rate it with extra stars or points. Visitors to the Kraton should definitely prepare well by reading about the palace and its history, or get a good guide; it's definitely worth it.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
Vi risiede il sultano ed il personale che ci lavora lo anima.
Ascolterete musiche suonate dai Gamelan e vedrete il personale del kraton vivere questo posto come se i turisti non ci fossero.

Keraton Jogjakarta Hadiningrat, bukan hanya sebuah bangunan bersejarah, tetapi pusat peradaban. Nilai2 tradisi luhur dapat kita rasakan manakala kita berusaha mengetahui lebih dalam keraton ini. They provide a written explanation too for you to read. Too bad when I arrived I couldn't see the inside of the Kraton because they specific time for that.

Sudah berkali kali ke sini dan saya tetap puas dengan apa yang di tawarkan oleh Kompleks Keraton ini. Bangunan dengan penuh nilai sejarah dan warisan budaya ini masih sangat terjaga dan ini adalah salah satusarana bagi pemuda pemudi yang ingin tau sejarah indonesia dan sejarah jawa. Guide sangat baik dan sangat mengerti tentang Keraton, saya hanya berharap agar kebersihan Keraton terus dijaga. Saya rekomendasikan tempat ini !

We went in the eArly morning 8:30am as it just opens. This way you avoid teh crouds and the heat. Make sure you take the right gate at the -west side, entrance fee is 12,500 pp +1000 for camera. Another gate (norths) charges 5000/7000 rupiahs, but that's giving you limited acces,no guide. (Taxi drivers and touts tend to drop you at the latter, so be prepared). 
The english guide (included in ticketprice) is really good and helpfull. After 10:00 you can witness a gammelan or wayong performance, depending on the day of the week

Review Text:
If you're thinking about a visit to the Kraton, make it one of the first things you do in Yogya or you'll be bitterly disappointed! As many of the reviews suggest, there are definitely better places to visit and many more interesting.

It's ok if you've got an hour to spare. If you want an English speaking guide, you can expect to tip them about 40-50,000rp ($5). The guide is definitely worthwhile as they can explain all the artefacts, etc and give you information that you wouldn't find on your own.

You don't want to miss the Water Castle (tamin sari), which is behind the Kraton... It will amaze you, especially after a visit to the Kraton!

Review Text: Sungguh sangat mengagumkan dan sangat Istimewa, karena nilai2 tradisi Kraton Jawa beserta budayanya masih diutamakan dan dijunjung tinggi disini, sehingga pantas selalu diagungkan, dan menjadi patokan dan pusat Budaya Jawa dan Indonesia.

インドネシアの歴史に興味があれば是非訪れたい場所。
　日本語では王宮の模様。王宮は北側と南側に分かれていて、入場料も別々。入り口は数百メートル離れているか。マリオボロ通からベチャで行くと、南側の王宮に行ってくれと言ったのに、北側で下ろされた（日常的なインドネシア語会話は結構自信がありますが...）。マリオボロ通から近い方が北側の王宮で、遠くに行きたくないからのように思う。北側の王宮の入場券を売っている所でも「ここは南側の王宮ですか？」と確認したのが、そうだとの返事。北側の王宮は南側に比べて見るものが少ないので、入場料を取る為にそういう返事をしたのかと今でも思っている。北側も南側も、入場料の他、写真機持込み料等が少額で必要。
　北側は行かずに、南側だけでも良いように思う。南側は午前中に曜日毎に芸能が披露される。見る価値あり。現王の父君のハメンク・ブオノ9世が蘭支配時代、日本支配時代、独立闘争と激動の時代を過ごしてこられ、独立の際に貢献された事もあったか、関連する展示が多い。
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
I went to Kraton expecting a lot, especially after reading the reviews here. I ended up quite disappointed.
Getting the tickets took a while and once inside, I realized not a single thing is described in English. 
Most of the stuff seemed like a pretty random collection of "old stuff" without even a date or anything. 
However, if you take a guide, they so speak English and tell you some things you might find interesting if you are interested in history.
I didn't stay for too long, also because it was quite crowded.
I guess if you have lots of time in Yogya and you have seen taman sari, Borobudur, etc you can check it out but personally it didn't compare at all.
Plek met geschiedenis, wat best interessant is, maar ik vond het kraton als 'hoofdattractie' van Yogja erg tegenvallen. Niet heel mooi, nauwelijks uitleg bij dingen. Tentoongestelde dingen oubollig.

Very little information is available to you once your inside, leading to a lot of confusion over whether your actually within the site or missing something else. It's very underwhelming especially compare to other sites near Yogyakarta like Borobudur. 

Getting a guide is recommended to be able to build an understanding of the history of the site - which can be very interesting.

However, be careful not to fall in the tourist trap they set up. You pay an initial low amount for a tour (which is great!) But end up being swayed to jump in becak to a "local" government owned shop; where they "make all the batik and sell it at a much lower cost than maliboro". By the time you get there is a complete lie and the products their selling are not only no different but also just as expensive. 

I would recommend a visit, but download all the info onto your phone and stay away from the scam.
外せない観光場所だと思い、徒歩でふらふらと。他の方が言うように、入り口が分かりにくく、ここか？とおもったら違い、結局ペチャで。古いジョグジャカルタの雰囲気や、インドネシアの文化の幅広さを味わえて、やはり定番だけどいってよかったなと思います。

I wouldn't make a detour to visit the Kraton Palace, but if you are in Yogya anyway, I would definitely recommend passing by the Sultan's palace. You get a guide that explains you all about the Sultan's life and his function, which was very interesting (though sometimes on the edge of being propagandistic). It is a huge place and you get to understand better why the Indonesian Muslims are so open to other religions.
En allant visiter le kraton, on peut se rendre compte de la gouvernance historique mais en même temps visualiser quelques exemples de traditions.

Its a 'must see' in Yogyakarta but it could be, and clearly once was, so much more. You get a guide included with the entrance ticket, ours was 84 years old and has been working at the palace since 1936 he said! Anyay only the front part of the palace survives, the ceremonial areas. The original palace complex was vast with the living quarters behind the ceremonial area, but it seems none/little of that has survived. The artifacts in the small group of buildings clustered around the ceremonial areas are somewhat worn and tired. Its interesting to learn about how things were in days of yore. Frankly an hour or so and its done

There are some interesting features here but they are not very well displayed. I would definitely find a guide at the entrance. Even if ours was a bit boring we got far more out of it than if we'd been on our own. Apparently they close early and don't do performances during ramadan, as we found out after arrival. 

We also visited the museum Ullen Sentalu which was a bit out of town but in better shape.

As the Kraton is the Royal Palace of the Sultan of Yogyakarta, the only sitting Sultan in Indonesia, it is a popular -- even a “must see” -- tourist destination, but one can’t help but come away with a feeling of faded glory, if not neglect, at least of the publicly available areas within the large complex.  Some of the buildings are in obvious disrepair and the museum artifacts seem to be frozen in a time warp, with nothing noticeably updated from my last visit in the early 1990s.  The museum devotes several buildings to its sizable collection memorializing the life of the current Sultan’s father, an important figure in the Indonesian independence movement and post-independence government.  They include personal artifacts from his childhood, china and other gifts from foreign dignitaries, as well as faded photos of him during the newly independent Indonesia of the late 1940s, 1950s and 1960s through to his state funeral in the 1980s.  Historically significant perhaps, but nothing particularly riveting to a Western visitor. The exhibits are sparsely described and only in Bahasa Indonesian but English-speaking tour guides are available.

Though the connection of the Sultanate with Indonesia’s independence movement makes the Kraton an important destination for Indonesians (with groups of students on school trips during our visit as well as university students even sprawling on the floor for group shots among the artifacts), for a Western visitor, the most important reason to visit the Kraton may be for its free (once inside) rotating cultural performances each morning.  The wayang golek puppet show accompanied by a gamelon orchestra on the day of our visit was interesting, though the noise from the waves of tour groups entering the Kraton was distracting, as was the feeling of musical chairs in the audience, with few people remaining seated long enough to watch more than a few minutes of the performance.  The show was enjoyable but could have been more captivating, given the small size of the puppets, if the audience had been able to sit closer to the puppeteer instead of about 20 feet away on the perimeter of the performance pavilion.

All in all, worth a visit to quickly see the layout of an Indonesian royal palace and then take in the cultural performance.  Choose the day of your visit to coincide with the cultural art you most want to see.

Il Kraton come Palazzo nn vale la visita ma se vi informate su quando ci sono le prove del Balletto Reale con l'orchestra Gamelan tutto cambia. Le prove sono bellissime: ballerini vestiti in abiti cerimoniali provano il Ramayana, balletto che narra le gesta degli Dei Induisti, che poi verrà eseguito nelle 3 notti di luna piena ai templi di Prambanan. Il tutto accompagnato dall'orch. Reale di Gamelan, percussioni metallofoneche emettono suoni dolcissimi e di grande potenza. Il tutto avviene nei padiglioni aperti del Kraton con tanto pubblico attorno ed è uno spettacolo che raccomando a tutti. Anche se nn vi piace il balletto, la bellezza dei costumi, la musica così diversa da quella occidentale e qualche notizia sugli Dei Induisti vi ammalieranno. Ci torno tutte le volte che sono nei dintorni.
The whole afternoon may not be enough to see everything here in detial. Lots of places with shade to escape the heat of Yogya.

If you come to Yogyakarta, this place is one of the place that must be visited. Because you can learn some part of Yogyakarta's history in the museum inside this palace. Maybe it is not so outstanding, but it is quite worth if you spare your little time to visit this place if you visit Yogyakarta.

Actually it was a very nice traditional place to be visited, but too bad it didn't maintain perfectly. It looks very old, dirty, and has bad smell. For the paintings and sculpture also unorganized well.

Un immense enchevêtrement de palais (chaque sultan construit son carré), ils en sont au 10ème sultan je crois. C'est typique avec ses gardes et leurs couteaux glissés dans leur ceinture mais ne vous attendez pas à visiter Versailles, sa vaisselle, ses meubles, c'est assez pauvre en décoration. Une belle balade pour se plonger dans l'univers d'un sultan toujours régnant (sur les affaires religieuses de son île Java) et ce pendant une heure trente.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Il palazzo del Sultano non è davvero un granchè. Evitate di andarci se avete di meglio . Decisamente deludente

Attention, il existe 2 partie du palais, avec 2 entrées bien différentes (et 2 billets à payer).

La première partie vers la place est sans aucun intérèt, n'y perdez pas votre temps. La 2ème partie plus au sud est légèrement mieux mais sans plus. Globalement les bâtiments sont mal entretenus, les collections exposées sans intérèt.

Perjalanan kami berempat ke Kerato Yogyakarta di mulai dari Hotel dengan naik Trans Jogja 1A. Dikarenakan rencana hari ini adalah keliling kota Jogja dengan kendaraan umum, maka kami putuskan untuk tidak meyewa mobil. Tarif yang kami harus bayar adalah @Rp3000/orang, kami mendapatkan tempat duduk yang nyaman di dekat turis Jepang yang baru landing nampaknya, terlihat dari luggage yang masih banyak.
Sesampainya di Jl Malioboro, tepatnya di depan pasar Beringharjo, kami turun dari sini kami melanjutkan dengan naik becak (kalau mau jalan kaki sebenarnya tidak jauh, tapi dalam keadaan puasa naik becak adalah pilihan terbaik) walau sedikit memutar. Kami di ajak untuk melihat lihat pertokoan dan pusat oleh oleh yang kebetulan memang harus dilewati. Si bapak pengemudi becak tidak segan dan tidak memungut tarif tambahan untuk menunggu kami jika ingin berbelanja dahulu.
Setelah membayar si pengemudi becak @Rp10,000 kami memasuki area keraton, dan kami di kenakan biaya @Rp7,000. Sedangkan untuk turis asing akan dikenakan biaya @12,500 plus untuk guide abdi keraton yang akan memandu dengan Bahasa sesuai Negara asal masing masing turis @10-20,000 (negotiable) .
Perlu di informasikan, bahwa kita tidak boleh mengambil gambar (memotret) selama tour di dalam keraton. Padahal saya sangat ingin sekali memotret benda benda keraton yang sudah berusia ratusan tahun.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Interessante l'approfondimento della cultura locale grazie all'accompagnamento di una delle economicissime guide disponibili. Il palazzo in se non è sufficientemente valorizzato né particolarmente spettacolare
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Pusat pelestarian budaya Jawa dengan peninggalan-peninggalan para Sultan yang masih terjaga.Dengan berbagai pusaka dan bangunan khas Jawa yang masih megah di Kompleks Keraton memang sangat menarik untuk di kunjungi. Tetapi semestinya bangunan-bangunan yang masih terjaga kelestariannya harus mendapat perhatian lebih khususnya cat tembok atau atap yang sudah kusam hendaknya dicat ulang sehingga terlihat lebih megah.

Review Text: Op zich stelt het niet zo veel voor. Wat gebouwen wat oude echte Javaanse mensen in klederdracht die kletsen en muziek maken. Onze gids was een vriendelijke mevrouw die gezellig het een en ander ( weinig interessants) vertelde.

Pada liburan lebaran lalu saat kami menginap di Yogyakarta dan Solo, banyak sekali tempat yang kami kunjungi, diantaranya Kraton Yogyakarta.
Sengaja kami pilih tempat ini karena selain bernilai sejarah tinggi, juga terletak di jantung kota Yogyakarta serta dekat dengan tempat kami menginap yaitu di Abadi Hotel Yogyakarta.
Ini adalah kali pertama anak-anak kami mengunjungi Kraton Yogyakarta, mereka sangat senang dan banyak bertanya-tanya, tempat ini saat kami kunjungi sangat padat pengunjung karena memang saat libur panjang dan amat dekat dengan lokasi wisata belanja Malioboro, dimana orang yang berkunjung ke Yogyakarta sebagian besar pasti mengunjungi Malioboro.
Kraton ini cukup terawat dengan baik, banyak benda bersejarah disimpan disini, foto-foto Sultan yang pernah memimpin pun dipajang juga.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Kami datang di saat liburan Lebaran, salah satu waktu tersibuk di Yogya. Tempat ini sebenarnya sangat bagus dan menarik untuk orang tua dan anak anak. Namun tour guide yang sedikit tidak teratur menyambut kita, dan tidak memiliki passion yang baik terhadap obyek wisata ini merupakan hal terburuk yang kita alami. Tempat ini juga termasuk kurang terawat. Barang barang bersejaran berusia ratusan tahun dibiarkan terbuka dan muda disentuh para turis. Sangat disayangkan. Namun bagi yang ingin mengetahui sedikit sejarah Keraton Yogya, dan mengalami seperti apa hidup sebagai abdi dalem, tempat ini sangat cocok. Saya hanya berharap para guide tidak terlalu aggressive menawarkan lukisan yang mereka buat, karena membuat ktia sedikit kurang nyaman.
I think visiting the Kraton is just something you need to do when you visit Yogyakarta. Not because it is something that unbelievable, but simply because it is such an important part of the district.

Palazzo senza infamia e senza lode
Poco valorizzato.

Il museo un po da svecchiare. magari mettendo qualche targhetta in inglese si può capire meglio quello che si osserva.

La guida ufficiale  all ingresso è offerta libera ma si è rivelata molto preparata e gentile . Suggerita per avere info e pettegolezzi sul sultano  che la guida (libro) non da
Matig bijzondere verzameling gebouwen met overblijfselen van sultans eigendommen. Geen informatie bij de beelden of gebouwen. Maar ja, if you pay peanuts, you get monkey.
Antiques in some of the pavilions were interesting but it's really just a "tick-it-off-the-list" kind of place. There were soooo many people. Don't go on a weekend.

Lokasi keraton sangat luas dan memiliki peninggalan kuno dari raja - raja kesultanan yogya . Daftar riwayat dan foto2 dpt dinikmati dan masih banyak benda2 kuno seperti guci, jam kuno dll. Hanya patut disayangkan di ruang 2 tempat foto raja 2 kurang terawat kebersihannya. Sarang laba2 masih menempel di bingkai foto dan ruangan terasa seperti ruanganya yang sudah lama tidak dibersihkan walaupun lantainya tidak kotor. Kebetulan anak saya alergi dengan debu sehingga begitu masuk ke ruangan di keraton langsung bersin 2. Abdi dalemnya masih ada dan kebanyakan sudah tua. Salut dengan pengabdian mereka. Maunya harga tiket dinaikkan sedikit jadi untuk pemeliharaan keraton dapat lebih optimal

Review Text: The place is nothing incredible, it does help that you are given a guide to help you navigate the place and they will give you all their insight on the place which is good if nothing else its worth it cause it helps one gain a better understanding of the city how its run and other things
I visited the Keraton Yogyakarta (Yogyakarta Palace) when I was in junior high. At that time my school held a Study Tour to Yogyakarta and Keraton Yogyakarta is one of the places we visit.
タマンサリを見た後歩いて行きました。入り口がちょっとわかりにくいのでベチャで行った方が無難かもしれません。行った日はラマダン明けの休日と言うことで、音楽の演奏はありませんでした。帰りのベチャは登り坂だから25000ルピアだと言われるが、無視して20000ルピアにしてもらい乗りました。

very poorly explained. little to see. except maybe to pair of socks that belonged to the sultan :))
nothing translated in english, you can not understand a thing.

Il Kraton di Yogyakarta è una cittadella chiusa da mura dove la parte principale, o comunque più interessante è costituita dagli edifici facenti parte la residenza dal Sultano reggente. In realtà, per noi europei, è un po' difficile capirlo in un primo momento in quanto quelle che noi siamo abituati a vedere come singole stanze di un'edificio, qui sono tutti singoli edifici, e nella maggior parte dei casi senza pareti. Tuttavia, affidandosi ad una guida esperta, questa, ci fa capire la funzione ed il valore dei varii edifici. Possiamo trovare l'edificio (sala) delle udienze, quello per gli spettacoli musicali i delle marionette, oltre che a quelli dedicati alla raccolta di oggetti personali del Sultano e della Famiglia Reale. Per una visita veloce è sufficiente dedicare un'oretta o poco più, ma se si vuole si può impegnare molto più tempo dato che durante il giorno si tengono vari spettacoli di musica e/o danze. La nostra impressione è che il posto meriti una visita per poter entrare nella mentalità Indonesiana, ma il nostro consiglio è di farla con una guida altrimenti può essere un'esperienza deludente.

It's a grand palace but  not as most of us would think of palaces - wide open spaces, open pavilions and a museum of great interest.  It's home to about 5,000 people who spend their days serving the Sultan in some form.  It's a place well worth a visit when you're in Yogyakarta.

Review Text:
The Kraton is the palace of the kings of the sultanate of Yogyakarta.  Because HB IX strongly supported the was of independence against the Dutch, Jogja is the only remaining monarchy in Indonesia, and the off-limits-to-the-public parts of the Kraton still serve as the residence of the hereditary governors of Jogja.  

The royal family is keen to maintain and support the traditional culture of Java.  Every day there is a different cultural show, at no additional charge beyond the incredibly modest admission fee to the Kraton.

On some days it's Javanese dance, or puppet shows, accompanied by gamelan music.  Yesterday being a Tuesday, it was a two-hour concert (10 to 12) by the royal gamelan orchestra.  Absolutely awesome.  Gamelan is a complex music, at times discordant to western ears, but incredibly rich layers of exotic interweaving melodies with soulful changes in tempo that can be hypnotic and ethereal.  In the West, Balinese gamelan is by far better known.  Judging by the pieces I heard yesterday, I would tentatively say Javanese gamelan may be more melodic.  The music is rich enough to have inspired classical composers such as B. Britton and C. McPhee to compose versions for full orchestra, and spiritual enough to have inspired its use by a number of New Age musicians.  Having said that, I have to admit that throughout the two hours, there was a constant shuffling of listeners in and out.  Indonesians as well as foreigners would wander in, listen for five or ten minutes, and then wander out.  So I guess if you aren't already a fan of classical Indonesian music, there's a fair chance you won't be enthusiastic about it.  The same is true for Javanese dance and puppet theater.  But if you like punk rock and sitcoms, not only the Kraton, but all of Jogja might not be your scene.

Do note all of the other museums within the Kraton.  The palace grounds are something of a labyrinth, and it's quite easy to miss many attractions by taking a wrong turn.  Of particular note is the remarkable textile museum, particularly of course the batiks.

Try to get there early so you not only see the day's cultural show, but have several more hours to look at everything else.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

進去後便有一個中庭，其中一個亭子有民族舞表演，但舞台四周圍滿人，插針不入。爪哇的傳統舞蹈有類泰國舞，但舞者有更多面部表情，粗眉仔個人覺得比泰國舞更有內涵。
表演場附近有另一個亭子，陳列昔日皇室用過的傢俬。亭子附近一個不起眼的角落處，有一塊當地人俗稱「中國碑」的物體，內容係有關兩國建交云云，一面是中華民國立的正體中文，另一面則是爪哇王國的爪哇文，俱往矣……
雖然是個「景點」，蘇丹皇宮仍有皇室人員居住，始終還劃了些禁地，不准遊客亂闖。
蘇丹皇宮佈局簡單，沒太多雕樑畫棟，千萬不要同紫禁城比。皇宮內有幾間小型博物館，但內裏文物不多，令粗眉仔有少許失望。

Review Text: 王宫就在日惹的市中心，很方便前往!门票不贵，大概在12人民币左右，主要捐给用于王宫的修善等。来这儿参观的游客很多，可见苏丹王室在人们心中的地位! 进宫时，男女都必须穿长裤，如果着短裤，景区会免费提供围裙和腰带，以示对王室的尊重! 我们4人同行，给我们配了一名免费的英语导游，带我们参观很多宫内值得一去的地方，导游其实就是王室里面的retainer ,讲解了很多苏丹王室与国民的故事!另我最值得敬佩的是，在如今印尼人们心中对苏丹王室的敬重一点也没有改变，而国王也是世世代代爱戴着他的人们!人们把对苏丹王室的虔诚，也当作他们的一种信仰!感同身受!

Review Text: For something that is promoted as "The Sultan's Palace" this was a bit of a let down. The Kraton takes up a large area of central Yogyakarta, with city walls, a couple of parks and a Water Palace. The real star should be the Sultans residence, but it comes across as a jumble of buildings with no explanation at all. The staff are nicely dressed in tradition costume but seem a bit unfriendly, maybe they have taken a vow of silence. It costs 12500rp and there are two entrances. It closes at 2pm and you only need an hour here. The Kraton seems to be a selection of unrelated pavilions in a large open space. One contains a large Gamelan orchestra, another has portraits of former sultans. Highlight is the Gold Pavilion with a beautifully carved red and gold ceiling.
We were touring around with a guide and this was part of the tour. Was nice and the guide we had in Kraton had many stories.

Be aware there are two entrances!! One facing the North Square allowing you an entrance without a guide and displaying only some old dusty dresses on models in two big “showcases” and some old buildings with fading pictures. The side entrance is where you apparently will be shown around by a guide and can witness a gamelan orchestra. In between is a museum where all the carriages are shown in a remarkably good condition.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

It is a shame to give such an historic attraction such a poor review, but Kraton is going to have to get a poor review. The place feels decrepit, a shambolic contemporary structure of bygone glories. If you have nothing better to do in Yogya, then you could come here to waste an hour or two, but I would recommend doing some shopping in nearby Malioboro Street instead. 

I didn't even know what I was supposed to be looking at here, as a lot of the exhibitions were in a state of decay, and there were lots of empty spaces, presumably because things have been take from the Kraton and moved elsewhere. Unless the authorities are planning to renovate this place any time soon, then I would suggest at least a partial demolition.

I didn't enjoy Tamansari that much either, but at least walking around there I knew a basic coherent story to the things I was looking at, plus Tamansari has many great photo opportunities. Unfortunately, Kraton does not have any photo opportunities worthy of the name.

This "attraction" is in extremely poor shape, with many of the buildings requiring help. The overall feeling is that someone has removed the pieces that they loved or were in good condition and left the unwanted pieces to form the basis of this attraction.

Yogyakarta is one of the most historic places in Indonesia and also unique since its the only functioning monarchy within a republic. The Sultan of Yogyakarta becomes the Governor without an election. 
His palace is the Kraton. If you have seen the palaces and castles of India and the West, this may not greatly appeal to you. However what is unique are the continuous live shows of gamelan or puppet show etc happen within the palace and is free for the public.
The entry fee is nominal and therefore its probably worth a visit if you have time available after you have visited the more famous and must-see places in Yogyakarta like Prambanan and Borobudur.

Review Text:
I understand that this place is supposed to be part of the sultan palace. However, nothing impress me at this site. The Kraton Palace is located at the southern end of Malioboro Road, and it is quite easy to be reached (20 minutes by foot from Sosrowijayan Road). If you take a becah is cost 10K rupiah. The entrance fee is RP 15,000 (tour guide is included) with additional RP 1000 for our camera. The palace is open to public from 8 am - 2 pm daily. The palace is closed to public one hour earlier on Friday.The Kraton Palace is a grand elegent Javanese architecture, lay in the centre of Jogja city. 

It was built in 1755 by Prince Mangkubumi was then called Sultan Hamengku Buwono I. The design of this historical building demonstrates that the palace, (the Tugu Monument) and Mount Merapi positioned in one line. It faces towards the volcanic Mount Merapi in one direction and towards the Indian Ocean.

If you look closely you  will notice there are Buddhist, Islamic and Hindi elements in the decoration in the central part of the palace. 

You will also find the sultan residence. If the lamps in front of the residence are turned on the Sultan is in. anyway you not allowed into his residence.

Many of the equipments and antiques which were used in olden days are still displayed in different buildings in the compund of kraton palace. 

it is not a huge palace but an old ancient palace. it just shows the simple way of life of the people of jogja.

We tried to visit the Kraton and got directions to the entrance from a local guy close to the complex.  At the gate we were told that the facility was closed for lunch and would open again at 2pm.  He suggested that we could check out a batik workshop in the meantime and gave us general directions.  We headed that way and soon another local asked us if we needed directions anywhere and then said he was heading in the same direction for lunch.  He led us to the shop which was indeed very nice and located in a really cool neighborhood where we wandered around for a few hours.  However, upon reading the Lonely Planet entry for the Kraton later that evening we realized that we got got.  It's a scheme to divert tourists from the Kraton and into batik shops.  We were directed to a fake entrance.  The real Kraton does not close for lunch and closes every day around 2pm.  At least we didn't buy any batik from the workshop.

Une fois de plus, nous sommes seuls… Le calme du lieu est impressionnant et favorise la méditation.
Imogiri is a very special place for me , the roots of my mother . The walk up is a great and healthy exercise. Been here for private ceremony without tourists or others.

My wife and I arrived just exactly when the cemetery opens on that day. It is open every Monday (10 AM), Friday (1 PM) and Sunday (10 AM). You can park your car or motorbike in the parking area and climb hundred of staircases before you can reach the cemetery complex. It is said around 400 staircases.

Basically, this complex is divided into three major areas. One is the tomb of Mataram Kings (before the kingdom was divided into two), one is the tomb of Yogyakarta Sultanates (Hamengku Buwono) and the other one is the tomb of Surakarta Sunanates (Paku Buwono).

For entering the graveyard, the visitor is required to wear traditional Javanese cloth. Local tourist is charged IDR 10,000 for this. And you shall walk barefoot.

And I urge you to bring small money in IDR (2,000 or 5,000). Because there are many posts where you shall spend that small money. (Of course, you can spend 10,000 or more at each post if you bring a lot of money in your pocket)

No taking pictures inside the graveyard.

And since it is considered a sacred place, the visitor shall behave during the visit.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: The tour was well guided, with an excellent historical perspective on this ancient area, which has survived multiple regimes.

The flight of steps to the entrance gate is good for exercises. Some locals sell the medicinal tea of Wedang Uwuh in the steps.It is beneficial for our health.

Review Text: We were in Yogyakarta around New Year's Eve, and all the other places we visited were very crowded. When we arrived to Imogiri on January 1, we found ourselves in a very quiet environment, which came as a relief after the crowds of the previous couple of days. To visit the tombs, you must accept to change into traditional Javanese attire (which is a lot of fun!). The visit itself is solemn: visitors are invited to remain silent, and the interior of the mausoleum of Sultan Agung is dark and very hot. There is definitely a spiritual side to this visit. A great moment.
Ini kunjungan saya yang kedua.kalinya. Bukit kecil inimenjadi tempat peristirahatan terakhir bagi raja raja Mataram sejak jaman Sultan.Agung.

Imogiri is indrukwekkend zelfs als je de begraafplaatsen zelf niet kan bezoeken. De begraafplaatsen zijn niet alle dagen te bezoeken en je moet Javaanse kledij dragen om binnen gesloten te mogen. Wij waren er op een dag de begraafplaatsen gesloten waren maar hebben toch een blijvende indruk van de deze grote site. Ieder graf is afzonderlijk toegankelijk via prachtige gebeeldhouwde deuren. Wij hebben de volledige toer gedaan rondom de site. Je kan de plaats bezoeken waar de huidige sultan zal worden begraven. Het geheel is indrukwekkend. Wij zullen zeker nog terugkomen om de begraafplaatsen te bezoeken.

Review Text: были удивлены когда наш гид завел нас на кладбище , конечно тут все помпезно и роскошно, только потом мы поняли что здесь захоранивали царей и всякую знать.
Misschien handig om van te voren na te gaan of het open is, anders sta je na 100 trappen voor een gesloten deur... En nog een tip, ga in de ochtend want het trappenlopen kost wat energie

First a few warnings:
STEPS - Unless entering through the top, there're about 500 steps between the car park and the entry so, come prepared.
DRESS CODE - Traditional Javanese. You can change into your own costumes there, or hire one. A staff will help you put it together (Tip 10,000 to 20,000RP)
FOOTWEAR - Not allowed inside the compound so, be prepared to tip toe if you come on a hot day. 
UMBRELLA - Not allowed inside so, for ladies, a scarf may be useful.
PERSONAL ACCESORIES - If considered 'loud' you may be asked to remove them.
TIPS - You'd be asked by almost everybody at every point so, prepare many small notes (I was told 2,000RP is reasonable)

The complex is about 370 years old, built by Sultan Agung of Mataram, and I was fortunate to be taken inside the room containing his tomb by a regular visitor.
 
Regulars will usually be let in first, to a hut housing Sultan Agung's tomb. They'd pray at the entrance to the inner chamber, and one by one, led inside the inner chamber for blessings. Entrance is almost by crawling through a very small door (small even for an Australian size 8). The chamber fits around 5 people. It is dark, smoky, and crowded, and you squeeze your way out after the blessing.

The complex contain many tombs from different sultans and their families, and they look pretty similar to one another. Some background reading may be useful if you're looking for any one of special significance. The more popular ones when I visited seemed to be the tombs of Sultan Agung, and the Hamengkubuwana (or Hamengkubuwono) lineage, ancestors of current Sultan of Yogyakarta.

If you're curious, interested in a bit of history (from your own reading, unless you have a guide) and nostalgia, the walk up is pleasant, the scenes quite beautiful, and the experience 'different'.

Not for those who're accustomed to comfort, or have an aversion to tropical heat, and the sun.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Op deze begraafplaats, bovenop een heuvel een stuk buiten Yogya, liggen sultans van het Mataram-rijk en van het latere sultanaat Yogyakarta begraven, vanaf de 17de eeuw tot de vorige sultan van Yogya. Wat de plek zo fascinerend maakt is alle ritueel, en de heilige sfeer van verering, waarmee de graven van deze vroegere leiders nog steeds zijn omgeven. 
Om naar binnen te mogen moet je je kleden in traditionele Javaanse kleding, die ter plekke voorhanden is. Voor de verschillende sultans worden doorlopend gebeden gelezen, bloemen worden op het graf gelegd. Vooral het graf van Sultan Agung, de stichter van de begraafplaats die nog steeds als een belangrijke leider wordt gezien, is enorm de moeite waard - beklim alle trappen en ga naar binnen in het kleine, lage, met kaarsen verlichte houten huis dat over het graf is gebouwd. Kniel bij een steen naast het graf zodat de sultan je voorspoed zal brengen. Fascinerende plek om te zien hoe men op Java met de graven van belangrijke historische figuren omgaat.
Ook een fijne plek om gewoon even de stad uit te zijn, en een wandeling te maken in de omringende bossen.
Waarschijnlijk is een bezoek het handigst te doen met een gids, omdat de begraafplaats een stuk buiten de stad is gelegen en op eigen gelegenheid moeilijk te vinden en bereiken is.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Imogiri is the graveyard of the royal hoses of Jogjakarta and Surakarta, better known as Solo. It has special significance for people who live in central Java. This auspicious location has been used for the Royal families of Jogjakarta and Solo for hundreds of years. Everyone with a royal connection wants to be buried there. Unless you know some of the history of Indonesia, it may not be all that interesting.

Review Text: When we headed to Imogiri Kings Cemtery on a Friday late morning, the rain poured like cats and dogs. We arrived at the hill bottom around eleven something, without any alternatives, we took our lunch at the nearby food stall as the ceremony would be held at 1 p.m. The cemetery is for the royal families of Yogyakarta, therefore we needed an employee of Sultan Palace to accompany us to attend the ceremony (IDR150,000 for his service). Nearly 12:30 p.m. we drove our car towards the hilltop, otherwise you should climb 450 steps. Before we entered the tomb, it was necessary for us to change the traditional Javanese hat and clothes that provided. Being worshippers, we brought along baskets with petals. At the appointed time, the door of smaller courtyard opened and all worshippers were allowed, lining in a queue, to enter the scared place. Inside the courtyard stood a small house with the tomb inside, all worshippers were waiting outside the corridor with a murmur of prayer. The tomb was for Sri Sultan Hamengkubuwono II, everybody entered the closet, then put petals on the top of his stone coffin, prayed wholeheartedly in order for blessing. Then we moved to the next room with his first wife stone coffin therein. All kings and their families were buried in the cemetery except the founder Panembahan Senopati of Mataram kingdom. The ceremony was only held on Sunday & Monday from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. as well as Friday from 1 to 3 p.m. It is extremely difficult to reach there without a car or a motorbike because the cemetery is at the outskirts of Yogyakarta. From the hilltop, you can really enjoy the beautiful scenery under your feet.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Located in the south part of Yogyakarta, this cemetery complex lies in one of the regency which is Imogiri. Public transport is a bit difficult to reach the area so usually rent a car or motorcycle will be the better option. Make sure to bring enough amount of water because you will need it. Need to climb many many stairs but worth it when you reach the top part of the cemetery complex. It says that along the way you better count the stairs as well and remember the exact number once you arrive. Based on the folklore, the number will be different from one person to another.

Our guide suggest us to visit this Graveyard, it is just a different place than other place we ever visited on our travel journey. The history behind made this graveyard looks so special.

Imogiri is a royal cemetery. It was established by the first sultan of Jogyakarta, Sultan Agung, in 1645. The site has mystical significance and access requires following certain rituals, such as wearing appropriate clothing. Imogiri is not close to Jogyakarta. A guide may be helpful, but sort out financial considerations in advance. An entrance fee is not charged, but a donation for the upkeep of the cemetery is suggested. Visitors without a knowledge of Indonesian culture may feel short changed.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Climbing to the cemetery of the sultans of Yogyakarta and Solo is a magical experience. The opening times are tricky, but if you manage to get there when you can actually go in, you will be taken through a real experience which includes changing your clothes and acting maximally respectfully.

Review Text:
Mengunjungi makam raja-raja Kerajaan Mataram di Imogiri ini selain mengenal budaya jawa klasik atau kuno, juga sekaligus dapat mempelajari sejarah kerajaan Mataram dan Yogyakarta. 
Untuk dapat memasuki kompleks makam raja-raja mataram ini, pengunjung harus melalui jalanan menanjak dengan ratusan tangga yang cukup melelahkan. Sebab kompleks makam yang sakral tersebut berada di atas bukit Imogiri. 
Setiap pengunjung yang hendak memasuki kompleks makam ini juga harus mengenakan pakaian adat jawa. Untungnya di lokasi makam raja-raja mataram sudah disediakan tempat penyewaan pakaian adat jawa tersebut. Tentu saja harus menyisihkan sejumlah uang untuk membayar sewa kostumnya.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
Kompleks Pajimatan Imogiri berada di sebuah puncak perbukitan yang tinggi. Misteri dimulai dari sini. Untuk mencapai Makam Raja-raja,  pengunjung atau peziarah harus mendaki lebih dari 340 anak tangga. Konon jika berhasil menghitung dengan tepat jumlah anak tangga yang didaki (karena setiap pengunjung akan menghasilkan jumlah yang berbeda ada 403, 407,dsb), keinginan atau kehidupan yang lebih baik akan terjadi dikemudian hari.
Makam hanya di buka untuk umum pada hari Senin, Jumat, dan Minggu.

Memang cukup melelahkan mendaki ratusan anak tangga yang menanjak dan meninggi. Ada trik tersendiri yang biasanya dilakukan oleh para abdi dalem. Menurut para abdi dalem, agar langkah mendaki terasa ringan, kita harus berjalan dengan pola zig-zag.
Untuk masuk ke makam Sultan Agung, maka selain harus mengenakan pakaian adat Jawa (peranakan) untuk yang wanita pakai kemben, dan pria pakai sorjan, semua sudah di sediakan (pinjam)disana. Juga kita harus melepas alas kaki, dan harus melalui tiga pintu gerbang. 
 Tidak ada biaya khusus yang harus kita bayarkan, tetapi hanya si iklas nya kita memberi untuk abdi dalem. Juga jika kita ingin membawa air yang ada di gentong, kita diwajibkan membayar ekstra juga seiklasnya.

Di sepanjang jalan menuju Makam Raja-raja Imogiri banyak terdapat warung yang menjual berbagai jajanan dan minuman khas Makam Imogiri, seperti Pecel Kembang Turi, Wedang Uwuh, Pecel Kembang Turi sangat khas karena sudah jarang dijumpai. Wedang Uwuh adalah minuman seduh yang  terdiri dari jahe, kayu manis, secang, dan rempah rempah lain. Minuman ini berkhasiat menghangatkan badan dan mencegah masuk angin. 

Dari terminal Giwangan ambil jurusan Yogyakarta-Panggang atau Yogyakarta Petoyan dengan harga Rp6000/orang (tetapi ada sebagian kondektur bis yang menawarkan kita untuk mengantar sampai pintu gerbang makam dengan tarif Rp20,000/orang). Setelah perjalanan 30 menit sampailah ke terminal Imogiri. Selanjutnya pengunjung cukup berjalan kaki sekitar 250 meter sampai anak tangga menuju makam. Atau kalau kita malas berjalan, bisa menggunakan ojek dengan tarif Rp15.000
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
Hutan pinus Imogiri – Jogjakarta masih satu lokasi dengan Kebun buah Mangunan dan Goa Gajah. Untuk rute menuju kesini bisa dibaca di Kebun Buah Mangunan. Saat menuju ke Hutan Pinus ini agak bingung sebetulnya karena dari jauh sudah banyak pohon pinus di kanan kiri jalan, tapi dimana parkirnya? akhirnya jalan terus. Ternyata di tengah jalan terlihat lahan parkir yang cukup luas, rupanya disinilah pusat segala kegiatan dan kegembiraan.

Lokasi di kiri jalan merupakan tempat parkir dan area camping sedangkan lokasi di seberang jalan adalah tempat segala kegiatan. Didalam hutan pinus yang buesar ini memang sudah disiapkan untuk lokasi wisata alam keluarga. ada bangku panjang cukup banyak untuk bersantai sekaligus foto-fotoan, ada juga bekas potongan pohon yang bisa dibuat untuk tempat naik berfoto, juga ayunan dan gardu pandang berupa pondok diatas pohon. Sayang untuk pondok dan ayunan saya hanya melihat 1 buah saja sehingga bila mau foto-fotoan harus bergantian.

Saya ke Hutan Pinus ini sore hari, matahari sore yang jatuh membuat bias sinar diantara ratusan pohon pinus menjadi sangat indah. Suasana alam yang sejuk ditambah banyaknya pohon sehingga tempat ini sangat nyaman untuk bersantai.

Cukup bayar parkir 10rb untuk mobil dan 3 rb untuk motor sudah bisa masuk ke hutan pinus. tapi kalo mau prewedding harus bayar 50rb/ sekali masuk.

Saat itu saya lihat ada sekitar 2-3 orang yang sedang melakukan prewedding dilokasi ini.

makam ini terdiri dari ratusan tangga, cocok untuk sekalian latihan fisik. menuju puncak tinggi yang terdapat makan-makam raja. disini juga terdapat hari-hari tertentu dilakukan upacara, sehingga apabila datang kesini, datanglah pada saat hari upcara dan anda bisa ikut serta, dengan menggunakan kain jarik dan kemben yang dililitkan di badan, anda bisa sekaligus mempelajari kebudayaan masyarakat imogiri.
jangan lupa juga coba wedang uwuhnya, banyak tersedia di warung-warung dekat parkiran menuju makam, cocok untuk menghangatkan tubuh.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah
