The ride from Jogjakarta to the Imogiri Kings Cemetery is a pleasant & scenic one, filled with green lush paddy fields along the way. The current map location on TA is inaccurate! Search for Makam Raja-Raja Surakarta & Yogyakarta on Google Maps or Waze! (TA map staff please take note; I'd reported earlier via TA mobile app)

There are prayer ceremonies on
Monday 10 am - 1 pm
Friday 1.30 pm - 4 pm
Sun 10 am - 1 pm (not sure on this one; stated by one of the online attraction rep)

As providence would have it, I went on a monday and managed to witness the prayer ceremony at the oldest tomb i.e. the first sultan (there are a few of em located at different sections of the complex). You have to dressed up like a local in a traditional shirt, sarong and head gear. For a small fee around IDR 14,000 all-in-all, you get to play dress-up and visit the tombs. It was around 10.40 am when I managed to climb right to the highest tomb where the prayers had started with a bunch of elderly local men. It didn't take long before they'd finished. You get to enter a small wooden enclosure where the tomb is. Before entering, a freewill monetary gift is expected. Inside, visitors can pray to the sultan if they want. It was totally dark saved for a small kerosene lamp. Quite an experience to witness the ceremony!

Later on the way back to Jogjakarta, I'd stopped at one of the many warung sate klatak (delicious grilled goat meat on wooden skewers) along the Imogiri Timur road. One of the best sate I'd taken ... well recommended. I was told most of the warungs serve good sate klatak, so you don't really need to search for the so-called 'best one'.

A worthy visit with pleasant scenery, traditional cultural experience, topped with a local delicacy!
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

une expérience à ne pas rater dans un site agréable.N 'oubliez pas l'appareil photo:le costume obligatoire vaut le déplacement

Die Sultansgräber bei Imogiri sollten auf einer Reise durch Java nicht fehlen. Allein die Fahrt von Yogya dortin, über die Dörfer ist schon ein Erlebnis. Wunderbare Landschaften und tolle Motive belohnen einen.
Bei der Anlage kann/muss man zunächst etwa 400 Stufen hinaufsteigen. Es gibt aber auch eine Straße hinauf, die die Guides kennen sollten. 
Die Anlage selbst ist sehr friedlich und kaum besucht. Allerdings sollte man beachten, dass sie nur an drei Tagen in der Woche geöffnet ist. Also vorher informieren, sonst kann man nur außen herumlaufen. 
Siehe auch: http://joinourjourneys.blogspot.com

My misgivings about the value of this visit were quickly confirmed on arrival. The month of Ramadan is probably the worst time (daytime at least) to come here so be warned! I was the only tourist visiting the site and it was a very disappointing experience. The self-appointed guide did not let my poor command of Indonesian get in the way of his spiel, for which I would eventually give a tip, of course. Almost no signage or tourist information makes it essential that you do your research beforehand and come prepared. The visit comprises mainly a steep climb to the top and back.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Kalau kita masih ingat pelajaran sejarah tentang kerajaan Mataram yang melawan VOC belanda pasti kita ingat Sultan Agung tapi tahukah dimana sultan Agung dimakamkan?? Imogiri terletak di kab.bantul DI yogyakarta, merupakan komplek pemakaman raja-raja Yogyakarta dan kasunanan Surakarta, termasuk di dalam komplek ini dimakamkannya Sultan Agung raja terbesar kerajaan Mataram. menuju ke lokasi ini cukup mudah ditempuh dengan akses dan infarstruktur jalan yang baik, sebelum masuk ke area makam kita akan disambut oleh ratusan anak tangga, akan cukup melelahkan tetapi bisa tereliminisir dengan sejuknya udara dan view sekitar yang asri dengan pohon2 besar.. ada beberapa ketentuan jika ingin ziarah di makam ini, di antaranya setiap peziarah harus memakai pakaian adat jawa, tidak memakai alas kaki, dan tidak memotret di dalam komplek makam. Terasa sekali suasana mistis di sekitar komplek ini, terlebih ketika memasuki area makam.. ketika masuk jaga etika berziarah, jaga aqidah (keyakinan) dan let's begin our adventure..
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: I came here with a friend from Yogya. A woman dressed us in traditional Javanese sarongs and we walked barefoot up the steps to the sultan's tomb. There are small wooden houses, very dark, lots of incense burning; you kneel down in front of the tomb and cover with flower petals. The experience is very sacred, solemn and intense. I felt fortunate to participate in this ritual that is so meaningful to people from Yogya.

this place is a cemetery for Kings of Yogyakarta and its Family, thousand of step ladder which no one can counting exactly the same amount of step he or she stepping on. Entering this places we should use traditional and unique shirt. Obey all the rules and regulation if you do not want to feel something goes wrong by itself

We visited the cemetery and walked the 454 steps to the sultan's grave. There are hardly any tourists and for a small fee you can borrow appropriate clothes to visit the grave. It was great experience, however please be aware that you should be in good shape (and drink enough) to walk those steps at very high temperature.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
Sebuah tempat wisata ziarah, dimana di lokasi ini terdapat komplek makam raja-raja kraton Yogyakarta mulai dari Sultan Agung yang meninggal tahun 1640an
Sampai sekarang, semua keluarga krato Ngayogyokarto Hadiningrat dimakamkan di sini.
Sultan terakhir yang dimakamkan di sini adalah Sultan Hamengku Buwono IX pada tahun 1988

masyarakat yang ingin berziarah harus mematuhi tata tertib di makam ini, antara lain memakai pakaian adat jawa dan beberapa larangan tentang sopan santun.

Suasananya memang sakral dan mistik di tempat ini. Bagi yang mencari kedamaian atau ingin menyepi dari hingar bingar dunia, tempat ini cocok untuk berkontemplasi.

Yeah, that's what's felt whenever we reach this place. Makam Imogiri (Imogiri Graveyard) is popularly known as one of spiritual/religious trip's destinations in Central java. It has such spiritual nuance other places may not have. With its mysterious stairs and sacred graves, many tourists keep visiting this place all the time.

Saya mengunjungi Imogiri bersama dengan keluarga. Sudah sangat lama kami merencanakan datang ke Imogiri tapi baru bisa telaksana pada bulan November 2014. Kami datang pada saat masih pagi sehingga belum banyak wisatawan. Bisa puas berkeliling. Ada Tour Leader lokal yang menawarkan jasa dengan tidak mematok tarif, cukup memberikan uang serelanya saja. Di sini saya bisa belajar banyak tentang sejarah masa lalu yang membentuk Yogyakarta sekarang ini: bisa banyak tahu riewayat para Sultan Mataram Islam (baik Kasultanan Ngayogyakarta maupun Kasunanan Surakarta) yang dimakamkan di tempat ini.

Terkenal dengan makam raja. Untuk mencapai makam tersebut harus melalui tangga yang tinggi, bisa sekalian untuk olahraga di pagi hari. 
Sehabis makan bisa membeli sarapan brongkos bubur dengan wedang uwuh. Segar sekali.

Datang ke daerah Imogiri pada hari Minggu untk jalan sehat atau sekedar trekking, disekitar makam raja Mataram. Setelah itu bisa dilanjutkan dengan sarapan makanan2 khas Jogja dan juga jajanan pasar. Murah.

Saya berkunjung ke imogiri siang habis dari parangtritis sehingga cukup panas. Tidak banyak area yang teduh. Pemandangan menuju imogiri cukup cantik. Guide menjelaskan dengan baik mengenai makam makam yang ada. Tidak semua tempat dapat dilihat, ada yang memerlukan persyaratan khusus. Agak tidak bisa leluasa tapi bisa dimengerti karena tempat ini dianggap sakral. Bila menyukai sejarah maka tempat ini layak dikunjungii.

My friend told me this satay is legendary around Jogja. Considering the remote location, I was surprised when I saw a bunch of foreigners enjoying "sate klathak" with us in the restaurant. The satay itself is quite delicious. If you like goat meat, you will definitely love this satay. It smells like goat. I myself found goat meat a bit... stinks, so it was not that great of an experience for me :)

I went there during the night, so I cannot say much about Imogiri region. It looked peaceful though and seemed nice if you're looking for a relaxing experience
Ive been to this awesome place just twice - Very traditional Java - Pay homage to the kings of Java - Dress up in full Java gear - Hired at reasonable cost - Not for your average tourist
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Imogiri merupakan makam raja raja mataram bila berkunjung kesini sebaiknya di pagi hari selain karena bisa melihat sunrise bisa juga sekalian berolahraga pagi dengan menaiki anak tangga yang jumlahnya ratusan itu. apalagi udaranya masih segar. bila sudah sampai puncak kita bisa berfoto-foto diluar bangunan yang arsitekturnya unik dan sangat tradisional. banyak spot2 foto yang bisa diambil disini. untuk masuk ke dalam ada hari2 tertentu yang diperbolehkan dan diharuskan menggunakan kemben untuk wanita dan sarung untuk pria namun jangan khawatir disini terdapat penyewaanny dengan terlebih dahulu menyumbang dengan minimal yang ditetapkan. jangan ragu untuk berkunjung kesini selain menyehatkan mata dengan pemandangannya yang indah juga menyehatkan raga. bila anda sudah puas diatas dan turun jangan lupa nikmati segarnya wedang uwuh yang merupakan minuman khas imogiri. selain itu juga mereka menjual wedang uwuh sachetan yang bisa untuk oleh2. selamat mengunjungi
If you would like to see the view from the mountain or to visit the tombs of the Kings of Mataram era, this is the place to be.
tanjakan imogiri sangat cocok untuk pecinta bersepeda setelah lelah bersepeda kita bisa istirahat di warung penduduk lokal sambil menikmati wedang uwuh
Makam raja-raja Jawa dengan sejaran panjang dan unik antara kraton Jogja dan kraton Solo dalam satu lingkaran (kawasan) yang terpelihara dengan baik bersama di makam raja Jawa Imogiri...
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
This listing is poorly named,  though I'm not sure how to get TripAdvisor to change it. Imogiri is the name of the whole district while the reviews here refer to the Makam Raja (Graveyard of the Kings) which happens to be in Imogiri. 

A beautiful quiet little tourist spot unless you visit on a public holiday or weekend when it can be over run with busloads of local tourists.

It's a great spot to visit early in the morning to climb the hundreds of majestic stairs and sip tea with the old Javanese guards before the heat of the day strikes. shopping for naturally died indigo batik at the bottom of the stairs is one of the most enjoyable ways and places to buy batik in Yogya and munching on pecel for lunch sitting on a mat on the grass beside the Creek is also pleasant. 

I often make a trip to imogiri part of a larger trip through the area, perhaps visiting the old unique Surakarta pendopo housed on a small distinct plot of land uniquely owned by the king of solo but in the kingdom of Yogya.

Sometimes I continue on up the steep hill past Bumi Langit permaculture farm up to d'lingo and make a day of it in Gunung Kidul,  Temple ot joglo hunting, or else do the day ride along the Gunung Kidul ridge through the UGM Casuarina and Bluegum forests,  dropping back down into Yogya after watching the sunset for dinner at Bukit Indah on Jul Wonosari.  

Or sometimes I head off exploring the windey roads and isolated beaches up in the mountains then head back down the way I came, passing back towards town and stopping at Pak Bari's foe Sate Klatak at Pasar Wonosobo. O4 else wind my way down to Parang Tritus beach to explore the only hot water spring in the area and have dinner at The Queen Of the South hotel or barbecued fish at the fish markets and rolick in the sand dunes with friends. 

I don't know why but for me, motor bike adventures to sleepy countryside attractions like Makam Raja is quintessentially Yogya. its what will last in my dreams if ever I stopped coming back.

Untuk mencapai makam, anda harus menyiapkan stamina dengan luu yang kuat karena harus mendaki ratusan anak tangga dari yang landai sampai terjal. 
Perjalanan sampai ke puncak anda akan disambut dengan pepohonan hijau, keramahan penduduk Imogiri, kicauan burung, dan semilir angin yang menyejukan. 
Tak terasa anda sudah tiba di puncak. 

Disana ada pemandu wisata yang akan menerangkan secara detail sejarah makam imogiri. Jika tertarik lebih detail, anda juga dapat membeli buku sejarah makam imogiri di sana.

Biaya tiket masuk gratis. Namun disana disediakan kotak untuk sumbangan sukarela pemeliharaan makam imogiri.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
terletak antara jalur alternative Yogyakarta - Wonosari lewat Bantul...bisa dicapai dg mobil walau akses jalan terjal mendaki perbukitan. sangat bagus untuk berfotoria dan melepas penat perjalanan... 
disarankan mampir saat terang, kalau malam sangat gelap dan tdk ada penerangan...
.. you are full prepared to dress as a java man or woman, and go inside at very limited moments. Nothing to see from outside the graveyard and no picture taking allowed.

This place made a big impression on me. The climb up the steps, through the trees and graves. We went early in the day, to avoid the heat.

Be aware that the compound with the graves is closed for the whole of the Ramadhan fasting month.

Jika datang ke makam Imogiri jangan lupa
1.  Minum wedhang uwuh (herbal)
2.  Main game..menghitung jumlah anak tangga
     Selalunya akan beda hasil jumlah nya dengan hitungan orang lain.
     Seru !!
3.  Malam jumat kliwon dan malam selasa kliwon selalu ramai yang ziarah ke makam ini.

I must say the makam is eye opening, especially when you see that the islamic dynasty has some european style on their casket. But you gotta brush up your bahasa indonesian if you would like to understand the guide. Only 15000IDR to wear the required clothes to go in.

Anda bisa mengenal sejarah jogja dengan mengunjuni makan raja-raja mataram islam hingga para susuhunan surakarta dan sultan yogyakarta. Siapkan fisik anda untuk menaiki ratusan anak tangga. tidak terlu terjal dan masih sangat terjangkau.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: I like to try lots of traditional foods from Yogyakarta , so i want to try this sate  and once more you crazy about this sate , different from others , the meet very soft and you want more and more, high recommended for this food !

for you that need some historic vacation in this places maybe be able to visited fo that,this is real cemetry,specially for keraton yogyakarta king cemetry ,position at south yogyakarta 25 minutes from central bus terminal.

Visit the cemetery from the family of the kingdom Yogyakarta, and after in the afternoor you can try Sate Klathak ( young goat with great taste and cheap ! ) Rent motorbike and you can enjoy Yogyakarta with great traditional foods !!!

When you visit this place, better in the morning, the air still fresh , and you can take breakfast there, there is traditional food you can eat there , just like gado gado but the use rice, you can also ask to not use rice.

Review Text: Letaknya di perbukitan, untuk memasuki komplek makam harus menaiki anak tangga yang lumayan banyak. Setiap pengunjung yang menghitung jumlah anak tangga dari bawah ke atas biasanya akan berbeda jumlahnya dengan dari atas ke bawah. Begitu pula dengan hitungan antar pengunjung makam. Pintu makam raja-raja juga tidak dapat dibuka setiap harinya, hanya pada waktu-waktu tertentu saja..

Review Text: Very nice surprise! Almost an honor to be able to greet the founder of the Mataram kingdom so closely. A place filled with serenity and mysticism.

This is quite a large complex, with a lot to see. It was warm when we went in the late afternoon. It was not really busy, and no tourists. It was quiet as well, something I really liked and very suitable for this place. There are enough photo opportunities with statues, huge stairs but also green sceneries. 
To see the graves of the kings and queens, traditional clothes are mandatory. You can hire those and you need to change clothes first. As for the woman the shoulders are naked, my wife did not want to do that on a hot sunny day. So we did not see the last resting places. But that will happen another time, I am sure.
You will feel the calmness when you entering the location. Many places to visit around the cemetery like the historical mosque nearby and ancient pool for the prince and princess.

Pemakaman raja-raja ini berada di komplek yang sama dengan masjid Kotagede. Komplek ini sangat terasa seperti tempat dengan toleransi agama yang sangat baik. Saat sebuah masjid yang merupakan tempat beribadah umat Islam, tetapi lingkungan masjid sendiri masih terasa arsitektur hindu di beberapa bangunan dan beberapa gerbang yang menyerupai Pura. Sedangkan saat memasuki area makam raja-raja, para pengunjung diharuskan memakai pakaian adat jawa. Sungguh sebuah tempat yang sangat mengagumkan.
Untuk mencapai tempat ii cukup mudah. Kalau memakai kendaraan sendiri, bisa mencari lokasi dengan maps, bisa juga menggunakan aplikasi ojek online. Kalau menggunakan bis umum turunnya agak jauh, tapi jalan kaki dari halte juga tidak terlalu capek
Tempatnya sejuk dan dekat dengan banyak sekali tempat kerajinan silver. Bagi yang menyukai atau ingin mencoba kuliner tradisional, bisa jalan sedikit ke pasar Kotagede yang sangat dekat dengan lokasi komplek makam. Banyak jajanan pasar yang enak dan wajib untuk dicicipi
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Tempat yang unik dan keren, pelayanan sangat ramah, disambut dengan baik dijamu dengan baik. yang menambah keunikan harus menggunakan kemben atau sorjan. arsitekturnya juga keren dan menakjubkan. kita juga bisa melihat ikan lele yang sangat besar dan tidak hanya berwarna hitam.
Faktor Penarik: Ketertarikan Budaya, Ketertarikan Fasilitas, Ketertarikan Suasana
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
Tempat wisata Religi ini merupakan kompleks pemakaman Pangeran dari Raja-raja Mataram, letaknya sekitar 300 meter dari Pasar Legi Kota Gede.

Tempat parkirnya merupakan halaman kampung yang luas, dan di pelataran parkir ini terdapat bangunan seukuran 3x6 m, yang didalamnya terdapat peninggalan sejarah Mataram Watu Gateng (Batu Gateng). 

Sangat cocok  dikunjungi bersama keluarga.

We walked from malioboro to tanansari with the help of google Maps. I wouldn't recommend this to anyone. The only reason we did it is because we love to explore, and we had an offroad baby stroller. To our luck the weather was cloudy and it was not too hot. 
Most visitors only come to take pictures, but tamansari has lots of great information about history. If you spend enough time, you will be able to explore pathways the guides don't show you, even climb up one of the buildings.

Taman Sari contains very interesting historical art. The story behind Taman Sari is very interesting and makes this place very memorable when visited. If you want to come and take pictures, you can do it yourself. But if you want to know this place well, it is highly recommended to use the services of a guide there.

Attractions in the city centre, many visitors. It is reasonable for foreign visitors to pay Rp 25,000 more than local visitors. After entering the Royal Palace, someone will ask if you need a guide, a guide fee is free, you only need to pay a small fee. I feel lucky to meet Salsa when our guide, she is good in English, speaking professionally and interesting, people are also sweet. Without her leadership, I would have missed many places, such as the palace kitchen, the bedroom, the place where the former Sultan and his wife prayed, the underground tunnel and the Sultan’s liturgical room. As other reviews say, guides will take you to places where souvenirs have been sold, let's go in and see, but Salsa didn't force us to spend. And the souvenir shop inside the palace, was run by the employees of the palace who used to serve the Sultan, some souvenir shops are actually quite characteristic and worth supporting. Salsa took us around for almost 2 hours, with no impatience at all, and pushed the sunny restaurants, ice cream shops and tea shops.
This palace is worth it! Also, a good guide is important!
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
Really disappointing. A poor dirty basin surrounded by crumbling walls. Go your way. 
On the other hand, around the temple, you will find some very interesting street art....you have to search a little, it is not listed in the guides...

The Taman Sari water palace of the Sultans of Yogyakarta was originally a walled bathhouse, surrounded by gardens with artificial lakes with islets. This complex was part of the huge park around the Kraton, the residential palace of the sultans. Today, only the bathhouse remains of this large bathing and entertainment complex. The rest of the palace garden has now been swallowed up by the Kampung Tamas district surrounding the bathhouse. The bathhouse that is still to be visited was built in the period 1758-1769 i.v. Sultan Hamengkubuwoni II of Yogyakarta 1750-1828). His successors and families will also have taken advantage of this bathing opportunity. The bathhouse is surrounded by high walls and contains separate large open-air baths for the Sultan, his wives and children. In one of the baths a two-storey building, from which the Sultan could watch his wives. If he was in the right mood, he summoned one or more women to his resting quarters in this little building .. for a meaningful conversation shall we say. The bathhouse complex has beautiful details and decorations and is definitely worth a look. Unlike some commentators on TA, I don't think the bathhouse of more than 250 years old looks dilapidated at all. Worth a visit, I think.
Faktor Penarik: Ketertarikan Budaya, Ketertarikan Fasilitas, Ketertarikan Suasana
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: The Water castle is another beautiful piee of Indonesia history. Many little nooks & cranny to search out. the view from the top of the tower allows for a great picture of the baths. We didn't have a guide but I do suggest that you do this to get all the history of the place
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Nice to walk around but not the most to see there. You'll need to use the local tour guides in the palace to get any information as there were no notice boards that we found.

My Uncle & I visited Jogja for the first time in September 2024 and we decided to visit a few tourist attractions in the city including the Kraton(Palace) and this Water Castle(Taman Sari). We had gone to the Kraton first, we almost got scammed by a local over there! Then we came over here, feeling a bit annoyed and apprehensive. 

First of all, do not let the term "Water Castle" deceive you into imagining something like Sleeping Beauty's Castle in Disneyland or anything even close to it! This "Water Castle" used to be the Royal Palace gardens several centuries ago, it has a few pools of water that were the swimming pools of the Royal family back in the days. 

Today, nobody is allowed to enter the pools, visitors can walk around the pools to take photos, that's all. There is an exhibition of Indonesian herbs & spices in a small room to the side of the large pool. Visitors can also climb up a very narrow and steep wooden ladder to the top of the watchtower that you see in the photos of this place, but the views aren't impressive at all. This attraction is actually quite small, you can cover this place in 15 minutes if it is not crowded. The exit of this place takes you through the local village next to the premises of the Water Castle and there are some interesting photo opportunities as you walk along the village paths.

If you have plenty of time to spare in Jogja, this place is worth visiting.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Absolutely disappointing! Visit not recommended. Very decadent structure, overrated by those who propose the excursion. It was a waste of time, considering that moving around Indonesia by taxi is madness. A few kilometers become a nightmare, causing traffic, rough roads and incapable drivers.
The pools adorn this kind of palace on the water with some sculptures on the doors and at the entrance. It closes around 3:00.
It is not worth going there on purpose, full of people but rather small. You pay the entrance and in half an hour going slowly you see everything. The tickets at the exit are prettier

Enjoyed.  Get a guide once you go inside.  It helps quite a bit as there is minimal signage.  We approached two guides, first asked for 100k with English that was a bit tricky to understand.  We chatted with a second guide whose English was better who charged 50k for myself and my son for 1 hr tour.  The tour lasted maybe 45 minutes? But was worth it to make it more interesting.
Besides the Sultan's palace is the other point of interest of the city. Worth a short stop but nothing more. Interesting the history of the place but on the state of maintenance there would be work.

These are beautiful baths, in which you can enjoy the atmosphere of the royal hygiene routine. There isn't a great deal here, to be honest, so, if you aren't careful, you'll find yourself in the exit after only 10 minutes. So take your time. 

Watch out for the aggressive hawkers outside the site.

My wife and I visited the Taman Sari as part of a larger tour of the Kraton area. 

This partially ruined complex was built as a pool and pleasure garden by the first sultan in 1765. It unfortunately suffered some significant damage in the Java wars and an earthquake in 1865 but has had some restorative measures undertaken. 

It was 25000K for a foreign adult to enter. There was a different price structure for locals. It took only about 30-45 minutes to get through, most of the time we spent by the pools which had a photogenic quality. There were guides available and more than one tried to attach themselves to us without our consent which was a bit annoying. I think they would be helpful potentially to have but I would advise you to make sure the terms of the arrangement are agreed upon early to avoid conflict at the end of the tour. Couple of exhibits to view with English translations.

Towards the back of the complex is the original entrance which if analysed properly will get you into a back street where you can freely visit a network of escape tunnels that were installed by the original sultan to allow escape in the event of an attack. If you have a guide they should show you this. 

Despite its negative reviews my wife and I actually enjoyed this more than the kraton. I think it’s worth including as part of larger tour of this area. On its own it probably doesn’t hold enough weight to justify the trip.
Faktor Penarik: Ketertarikan Budaya, Ketertarikan Fasilitas, Ketertarikan Suasana
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: This was well worth visiting. Having read many half-hearted reviews of it I was hesitant but am glad I went. It only takes an hour or so to see it thoroughly but it's pretty and well-maintained. It's also worth paying one of the guides who'll (politely) approach you after you've purchased your entry ticket. It only costs a few dollars for about 30 minutes. I noticed that my guide showed me into many areas that didn't have signs and were therefore completely empty of visitors. He also took me into the laneways that surround the water castle where local houses have been built in parts of the old castle. I learned a lot about how the sultans and the people around them lived, and also the uses for many of the buildings and pools. Beyond the pools, there are the old sections of the castle that used to be a library, kitchens, rest areas, the WC...
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: A fantastically beautiful complex, the entrance fee includes (if you want) a private guide who takes visitors to corners that you would otherwise hardly get to see - but he would be happy to receive a tip!
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: There is not much to see and no guides were present at the time I went. The "castle" is not well maintained and I am not sure if it worth the visit.

Tamansari closes at 3pm and we reached around 1pm on a Thursday, luckily it wasn't too crowded. The castle is well maintained and pretty but personally it wasn't breathtaking. Still worth to visit though.

After the Sultan's Palace it is quite a classic to also visit the Water Castle. While its story is interesting, it's certainly nothing captivating or unmissable to see. Furthermore, it is not even well maintained. However, a short stop can be made to complete the tour of Yogyakarta's attractions.

Tamansari (Water Palace) is a palace in Yogyakarta. It is now a popular tourist attraction. When we visited, it was the dry season, and there was no water in the various pools. However, I found it to be a beautiful place with lush vegetation and intriguing architectural structures.

Yogyakarta, as the former capital of the Sultanate, has many historical sites, and it feels very much like Xi'an in Indonesia. The Water Palace in the city is like the Huaqing Pool, which is worth a visit. 🕍＞ Taman Sari The Water Palace is called Taman Sari in Indonesian. It was originally built for various purposes. It is said that the Sultan invited a Portuguese architect to build this exquisite holiday villa so that his leisure and entertainment space could remain hidden. The Water Palace was once a luxurious entertainment park for the royal palace, and it was also a swimming pool and waterway for the Sultan and his entourage. The Sultan would throw a rose from the high tower on the south side of the swimming pool, and the concubine who could catch the rose would be his "wife". In other words, whoever caught the rose would be the Sultan's queen or his concubine. The Water Palace was originally damaged in the Diponegoro Java War, and was later completely destroyed by the earthquake in 1865. Most of what we see today are just the remains of the past. The bathhouse has been rebuilt, and the tunnel and underground mosque are very special. The Water Palace is actually very small. You can see it all in half an hour. You can visit it together with the nearby Sultan Palace. However, the palace is closed on Mondays. Please pay attention to the time. 🕑＞ Opening hours: 9:00-15:00 🎫＞ Ticket price: 25k
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:

The entry garden soon disappeared and men were smoking in the shade shelters.

En fait Yogyakarta est une ville sympathique qui s’est bien agrandie depuis mon premier passage fin 1978 et ses joyaux sont à rechercher dans les environs : le complexe de temples hindouistes de Prambanan et le mandala bouddhique de Borobudur - avec un prix considérablement augmenté et un accès restreint  aux sites en 2022 pour maîtriser l’afflux de touristes; quant au Merapi, son activité volcanique en a interdit l’accès pour un temps au moins …. mais cela ne m’empêchera pas de retourner à Yogyakarta si une autre occasion se présente : on s’y sent bien et c’est l’essentiel.

Review Text: Avant toute chose, en sortant du Kraton, renseignez-vous pour trouver "Water Castle". Nous, nous avons eu de la chance: nous avons fait une très belle rencontre avec un guide indonésien charmant qui, pendant deux heures,  nous a accompagnés par de petites ruelles vers le Taman Sari ( le Water Castle), magnifique endroit qu'il ne faut pas manquer à Jogja avant de nous montrer la magnifique mosquée souterraine.

Taman Sari Complex is one of the historical and cultural heritage tourism sites in Yogyakarta. Taman Sari Complex is nicknamed as the Water Palace. It is located southwest of the Yogyakarta Palace. Historically, the Taman Sari was built as a garden and a bathing place for the royal family and also functioning as a stronghold for the kingdom.
The Taman Sari Complex is divided into 4 sections, Some of the parts that I like from the four sections are:
1. "Umbul Pasiraman" or "Umbul Binangun". At Umbul Pasiraman there are three large pools which spoil my eyes. Umbul Pasiraman is surrounded by high walls. That said, Umbul Pasiraman is used for Sultan, the empress, concubines, and their daughters as a bathing and rest place.
2. "Sumur Gumuling", also known as a secret mosque under the ground. Its location some distance from the Taman Sari Complex. Long time ago, Sumur Gumuling functioned as a secret mosque for  worshiping.
To reach the Sumur Gumuling, we will go down the hallway to the bottom of the ground. It is said that the Gumuling Well was built with the aim of tricking the Dutch army during the colonial period. Access to the Gumuling Well is made like a hidden passageway and leads into the ground. Interestingly, if we shout inside the Sumur Gumuling, the echo of our voice will be heard to a fairly distant radius.
Sumur Gumuling is one of the favorite spots for prewedding photos and Sumur Gumuling is one of the instagramable spots.
Taman Sari Complex's opening hours are 8 am to 2 pm. In my opinion, the best time to visit Taman Sari Complex is in the morning, especially if you want to take lots of photos. Usually at noon, the Taman Sari Complex is increasingly crowded. In addition, if you come in the morning, there is a longer time to explore all parts of it.
The ticket price is affordable. The ticket price for domestic tourists is IDR 5000 and for foreign tourists is IDR 7000. For those of you who bring a camera will be subject to an additional price of IDR 2000.
Faktor Penarik: Ketertarikan Budaya, Ketertarikan Fasilitas, Ketertarikan Suasana
