 Niets bijzonders te zien dus. Alleen gesloten gebouwen.

setiap ke jogja pasti berkunjung kesini,entahlah liat bangunannya saja sudah senang.
selain bangunannya yang menarik, tiket masuknya juga murah cuma Rp 5000 saja.

This place is OK to visit if you have some free time to spare. Cheap entrance fee, good spots for photo but very crowded. Walk towards the entrance and tour guide will start to bother you. Reject them politely if you want to skip the history of the water castle. They will ask for a small fee after the end of the tour. Overall nothing special.

We spent around 30 minutes here and it was okay. We were given an information leaflet about the place. The tour guides hassled us to give us a tour but we declined time and time again, it got a little annoying because we just wanted to enjoy it by ourselves.

Es un auténtico timo la entrada son 3,6 €
Q es poco pero es que es una auténtica estafa de templo, está en obras y vas a ver una piscina vieja vacía, es de coña... no merece la pena en absoluto

Love this place very much!! 
There is a tour guide available for a tourist who want to now the story of this place with additional charge.

Tourist, $1.50 per pax. 
Nothing to shout abt in there. 
The so called water castle have no water inside at all. Badly maintained.

Пришли в "замок на воде"... а воды-то нет! 
И это после "посещения" дворца Кратон, который был закрыт. Занавес!

Tamansari, a recreation place for Sultan (King) in old times, and for the Sultan's Mistresses to swim and have fun. Now become a heritage and historical place. Located in the centre of the city of Yogyakarta, recommended for architects to study, for young children to study history. Ask for a guide, they are not set a price. it's really helpful to go with a guide. Cheap price for entrance tickets, nice ornaments and architecture.
Faktor Penarik: Ketertarikan Budaya, Ketertarikan Fasilitas, Ketertarikan Suasana
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
great attraction with historical building and more story from this place, many gem's spot, beautiful, and you can enjoyed this area slowly
but a lot of visitor and this area inside in housing make so crowded

The location of Tamansari is in the downtown of Jogja. It's approximately 2 KMs from Malioboro.
This place is a part of historical place owned by Keraton Yogyakarta and now become one of a must visited places if you want to explore Jogja.

This place is getting busy and lot of improvement from my last visit in 2013.
Suggestion: need to have somebody to in charge for photo in certain/good spot of photo area, this is to avoid long queue and mess up photo.

For me the best attraction in Yogya city! The palace is beautiful and it feels like you are in a theme park. Also please do not forget the mosque!! The architecture is stunning! But it is a bit hard to find.
Faktor Penarik: Ketertarikan Budaya, Ketertarikan Fasilitas, Ketertarikan Suasana

Review Text:
Quand on arrive dans un tel lieu, on s'attend a autre chose.
En effet, hormis le fait qu' il est impossible de trouver la moindre information en Anglais pour comprendre un minimum, on sent bien que ce palace n'est plus entretenu depuis bien longtemps. Les bassins sont sales, vides pour la plupart et ce qui pourrait etre une une attraction incontournable n,est en fait, qu'un piege a touristes sans interets.
Le Water Palace fermera ses portes courant novembre, suite à un don de l’ancien président américain Obama le Water Palace sera en grande partie rénové.

El castillo del agua es chico, cuenta con 3 piscinas pero solo 1 con agua, otra vacía y la última en reparación.
Se dice que el sultán lo construyó como casa de relajación y ahí llevaba a sus concubinas.
Esta bonito para tomar un par de fotos y conocee l historia, si te sobra tiempo vale la.pena ir, a lo mucho te tomará 1hr
La entrada cuesta 15,000 IDR + 3,000 IDR si quieres tomar fotos con cámara,  el celular no paga.

Tempat bersejarah, tempat nya masih sangat bagus, untuk permandian raja tempat sauna jaman dulu, dan masjid bawah tanah yang membuat saya terkesan, meski pun di bawah tanah tempat nya tetap sejuk, yang jalan* ke jogja wajib ke sini ni
Faktor Penarik: Ketertarikan Budaya, Ketertarikan Fasilitas, Ketertarikan Suasana
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: We visited Tamansari in weekday around 1pm, it was raining, so there wasn't many people here. This place is historical and instagramable haha. In Tamasari, there will be many tour guide to give you a tour, af first we didn't intend to hire a guide to go to the underground mosque but it turned out that we got lost because we need to pass the residents' house and there's no clear sign so we decided to hire a guide. He didn't say how much the fee we should pay so we gave 25.000 IDR.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Está bien. No es nada del otro mundo, pero después de la birria del palacio del sultán, esto te parece hasta bonito. Tampoco es que sea una maravilla de obligada visita. Se puede prescindir a mi juicio.

The water castle is a nice relic from Yogyakarta’s history and you can take some cool pictures. However it’s not that special to go visit, we only went there because we had so much time to spare during our visit in Yogyakarta. 4 days here is way too long to see the city, we recommend max 2 days. In 2 days you can see the city center, the Borobodur temple, Prambanan and hike up a mountain or etc. That’s basically all that Yogya really has to offer in our opinion.
クラトン王宮から路地を通って南に１ｋｍほど向かうと、水の王宮と呼ばれる離宮があります。門をくぐると壁に囲まれた浴場があり、かつては王に仕える女性たちが水浴びを楽しんだ場所だとのこと。現在は解放されており、王宮と並ぶ観光名所になっています。
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
Het is leuk om het Kraton en aansluitend het waterpaleis te bezoeken met de riksja.Het kraton vonden we maar gemiddeld interessant.
Het waterpaleis is mooi maar de waterpartijen zijn weinig onderhouden Pluspunt - Het paleis(je) heeft een zeer originele centrale trap voor fotografen een tip!
You will need one of their many guides if you would like to know the history of the place, as there are not many signs around.

王宮から徒歩10分くらい。あとから思いましたが市場の中突っ切ったら近道だったようです。チケット買って見学してたら地元のおじさんが説明してくれ(日本語で。)塔の上にもあがれるとのこと。3階まであがれます。梯子階段なのでおりるのこわごわ。他に上ってくる方いなかったからスレ違いは気を使わなくてすみました。
噴水もあり見ているだけで暑さ紛れました。
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: tempatnya bersih, biaya masuk murah banget. ada guide yang menunggu di setiap sudut jalan yang siap ditanyai tentang sejarah bangunan dan aarah tujuan. di sepanjang perjalanan menuju pusat taman sari juga terdapat kampung cyber, tepat penduduk sana berjualan dan segala macam informasi tersedia. tempat yang menarik sekaligus jalan jalan murah.
Faktor Penarik: Ketertarikan Budaya, Ketertarikan Fasilitas, Ketertarikan Suasana
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Taman Sari 被稱為水宮，因裡面有幾座大池而得名，屬以前皇室的娛樂場所，目前多數已荒廢，僅存既有建築供人憑弔，其實水宮範圍不小，有很多地道可以連通，並與周邊民居相通，沒熟人帶領確實會有點摸不清方向
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Lugar interessante pela história do sultanato. Rende boas fotografias. Interessante visitar com guia, não há muitas informações no local e achar os túneis e a mesquita sozinhos deve ser muito difícil.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
Taman sari water castle is one of an historical place in jogja.. here, the princess of the sultan had their bath and the place was so stunning. You can also follow the path to the under ground mosque which used by the sultan to pray. 
You have to pay some retribution to get in there and sometimes you'll be follow by the unlicensed guide. If you interested to know about the history you can consider to take one of them with you otherwise just walk away and have your own exploration
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: This place was a lovely little find in the city tucked away the back alleys surrounded by houses so it is a little hard to find so I would recommend getting a guide otherwise you might miss parts of the complex. Not only that but the history is very interesting and you learn a lot from the guides
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
It's pretty, though not particularly interesting, and whilst it's probably historically significant, there are no signs explaining what is significant about it.
It's cheap to get in so you might as well visit if in the area, but note that the one-way route through will leave you nowhere near where you came in, and in laneways unmarked on Google Maps!
這是個收入場門票的觀光點，入面除了水池範圍之外，還有好幾個建築在附近，被旁邊的舊村落包圍着，記得要拿着觀光地圖。

designed similar to some sultan palaces in the middle east.  stories and anecdotes interestingly told by a guide who actually works for the sultan, rupiah 50,000 guide fee.  don’t forget to visit the mosque, or sumur gumuling, a very uniquely designed structure unlike others.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
王宮からちょっと歩いた場所にあります。
王様が使っていた離宮で、お気に入りの女性達と遊ぶためのプールだったということです。王様用の更衣室や専用プールなど見どころがそこそこあり、楽しめます。
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Nuansa keraton masih sangat kental di tempat ini, pengelola juga ramah, tiket masuk terjangkau. Cocok bagi yang suka hunting foto.

Hay guys... 
Saya lagi di jogja nih...mencoba untuk berpetualang sendirian.. Setelah melihat film nekad traveler akhirnya saya terinspirasi untuk melakukan hal yg sama yakni keliling Indonesia dengan tekad dan niat.. Kota pertama yg saya kunjungi pertama kali seorang diri adalah jogja.. Saya hanya libur kerja sehari dan langsung nekad berangkat ke jogja.. Sebenarnya gak cukup cuma sehari untuk mengexplore kota istimewa ini.. Tapi apa daya.. Sekali ada kesempatan langsung saja saya ambil.. Okey kita mulai..Tujuan pertama saya adl taman sari..dimana tempat ini selain tempat yg dahulunya rumah para raja dan permaisuri mereka..masih berdiri kokoh semua bangunan di tempat ini.. Yang membuat saya kagum adalah bangunan yang kuno dan menyimpang banyak kenangan sejarah yg sampai saat ini masih sangat bagus.. Selain belajar sejarah jaman dulu kita juga bisa berfoto dengan spot foto yang tidak ada di tempat lain.. Jadi jika kalian berada di kota jogja jangan lupa cantumkan taman sari di list/daftar tempat wisata yg akan kalian kunjungi...
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: A decent way to spend an hour or so. Just an old castle with a pool at the back. Can catch a couple nice photos. Maybe a tour guide would make this place more interesting! Tour booklet offered basic info. The underground mosque was ok too. If you have a few hours to kill then come here, the entry price isn’t expensive so can’t really go wrong.

Tal y como comentan otras personas, no se trata solo del edificio principal que se ve en las fotos normalmente, consta de varias construcciones interesantes. La parte menos positiva es que no está tan cuidado y arreglado como podría estarlo. Nosotros fuimos con guía que nos fué llevando a cada uno de los lugares y contando la historia lo cual es recomendable ( o al menos leerse la explicación de todos) sino simplemente paseas.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
Our expectation was high because we have saw a lot of great pictures and reviews on social media. However it was not one of the best place to visit in Yogyakarta and it seems like a little bit overrated. We came here around 12PM afternoon where the weather is extremely hot and this place is super crowded. There is nothing too special it is just about seeing around and we hardly take a good picture because people is all over the place.
Please do not come in afternoon, you can come very early right after they open. (opening hours 09:00 AM - 02:00 PM)

Unless you really enjoy a historical site and all its story, this place is not so recommended.

Tips: if you bring additional camera (beside your phone), you have to pay extra charge aside from ticket.

This place is a bull's eye for you who loves a history and heritage. You could feel the ambience of the building who speaks so mystical and historical as well. Also what I love the most about visiting Jogjakarta's attraction is it wouldn't waste your money. The value? You'll got more than your pay seriously. This place has a hidden gem. Try to sneaking around the alley on the right of this building, and let the local took you to a hidden gem inside and they'll tell you the story behind the place as well. Appreciate them with the proper numbers from your pocket. They genuinely helped you to took a picture as well. The local who super kind and nice are another hidden gem from Jogjakarta.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
I like visiting castle. And this one has a beautiful architecture!
After 20 minutes we saw all.
But still for me worth it to see!
It is just 15k entry and 3k for parking the scooter.

Op de foto’s ziet het water er prachtig blauw uit, in het echt is het groen en weinig onderhouden.

3 baden bekijken, meer is er niet echt te zien.
Visited as part of a multi temple trip. Interesting insight into the days of old when rulers governed with impunity
Rien d'exceptionnel... Juste passer un moment tranquille au calme et découvrir quelques ruelles typiques !

It's definitly not the nicest palace you will ever see or a mustsee in Yogjakarta. But when you have some time left it is nice to visit. 

A bit of paint would help to give the place some more appeal and look like it's glory days. Also there is no furniture or decor inside. It's just walls, floors and ceilings.

郊外からのホテルで何時間もかけていくほどじゃないですが、街に出てれば行ってみて良いと思います。
無料のガイドが着いてきましたが、自分達のペースで回りたい方はしっかり断った方がいいです。
あとで自分が書いたという絵を売ろうとしてきます。笑
しつこくないので良いですが。

Hati-hati jika pergi ke tempat ini dengan membawa kamera dslr. Ada pungutan dengan berbagai jenis yang harus dibayarkan di luar biaya tiket masuk. 

Petugas pengawas juga kurang ramah dibanding petugas tiket. So far kalau ke situ jangan siang-siang. PANAS.
En un ambiente especial, pueden verse un complejo de baños en forma de piscinas, parte de lo que fuera un gran jardín de descanso con varias áreas.

Naja,ich habe mehr erwartet und bin entsprechend enttäuscht. Nichts was mn sich unbedingt einplanen muss, aber es ist so nahe das man gut einmal vorbeischauen kann. Am besten gleich mit dem Sultans Palast verbinden, dann hat man die must do's in einem Gang erledigt.

A 15000rp l’entrée ne vous ruineras pas lieu en décrépitude avancée il pourrais au moins le repeindre oublier les guides car à par la pièce centrale et ses deux points d’eau de nombreuses petites pièces sans grande interêt à faire si vous êtes dans les parages
It is a very nice place but i think it should have been well maintained knowing that it is a historical building.

Arrive before 9am and ask your guide (given free with admission) to take you to the back stairway.  This stairway is featured in tons of photos and it’s beautiful to have it all to yourself for a few minutes.

We learned tons from our guide who was assigned to us upon entering.  He gave us a long history about how this was a palace that sat in the middle of a man made lake. Now, the former sultan workers have created houses on the same grounds as the lake was. It’s not easy figuring it all out and it’s somewhat spread out (7 min walk from entrance to furthest part). Good thing our guide took us.  The palace also has an exquisite pool that is still filled with water. Also there is a batik coop and lawak coffee place (120k rp or $9usd for 1 cup).
Faktor Penarik: Ketertarikan Budaya, Ketertarikan Fasilitas, Ketertarikan Suasana
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Das Watercastle on yogya sowie der sultanspalast sind ganz ok...den palast muss man in 2 etappen anschauen und beides mal eintritt Löhnen...die Locals bieten dir kostenlose Führungen an die dann in einem Batik Store oder einem Café enden...man ist wenn man das watercastle sucht auch relativ machtlos..man muss durch kleine gassen laufen dann trifft man auf einen local und er quatscht euch an ob ihr zum wstercastle wollt dann zeigt er euch den weg und tadaa ihr habt ne Führung..die Gebäude an sich waren früher sicherlich sehr imposant heute ist alles sehr runtergekommen..man darf auf keinen Fall deutschen "Standard" erwarten was den Palast des Sultans angeht...die Preise für den Eintritt sind an sich in Ordnung...ob es das totale Must see hier ist möchte ich nicht beurteilen :)

Taman Sari Water Castle was indeed a hitorical avenue of how sexism, manliness, toughness and male chauvinism was practiced and celebrated using their title and power.
Equality was not practiced earlier that time as children and concubines of the Sultan had to use separate pools.
These women even compete to be able to have spend time alone with the Sultan on the 3rd exclusive pool of this Water Castle.  This fight was being witnessed and watched over by the Sultan himself.
Glad that today, it was just a history... or we can never tell, it may repeat itself without we knowing it... 
He may not be a sultan, yet someones doing the same.
it is a recomended place with historical heritage. but when you drive to this place, please be careful because you will meet crowded ride.

Palazzo delle acque molto carino, che permette di entrare nella cultura locale.
Non si può non visitarlo!
Ảnh quảng cáo đẹp lung linh nhưng khi đến tận mắt thì không như mong đơi. Đi để biết, để tìm hiểu chứ không để lại nhiều ấn tượng

El Castillo del Agua no es sólo el estanque principal que aparece en casi todas las fotos. Se trata de un grupo de puntos a visitar, que se encuentran muy cerca unos de otros. Pasearás por callejuelas llenas de arte urbano y visitarás rincones ocultos a los que se accede por túneles y tejados aledaños.
Sal por la parte trasera del edificio principal y vete preguntando porque te va a encantar.
Necesitarás una hora mínimo para disfrutarlo.

Most of the architecture there are just ruins of the castle without anything inside. We weren’t sure what the place was about except reading from what’s in the brochure that was given to us when we paid for the entrance tickets. 

Many people were just looking for the iconic flight of stairs which was not located inside the castle but a short walk away from it. 

I wouldn’t really recommend this place to anyone who has a tight schedule.
a lot of history and never imagine that history inside history. good to know the history about the castle.

Visite sympa et agréable ! Intéressant lorsqu’on prend un guide local qui nous a permis de comprendre l’histoire de ce site 
À faire si on est dans la région

You can visit here if you have nothing to do on your last day. Not much thing to do. Crowded with people taking photos thus high chances of your photos being photobombed. During my visit, there was a newly wed couple who did a wedding shots so you have to wait for quite sometimes for them to finish shooting to get the perfect spot. Nevertheless, it was a nice visit at historical place.
国王はここのプールを使う女性からお気に入りの女性を見つけ、声をかけたとか。人が多いですが、国王の権力の大きさがよくわかる建物です。

Es un bonito palacio con piscinas de agua, aunque está un poco descuidado y el agua de las piscinas está un poco verde, merece entrar para hacer un cuantas fotos ya que es algo curioso. La entrada en el recinto cuesta menos de un euro.
Faktor Penarik: Ketertarikan Budaya, Ketertarikan Fasilitas, Ketertarikan Suasana

Review Text:
Le bâtiment est dégradé. Des graffitis sur les murs.On pourrait presque dire que c’est laissé à l’abandon. C’est dommage car avant ce bâtiment devait être magnifique! La piscine est remplie avec 15 cm d’eau et est sale. Je suis réellement déçue.A la vue des photos, je m’attendais à quelque chose de vraiment meilleur. Il y a des prix pour les étrangers et les domestiques. 2x plus chers pour les étrangers. 
Il n’y a rien pour se situer.
Basically only visit this place if you are bored and run out of things to do here . Only a dollar to enter so not too bad
Can be crowded hence had to 'fight' for spots for good shots. We spent almost an hour there. If u have the time, worth the visit.
Went here cuz of the hype. It was amazing to hear stories and the place itself is beautiful we really enjoyed it.
Bellissima!! A noi è piaciuta molto più del kraton. All’ingresso ci sono delle ragazze carinissime che studiano lingue e si offrono di farti da guida per il taman sari e la moschea sotterranea.
Sehr schöne Anlage, die nicht schön überlaufen ist und sehr gut erhalten ist. Ich finde das einzig interessante in Yogyakarta. Es ist auf jedem Fall einen Besuch wert.

Hemos ido a este palacio y a la entrada resulta que si esta bonito con su fachada muy bonita y su estanque de agua dentro muy bonito tb pero pa la caminata q nos pegamos fue poco, recomiendo cojan un medio de tranposte para trasladarse

A faire après le palais du sultan c'est même plus jolie !
Et c'est gratuit une bonne restauration ne serai pas un luxe
Sangat layak dikunjungi. Peninggalan bersejarah dengan lokasi ditengah kota, sangat mudah dijangkau.

Het paleis is erg verpauperd. Er wordt duidelijk zeer weinig onderhoud aan gepleegd. Architectonisch gezien is het niet heel bijzonder. Al met al leuk om even (een uurtje) gezien te hebben voor die prijs.
This place is cute but in desperate need of maintenance. Nothing crazy about the site, it is cute, but wouldn't make it a must go attraction.

Selain belajar sejarah, taman sari menawarkan banyak spot foto unik. Ada 3 lokasi yg wajib dikunjungi disini, jika anda tidak menyewa tourguide, banyaklah bertanya dengan ramah ke warga sekitar. Bakalan dibantu kok 😁
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Bagus. Ini merupakan tempat bersejarah. Ada beberapa tempat yang bisa dikunjungi. Untuk mengunjungi 1 tempat dan lainnya melewati perkampungan.

Nothing really exciting. Clean and well preserved. It is really hard to find the way to the Mosque, ask people around unless you want to pay for a guide. The Mosque is under the ground level and completly circular. Price to go into the site is really cheap.

Sebelum check out dari hotel di area Wirobrajan , kami mampir dulu kemari. Dan kami disambut oleh Bapak² Pemandu Wisata area ini. Jika ingin explore sendiri tanpa pemandu juga boleh. 
Area ini cukup luas. Mulai dari kolam pemandian untuk keluarga kerajaan , sampai ke terowongan bawah tanah. Rutenya pun keluar masuk ke pelosok pemukiman penduduk setempat. 
Meski bangunan tua , tapi betul² terawat dan bersih.

I must be honest that when I read about this place I was tempted to skip it. I am glad I didn't. The castle is a lovely blend of architecture and local village life. Walking through the alley ways is a wonderful experience. In addition, it was interested to learn about Mark Zuckerburgs visit here and giving the village free wifi!
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: El Palacio de Agua (Tamansari) es un lugar bonito, aunque me lo imaginaba más bonito por todas las descripciones que hacenen las guías. Lo que pasa es que está descuidado, con un mantenimiento bastante pobre.
The Water Castle itself might not look like the best attraction, but it's worth a visit. We got lost in the compound, and that was the key of the visit, not the temple itself.

J'ai eu un peu peur en voyant le prospectus à l'hôtel mais c'est à faire!
Le temple est petit mais tres beau avec son bassin intérieur et cela vaut vraiment le coup de se perdre dans la ville intérieure où se mélange les vieilles maisons avec des graff contemporain. 
Seul petit bémol, les différents lieux ne sont pas tres bien indiqués mais il y a des gens pour vous aider sinon suivez les groupes avec guides!
Worth the admission and a half hour, but it isn’t on your bucket list.  You can see all the Yogyakarta city sights in a morning.

The place is very nice but very crowded and is definitely full of people. It definitely needs some maintenance to be well preserved. The interesting part was actually after we left the place though the exit sign, there was this small shop that has a very artistic garden. I thought it was a happy secret surprise to see.

Quite extensive and historic. However badly preserved. One can imagine that it would have been very pretty. But not in its current state. The approach to underground is through long back lanes. Here again it’s all pretty much barren. 
Essentially being used as photo taking site more than of real discovery quality.
Good place to visit if u wanna know history and castle in yogyakarta.  Its good places to photography too

This historical site could be better maintained but it is worth of visit. The most attractive point of the castle is the bathing complex that belonged to the Sultan and his wifes. Entry ticket is cheap (1$).

De oude badplaats van de Sultan is best wel indrukwekkend. Je betaalt 15.000 roepie per persoon. Via ruïnes en ondergrondse gangen wandel je door en onder een wijk van gezellige straatjes waar restanten staan van de sultan zijn rustplaatsen. Het waterkasteel is mooi onderhouden. Door de Portugese architectuur waan je je soms in de buurt van Marokko! Let op: schenk niet te veel aandacht aan de locals die je willen helpen met het zoeken naar de volgende locatie van het complex. Ze zijn behulpzaam, maar moeilijk weg te krijgen. Ook al heb je duidelijk gemaakt dat je geen koffie in hun zaak wil drinken, wat verderop.

Review Text: For historic purposes, this one of the required steps on a city tour. It's worth a few photo ops and the nearby underground mosque is interesting.

Taman Sari Keraton Yogyakarta adalah situs bekas taman atau kebun istana Keraton Ngayogyakarta Hadiningrat,

Taman ini dibangun pada masa pemerintahan Sultan Hamengku Buwono I (HB I) pada tahun 1758-1765.

Awalnya, taman yang mendapat sebutan "The Fragrant Garden" ini memiliki luas lebih dari 10 hektare dengan sekitar 57 bangunan, namun saat ini, sisa-sisa bagian Taman Sari yang dapat dilihat hanyalah yang berada di barat daya kompleks Kedhaton saja.

Konon, Taman Sari dibangun di bekas keraton lama, yaitu Pesanggrahan Garjitawati, yang didirikan oleh Susuhunan Paku Buwono II,
sebagai tempat istirahat kereta kuda yang akan pergi ke Imogiri (Komplek makam raja-raja mataram islam di Tenggara kota Yogyakarta). Meskipun secara resmi dikatakan sebagai kebun kerajaan, namun beberapa bangunan yang ada mengindikasikan bahwa Taman Sari dapat difungsikan sebagai benteng pertahanan terakhir jika istana diserang oleh musuh.

Kompleks Taman Sari setidaknya dapat dibagi menjadi 4 bagian.

Bagian pertama adalah danau buatan yang terletak di sebelah barat.

Bagian selanjutnya adalah bangunan yang berada di sebelah selatan danau buatan antara lain Pemandian Umbul Binangun.

Bagian ketiga adalah Pasarean Ledok Sari dan Kolam Garjitawati yang terletak di selatan bagian kedua.

Bagian terakhir adalah bagian sebelah timur bagian pertama dan kedua dan meluas ke arah timur sampai tenggara kompleks Magangan.
Faktor Penarik: Ketertarikan Budaya, Ketertarikan Fasilitas, Ketertarikan Suasana
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
Awal mengira destinasi wisata "Taman Sari" itu tempat wisata seperti pada umumnya. Setelah langsung ke sana , ternyata Taman Sari itu desa dan warga lokal banyak yang tinggal di sana. Kagum dengan keramahan warga Jogjakarta yang bersedia tempat tinggalnya dilalui wisatawan setiap hari.

Saat berwisata, saya meminta panduan dari pemandu di sana. Mereka tidak meminta bayaran, serelanya kita ingin memberi berapa. Tapi untung saja kami meminta panduan, karena tanpa pemandu kita tidak tahu harus berjalan ke arah mana; pada dasarnya wisata ke Tamansari adalah wisata mengelilingi desa. Pintu masuknya pun tidak begitu jelas seperti tempat wisata pada umumnya.

Untuk teman- teman yang tertarik pada sejarah Kota Jogjakarta, Tamansari menyajikan cerita menarik untuk dikagumi, dengan penjelasan dari pemandu, kita bisa terkagum" dengan filosofi dan sejarah yang terkandung di Tamansari. Untuk mengitari seluruh desa Tamansari, dibutuhkan kira" waktu setengah hari. Kita juga bisa membeli kain batik asli buatan desa Tamansari. Harga yang ditawarkan mulai dari Rp 200.000,-. Pengrajinnya pun dengan ramah menjelaskan proses pembuatan batik. Mereka cenderung tidak memberikan harga yang tinggi untuk menjual kain batik. Prinsip mereka, wisatawan berkunjung, membeli karya dengan hati sukacita, dan niscaya hari nanti akan kembali membeli batik dan memberitahukan pada saudara".

Review Text:
Tamansari Water Castle is the abandoned site of a former royal garden, though it is hardly short of visitors. The thing we noticed about Yogyakarta is that tourist destinations are visited by many locals and few tourists, so these places are usually crowded, especially on weekends. 

Nonetheless, the castle offers quite a few sites for photo taking. As you walk along the castle, you will be offered a tour by their licensed (English speaking) guide who can give you a history and introduction to the place. We suspect they will also bring you to the underground mosque (more on that later). We did not take up his offer though.

The castle interior is interspersed with shops that sell cheap snacks and drinks and souvenirs, and the use of their toilets for Rp. 2,000. We were glad they were not pushy with their wares. 

Instead of (what I presume) paying the guide to bring you to the underground mosque, ask around the locals (or show them a picture of the mosque) who will be happy to show you where it is. You have to walk through an nondescript alley, and up some stairs and turns before you reach the entrance of the tunnel to the mosque. We were led by one such local. Keep the ticket you paid for at the entrance, as the caretaker will ask to see your ticket again. He will tear the ticket upon entry, which we assume it means it is for a single entry only. 

A Google search of the underground mosque will show pictures of people standing alone at the staircase with the light shining down on them. We have no idea how they managed to do that since the staircase is THE place to take pictures and everyone is waiting for their turn. Waiting till closing time (3pm) might do the trick, but we didn't do that.

Entrance fee is Rp. 15,000 a pop for foreigners so it is still worth a visit if you are in the area, or want to kill about an hour of your time.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Taman Sari Water Castle, more fondly known as Taman Sari amongst the locals in Yogyakarta, is the site of a former royal garden of the Sultanate of Yogyakarta. It is located about 2 km south within the grounds of the Kraton, Yogyakarta, Indonesia. It is a beautifully maintained property with many beautiful spots for photography. Le chateau d'eau du sultan est un lieu plutôt joli à visiter mais n'est franchement pas exceptionnel. C'est plutôt un attrape touriste.
A notre entrée dans le chateau, un guide nous a alpagué en commençant à nous présenter les lieux alors qu'on avait rien demandé. Après 1h30 de visite, il nous amène dans un restaurant appelé "restaurant du sultan" où un buffet attendent les touristes. Le buffet était plutôt bon et le prix raisonnable (85 000 roupies par personne). Cependant le guide demande un rétribution de 50 000 roupies, sauf que comme il ne nous a rien dit sur ses honoraires au début de la visite, nous nous sommes trouvés fort embarrassés car nous n'avions pas la somme qu'il voulait. Alors notre conseil c'est : FAITES TRES ATTENTION AUX GUIDEX. Si un guide commence spontanément à vous faire l'histoire du chateau d'eau sans votre avis, demandez lui bien combien cela va vous coûter avant de vous lancer dans la visite. Globalement en tant que touristes, nous avions un peu l'impression d'être des portes-feuille ambulants. Les guides vous emmènent dans différentes boutiques ou encore des petits cafés pour que vous achetiez des choses à leurs associés. Les vendeurs dans les boutiques sont même assez insistants, voir un peu trop. Une sorte de réseau semble s'être constitué pour soutirer le plus d'argent aux touristes, ce qui n'est pas du tout agréable en terme de ressenti.

It's not a big area and it is located at quite a strategic location in Jogja. Tamansari is apparently one of the historical buildings of Sultan Palace or Keraton Yogyakarta. Tamansari means "A Beautiful Garden". During its heydays, Tamansari was a recreation and a royal bathing place and also a retreat place for the Sultan of Yogyakarta and his family.

Satu dari sekian banyak tempat wisata sejarah yang ada di Yogyakarta, tepatnya di Jalan Taman. Taman Sari sendiri terletak sangat dekat dengan Keraton Ngayogyakarta Hadiningrat dan hanya memerlukan waktu tempuh sekitar 15 menit dari alun-alun utara keraton. Dulunya Taman Sari merupakan tempat rekreasi bagi keluarga kerajaan sekaligus sebagai benteng pertahanan yang dibangun oleh Sri Sultan Hamengku Buwono I. Kini Taman Sari menjadi salah satu cagar budaya sekaligus tempat wisata populer di Yogyakarta.

Review Text:
I was impressed by the size of the bathing pool (which occupies pretty much the whole "inner area" after going through a short pathway from the entrance gate); but I was also "unimpressed" by barely a foot of water in it (clean water though), no water coming out of the fountain pillars in the pool (actually there was but just a tiny negligible amount), and dirty walls around that inner area where the pool is.  Then beside one end of the bathing pool is a small tower that can be gone up (from which there's a nice view of the pool below), and beside both ends of the bathing pool are some rooms that can be gone in (which are mostly empty except for something like a "big bed" in one of them if I recall correctly), and on the other side of the small tower is also another bathing pool (of a smaller size than the main one).  More than anything though, what fascinated me most at this place is "the big face with the tongue sticking out" which I presumed is like the symbol of the sultanate (there are about three of those identical faces here that can be seen above the gates).  And if you're into some "pricey" souvenir shopping like beautiful batik-designed paintings for something like 100,000 rupiah, there are some of those shops just on the other side of the exit gate from the inner area (where the big bathing pool is).

And nearby (just about a 5-minute walk to the north from the area with the souvenir shops as mentioned above), worth stopping by is the ancient mosque which is "mostly underground" but also with a "circular open area" surrounded by these "tall archways" where you can stand and look down into that open area or look up above at the sky.

If coming by the transjogja bus (2A, 2B & 3A are the numbers that I know of), a good bus stop is the one right in front of Fort Vredeburg on the south end of the "shopping street" Jl. Malioboro (both great places with nice "diorama displays" inside the Vredeburg Museum and plenty of shops & streetside vendors along Malioboro); it's a walkable distance to the south (although I would suggest taking a rickshaw or a horse-drawn buggy due to like the "maze" of narrow streets in the area) from that bus stop to Kraton or the Sultan's Palace (with a number of small museums to learn about the past sultans) followed by this place which is just about a 10-minute walk from the exit gate on the south side of Kraton.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: A very qute site which was interesting to see, but wont take too much of your day as it is really quite small. We had a local guide to take us to s little underground ”cave” just a cross couple of roads and that was also ok.

Het Water Castle is leuk om te bezoeken. Het is niet super spectaculair maar voor 33000 entree (2 personen) is het een leuke activiteit. Het terrein heeft wat achterstallig onderhoudt maar is nog steeds mooi om te zien. Ook de ondergrondse tunnel die iets buiten het terrein valt (wel even zoeken) is de moeite waard.

We got the entrance ticket as usual and entered the castle to see two outdoor swimming pools and thought, nothing special. As we exited, we overheard this local giving directions to some tourists. Curious, we paused to listen too, not wanting to miss anything. It turned out that this man is a local guide and is offering his service to us. Sensing his sincerity we went off with him. Although his english is not very good, we are still able to hold short conversations and get to know this place in detail through him. It turned out that this place is actually filled with water in the past and people needed to travel by boat. It did not have houses that we see and roads that we are walking now. There are tunnels that can lead the royal family to the sea in times of invasion, underground mosque and lavatories. The guide said the country is filing this to be under UNESCO world heritage site and once approved, these houses will be demolished and the water castle will be restored to its former glory. Can't wait to witness this!
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
So after reading some not so good reviews about guides, my husband and I went to Taman Sari adamant on exploring it ourselves. After all, we had a pamphlet showing the landmarks and GPS right?

Quite wrong we were. Once you're in the compounds it's a labyrinth that snakes around the locals' homes - it isn't easy to find all the spots and coupled with the heat, it can get pretty frustrating. Furthermore without an explanation, the ruins seem sad and... well, they just look like a poorly maintained mess.

After we found the second building (Pulo Kenanga) and feeling extremely lost, we were picked up by a guide and though we were wary at first, he was actually very helpful in turning our negative Taman Sari experience into a positive one! He spoke very good english and expertly brought us through the compounds with a very good commentary. He explained how the whole area was originally just water, why doorways were built so low and explained the interesting mechanisms of the King's bedroom. We ended the informal 'tour' with a better appreciation of the place, and tipped him IDR20,000 for 40 minutes.

Bottom line, a (good) guide would be extremely helpful for you to understand the history of Taman Sari. So be discerning when picking one out - gauge their level of English, the amount of "hard selling" they do, and don't be afraid to turn them down if you feel uncomfortable.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: taman sari adalah salah satu destinasi wisata sejarah yang terletak di tengah Kota Jogja. lokasinya yang mudah dijangkau dan daya tarik wisatanya membuat para wisatawan memenuhi tempat ini hampir setiap hari.

The name Taman Sari comes from the Javanese words taman, meaning a "garden" or "park" and sari, which means "beautiful" or "flowers". Hence, the name Taman Sari means an area of a beautiful garden adorned with flowers. An old article described it as a "water castle" (Dutch: waterkasteel); as by shutting the watergates, the complex would be completely immersed in water, leaving tall structures standing out.

The building of Taman Sari commenced during the reign of Sultan Hamengkubuwono I(1755–1792), the first sultan of the Yogyakarta Sultanate, and was completed by the time of Sultan Hamengkubuwono II. The building site, however, had already been known as a bathing place called Pacethokan Spring since Sunan Amangkurat IV’s reign (1719–1726).[6][7] According to Kitab Mamana in Yogyakarta Kraton, the project leader for the construction of Taman Sari was Tumenggung Mangundipura. He had travelled twice to Batavia to learn about European architecture, which is the reason why the architecture of Taman Sari has marks of European style.[8] The Regent of Madiun, Raden Rangga Prawirasentika, participated in funding the construction of Taman Sari. Prawirasentika also beseeched the Sultan to be relieved of Madiun's tax obligation. He offered other alternative ways of payment. The Sultan accepted his proposal. In 1758, the Sultan commanded the Regent to supervise the making of bricks and various complements, which would be used to build a beautiful garden. The sultan wanted a place where he could spend some time to relax after many years of wars that he had just experienced. Raden Tumenggung Mangundipura, under supervision of Raden Arya Natakusuma (who later became Sri Pakualam II), was responsible for the construction. The building was started in 1684 Javanese year (1758 AD). After finding out how large the complex was, Raden Rangga Prawirasentika realized that the cost would have been greater than the taxes. He resigned from the project and was replaced by Prince Natakusuma who continued the project to completion.[9][10]

Taman Sari was built three years after the Giyanti Agreement as a resting place for Sultan Hamengkubuwono I. The complex consists of about 59 buildings[4] including a mosque, meditation chambers, swimming pools, and a series of 18 water gardens and pavilions surrounded by artificial lakes. The complex was effectively used between 1765–1812.[11]

The British invasion of the Yogyakarta Kraton saw considerable parts of the complex destroyed in 1812.[12]

The building of Taman Sari ended upon the completion of the gates and the walls. A sengkalan memet (a Javanese chronogram)[13][14] on the western gate (Gedhong Gapura Hageng) marks the year with the Javanese words Lajering Kembang Sinesep Peksi, denoting the Javanese year of 1691 or about 1765: lajering, "core" for 1; kembang, "flower" for 9; sinerep, "suck" or "drink" for 6; peksi, "bird" for 1; the sentence can be read as "birds gathering nectar of the flower". The relief around this sengkalan memet shows birds siphoning honey from flowery trees.

The maintenance of Taman Sari was abandoned shortly after Hamengkubuwono I died, partly because the elaborate hydraulic works were so difficult to maintain. The gardens were neglected and the buildings suffered some damage during the Java War of 1825–1830.[6]

Taman Sari Water Castle, also known as Taman Sari (Javanese: ꦠꦩꦤ꧀ ꦱꦫꦶ), is the site of a former royal garden of the Sultanate of Yogyakarta. It is located about 2 km south within the grounds of the Kraton, Yogyakarta, Indonesia. Built in the mid-18th century, the Taman Sari had multiple functions, such as a resting area, a workshop, a meditation area, a defense area, and a hiding place.
Taman Sari consisted of four distinct areas: a large artificial lake with islands and pavilions located in the west, a bathing complex in the centre, a complex of pavilions and pools in the south, and a smaller lake in the east. Today only the central bathing complex is well preserved, while the other areas have been largely occupied by the Kampung Taman settlement. (Wikipedia).
