Review Text:
Actually it is not a palace, because the sultan did not live there;  he went there for relaxation only, along with his harem ladies. The complex consists of two walled baths. As you walk in through the gate, you come to the first and biggest bath. These days it takes some effort not to be distracted by the poor state of repair. But the flower pots around the pool, the stone ornaments that represent lotus blossoms and jasmine flowers, the plants in the pots and the sun that shone in the water, helped us to imagine the luxury and opulence when it was in use. In the middle between the two pools is a gallery with the private room of the sultan. In it is a bed on a large platform. There under a cavity, which had the function (according to our guide)  to create a kind of sauna.

But that was not the only function of this room; through the window with the bars the sultan could overlook the main pool. Reportedly there were also women received, who had the honor to be invited as a candidate for the harem of the Sultan. And what did the sultan do if  he wanted to get to know one of them better? As sultan you are not going  to shout through the window  to the lady. No; you hang a colored cloth through the bars outside. How the match exactly was made, our guide did not know. So I wondered:  did  the color of the cloth match the color of the dress or bathing suit of the chosen one? That would have made it a  wet T-shirt contest  ‘avant-la-lettre’ . Or wore all the ladies a different colored flower or ribbon in their hair, because that's all you need, right?  Or was it just one applicant at a time? Anyway, the fact that the water palace has so much deferred maintenance, also made clear to us, that these scenes belong to the past.

Enriched with this knowledge we walked further, to conclude our visit with a climb to the top of the gate, opposite of the gate where we came in.  Formerly there was outside this part of the palace a park that stretched to the presidential palace. Now you can see houses and small streets running down to the walls. It's pretty fun to go down there and walk clockwise around the water palace through the small streets. Stay as close as possible to the wall. At one point, after an uphill street, you see at your right, and somewhat lower, a covered waterway, which is now dry. Go in, and you exit again near a street, close to the palace gate, where you started
. 
All in all, we found the water palace more unique than the 'normal' palace of the sultan and it’s worth a hearty recommendation.
Faktor Penarik: Ketertarikan Budaya, Ketertarikan Fasilitas, Ketertarikan Suasana
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
We went to the water castle on a Saturday which was a mistake as the pool was being cleaned (or so our guide told us). The place would look better with the bathing pools full so be careful which day you go. Can be a little hard to find so we took a becak from the main street and we were glad that we did.
Our guide was informative but seemed to be more interested in taking us into the batik shops than telling us about the history of the building.

You can go here from Sultan's Palace (it's at the back) or enter the site independently. It has it's own entrance area. It is a pretty place with fountains and olden days feel. It's authentic and will provide you many photo spots. But there are a few negatives that will spoil your trip. I reaally hope for one thing to be improved at least...provide a map!!

It's a huge place to explore, like an open air museum. It's mysterious and like a maze. You can get a guide for a little backstory or venture on your own. They don't ask for payment. The most confusing thing is that there are many ways to enter the place and suddenly they asked for tickets (you don't even passed the ticket kiosk but you're already 30mins inside lol)

The site sits intertwined with a sizeable settlement of locals, which is weird but that's how it is. You'll enter someone's backyard and still inside the compound. I was there for about 2 hours but couldn't find all the places stated in the brochure. There are maps on the information board but it's unclear and not useful. 

And seriously avoid weekends...there are way too many people. 

We went there walking from Kraton area. It is doable but tiring in midday heat and the complex roads is confusing. You can just chart a trishaw ride from wherever you stay in the city centre and it'll not cost you so much (just 10k-20k rp).
There are drink stalls and some local food inside and places to sit when you're tired.
Tempat zaman dulu Raja mataram mandi.enjoyed dengan cerita tourist guide.bagus untuk selfy.kolam renangnya yang indah dan cozy banget.
Faktor Penarik: Ketertarikan Budaya, Ketertarikan Fasilitas, Ketertarikan Suasana

Review Text: Noting special about this place but worth the visit. Your tour to jogya wont complete without visiting historical place. Just a couples of pools,spot for photos and guide will bring u to few shops selling souvenirs.
Photoable. Good spot for take a photo. There is many history here. Good hospitality and cheap price with a good tour guide :) very nice
Accueil décevant, site très mal entretenu, rénovation nécessaire. Pas à la hauteur des espérances pour un site touristique. Entrée pas excessive mais ne mérite pas de payer plus.

Taman Sari offer historical site of Yogyakarta Kingdom in the past. The site is a castle with 3 pools used as the princesses royal bath.
As a stand alone object, Taman Sari not offer much, you can explore the site for less than an hour. But it completes your historical journey after visiting the palace, the fort, and other historical sites 
Good for photos, but can be overcrowded on the holiday.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
Payed the entrance fee which wasn't that expensive. 
A lot of guides offer you explanations for free (but then look at you intensely when they finish so that you give the biggest tip possible..) 
Our guide was talking faster than he should have (not the best english) but we still managed to understand a little about the back story of the castle. 

The installation has a very old look to it but in a very charming way. 
I liked it a lot. 
I would have loved more if we could have gone into the pools since it was a super hot day! 
The visit didn't take that long and there were a lot of people visiting so sometimes the rooms get a little crowded. 
Its worth a visit but only if you're already in the neighborhood.

It was okay, worth the entrance fee as it was very cheap. My tips is have a guide, because there's no information or anything, and not that nice if you only look around without knowing things. I didn't have a guide, but I overheard some other guides who were giving info.
If you're okay to walk, walk more outside the castle, explore the villages it's nice with many mural painting, art galleries etc. At the end you'll suddenly arrived at Pasar Ngasem.
Tempat yg bagus, ini pertama kali saya kesini, Akan tetapi tempat ini kurang terjaga dengan back. Banyak sampah dan bekas botol Minuman.
The palace truly reflects the royal style of the rulers having swimming pools places to rest watch tower etc.

Der Eintritt von 30.000 IDR pro Person ist in Ordnung. Jedoch ist das Wasserschloss an sich kein wirkliches Highlight. Im Endeffekt macht man die gleichen zwei Bilder, die auch alle anderen Touristen machen (einmal das Schloss an sich und dann die vielen Treppen), denn mehr gibt es kaum zu sehen. 
Dazu muss man sagen, dass es sich um eine riesige Anlage handelt. Es ist quasi wie ein eigenes kleines Dorf in der Stadt. Wenn man das Wasserschloss passiert hat, kommt man durch verschiedene enge Gassen zu den weiteren "Sehenswürdigkeiten". Der Allgemeinzustand ist eher ungepflegt. 
Ein Guide ist hierfür übrigens nicht notwendig, zur Not kann man sich durchfragen oder andere freundliche Besucher weisen einem den Weg. 
Für diesen günstigen Preis kann man das Wasserschloss aber guten Gewissens besuchen und mit ein bisschen Glück auch ein schönes Foto (ohne chinesische Reisegruppe) schießen ;)

Auf jeden Fall ist das Water Castle eine Empfehlung. Wenn man alle Verästelungen besucht mit Unterwasser Moschee etc. bekommt man einen Eindruck wie einzigartig es gewesen sein muss. Auf jeden Fall muss man etwas über die Historie des Water Castle gelesen haben oder einen Guide mitnehmen.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: if you want to know more about the story, better you come with a local guy. they will bring you to the area that you can explore. if you here on the weekend you will find many domestic and foreign tourist. this site is romantic ambience
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: We saw the water castle from someone's backyard and we were happy we didn't pay entrance fee for it.
This is the Sultan's weekender from previous centuries.  A guide is available with entry ticket.  There is an art shop which has some great batik art works. Negotiate hard!!
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
チケット売り場でチケットを購入したらすぐ目の前に宮殿があります。
中にはいるとすぐにプールが。思った以上に水が汚くてうわー…と思ってしまいました。
見どころはココのみと言って良いかと思います。すぐに見終わります。
昔は綺麗な宮殿だったのかもしれませんが、とにかく水が汚くて台無しです。
地下井戸があると地球の歩き方に書いていたので探したんですが、井戸に行く道を見つけられず、結構宮殿周辺をウロチョロしたんですが、最後まで見つけられず断念してしまいました。

Enter this enchanted but run down place by paying small fee at the front. My advice, get a guide. They don't charge u anything but they tell you stories and histories as you stroll and discovering the area. They'll bring u to areas, passage and places that you'd never expected. Mind u, it's a long walk inside once you explore. The mosque inside also worth a visit. Don't forget to tip the guide tho'.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Tempat wisata yang baik,untuk mengenal sejarah dan atau mengetahui lebih detail tentang fasilitas kraton Jogja ,kebersihan cukup bagus ,tetap terus di jaga dan di tingkatkan ,perawatan bangunan beserta tanaman perlu selalu di perhatikan ,salut dan apresiasi ,maju terus

È un luogo molto suggestivo ma poco curato! 
Le stanze de sultano sono ancora intrise di umidità e non sono mai state ristrutturate!

it's better you be here with a local guide, who will tell you something about the story, adding spices to the site
i like the colour and the romantic atmosphere here
Le water palace est très petit mal entrenue et surtout commercial attention aux arnaque de bakit et marionnettes. Mais pour 1euro c'est pas non plus la mer à boire.

チケットを買って入り口で人数を聞かれ、複数だと分かると勝手にガイドされる。
説明は良かったが、途中、切り絵の工房に立ち寄ろうとするし、最後にガイド料金を請求された。
切り絵の工房に寄っていたら、商品を売付けられていただろう。
時間が無いことを告げて、とにかく断った。
遺跡としては、昔の王が女性を観察していたことがよくわかる施設だった。

If you are arriving in Yogja and need to acclimatize a day, then the Water Castle is an OK way to spend a little time. We probably would have appreciated it more with and English Speaking local guide, but the ones we talked to had poor English.

Slightly disappointing but still worth the visit, its not as grande and little explanation. Try to avoid 'walking tour guide' -you think its free but they charge you unnecessarily although there's an entrance fee. Overall its ok, but not something you would go out of your way to see.
Wenig erwartet, wenig gesehen. Heruntergekommene Anlage...ziemlich dreckig...15min reichen um alles zu besichtigen...

Nous nous réjouissions de visiter ce lieux.. Très joli endroit en photo .. en vrai, nous avons été un peu déçu .. entretien du lieu moyen .. 
nos recherches sur le web étaient plus vendeuse que l'image réelle ..
À conseiller toute fois ..

Don't expect a large castle with a lot of fountains and fancy guards or something. You can have a little idea how it must have been in the years of the sultan. Now the glance is fading away. But it is still a cheap place to visit and worth a look!

Omdat deze locatie in bijna alle stadsrondleidingen zit zijn wij er ook naar toe geweest. Had er iets meer van verwacht en kan zeker op enkele plaatsen wat onderhoud gebruiken. Gebruik zeker een gids om toch iets van de historie op te steken.
Helaas is het water castle niet goed onderhouden. Het is erg vervallen. Er zit een klein dorpje bij, leuk om te zien.

If you like taking picture of an old place with historical story, Taman Sari is one of it, not much to see actually, hopefully the local government restoring this location, so it can be more to be an interesting place to visit by tourist.

A visita foi diferente: estávamos indo a pé e nos perdemos na ocupação que está ao redor do local. As ruas pequenas dão várias voltas, não há um caminho reto a seguir. Como ficou tarde, perdemos a hora para entrar no local. No entanto, um morador nos ajudou a vê-lo de cima através de uma pequena entrada por trás. Ele também nos levou para outros lugares que foram cozinha, sauna e outros espaços do antigo castelo, todos em meio a ocupação hoje em dia. Foi muito bacana!

Old-aged royal watercastle. If you want to see some vinatages, not the new ones, this place is a great place for it. My first impression was the old ponds, and I thought that these ponds were the main attractions. But, after I walked some metres, I found underground tunnels that were crowded by people, then I knew what the really journey was these tunnels.
Petit temple avec bassin d'eau pas du tt nettoyé. Eau pas du tt propre. Beaucoup de shop et de rabatteurs. Décevant

It's a nice place to visit if you are in the area. Better to go in the morning or late afternoon course it can get really hot during the day. It can be quite crowdy and hiring a local guide is a clever idea if you want to know a bit more details about the place wich I'm sorry we didn't do. Best way to move around Kraton area is to hire a Pejak, there are many around and are very cheap just remember to bargain for the price. And smile off course. We moved just about anywhere for about 10.000 IDR.   The best were underground tunnels.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
Every Yogyan knows this place is one of the best location for photo session, so one of our prewedding photo session held in here.
It was nice actually; every corner can become a good angle. But we came at the wrong hour. The place crammed with so many people; at least there were three couples holding their prewedding session there. Best time to be here: before 10.00. Bring much drinking water, and mini-fan. In some place I felt a little nausea :(

Place was fairly maintained, they let the tour guides everywhere to source for their own customers and can be seems like "insisting" you to take them with you. It is just sort of "swimming pool" in a huge bungalow.

Didn't plan on visiting but the Kraton Palace was closed for 2 days so I went walking and found myself in the midst of it. 
Interesting snapshot of the past.
Photographically fascinating, lots of subject matter both in ruined architecture and people watching.
I somehow missed the underground mosque!
I'd recommend it if you had several days in Jogja.
Most favorite place in Jogja I think.  Architecture is lovely and colors are great. You also get a guide inside and amount of donation is up to you

Dahulu tempat ini memang Water Castle. Tapi dengan berjalan waktu dan pemerintahan kerajaan, tempat beralih fungsi dan sekarang menjadi sebuah tempat wisata yang sayang jika anda lewatkan.

Begitu masuk dari pintu depan, anda bisa langsung menuju loket tiket di sebelah kanan. Local guide? Yes, anda butuh local guide, supaya anda tidak bingung dan memiliki kesan biasa saja dengan Taman Sari ini. Local guide akan dengan senang hati menghantarkan anda dan menuturkan banyak hal yang berhubungan dengan Taman Sari. Mulai dari bagaimana tempat ini ada sampai kepada beberapa simbol yang kerap kita lihat di setiap bangunan bersejarah. 

Taman Sari hanya terdiri dari area depan, area tengah dan area belakang. Tapi kalau anda minta ditemani oleh local guide, saya yakin anda akan terkesan dengan Taman Sari. 

Waktu yang tepat untuk datang ke Taman Sari adalah pagi hari menjelang siang.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
The place was mostly in a bad shape. The pools didn't look like they had been cleaned in a long while. The rooms were in a sad state with lots of modern 'artwork' on the walls. Broken stairs, empty rooms. 

The interesting history. .. dunno if the story is true but apparently this was the place where the sultan chose the lady for the night while they had their fun n frolic in the pools. Three pools one each for the family, the ladies and the sultan n chosen one. 

The kitchen was just a collection of rooms, so also the so called library. The bedroom had a huge concrete bed with a headboard. The rooms below for meditation were interesting but unfortunately or baby had had enough by then so we couldn't explore them much. The tunnel that apparently lead to the sea but had now been closed since those that went in never came out again added a later of mystery.

My best experience the red berries on the bushy plant at the entrance make a lovely natural, if temporary, sheer nail varnish.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Must visit place in Yogyakarta moreover the underground mosque. You have to take picture in that mosque! Amazing view!
Guide is a must as one can learn more about the history and stories. Be prepared to do a lot of walking.
仕事の合間に訪問。朝いちばんだったのでゆっくりと散策できた。園内すべて地元のガイドのおっちゃんに案内してもらった。なにやら昔の王様の第二夫人の別荘とか。もっときれいに整備されていればと思った。
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: buka pada jam 9 dan sekitar tempat wisata ini menyatu dengan rumah penduduk. setiap menyusuri sudutnya bangunan nya sebagian terawat sebagian lagi ada yang berubah fungsi seperti waktu itu didalam bangunan ada motor yang sedang diparkir, saat saya sudah mengitari taman sari saat saya mau kembali ke bangunan depan (karna belum puas) malah tidak boleh sama guide nya harus keluar dahulu dan masuk seperti awal membeli tiket kembali dengan nada tinggi. dan yang paling saya suka disekitar taman sari adalah ada masjid yang terawat bersih. saya suka dengan hal yang berbau sejarah.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Tamansari Yogya msh menawan utk dikunjungi...saya meditasi sebentar dipojok utaranya sebelum secangkir kuhirup pelan...RUMAH TUA ITU JADI PANCURAN AIRNYA JERNIH LEBUR DIRASA...meneduhkan begitulah tinggalan cagar budaya ini menyapaku...

Tamansari adalah tempat pemandian para raja dan selir pada zaman kerajaan mataram dahulu. Kini tempat ini dijadikan tempat wisata untuk umum. Bagi wisatawan bisa masuk dan berjalan kaki menyusuri setiap tempat yang ada. Ada juga bangunan yg rubuh gara gara kejadian gempa yang terjadi di jogja pada tahun 2006 lalu. Kemudian ada juga lorong bawah tanah yang di bangun pada masa penjahahan belanda. Dan di tempat itu dahulu di gunakan untuk bertapa. Dengan segala sejarah dan peninggalannya kita bisa belajar / mengetahui sisa sisa kerjaan yang masih berjalan hingga kini.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Ce lieu extraordinaire rempli de sérénité et laisse aller à la  méditation.  Il faut se laisser porter par la sérénité des lieux.

Try to come here in the morning to avoid the crowd of tourist. It will give you a chance to take some great pictures. There a lot of tour guide in there. If you don't really need their help, just tell it straight up front whenever they try to give you a guidance.

Halo jumpa lagi di Yogyakarta. Buat kalian yg mau liburan atau cari view buat foto-foto. Waktu itu saya masuk lewat belakang, jadi lewat rumah2 warga gitu. Ga tau asal ngikut jalan sama GPS aja (Gunakan Penduduk Setempat)

This place is located at the back of the Sultan Palace in Yogyakarta. It was the private pool of the queen and the princess. There are seperate rooms at the top from where the kings used to rest and also keep an eye on the queen. Visit this place and try to visit with a guide who can explain more details of the place. Truly amazing.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: ходили по городу и зашли в водный дворец, перед входом можно выпить кокос и сходить в туалет, внутри не особо интересно, но можно сходить от нечего делать
Very interesting place to visit, you can hired a private English guide for water castle,he will bring you around to explore the place
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Hatte ich mir viel größer und besser erhalten vorgestellt. Ticketschalter schliesst bereits um 15h. Es war nur noch  ein Becken mit Wasser gefüllt, die unterirdische Moschee war ganz interessant.
I took a becak ( a carriage driven by man) from Keraton ( The King  Palace) to Taman Sari.  It was so fun to enjoy the eco friendly ride though.

Wisata air ini buka jam 9 pagi.
Tempatnya hampir menyatu dengan perumahan warga, dan banyak juga rumah warga yg menjual baju batik dsb, dgn kualitas yg bagus dan harga miring. mungkin agak bingung kalau jalan sendirian.
Tempatnya bagus untuk spot foto.
Tidak dianjurkan datang kesini pada siang hari,krna akan sangat panas.
Tp untuk keseluruhannya bagus
Another site worth visiting around the Kraton Palace. The walk from the actual palace to the Water Castle is a must.
Amazing historic architecture perfect for explore and photo. Great discovery and history study. Was amazed with the ancient creativity.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
A me è piaciuto, sia il palazzo che l'ho trovato un posto incantato, sia il "perdersi", lasciarsi guidare dalle viuzze intorno.. abbiamo parlato con diverse persone, bambini e anziani, tutti sorridenti e incuriositi dagli europei. 
Mi viene da sorridere perché sinceramente non l'ho trovato tenuto male come ho letto in diversi commenti; e poi non bisogna dimenticarsi che siamo in Asia.... È normale!!

Pros:
1. Nice and friendly tour guides with various of language talents
2. Nice heritage from the bathroom till the admin office for the previous sultans
3. Good for pre wedding or special photoshot

Cons:
1. Need to give a sign or introduction's board on each side for explanation as well
2. Need to give a map brochure for tourists

Overall: you can try this for selfie lovers
Sembari menikmati pariwisata sejarah dari kerajaan kerajaan mataram kuno. Tempat pariwisata yang berada di tengah kota cukup terjangkau..

This place has an interesting story of how the Sultan will look for his wives or consorts via a tower which overlooks the bathing pools. During the war, the underground passage ways were used for the royal family. There is also an underground mosque.
tamannya msh terawat dengan bagus...dan langsung bisa membayangkan kehidupan dalam istana jaman dulu

昔の王様が，女性をプールで泳がせ，それを上から眺めて，その日の夜のお供を選ぶという，男性にとっては，夢のような楽園なのではないでしょうか。
今は使われていないので，プールは綺麗ではありませんが，
昔の風景を思い出すと，優雅だったんだろうなと，思いを馳せることが出来ます。

Si estás en Yogyakarta y te sobra tiempo pues sí, la entrada es barata, pero es una visita de 10 minutos alargandolo mucho... No te esperes mucho para ver, se queda bastante corto, pero al fin y al cabo curioso de ver!

This place is not maintained, ugly, old so called palace with three swimming pools filled with dirt and mold. 

Upon arrival a "friendly" guide will immediately start to talk with you, making difdicult for you to decline his assistance. At the end of course you will be visiting a batik gallery. 

Of course you are being told that this batik here is better ualuty but cheaper than somewhere else because this is direct selling from artists and not like in other shops.

We didnt buy anything but we ended up not seeing the tunnel and a mosque because of the "guide" who we eventually even pay 50000 rupiah!

Dont bother go there and support those greedy people trying to get money out of you for things you didnt come to buy!

E' uno dei posti che di solito le guide di Yogja portano a visitare. Complesso di piscine utilizzate in passato dal sultano. Non è un posto imperdibile, ma la visita offre l'occasione per scattare qualche bella foto.
Assez décevant dans l’ensemble. Ce "castle" est petit et dépourvu d'explication et d'entretien. nous nous attendions à mieux

Er lopen vele gidsen rond die je voor een fooi na afloop willen rondleiden. Doe dit vooral, want anders is het niet echt duidelijk wat hier te doen is en waarom. Onze gids was een enthousiaste vent die ons maar wat graag van alles liet zien en erg veel informatie gaf, dat maakt het allemaal wel wat leuker.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Local guides tend to "omit" to show the mosque within Tamansari. For me that's one of the highlights. The access to the mosque is solely underground. From what I understand the mosque was surrounded by water before an eruption of Gunung (Mount) Merapi destroyed the grounds. Some of it's firmer splendour has been restored as a tourist attraction and gives you an idea about the incredible wealth and power of the Sultans of Yogya a few hundred years ago when most if the common people lived in abject poverty.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
Quite unusual place to visit. Make sure you get a local guide, they will tell you stories from the past, some of the will awe you.

Also don't skip underground mosque and Cyber village
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Terawat dan rapi. Banyak sejarah yang dapat dipelajari di sini. Bagus juga untuk foto-foto, khususnya pre-wedding.

Penasaran niyh sama tempat yg satu ini spot fotonya unik2. Terutama di tangga2 bawah tanah Sumur Gemuling. 
Mesti sama guide nih kalo kesini jadi kita tau cerita sejarahnya. Dan ternyata istana ini luas lhooo jadi siapin kaki untuk jalan jauh dan naik turun.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
Hal pertama yang membuat saya kecewa adalah petugas di loket masuk. Disitu tertera harga tiket masuk wisatawan domestik IDR5000, kebetulan saya datang bertiga. Saya membayar dengan uang cash IDR16000, si petugas tanpa rasa bersalah dan tanpa basa basi tidak memberikan uang kembalian maupun ucapan terimakasih.
Menurut saya ini bukan perkara uang seribu akan tetapi budaya korupsi dan keramahtamahan si petugas dalam menyambut pengunjung yang datang.
Bayangkan saja bila banyak orang yang bernasib seperti saya, dari uang kembalian yang sengaja tidak diberikan si petugas itu akan mendapatkan keuntungan sendiri.
Sedangkan si petugas tersebut tidak bekerja dengan baik dan ramah.
Saya rasa semua turis domestik maupun mancanegara tak akan segan memberikan uang tips apabila pelayanan yang didapatkan bagus.
Sangat disayangkan banyak terdapat vandalisme dibeberapa lokasi Taman Sari. Seharusnya hal tersebut bisa segera diatasi karena vandalisme merusak keindahan situs bersejarah tersebut.

Visiting this place was a last minute decision as we happened to be nearby and hence we did not really read up about it prior to the visit.  We were dropped off by our becak driver at the motorcycle parking entrance.  Before we could even get our bearings, this guy (tout) approached us and started to be really friendly.  Immediately we knew the guy was trying to be our ‘guide’ and would expect a tip in the end.  Throughout our trip we did not use any guides preferring to explore on our own and this would be no exception.  We could not see a ticket counter from where we were (all ticket counters in the tourist attractions in Yogyakarta will have the sign ‘Loket’).  However, there was a makeshift signboard that said ‘Tamansari’ with an arrow pointing towards the right side of the area.  Our becak driver said that’s the way to go and so we did.  

The path was exceptionally quiet with no other tourist in sight (this path happened to be one of the many alternative routes into Tamansari).  All this time, the tout kept trying to be friendly with us.  As we did not want to be rude, we answered some of his questions about where we were from, etc. and told him that we were okay to be on our own but he still persisted to walk with us.  We finally came to an area where we could either walk straight ahead (the path that leads to the main entrance where the ticket counter was) or go down a flight of steps into a dark tunnel.  At the entrance of the tunnel was a man with a ticket clipper who told us that to get to the ticket counter, we had to walk the path straight ahead.  The tout said that we could go through the tunnel and that as long as we’re with him, we did not need any tickets!  We were already annoyed by his persistence and told him firmly but politely that we could manage on our own.  As we walked away from the tunnel, the tout who was clearly angry that we refused his so called help started calling us names for not listening to him; all the while claiming that he was just being helpful.  We ignored him and walked off. 

While finding our way to the ticket counter, another guy approached us (wearing a batik shirt) and asked us to follow him; we did not.  Perhaps he was an official guide, we do not know as we were already so skeptical after the incident with the tout.  After going through a maze of sorts, we finally found the ticket counter by the car park.  Once we bought the ticket, the guy in the batik shirt followed us again but we told him we were alright on our own and he went away.  We realize that we could actually explore some parts of the area even without having a ticket depending on which entrance you came in from.  There were no signage throughout the place but I guess that adds to the charm of discovering the place for yourself.  We would have enjoyed the place more had it not been for that awfully rude tout encounter.
Stukje heen gereden.vonden kleine royal bath toch wel stuk leuker.betaalde hier 35.000 kleine 20.000

I tried visiting this attraction two times while in Jogja, but my efforts went just in vain. I never heard any touristic attraction getting closed by 2:30 PM. And even if we could see people around, the management is not ready to get us in!!

Viele kleine Gänge entführen die Besucher in eine Welt voller kontrastreicher und charmanter Farben, die einen an die glorreiche Zeit von Sultan Hamengkubuwono I erinnern lässt, der einst hier seine Füße voller Entschlossenheit ins Wasser hielt. Der Eintrittspreis ist günstig, es gab einige Touristen.

Review Text:
I had managed my expectations after reading reviews online so what I saw when I got there was pretty much in line with my expectations.

The place is sadly lacking in upkeep, however, with some imagination, you can see how it would have been a beautiful place to relax and spend leisure time.

The sultan's room at the top of the tower is wonderfully breezy, don't be daunted by the somewhat minuscule and steep steps on the stairs.

Our guide was not very good and did not take us to the circular mosque. Good thing I read about it and asked him, he at least pointed us in the right direction.

I'll try to describe how to get there but hopefully your guide will be better in leading you to it.

Facing the entrance from the parking lot (before you go into the front yard where you buy tickets) there should be a doorway to the right. Go through that and walk through the alleyway, then turn right at the end. Once the alley widens, there should be a door on your left that leads underground. Follow it and up the other end, back to ground level. Proceed forwards a few meters and you should see a small dirt road/alley on the right side (there will probably be a lot of people milling around). Follow this small path and you should encounter a few steps that lead to another doorway to the underground. The guard will punch your tickets again. This second underground path will lead you to the circular mosque and its 4-way staircase.

All in all, not a bad place to spend maybe an hour or so.
We've been here for a vacation and it's awesome place. Water palace for the king. If you want to have better explanation and rooms to explore, you better ask guide to join with you.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:

Qui il sultano vedeva da una torre le sue mogli, circa 50 se non ricordo male, farsi il bagno nella piscina grande, ne sceglieva una e la portava nella torre dove c'era una sauna e sul lato dietro una piscina piccola.
Particolare anche i tunnel sotterranei che sbucano nella famosa scala a tre vie con pianerottolo e scala unica di salita. Difficile farsi una foto da soli, prendendo spunto dai vari fotografi di top-model anche molti turisti amano farsi fotografare sul pianerottolo e aspettare il proprio turno è stressante.

Review Text: La ciudad de Yogya, tiene poco que ver la verdad. Esto es alguna de las cosas, pero no merece mucho la pena. Esta mal conservado. Solo merece la pena, si vas al Kraton, ya que esta al lado y aprovechas el paseo por Yogyakarta.

Bekas Pemandian raja-raja keraton Jogja ini masih menyisakan bangunan yang mempesona. Taman indah yang terletak di tengah-tengah danau pada masa lalu masih menyimpan banyak misteri yang perlu diwujudkan. Semoga keindahan dan keajaibannya masih kita saksikan pada masa kini.

Maybe due to old age, it seems ancient. But the guide (who keeps following us even though we didn't ask) told us it was still used at least on 20 century. This was the place when Sultan can watch his concubines took open air bath, and he can pick his favorite by throwing flower from top tower. Then the chosen one will be taken to different pool to have private bath session with Sultan, and then to spa chamber and you can imagine the rest.
The guide took us to artist who drew tapestry in frame. Not exactly cheap, but he painted in wide selection.

It's actually walking distance from kraton, if you don't mind 2 km. I decided to go back with becak, and you can ask him to go to traditional snack shops.

if you visit tamansari, i think it's better to use a guide so you can get a full history about this place. You can know what this room use for and any others. Because if you walk without guide, you will confused and didn't get any value.
good for short visit. nice. entrance fee for locals is Rp.2000 but that for foreigners is Rp.10000, not expensive though.

Got to see the old water castle of Sultan in Yogyakarta. A relaxing place. You can still see the structure and the swimming, sultan's room

One of the many heritage site you can find in Yogyakarta. This place is where the Queen and concubines took their bath during the Imperial period. Has beeen renovated after the earthquake, but you'll be surprised to see how ancient people did not use modern tools like we do but able to build something much stronger. A lot of lesson to be learnt.

Bueno, el castillo del agua está bien, es bonito, pero yo por lo menos no pude disfrutarlo. El problema fué que cuando nosotros llegamos el castillo estaba cerrado, pero nosotros no lo sabíamos. Entonces un hombre nos dijo que de donde éramos y que nos acompañaba a la entrada, total, que como nosotros no sabíamos ni cómo había que entrar ni como era la entrada fuimos con él. Nos empezó a llevar por calles y callecillas, pasando delante de casas muy raras...y vecinos que nos miraban un poco raro. No nos pasó nada pero cuando ya te das cuenta de que el hombre se ha convertido automáticamente en tu guía y que te ha metido por calles raras...pues a ver quien es el que le dice que no te interesa su servicio de guía y que no le vas a dar ni una rupia...y esa situación..ya te hace estar incómoda y no disfrutar de la visita. Sí es cierto que al final no pasó nada, que el hombre nos guió bien y que incluso nos metió a través de atajos de gratis al castillo (aunque nosotros pagamos religiosamente una vez que salimos del castillo!!), y se conformó con 20000 rupias pero estos trapicheos a mi por lo menos no me hacen disfrutar de la visita.

Its an easy walk from the sultan palace provided you have cover for sun or take a bechak, one of the cycle rickshaws. The castle itself is poorly maintained with virtually no signage in English and this was one of the disappointing parts of my jogja trip

The gates open into two octagonal courtyards which lead into bathing complex which has 2 buildings on the sides of the pool.After visiting the bathing complex,take the  bylane and visit the underground mosque.Nice place to  visit but nothing in comparison to sultan's palace.
