You won't be disappointed by taking a slow stroll in labyrinth of lanes plus unique looking houses surrounding the castle. 
Some photographs features Facebook founder's visit to the area were proudly displayed.

Quizás dar un tres es quedarme corto pero un cuatro de cinco me parece algo excesivo.
Al sitio nos costó llegar, lo cual no facilita las cosas porque estás rodeado de ggente que quiere ayudarte...cuando tu solo quieres 3 minutos para mirar la guía.
Una ve dentro de lo q era una plaza, un hombre local nos indicó primero por donde ir nos acompañó después (por sitios rarillos) y finalmente se convirtió en nuestro guía particular.
Hay que decir que sin él no habríamos encontrado el lugar por lo que, además de darle la propina que buscaba, le estamos mi y agradecidos.
El sitio es sí diría que es normal comparado con otras cosas de otro a países pero tiene su encanto. No es de los sitios q hay que ver sí o sí en una ciudad... Pero es que en esta ciudad hay poco que ver, por lo que si se puede hay que intentar hacer una visita al menos :)

Gironzolando per Yogyakarta potete effettuare una breve visita in questo "palazzo" comprendente tre vasche e qualche edificio purtroppo mal tenuto. Serve un bel po' di fantasia per figurarselo come "luogo di delizie per il sultano e le sue concubine". Tuttavia è possibile scattare qualche bella fotografia ai particolari. Costo del biglietto 12.000 rp.

Abbiamo visitato questo castello perché compreso nel tour che avevamo organizzato con indoparadiso! 
Il luogo è veramente spoglio tenuto malissimo. 
Se ne n avete nulla da fare una scappata ce la potete anche fare!

เป็นสถานที่เที่ยวขนาดไม่ใหญ่มาก ใช้เวลาไม่นาน  ภายในตรงบริเวณสระน้ำไม่ได้สวยอย่างในรูปเนื่องจากตอนที่ไปมีน้ำน้อยมาก เดินอ้อมไปด้านหลังจะเป็นชุมชน มีขนมคล้ายขนมเบื้องแต่แป้งบางกว่าข้างในใส่กล้วยมะพร้าวและน้ำตาล เป็นของกินที่ควรจะลองเมื่อไปถึง
La verdad es que nos esperamos algo mas del recinto, hay que visitarlo pero si no tienes tiempo suficiente puedes prescindir de el para ver otros lugares de Yogyakarta.
Sarebbe anche carino se non fosse per la trascuratezza, che lo fa sembrare una villa abbandonats da una decina di anni.

歩いて行ったのですが場所が分かりにくくて迷ってしまい何とかたどり着くと入口には観光客を取り合うようにガイドが多数…
綺麗な建物ですがはられていた水は緑でここで水浴び？？と思うような水質でした。
声をかけてきたガイドの一人はまだ学生で日本語はかなり初級だったので日本語を教えてあげる立場になりました。
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: La visite est intéressante, les bassins sont colorés et méritent d être vus. A ne pas manquer si vous vous trouvez ds les alentours.

The Keraton Palace is not that grand (or what's left of it). However the Water Castle, even though a bit sparse, gives a different tempo to all that visiting. The greenish pools of water with the observing tower stands unique amongst the others.

Inside one of the compounds, there's a small art gallery. A wayang kulit artisan hammers on a dried cow skin to make a new wayang kulit character. He asks for money if you want to take his photograph.

Nearby is the Sumur Gumuling, the said underground mosque. Just ask the locals and they will direct you there. Another unique place to visit besides Tamansari. Don't miss it!
Faktor Penarik: Ketertarikan Budaya, Ketertarikan Fasilitas, Ketertarikan Suasana
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Tempat pemandian peninggalan raja keraton ini terbilang cukup terawat, tapi bila saja lokasi di sekitarnya dibuat msh spt asal sejarahnya mungkin akan terlihat lbh megah dan menarik.

Nos dejamos guiar por un local,al principio con un poco de desconfianza sobre que querria,pero al final lo descubrimos,te guian todo el camino para que al final vayas a su tienda de arte y compres un cuadro (no te obligan,solo si alguno te gusta y encaja el precio). En nuestro caso acabamoa comprando uno q nos gusto mucho por unos 40eur (ya lo habiamos visto por 80eur en otra tienda).
La visita muy bien te llevaban por calles q ni se te ocurriria y te suben a un muro desde donde se ven las piscinas del sultan.
Nuestro consejo dejaros guiar y regatear con el cuadro si os gusta.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: In je rondje rondom Kraton is het makkelijk mee te pakken en voor de euro entree hoef je het ook niet te laten. Het aangelegde ondergrondse gangenstelsel is indrukwekkend!
El lugar es bonito pero creo excesivo el precio que cobran por entrar. Todavía hay mucho a reconstruir alrededor pero las "piscinas" son muy bonitas.
Tersedia penghantar di dalam. Lokasi pusat kota dan melihat kolam dan jalan ke jalan rahasia sultan dulu, daerah pemukiman warga.

Tempat ini dekat dengan pusat Kota, bisa naik becak dari Malioboro hanya membayar Rp. 5.000,- kita bisa melihat tempat permandian istri dan putri raja. Di tempat ini juga terdapat mesjid bawah tanah. Tersedia pemandu lokal yang akan menerangkan sejarah tempat ini (biaya sukarela)
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: One of the places you'd go to if you had nothing else to do. One of the caretakers can take you around.
Visite des bains du sultan. Intéressante avec un guide mais la visite reste très courte. Vente de batik pas loin du site.

The name sounds better than the place actually is. It's a relatively small complex of courtyards (with pools), underground passages and a few rooms. It is poorly maintained, some walls are suffering from damp and it is not very clear (poor curatorial discipline) which parts are restored/re-created and which parts are original. The water in the pools are green with slime. The water lilies look sick.

Okay, so the place has historical relevance and should give an insight into the lifestyles of the court during a certain period, but there are no -- absolutely none -- plaques providing explanation as a museum should. I guess if they did so, they would undercut the income stream of the unofficial touts who claim to be guides. 

Nonetheless, a short visit is instructional, not about Yogyakarta's history, but about how NOT to run an historical/archeological site!

Went back from my trip last night.  It was a great visit to Taman sari with a guide.  Artistic village.  Great structure. We went before the opening hour so we went in with a guide from side entrance and pay ticket on our way out. Can see the 1&2 sultan really enjoying their life with pools sauna , dance and spiritual prayer.
Faktor Penarik: Ketertarikan Budaya, Ketertarikan Fasilitas, Ketertarikan Suasana
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: You could get wrong when you see nothing from entrance because the water castle will found in the hidden secret place. It is located about 2 km south within the grounds of the Kraton Yogyakarta. You can come at 9 am till 3 pm. The place is fascinating and has secret tunnels. I hope to find treasure inside the tunnels :) and don't forget the go to other tunnel that a hidden mosque waiting for you. Worth to visit.

Stedet har en flot historie, og man kan godt fornemme, at det engang har været 'a big thing', men så er der heller ikke mere i det.

Stedet er meget nedslidt, og det er lidt en skam, at man ikke har brugt tid på holde det ved lige

Det kostede omkring 20.000rp at komme ind for to personer, så det ruinerer ikke nogen, men er man på en stram tidsplan, kan man med god samvittighed springe det over.

又是一個必到的景點，但沒有什麽特色。 就是簡單的幾個水池當年由日惹王建找尋歡的地方，讓人忍不住想起酒林肉池的畫面==。拍拍了幾張照片就離開了。和朋友去了地下室，因爲功課做不住，找了又找，問了當地人，講了講就說可以帶我們去但要付他錢，本來5万卢比說收我們兩人4万卢比。結果只是在從旁邊繞過幾戶人家的家就到了- -嗚嗚， 感覺有一點被騙。
個人覺得這裡十分特別比起水宮。5個階梯不同角度有不同的景象比較有可看性。在那裏還遇見拍結婚照的夫妻。 
那位帶領我們的人，有簡單的介紹~到外面之後經過非常多小巷，他指著不遠處一棟廢墟說2006年有一次地震當天就是200多人。霎那覺得人的渺小與無常。 總結，可以到水工看看，也試著找找這藏起來的地下室吧
就在苏丹王宫附近，很方便前往，门票也很便宜，只要人民币两三块钱。我们是自助游，所以时间宽裕，可以到处走走，时间紧的话不看也无所谓。

Ко всем выссказываниям могу добавить лишь свое восхищение системой кондиционирования в спальне у султана. Спальня как бы находиться на заднем дворе с кухней,  с как бы холодильником и "шкафами купе ". Кондиционер в спальне султана представляет собой систему водных каналов, в том числе под циновками на которых он возлегал. За окном спальни была сделана специальная система где вода, ударяясь в перегородки превращалась в водную взвесь, тем самым осуществляя кондиционирование. Я такого еще не видел ни где. Про гидов все верно, нам попался не плохой, даже после покупки в его магазинчике он продолжал рассказывать и лазить по деревьям за различными плодами. Нам понравилось.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Il Tamansari merita una visita dopo essere passati dal Kraton. Per quello che può offrire Yogyakarta, si può perdere un'oretta tra questo sito, il dedalo di vie circostanti e la moschea sotterranea. Noi abbiamo trovato un aiuto in una "guida" locale che per poco più di 3€ ci ha accompagnato nella visita.
When i saw this place, this place good to take a picture for pra wedding. Full of art, unique. If you like culture of jogja, you have to come here. Feel excited!!!
It's under construction during my visit, hence there's nothing there. I like the cafe nearby though.

We had a luck to visit the place in the morning so without crowds. It was a lovely, relaxing walk through this complex of pavilions and pools. It's a real pity that this place is not very well maintained.

After renovation, the bathing complex looks fabulous. I could imagine on King and Queen take and enjoy a bath there. The surrounding complex is nice too, you could feel Javanese culture by taking strolls within the complex.
Faktor Penarik: Ketertarikan Budaya, Ketertarikan Fasilitas, Ketertarikan Suasana

Review Text: The water castle consists out of 2 water pools. Sadly there was almost no water in it and the water in the pools was not that clean. It'd okay to visit this place. Don't expect to much...

very vast field and many kinds of underground vault that lots ladies were accommodated for king from time to time. If you well learned about the former Indonesia and the Dynasty before visiting here, you could think of what happened here. To clarify avoidance of misunderstand, the Dynasty never treat ladies in slavery, but they were treated like a hostess according to my guide man.

Het waterpaleis is leuk om te bezoeken, al ben je er snel uitgekeken. Het is leuk om het te combineren met de ondergrondse moskee. En de wijk is leuk door de kleine straatjes en wat leuke eettentjes.
Het is een hele uitdaging om aan de gidsen te ontkomen.

After being disappointed with the sultan palace, we went to see the water castle. It is much nicer, the water pools are quite green, as they should clean the water more often. However, we have really enjoyed it there and would recommend it.
Beautiful place. The uncles who sit at the enterance will follow you and be your tour guide, just gv them some decent tips (idr 20k or so)..they will be happy already.

Istana Air Taman Sari.

Akses:
akses kendaraan umum cukup sulit, lebih baik sewa taksi atau menggunakan mobil menuju lokasi ini. Lokasi terletak di tengah kota. Petunjuk jalan cukup mudah, lokasi parkir terbatas, mungkin di hari libur bisa ramai dan peuh tempta parkirnya. b

Jam Buka:
Taman Sari buka hanya sampai jam 3 sore, setelah jam 3 sore loket karcis tutup dan pengunjung akan diantar oleh pemandu lewat pintu belakang (tempat keluar), sehingga kurang nyaman. Usahakan datang sebelum jam 3 sore.
Harga karcis Rp 5.000/orang

Atraksi:
TamanSari adalah tempat pemandian selir & putra-putri Raja pada masa pemerintahan HB I-III. Sayangnya, keadaannya kurang terawat dan banyak coretan dimana-mana. dinding pun terlihat kurang perawatan.

Perhatian:
Untuk pengguna kursi roda, sangat tidak disarankan karena fasilitasnya tidak mendukung. Untuk lanjut usia & anak kecil, tanggal menuju kolam pemandian cukup tinggi tanpa ada pegangan tangan di sisi kanan & kiri.

Pemandu tersedia di pintu depan & biayanya sukarela.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Tempat pemandian dekat kraton Jogja, dulu dipakai para selir, sekarang sudah tidak digunakan.. bila tahu jalan berikutnya akan ketemu masjid bawah tanah, dekat dengan tamansari

Non è una meraviglia imperdibile, a yogiakarta le mete obbligate sono Borodurum e Prambanam, ma se prima di partire per le escursioni ai vulcani volete fare un giretto esplorativo della città, noleggiate uno scooter (60000-70000 IDR ovvero 5-5,70 € e girate in lungo e largo non facendovi mancare il Kraton (perdibilissimo) e questa stranissima costruzione settecentesca fatte di vasche con le scalinate che scendono dentro l'acqua che serviva al sultano sel tempo per il suo tempo del piacere con le concubine. Non è uno stile architettonico che lascia senza fiato, ma la concezione è curiosa e tutto sommato armonica e quello che colpisce è una sorta di fusion tra lo stile europeo del tempo che definiremmo coloniale ed alcuni elementi, soprattutto decorativi, tipicamente autoctoni. Non è all'altezza il livello di conservazione e restauro.

Mooie overblijfselen van het waterpaleis. Loop vooral ook door de wijk Kraton waaraan dit grenst. Dit kan prima op eigen initiatief! Ga dan ook binnen in de ondergrondse moskee, even zoeken maar heel bijzonder!

menjelajah taman sari itu sambil membayangkan para putri raja dan permaisuri mandi, hehehe.. penataan nya menurutku luar biasa. desain kawasan yang unik dan berselera. khas. berwibawa pula. menyusuri lorongnya seolah perjalanan mendapatkan harta karun yang luar biasa. sesi foto outdoor akan menjadi istimewa disini. sayangnya saya ga berbakat fotografi. hiks.. keanggunan nya terpancar, bagaikan mengintip perawan. ah, sungguh eksotis

Unfortunately the main part was closed due to construction until December 2015. BUT the area is filled with amazing sights which are the best. We found a guide to show us around, or probably more like a local and not an in general tourist guide. 
Before we noticed the time flew by and 3 hours had gone by. We visited parts of the palace which belonged to the previous kings along with viewing the pool area for the king, the queen and all the concubines. We found an amazing guide which showed us a bamboo t shirt store, puppet store and he showed us his house and where he and his kids lived. The experience was amazing and is probably the highlight of the trip in general. 
A must see place!

Het ´waterkasteel´ is minder bekend dan het het in de buurt gelegen Sultan Palace, maar kent opmerkelijk meer historie. Hier hebben van 1625 tot en met 1889 de sultans 2 tot en met 6 en hun harems geleefd. Je vindt er talloze ondergrondse gangen, een ondergrondse moskee, diverse zwembaden en natuurlijk de slaapvertrekken. Het immense complex is in een erbarmelijke staat. In 2004 startte een grootschalig restauratieproject, maar de aardbeving in 2006 heeft alle werkzaamheden stop gezet.

Daarom oogt het allemaal minder, maar het heeft heel veel inzich. Neem een gids mee (wel vooraf een prijs afspreken) en laat je vertellen en ervaar hoe de sultans hier leefden op hun buitenverblijf?! Hoe de harems in het castle moeite deden om in favour te komen bij de sultan.

Het is te hopen dat de restauratie werkzaamheden snel hervatten want het is een in potentie prachtig stuk World Heritage met een rijke historie.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Found the place from a postcard sold in Kraton. When my friends and I saw the place, we lauhged! It happened to us that what we saw in the picture was different from what we were seeing. But the story of the place was quite interesting. It was the place where sultans came daily to choose a concubine to sleep with while concubines were bathing.

Dont waste time to visit, very run down. Beware of the those tour guide because is not free. They bring you to those private batik shop and ask you to buy. At the end they asked you for tips. The guide only spend less then 20mins with you.

This water castle is now only familiar because of its function as the pool of the old sultan, but has a rich history about the sultans palace which was standing in the same place. This place is much more interesting than the current castle, but only if you get a guide!

It was so-so.  Go only if you have time to kill.  This is one place that you can visit on your own without a guide.  So save some money and visit it on your own.  There are 2-3 separate buildings which are very small.  We visited it within 20 minutes. There is a batik art gallery.  Beware of the lady doing the batik.  She will ask you for money if you take pictures and she does not give any change back.  She is very dishonest.  Go to a proper batik factory if you wish to see how they do real batik.

The water castle is not so well maintained. Nothing spectacular about it. Upon your entrance, there will be a few local guides who will agree to take you. You would need to give them a small tip after the whole trip. But if you are in a tight schedule, you can afford to skip this place.
Na bezoek aan het Kraton is dit een leuke aanvulling. De wandeling door de kampong is zeker aan te bevelen. Verder ligt hier een mooi stukje historie en nastolgie.

This complex is situated not far from the Kraton, or palace of the Sultan. Its a bath house used by the Sultan and his family/concubines. I suppose for the period, it was something spectacular. I can imagine it being an oasis of tranquility. The bath house isnt well maintained and it isnt in use as a bath house. So dont expect pristine waters etc. See it as a part of history and you will appeciate it as such. 
In the vicinity of the Water Castle are nice and quaint shops selling batik. I think this whole area is the boutique batik centre for the city.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Really retry, very different to where I've been before. Only one real main bath to really capture however can get amazing pictures and locals are so friendly.
크라톤 부근에 있어요. 크라톤보다는 볼 만하고요. 자그만한 풀장이 몇 개 있는데 왕이 수영장에서 노는 후궁들 보고 윗층 방에서 꽃을 던져서 그 후궁이랑 밤을 보냈다네요. 수영장이랑 그걸 둘러싸고 있는 간소한 방들을 볼 수 있어요. 고즈넉한게 족자 시내에서 가볍게 구경갈 만 합니다.
La piscine du sultan ... C'est à voir et à mon avis bien mieux que le palais du sultan. Promenez vous ensuite dans les ruelles alentours.

Lugar de ocio del sultan,donde podemos ver tres piscinas,una de ellas era la privada para la mujer elegida.Debajo de todo esto podemos disfrutar de unos tuneles subterraneos.El lugar me parecio interesante.Tambien llamado Castillo del Agua.Se encuentra cerca del Kraton.El horario es hasta las 2 de la tarde.La entrada cuesta 12.000 rupias

Si trova a pochi passi dal Kraton, questo complesso formato da piscine, palazzi e canali era un tempo la dimora del "piacere" del sultano e della sua corte. Per evitare che l'architetto che progetto' il Taman Sari potesse rivelare l'ubicazione delle sale del piacere, fu giustiziato dal sultano. Se non fosse così poco curato, sarebbe ancor oggi un bellissimo complesso. La cosa simpatica e' affacciarsi dalle varie finestre ( dove il sultano spiava le donne che facevano il bagno nelle piscine,  che poi sceglieva come concubine). Anche per entrare qui bisogna pagare il biglietto.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
勝手にガイドを始めようとするおじさんがいます。
水はあまりキレイではなかったのが残念。
でもいい雰囲気の場所なので、現地のモデルが撮影をしていたり、カップルが座って景色を眺めていました。

This would have been a nice place to visit if it wasn't for all the rubbish around the area.. The place could've been better maintained and cleaned seeing how it's quite popular. Pictures look better than in person for sure. Cheap entry fee but seeing how we spent such little time in it, not sure if it's worth the money at all.
The pool doesn't well maintain. It does not as expected in my imagine as the pool doesn't well preserved. the paint is exfoliate. there are mildew everywhere

El sitio tiene un potencial muy grande pero necesitas mucha imaginacion para verlo. Encontrar la entrada desde el Kraton es una odisea y una vez dentro es muy dificil comprender nada si no te lo explica algun local. Faltan mapas, reconstrucciones, indicaciones... (aunque esto es bastante común en yogyakarta). Encontrar la mezquita subterránea no fue nada fácil. Aun asi, el water castle y todo su entorno serian tratados de valuoso patrimonio en las ciudades occidentales. 

Está muy bien para completar la visita al kraton.

Лично мне этот водный дворец понравился намного больше, чем дворец султана ("кратон"). От дворца султана дошли пешком, спрашивая дорогу у местных. Вход в сами купальни стоит 12 000 рупий и 2 000 рупии за фотосъёмку. В какой-то момент, глядя на эти бассейны с башней, возникло ощущение, что находишься в Италии. После посещения купален можно побродить по окрестностям по узким улочкам. Таким образом, опять-таки спрашивая дорогу у местных, дошли до подземной мечети Sumur Gumuling, так как на карте она не обозначена. При подходе ко всему комплексу к нам привязался "местный житель", но мы его отшили сразу.
Judul tempat dan faktanya sungguh berbanding terbalik. Tidak ada apa pun di tempat ini hanya 2 bh kolam ukuran besar saja dengan kondisi tidak terawat dan kotor. Sangat mengecewakan tempat ini
Pas grand intérêt pour ce lieu qui manque gravement d'entretien. Avec un peu de volonté et certainement d'argent,cela pourrait devenir un lieu magique.
It's quite small. We spend around 20 mins there for take a picture and walk around. Entrance fees is cheap, You should try.

This place is very well preserved (maybe too much restored, looking almost as new) and a good example about the luxurious life of the past sultans. Once secluded for the rest of the mortals, the Tamansari consists of two water pools for the private recreation of the sultan and his numerous concubines, and a little tower to see this nice view. You must not miss it when in Yogya.

I find The Water Castle or Taman Sari is not as spectacular in comparison to the other World Heritage Sites. The architecture is not so intricate. It is located about 2km south from the Kraton Yogyakarta ( Sultan Palace ). The main attraction is the central bathing complex. There are 2 gates that leads to the bathing complex. Within the Taman Sari compound are some house which used to house the Sultan's concubines.

Jaman dahulu kala tempat ini menjadi pemandian bagi raja raja Yogyakarta, dan alhamdulillah sampai sekarang tempat ini masih terawat. Air yg jernih di tambah arsitektur bangunan khas jogja menambah keindahan water castle ini

Gak jauh dri alun2 kidul lokasinya dri luar seperti benteng yang perkasa yg telah dimakan jaman tpi keindahan dari masjid bawah tanah dan kolam air taman sarinya sungguh anggun penataanya bagus untuk segala moment
Faktor Penarik: Ketertarikan Budaya, Ketertarikan Fasilitas, Ketertarikan Suasana

Review Text: Lite roligt att se, väldigt lite turister. Vi fick en guidad tur av en vaktmästare till ett mycket bra pris.

The entrance ticket was really cheap (Rp3000 for locals and Rp7000 for international tourists *regularly 1 USD=Rp13.300*). However, the place was really badly organized. Once you enter the main entrance there would be so many tour guides that would keep bothering you to hire them unless you keep walking straight and saying no. Make sure you have reliable and clear information-a friend who has already been there-since there will be no sign where to go next and what there is. Otherwise, tour guide would be an alternative. One thing to be noted is that the place is actually not separated from locals’ housings making you would feel lost. What I would suggest if you don’t want to spend money on tour guide, you can follow other groups or asking locals where to go (unfortunately Indonesians are really limited with their English as it is not their mother tongue). Normally, it would take two hours to explore the place.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Nice but no must. I worth visiting as a stopover while visiting Yogya but if you're not in the neighborehood leave it as it is.

El Taman Sari o castillo del agua se sitúa en la ciudad de Yogyakarta junto al Palacio del Sultán. Es un conjunto de fuentes y piscinas junto a jardines al estilo de la Alhambra de Granada (aunque evidentemente sin punto de comparación). Lugar de recreo del sultán, vale la pena su visita de paso que se visitan los templos de Borobudur y Prambanan.

This is the ruins of the Sultan's private bathing area with some raunchy little tales attached.  There are no guides and no information available so research before you go. It is set in lovely quiet back streets and is very peaceful. However, it was quite tricky to find; we ended up at the ruins of the water castle first and thought we had seen it: thankfully we stumbled upon Taman Sari quite by mistake.
It's nothing spectacular but fascinating all the same.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
The photos we had seen made this attraction appear stunning. However when we visited on May 21st it was just the opposite.

The pools had been partialy drained and what was left in them was weed infested and stagnant. Maybe it had been undergoing restoration or maintenance, but nobody told us that when they took our entrance fee.

The architecture was quite interesting and we did have a wander around, finally finding the third pool, which was in the same poor state.

However, the best part was when we left through the small rear entrance and wandered around the village, which will be demolished if the Tamansari becomes a World Heritage site. Around here somewhere we had read there was the remains of an underground river complex and an underground mosque (see reviews for Sumur Gumuling). Finally after lots of twists and turns we found them both and they were more interesting to us. Just ask the locals in order to find them, plus there are more remnants of the old walls to explore outside.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Un sitio más que ver en Yogya, si te sobra el tiempo no está mal por la historia y mitología, pero si vas justo aconsejo no visitarlo.

Istana ini dikelilingi oleh pemukiman penduduk yang cukup padat. Yang mana itu adalah abdi dalem keraton Jogja. Bagunan istana ini khas tradisional Jawa. Di dalamnya terdapat beberapa kolam. Air di kolam tersebut berwarna toska yang cantik.
Tempat ini lumayan romantis tapi menurut saya butuh perawatan yang lebih baik lagi.
it's ok, normal place, not clean like this picture, and the exit very complicated, you can lost way :)

With A LOT OF IMAGINATION you can imagine how cool it would have been for the sultan to take a bath there or a steam one. All the women ( wives most) and the kids on one side in two pools and the sultan on the other one. He could look at the kids and women and could invite anyone he pleases on his side. Yeah , ha ha ha. Well besides some imagination this place is not very well maintained like most of things to visit here.
a relic of history that should be visited in Yogyakarta. beautiful and leisure castle of the king and queen in Yogya in the ancient Javanese kingdom era.

Bangunannya romantis sekali, cantik dan memukau walau dikelilingi rumah penduduk yang dulunya merupakan abdi dalem. Tempat ini menjadi salah satu lokasi syuting video klip KLa Project saking cantiknya.

this place is very unique : its like a little spa & resort from old time for royal ladies.
i went there with my friend and with her guidance : we explore all the place and surrounding it. it took us around 1,5 hours to explore all the site.
to bad the water in the pool is dirty so we avoided to take picture around the water.
if you go to Yogyakarta : this is a must visit place !
i really enjoying it

Halo temen-temen, belum lengkap rasa nya kalo kita kejogja belum mampir ke istana air taman sari. Selain malioboro ternyata jogja menyimpan tempat wisata yang menakjubkan untuk dikunjungi. Bangunan kuno yang masih terawat rapi menjadi ciri khas kota jogja. Istana air taman sari terletak dalam satu komplek keraton jogja yang sangat luas, walaupun seiring bertambah nya tahun pemukiman penduduk mulai berdiri disekitar komplek keraton. Ini menunjukkan bahwa sultan jogja sangat mencintai rakyat nya begitu juga rakyat nya sangat setia kepada sultan nya. Kita kembali ketopik guys, istana air taman sari merupakan tempat rekreasi sultan ngayogyakarta hadiningrat I. Disini dahulu biasanya tempat pemandian sultan bersama putri dan selir- selirnya. Disini juga merupakan tempat meditasi sultan. Di komplek istana air dikelilingi tembok tinggi, terowongan bawah tanah dan bangunan lain nya. Arsitektur bangunan merupakan campuran dari belanda cina indonesia dan arsitektur kerajaan zaman dahulu. Terowongan bawah tanah merupakan tempat bersembunyi dan melarikan diri apabila ada serangan musuh. Didalam terowongan bawah tanah ini ada sebuah tempat shalat yang design nya sangat jauh berbeda dengan design mesjid atau mushala sekarang ini. Ada beberapa bangunan di kompleks ini mulai pugar kembali karna sudah termakan usia dan terkena dampak gempa jogja,tetapi pemugaran tidak menghilangkan nilai asli bangunan tersebut. Cukup membayar tiket masuk Rp. 3000/orang kita bisa menikmati keindahan istana air taman sari. Kita juga bisa menggunakan jasa pemandu untuk mengetahui secara detail tentang sejarah komplek istanan air dan kita akan diajak berkeling kompleks. Untuk jasa pemandu, mereka tidak mematok berapa, melainkan seiklhas nya guys. Banyak turis mancanegara berkunjung kesini. Yang pasti kita akan terbawa suasana tempo dulu. Jangan lupa mampir guys. Jogja ngangeni. Thanks.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
Our guide took us here during a private tour of Java. While the white gates are lovely and make for interesting photos, there is really not much else to see aside from a pool with green algae growing in the water. 

The complex was destroyed first by war, and then by an earthquake. Much of what you see lies in ruins although the pools have been restored.

Snap a few photos, and then move on.

ラマダン期間の平日に訪れたためか比較的空いていました。ガイドさんの説明を聞きながら１時間ほど見学しました。
王宮の中はたいへん広く、ガムラン演奏が行われる大広間や闘鶏場、装飾品の展示部屋、或いは各王様ごとの肖像画と家系図（夫人と子供を表したもの）などもありました。少し離れたところには大きな沐浴場を備えた離宮もあり、１０代に及ぶ王家の権勢を忍ばせます。末裔の方が住まわれているようですが、維持していくにはかなりのお金が必要と思われます。
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Tempatnya menarik. Wisata sejarahnya kental di sini. Lokasinya tidak jauh dari Keraton di tengah pemukiman penduduk. Area yang bagus buat foto-foto. Serasa hidup di zaman kerajaan Jawa kuno.

Review Text: Situs pemandian putri raja zaman dahulu, sering dijadikan lokasi foto prewed. Banyak spot untuk foto-foto. Jangan lupa, sisiri juga sumur gumantung dan sumur gumuling yang ada di sekitar wilayah Ngasem.
We had high expectations going here but it is poorly maintained and looks very run down and not very attractive. I wouldn't recommend it as a must for travelers :)

i was asking a local person how to get to the water castle from the sultan palace & he volunteered to show me. he walked me around, through the ruins while explaining to me the history of the place. usually i don't like or trust people to walk with them like that but i felt safe (i am an older solo female). then i paid for myself to enter the site & we saw the pool, the mosque & he made history so vivid. after that we walked around the sultan village & i heard more about his family who lives there & about his life. don't give up on wondering around the sultan village as part of visiting the water castle. the area is quaint, small houses, narrow streets & you can see workshops in some houses, including how they make masks & also hear the story of the masks & the symbolism of it.
i paid my guide as much as i felt, he never mentioned being paid. i was so happy with the way my day turned to be, only because of him.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: It was a pity that this historical heritage is poorly managed. It does not look like as in the photos shared by previous visitors. The entry was cheap, only IDR. 5k for domestic tourists. The water castle itself was dirty. There are a lot of houses built alongside the building that confused me when getting around. The ticketing counter didn't even provide us with a map. So pretty hard to get around and know your direction.
Whatever you have seen in the pictures will not be the same when you go and see it with your own eyes. The place is not maintain very well and the pool is somehow looks dirty.

Include this place and the Sultan's palace only if you have plenty of time to laze around in Jogja. Even though there is some history behind this, it is not at all maintained with dirty water in the lakes. Pls do not be fooled by the published photos - they are all edited ones

In unmittelbarer Nähe zum Kraton liegt der Wasserpalast. Wenn ich mir hier die Bilder ansehe, frage ich mich, ob ich veräppelt wurde und woanders hingebracht wurde. Der Ort an dem ich war, ist inzwischen doch ziemlich heruntergekommen. Er war sicher mal schön und ich denke man kann auch etwas daraus machen, aber dazu müsste mal einiges restauriert werden.

Taman ini merupakan taman kolam mandi , dimana ada tiga kolam di dalam nya yaitu satu kolam untuk selir , satu kolam untuk anak para selir , dan yang terakhir kolam untuk raja bersama selir bermadu kasih .
lokasi nya sih cukup luas sebenarnya tetapi sayang sudah banyak di bangun rumah rumah untuk anak cucu selir sehingga hampir tidak kelihatan bangunan utama taman ini , apa lagi taman nya sudah tidak ada lagi di ganti dengan bangunan rumah.

Review Text: My 1st impression was, this must been one amazing palace back then. Even though it is already tired-looking place it's still worth to visit, especially if the staff already clean the pool. Tips: do use the official tour guide (they wear 'kesultanan' badges), they're friendly, speak adequate english, most of all you could help the local also since they have been working since ages while learning some indonesian history.

Taman Sari or Water Castle was recreation center of the Sultan. It had  a large artificial lake with islands with Bathing area. Today however you can see only the bathing area and the surrounding is a housing colony. It's occupants are the descendants of the workers who built it for the Sultan.

It is not maintained very well. I had seen pictures of clean pools with clear water, but in reality the water stinks and full of green moss and agile.

There is a underground mosque nearby, which was used by Sultan.

It is part of day tour and one can spend one hour to see the entire area.

Интересное место. Жаль почти не читается былое великолепие, но побродить занимательно. Если вам не хочется тишины и не жалко немного денег, не отказывайтесь от самозваного гида при входе (вход бесплатный). Он проведет вас по узким улочкам, остаткам зданий и подземным коридорам, расскажет о месте, его обычаях и былых обитателях; и будьте готовы - конечно же потащит вас посмотреть лавку, где продается батик. Можно подняться на развалины центрального строения и посидеть там, созерцая черепичные крыши... На территории Тамансари до сих пор живут потомки тех, кто когда-то служил султану и получил право жить в домиках на территории дворцового комплекса. Атмосфера кажется пропитана единством прошлого и настоящего... А еще покоем и каким-то всеприятием...
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: I was really disappointed with the water castle. These historical ruins are being used as a hangout point for teenagers, and a football pitch for children!! I was told by a local guide that Unesco are funding a renovation of the castle, yet local boys were kicking a football around and no one was stopping them, not even the guides. No wonder the sight is in such poor condition. Rubbish and rubble everywhere. It doesn't seem as if there is any respect for this place so I think money would be better spent elsewhere.

vai pure a vederlo ma non aspettarti molto. Anche la sua conservazione non è granché. Almeno l'acqua, elemento caratterizzante, potrebbe essere tenuta pulita. Resta l'immaginazione del sultano che, nascosto dietro la finestra, sceglie le sue concubine. Il prezzo di ingresso è irrisorio e lo trovate uscendo dal Kraton, dirigendovi verso la moschea sotterranea
Dit paleis moet prachtig geweest zijn en ernstig decadent. Het ziet er vergaan uit en ook dat is weer mooi. Het complex is als een labyrint, leuk om te ontdekken en vooral zonder gids.

Saya mengunjungi taman sari awal oktober 2014. untuk sampai di tempat ini, saya cukup jalan kaki dari alun-alun selatan sekitar 2 km. Tempat ini adalah tempat yang sangat menarik, dengan bangunan yang megah khas kastil. Yang menakjubkan dari tempat ini adalah ruang bawah tanah yang seperti scene film beautiful creatures (2014), menyusuri tempat ini sangat keren. seperti berpetualang. sangat recommended untuk bersantai dan menikmati sejarah khas yogyakarta

When I last was here they were under renovation. So I guess I wasn't able to see its full glory. The place is reach in history but shows more promise if the place is restored to its former glory. Historically it is a famous bath house of royalties, just imagine how it would had looked like in the past.

It is part of the Yogyakarta walking tour. It depends on where you start your trip. If you start from Marlioboro St. this would be probably your last stop for the day.

Review Text: bagi yang suka trip ke situs-situs bersejarah, boleh juga mengunjungi tamansari di jogjakarta, situs ini merupakan bangunan dengan kolam besar katanya sih tempat pemandian raja ataupun selir-selir raja, sebetulnya situs ini bernilai sejarah tinggi. hanya saja kurangnya papan informasi tentang sejarah situs ini, kolamnya juga sudah banyak lumut kurang terawat ditambah coretan-coretan di dalam ruang-ruang sekitar kolam mengurangi keindahan situs ini...

The Water Castle lies in the surrounding houses and mosque. Former royal garden of the Sultanate of Yogyakarta. Amazing Water Castle with cute living accommodations. Review Text: This was apparently the place where the sultan took his concubines. Walking amongst the ruins, one can still imagine how romantic the place must have been.

Istana Air Taman Sari merupakan salah satu situs sejarah favorit di Kota Yogyakarta. Tidak sulit mencapai tempat ini, berada tidak jauh dari Keraton Yogyakara. 
Tarif masuknya tidak mahal, jika membawa kamera ada biaya tambahan yang tidak mahal. 
PAda musim liburan, tempatnya ramai sekali, sehingga agak kurang nyaman. Ada berbagai ruangan kecil di tempat ini yang sering dimanfaatkan untuk berpacaran, beberapa kali meilhat orang berpeluk-pelukan di situs sejarah ini. Juga ada banyak coretan-coretan di dinding. Sayang sekali fasilitas ini kurang terawat, padahal tempat ini sangat bagus.
Arsitekturnya bagus, seperti bangunan di Timur Tengah menurut saya, dengan kolam di tengah-tengah bangunan. 
Semoga tempat ini bisa dilengkapi CCTV sehingga tidak ada pengunjung yang merusak tempat ini.
Datanglah pagi hingga siang hari, menjelang sore hari tempat ini tutup dan pengunjung harus memutar melewati rumah-rumah warga untuk keluar dari tempat ini.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: tempat wisata ini kurang dikelola dengan baik, kondisi kolam-kolamnya banyak berlumut dan tidak ada nya pusat informasi bagi para wisatawan.

Ancient historic buildings. Yore used bath by a princess. But unfortunately now so do not wat, mossy dirty water and a lot of graffiti on the wall
And to get into this place we were charged admission, so where are the endless money entrance ticket? Should be used for the treatment of this place

Better ask a local guide to take a tour in this place. They know very well about every detail, every story. Its very big place, around 1hour is not enough. Good to know about the history and what was this place like in the past. Inside the complex there is one shop that sell a t-shirt. Its good quality and nice design. Review Text: От нечего делать пошли искать султановские купальни. Как только подошли к жилому кварталу, где запрятаны эти купальни, к нам подбежал дядечка помочь найти их в жилом лабиринте. Ну привел, спасибо, но смотреть оказалось там нечего, пустой бассейн и старое каменное здание за каменным забором. Внешнее впечатление никакое. Во внутрь естественно не пошли.

There isn't a lot of water left in the Water Castle (Taman Sari), despite its name. The complex itself is quite impressive - there are a series of underground tunnels and some ruins apparently destroyed in the 1949 war of independence. The complex used to be bigger - now with houses popping up all over the site it appears disjointed from each other. A pity they have allowed it to ruin the overall grandeur of the palace itself.

Some people recommended to us that this place was plain and no need to be visited. However, hypnotized by the beautiful photos we found in the internet and since it is located near the Keraton, we decided to go there. Following the directions from local people and passing through the batik village are some kinds of unique experiences in which we could interact with friendly locals. The entrance was not visible. Luckily we met a local guide who offered guiding us through the Taman Sari complex, who happened to be a fun and kind man. He guided us to all the area of Taman Sari, telling us histories of the place. (If you plan to visit, I recommend you to look for a guide).
When we reached the Taman Sari pond, we were not disappointed at all. After walking quite a long distance with burning sun, it was a relieve when we saw the glistening clear blue water. We just hoped that we could jump in to the pond. Unfortunately it was not allowed. But we did have our feet in the pond to feel how calm and relaxing the water is.
The underground mosque was also quite attractive. It offers us a unique feeling and sensation.
In conclusion, we will regret if we have not visited this place. Maybe it is boring for some people. But for us, it is rich with culture and worth visiting.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: This is just a swimming pool used in the past by the sultanate. It is not a must visit place. It is nearby sultan palace. I recommend to skip this.

We were slightly put off by some poor reviews, but still wanted to visit the underground mosque and water castle. We walked from the Kraton along colourful streets and found the art centre in the old bird market, where bands were practising for an evening performance which added to the ambience or the place with its rustic character and crumbling walls. After a walk through the mosque and a welcome stop at the beautiful Water Castle cafe, we thought we would go and look at the water castle even if it was a bit dilapidated. A guide attached himself to us at the cafe, but he wasn't pushy and helped us find our way around and where to take the best shots and gave us some of the history of the place. (Seemed happy with 30000 tip, which he didn't ask for). Amazing to think we were walking in the footsteps of the Sultans of the 18th century. The baths were used from the mid 1700's, suffered some damage when the British came along in 1812 and then they had trouble maintaining the complex waterworks and it fell into disrepair mid 1800's after another earthquake(1867). Hard to imagine how beautiful it must have been but still peaceful to wander through the alleyways of the Kampong Tamon that has grown up around the palace where the gardens used to be. Well worth a visit. We were there for about 3 hours, returning to the cafe for a rest and delicious lunch while the bands still played on. Shame they cannot restore baths to their original glory. But much more interesting than the touristy Sultans Palace (Kraton).
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: It's a series of dilapidated complexes with a dirty pool in the middle, we were there for 10 mins and and left.  Only a 5 min walk from palace.

We kind of got a guide without planning to- someone coming up to us at the sultans palace saying "We should trust him" and he'd bring us to the water palace. Well we didn't get rid of him then, but we're glad he brought us because at least the way we took would have been difficult to find by ourselves. 
The water palace is not by itself so extremely fascinating, but with the guide it was very interesting. He explained what all the rooms had been for, told us the history of the palace, showed us where had been water and where not and so one. We later agreed we would not have seen as much without him and probably would have walked through quite quickly and without much interest. 
At the end your supposed to give the guide a tip of something like 30.000 Rupiah. I do not like this whole set-up but it did indeed work for us this time.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Paleis is zeker niet de moeite waard. Sterk verouderd en slecht onderhouden. Water is vies, 'paleis' staat middenin een krottenwijk.

Review Text: Seriously! The story behind it is of aristocratic opulence and of kings and queens but the place it self now looks like a swamp site! Really... Can't you take pride in it and at least do the basic sweeping, mopping, dusting and wall scrubbing and painting?! And how healthy can  3 large pools of dark green slimy murky water be! I'm sure it was beautiful during the time of use... But now it's just sad to see how dirty and filthy it is. Be careful when you walk as it is very slippery with slim and mold everywhere.
王様が水遊びしている女性を選んで、夜遊びをしたらしいですが、ちょいとエッチな感がありました。来館した時は、時期的なものなのでしょうか、プールの水がどれも緑色に濁っており、少々臭いも鼻につきました。それでも、建物の白、空の青、コントラストが美しかったです。観光するにはなかなか素敵な場所だと思いました。

Ik denk dat het normaal wel een hele mooi plek zou zijn maar de gids heeft ons niet mee genomen naar de ondergrondse gangen en het zwembad van de vrouwen van de sultan was zwaar donker groen van de algen...

Leuk om te zien, de ondergrondse moskee, de baden en uiteindelijk het privé bad van de sultan. Nu buiten gebruik en het water is erg vies, maar je kan je de grandeur voorstellen. Neem wel een gids want het is een enorm doolhof daar. Je moet dit bezoeken jn combinatie met het kraton.

Review Text:
The Water Castle was beautiful and we loved the walk through the urban and artsy streets and alleyways that lead from the castle out to the main road. Only downside was the tour guides in the area didn't seem legit. We took a taxi and arrived at the area, funny that the local taxi driver didn't really know where the actual entrance to the water castle was and had to stop at the roadside to ask some locals. We stopped nearby and a man approached the taxi driver and they talked for a bit and the taxi told us that the man knew how to get to the water castle and asked us to follow him. 

So, assuming that this guy was being friendly and was just trying to show us the entrance to the place we followed (we were a young couple). He went on taking us further into some alleyways and started talking about the history of the place and pointed out to some scenery at the top of a an old building. At first it felt kind of nice that this guy is going out of his way to tell us a bit more about the place but then he started taking us further into the compound and there were many many alleyways and turns and corners and at some point we were lead down to a very very dark underground passage (imagine what we were feeling then! Our first thought was "omg we are going to be mugged and killed in this dark tunnel and nobody would know!!"). Also because there wasn't many tourists or even people around when we were walking deeper into this maze of alleys and dark tunnels. I swear I was gripping my bf's hands so tight I almost cut-off his blood circulation! And all that initial fear and anxiety kinda overcame the joys of exploring this beautiful place. Until we reached the official entrance (it was rather small and really could be missed otherwise with tiny signs) and the ticketing booth, only then did we let out this huge sigh of relief that we were not going to die after all! 

The tour guide followed us and explained the history and how each pool was used back in the day and we managed to enjoy the rest of the tour. The whole tour maybe took under 2 hours from where the taxi dropped us off until we walked out to the main road with the guide. The main pool is a great photo op as the water is very clean and clear and the outside courtyard/garden was lush and green. After the tour we were guided to one of the narrow alleyways and this rugged little tshirt shop where we talked to the owner of the shop and he said he designed and printed/painted all these cool tshirts and bandanas himself. It was pretty cool and we weren't pressured to buy anything. 

By the time we got out, we thought that the tour guide came with a fee but surprisingly he told us the tour was free and he declined when we asked how much should we pay. We gave him a big tip instead (later rationalising that he could've killed us in one of those dark tunnels and whatever money/tips he wanted after we would pay to avoid any unfortunate events lol). 

I think all this confusion and anxiety could have been avoided if the tour guides wore a tag/lanyard with their names and maybe a title saying that they were official tour guides for the water castle would have been great. I could see so many things that could go wrong here. Other than that initial terrifying feeling, this place was great and worth the visit.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Could use  a little up keeping, but still very interesting and beautiful place.   I likes it better than the Sultan Castle.

Tempat ini kurang menarik untuk dikunjungi, tempatnya yang kurang terawat juga kurangnya informasi yang ada di tempat ini membuat kita sedikit bingung. Airnya pun kotor. harga untuk masuk kesini cukup murah yaitu 5000 buka jam 09.00 – 14.00

After visiting the kraton we went to the watercastle. It was not clear how far the walk was so we wanted to take a taxi as we were with 3pax. We wouldn't fit in one becak. And we thought a taxi is a bit more comfy. However there wasn't a taxi to be found nearby. So eventually we took two becaks which cost 10.000 per becak. They dropped us at the taman sari after a 3 min ride, so you can also just walk to the entrance. However it was not at the main entrance we found out later(I posted a photo in the gallery of the real entrance and the fake entrance). It was at the other side which requires a walk in a tunnel and in narrow alleys. At first we didn't trust it as the place was full with hagglers who where claiming to be guides were trying to walk along and guide you through the the walk to the real entrance of the watercastle without our consent or even asking for a guide. So watch out if any of them tries to direct you a certain way.when you are at the real entrance you have to buy a ticket for 12,500 IDR. You can thereafter go to the entrance and right after your ticket is checked you can get a real guide. The place itself is not very well maintained. So do not expect anything spectacular. It is basically a walk of half an hour. The pools were filled with green water and bugs everywhere. I would not advise going there with small children. After the taman sari you can walk to malioboro or pasar beringhardjo it's a 10 min walk. If you take a taxi it will cost you around 30.000 depending on the traffic.

Tamansari has lost her glorious past, but I really like it more than the Sultan palace. Many guides are available at the entrance, and they are not push you around for sightseeing. One man even showed me a staircase to climb up to the roof-top of a building so that I could grasp a whole picture around the castle. There is a ruin stood in a far distance with houses clustered around; without the help of a guide, I dared not to go any further through the winding lanes. The waters of the pool flowed out over a large dragon head-designed mouth at the edge of the pool, beside the passage that was not easily noticed outside a room. Outside the castle, there are lots of stalls selling all sorts of souvenirs. My wife bought a pant and a musical instrument for IDR35,000 in total (the asking price was IDR50,000), I gave a 50,000 note to pay the bill, but the vendor only handed me a 5,000 note in return. On spot I turned down her offer because she was dishonest, I could not bear her common trick.Moreover, try a cup of herbal tea for IDR5,000 that is welcomed by the driver.

Review Text: Keadaan taman ini amat buruk kerana tidak dipelihara. Airnya amat kotor dan dinding dipenuhi dengan grafidi. Tour guide di depan pintu masuk ini akan mencoba menceritakan sejarah tempat ini. Tetapi, anda harus berwaspada kerana mereka akan mengenakan yuran yang mahal! Tiket 2015 rp 5000/orang, kamera rp2000/orang. Tour Guide rp 50000/4 orang

We first visited Tamansari on the first day here and were "conned" by the bechek driver that it's still opened. Upon arrival, a man simply asked us to follow him. We assumed he was a guide. he could barely speak English. We were led to what look like someone's backyard, had to squeeze through a narrow gap to get a glimpse into the pool then quickly led back to the entrance. For that, he asked for a inr10,000 tips. It was a total waste of money n time. Beware of such guides. 

On the second day, we explored the fresh market and stumbled upon other parts of Tamansari. It was a pleasant discovery. We chanced upon a underground tunnel leading to a structure we later found out to be a mosque back in the heydays. It's interesting to wonder aimlessly into the kampung residences. It would be useful to have a guide who's knowledgable about the history and the layout of the area. Definitely worth exploring and a peek into daily yogyakartians' life.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
The castle was originally built with a lake around it and can only be accessed by boat, but now the locals have dried the lake and built a maze of houses surrounding the castle, making it tricky and amusing way to find the castle
there is a mosque in the center of castle and it feels like you are in a cave with a hole in the middle for sun-light

I suggest to learn about the history before visit the place.

水の離宮だそうですが，残念ながら私たちが行ったときはあまり水が張られていませんでした。

Upon paying my ticket and entering I was approached by a guide.  I said no thanks, for fear of the costs and he insisted it was free. 
Indeed it was, there was no request for money at the end, especially after he could tell I was not interested in paying for the Batik at the shop they keep at the end. (likely higher priced). 

Nonetheless, the guide did enhance the experience by providing information on how the water castle was used and what each pool was for.   It was a unique view to see.
If you have time the area around the Kraton, including Taman Sari is worth exploring but if you are only in Yogya for a few days give it a miss in favour of the temples around Yogya.

Le Water Castle n'a rien de vraiment extravagant, c'est sympathique mais ça prend 10 minutes ; en revanche le quartier autour est vraiment très beau et on sent une vraie "âme", graffitis, artistes qui jouent de la musique, peintures, vraiment très agréable !

Braucht man nicht gesehen haben - ist schön, kulturell und architektonisch , aber eher ein Zeitvertreib !!!

Kann man machen, wenn man eh vom Süden her auf den Weg zur City ist...

From Kraton, there were a lot of tricycle drivers asked me to hire them to Taman Sari. I walked and have known that why did they tried to followed me.

Taman Sari is about 1 km away from Kraton and free map is not giving fulled detail. However, positive side is I'm getting there through the charming old town neighbor and having a memorable with an indisian guy who kindly tell me the way.

This historic site have no English clear signage and information. One characteristic I like is ancient tunnel which lead me to the site. Little exciting!

difficile à trouver mais il se répend dans les dédales d'un quartier hyper arty de "djoja" 
c'est gratuit sauf le watercastle en lui même

We asked at the Keraton how we get to Taman Sari and happened upon a woman who appointed herself our guide. We conversed in my rudimentary Indonesian as she led us through charming, side streets (jalan tikis = mouse streets) to Taman Sari. Just seeing this side of Indonesian life was interesting as she explained that these small houses were the homes of people who worked at the Keraton. When we arrived at the Water Palace, it clearly is the FORMER home of the Sultan and not the current one and hence less upkeep, as she explained the uses of the tower and the pools. She then led us to the underground mosque and explained the alcoves for meditation and showed us the M.C. Escher-eque stairs. She then led us back to the Keraton. I asked her what she wanted to be paid for her trouble, she left the price up to me. I gave her 100,000 Rp for about an hour, so I probably overpaid her but she was delightful in her own way and added charm to the existing historical site. Not a single regret!
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Beautiful buildings, helpful guides. Really interesting place to visit and learn some of the history and culture of the area. Easy to find and cheap to enter. Not too busy either so you get to really see everything.
