Previously it was a wate castle complex for the King's family rendezvous. The water castle concepts was amazing but it can not restore completely the whole area like it used to be.

Nowdays we only can see a small King's bathpool complex. Relly need to keep this place save in the future. So sad if we have to loose this wonderful place again.

Liburan ke jogjakarta tidak lengkap rasanya jika tidak mengunjungi Taman sari atau lengkapnya adalah Istana Air Taman Sari. Bagi teman-teman yang menyukai fotografi tamansari adalah tempat yang eksotis untuk menambah koleksi foto. Taman sari sendiri terdiri dari beberapa bagian, saya tidak terlalu hafal apa saja nama bagian di taman sari tetapi yang jelas setiap bagian tersebut mempunyai nama tersendiri dengan sejarah tersendiri. Salah satu favorit saya adalah bagian yang disebut umbul pasiraman. Menurut cerita di umbul pasiraman inilah dulu sultan dan permasurinya mandi. Disini terdapat pot-pot bunga berukuran besar serta terdapat kolam dan air mancur. Waktu paling tepat untuk mengunjungi Taman sari ini adalah sore atau pagi hari, karena ketika siang hari taman sari sangat panas. Bagi wisatawan yang akan berlibur ke jogja jangan lupa ke Taman sari dan jangan lupa membawa kamera.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: The Water Castle is just outside the Kraton (the Sultan’s Royal Palace in Yogyakarta) in the palace complex, but it can be confusing to get there, so we caught a “becat” (rickshaw) rather than walking in the heat and getting lost.  The pools and structures within are very photo-worthy. It’s a lovely place to enter and relax.  The pools are pretty, the gates are decorated and you can climb to the top of the octagonal courtyard for a view of the pools.  The bathing complex has a pool which used to be where the sultan and his concubines were the only ones allowed to enter.  Stories like this make it interesting.If you walk further inside, there are craftspeople who are there to show you how puppets and batik are made.  There are shops, too, where you can buy beautiful examples of these.   We didn’t take advantage of the guide who was waiting at the entrance when he asked if we wanted him to accompany us, but it’s not a bad idea.  It would have helped us understand what we were seeing there. Nevertheless, we enjoyed sitting by the pool and investigating all else that was there.
Faktor Penarik: Ketertarikan Budaya, Ketertarikan Fasilitas, Ketertarikan Suasana
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Konon istana Taman Sari merupakan situs bagi para putri Kraton Yogyakarta untuk mandi rekreasi. Rancangan bangunan terlihat masih bagus. Pengelola situs bersejarah ini perlu memoles dan merekonstruksi banguna agar suasana bisa kembali ke jaman raja-raja Kraton Yogyakarta dahulu.

Within the grounds of the Sultan's Palace or the Water Castle, can be found the most stunning works of art.  Watching the craftsmen creating these intricate puppets with tiny chisels (fashioned from bicycle spokes!) is almost hypnotic.  Don't hesitate to pay a guide $3-$4 for a tour around the Water Castle, as there is so much you will miss, without their intricate knowledge of the place.  It really is quite remarkable: I had gone there planning to have a quick walk through, without a guide, but soon found myself chatting and ambling along, agreeing to be escorted in and out of various narrow passages and gardens.  So glad I did - my charming guide today, took great delight in telling me how Prince Charles had chatted with him and visited his family's small house within the grounds during a visit a few years ago.  My guide also introduced me to his 104 year old Grandmother in Law, who lives in a small cottage nearby!  (you won't find that in a guide book....)  The time and craftsmanship that goes into the wayang puppets mean that many of the younger folk aren't going into that line of work any more.  About 200 wayang craftsmen remain in Jogyakarta and these wayang puppets will one day become highly sought after, I am sure, as they become more rare.  For something pretty special - and as a way of supporting a community that has suffered many natural disasters over the years, do have a look at the small shop at the Water Castle.  You can bargain there; and you will know that you have bought something from some of the best craftsmen in the world.  Nogroho was the young man who showed me stunning pieces that the 'elders' had made, but every day a different sales person and 'apprentice' will be on duty.  Highly recommended.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Yang paling membuat saya takjub adalah tempat imam sholat di masjidnya, yg dibuat sedemikian rupa sehingga tanpa pengeras suara, suara imam akan terdengar di seluruh bangunan. Namun sayangnya, di dalam lokasi banyak terdapat penjual-penjual makanan sehingga terlihat tidak tertib. Dan untuk ke bangunan lainnya kita harus melewati perumahan penduduk.

we were late in the afternoon and the garden closed but  a guide took us to the tunnel below taman sari and a walk thru an artisan village. An interesting tour of the underground mosque and overlooking the garden from the village nearby.  Lunch at the keraton restaurant unfortunately the air conditioning hall is closed so its a sweaty meal but the food is good though. must try the jawa beer!!

Review Text: Budaya berenang para bangsawan Yogya masa lalu tercermin dari arsitektur Istana Air Taman Sari, merefleksikan kebutuhan kegiatan  berenang secara eksklusif. Arsitektur kolam renang yang mempunyai ruangan bentuk labirin menambah suasana misteri. Mungkin perlu polesan yang lebih apik untuk pemeliharaan peninggalan budaya ini.

We arrived there in the morning. One kind man came to us and introduced he's a guide. He was so kind with smiling and told us all about this place. He took one red tiny seed from the tree and sqeezed on to our nails. After some minute when it's dried, it changed to glossy manicure. Interesting place to see and to take pictures. Inside there, you can buy real handmade batik products in batik shop. After tour, I wanted to show my thanks with giving some money. But he said he's an employee hired as a guide, and he denied to get money from tourists.

Agak kurang terawat sekilas, tetapi bayangkan saat zaman dahulu sudah ada fasilitas ini untuk pemandian raja dan selir-selirnya.

Mewah, megah, dan cantik pada saat yang bersamaan. Terdapat tangga melingkar di salah satu bagian Taman Sari.

Saat masuk hanya membayar Rp 4.000 dan tidak usah menggunakan jasa guide, karena kunjungan cenderung singkat. Lokasi yang menarik untuk berfoto.

Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Small King's Water Palace with Beauty of it own; Magnify of Decoration; The pool itself and The panorama view Tower. Must Visit!!
Faktor Penarik: Ketertarikan Budaya, Ketertarikan Fasilitas, Ketertarikan Suasana

Review Text: At a glance when you enter the area, all you see are forlorn ruins of old buildings, the remains of a castle. Some places have been restored but in the restoration, the 'feel' of history is lost. There are lots of alleys ways and inside the grounds, there are houses where people still live.  A local guide approached us and told us the history of the place. We were lucky because he did not insist on us paying him. It seems that he was proud to relate the history of the castle to us. He led us through the alley ways. We even had a chance to see the underground mosque. It is a good place for photography.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Very nice water castle, and you need to hire a guide to tell you the history behind the making of this castle! Some of the castle part  are broken, and some people (one village) really live inside this castle
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
Istana air taman sari letaknya tidak jaug dari Keraton Yogyakarta. Namun apabila anda malas berjalan kaki, anda bisa mengunakan jasa becak dari Keraton ke taman sari dengan membayar Rp 15,000. 
Taman sari merupakan komplek atau bentuknya mungkin di jaman dulu adalah benteng. Anda dapat menjelajahi dan mengelilingin tempat ini. 
Lebih baik apabila datang ke tempat ini bersama teman yang memang tinggal di Yogyakarta. Karena luasnya tempat ini kemungkinan anda bisa kesasar apabila anda datang sendirian.
Untuk masuk ke tempat ini cukup membayar Rp 5,000.
Walau tempat ini tidak terlalu menarik tetapi apabila anda mempunyai banyak waktu di Yogyakarta dapat datang dan menjelajah, mengetahu dan menikmati sekilas keindahan masa lalu di masa kini.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Beautiful old water castle in the heart of Yogyakarta, looks dirty and mouldy but I felt it added a touch of nostalgia to the building - walking around, you'd notice many hidden alleyways and it was interesting to note how some alleys lead to occupied homes and shops

Kompleks Istana Air ini sangat megah dan sangat luas. selain pemandian, ada jalan dibawah tanah yang berada 2 tingkat dimana dulu dipakai sebagai mesjid. Dengan para petunjuk jalan seharga kurang lebih 30rb anda akan diajak berkeliling sambil diceritakan sejarah istana air ini.

Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:

It is worth seeing if you are spending several days in Jogja, but we also had as fulfilling experience by just walking in the back streets afterwards.

tempat ini secara keseluruhan terawat dengan cukup baik. Turis lokal dikenakan biaya masuk 5000/orang dan kita perlu jalan kaki cukup lama jika ingin mengelilingi seluruh komplek taman sari ini.

semua wisatawan akan memulai tur disini. setelah membayar retribusi, kita akan melewati gerbang dan selanjutnya akan sampai di kolam pemandian.

2. lorong bawah tanah
tanyalah pada warga sekitar (jika tidak memakai jasa pemandu) mengenai terowongan bawah tanah ini. terowongan ini sangat besar dan diujung terowongan kita akan sampai pada sebuah reruntuhan bangungan.

3. mesjid bawah tanah
ada sebuah pintu masuk di dekat parkiran motor yang akan langsung mengantarkan kita pada mesjid unik ini. Mesjid ini hanya bisa digunakan untuk shalat (pada zaman dahulu) pada waktu dzuhur dan ashar karena tidak dilengkapi dengan sistem penerangan. kubah mesjid berbentuk cekung ke dalam bangunan dan ada tangga yang mengarah ke empat arah.

kekurangan dari objek wisata ini adalah letaknya yang berdampingan langsung dengan permukiman warga sehingga terlihat sangat semrawut dan terkesan seperti "wisata keliling kampung" daripada "wisata ke situs sejarah".
Petunjuk arah juga sangat kurang sehingga kerap kali kita perlu bertanya pada warga setempat (tapi pastikan warga tersebut bukan pemandu jika anda benar2 ingin bertualang tanpa pemandu).

oia, dekat dengan taman sari juga terdapat "mesjid kraton sokotunggal" yak, mesjid yang ditopang oleh satu tiang. Mesjid ini cukup bersih dan menjadi tempat ibadah yang nyaman.

ingat, taman sari hanya buka sampai jam 3 sore, jadi pastikan anda datang sebelum jam tutupnya ;)

Review Text:
The water palace is one of the best spot in the palace complex and the only restriction would be no entering the pool.

The place is quite big, but wouldn'ttake much time to explore.

The thing that surprised me the most is not just that the current sultan is not using the place. His ancestors also don't use the bath other than HB3 (the builder). At least that's what the guide told me. Quite a waste.

BTW, you are allowed to dip your feet in the Sultan's bath, just stay on the stair.
The bath's watchtower is a good spot too. The floor is still strong enough to go To the third floor.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
Great places for photo hunting and learn about the history
a must visit place in Yogyakarta..

Hope there will be any better maintenance to keep the building great to look and comfortable
Jika msk sebaik kita ditemani oleh petugas disana agar diterangkan dgn detail, sayangnya tempat tdk terawat dgn baik.

I've been to Jogya many times but never the Water Palace. Firstly, I was astonished at the price of the entrance fee only Rp5,000 ea (50c) - we would be happy to pay more and see some renovations done. However, the previous comment about graffiti was confusing for us as we didn't encounter any of that. What I loved was the simplicity and grandeur; metre thick walls with Moorish arches; gargoyles and flower designed spring water spouts and fountains. It doesn't take much to imagine how it would have been back in the day. So interesting and definitely worth a visit if you appreciate that kind of history. A lovely walk through the narrow streets outside the gates of the palace will bring you to the underground mosque. Shots of this building were used in scenes of the movie Tomb Raider. Another more simple structure, though beautiful in its simplicity.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: i really missed the "old" tamansari, which is most of the wall had green moss. more natural look and great for photo hunting
At the first sight, there were just pools and old building without renovation. But fortunately the villagers told us to walk further to explore the underground mosque.

塔曼水宮（Taman/ Water Castle）曾是蘇丹皇宮的一部份，走路去不消五分鐘。
原來的前門被堵，遊客要由後門進入，穿過後門後，便是一個小花園，有幾所石屎建的樂亭。
穿過花園後，便是一個裝修華麗的游泳池。後來才知道，這個不是游泳池來的，是個浴池暨水療中心。聽導遊講，昔日蘇丹就是站在閣樓，憑窗揀選浴池中的佳麗，非常香艷。
水宮的前門部份原本有一所巨型建築物，但早給夷平，慘成空地。粗眉仔爬上前門城樓，睇睇後恍然大悟，原來正門的路是被民居佔領了，所以進不了。
塔曼水宮其實沒甚值得看的東西，但因近皇宮，如去皇宮可順道一遊。
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: tempatnya sangat artistik,cocok bagi wisatawan yg gemar wisata sejarah, walaupun terkesan agak  sedikit menyeramkan karena ada bagian bangunan yg terletak agak di bawah tanah tetapi tempat ini tempat yg sangat indah apalagi untuk dijadikan tempat berfoto,sehingga tempat ini menjadi pilihan saya sebagai salah satu spot foto prewedding saya.dan yg membuat saya agak kecewa adalah, tempat ini sangat berdempetan dengan rumah warga sekitar dan peremajaan sebagian bangunan yg diberi warna sangat mencolok sehingga menghilangkan kesan antiknya.
Very interesting water palace.  Well worth getting a guide as you find out such interesting facts about this water palace.

Le water palace n'a rien d'exceptionnel mais reste sympa à faire. C'est un peu excentré à pied.
Le jardin pourrait être plus joli sans trop d'effort.

The Water Castle was once part of the broader Sultan's Palace, which we also visited.

Clearly the removal of royalty from power after Indonesian Independence has mean that funds for upkeep and enhancement of the sites have been limited. 

Having said that the Water Castle was the better of the two attractions.  The guide we had was informative and, being a benefactor of the Sultan's employment, very keen to see the site continue and be enhanced.

The surrounding village, where most of the Sultan's employees live, and are employed as artisans creating handcrafts such as batik and shadow puppets were enchanting
Faktor Penarik: Ketertarikan Budaya, Ketertarikan Fasilitas, Ketertarikan Suasana

Review Text:
Enjoying a historic place, just west of the Kraton, as Taman Sari Water Castle requires a well-informed and voluble guide, who will enliven the history, the story and the purpose of the ruins, pools, arches and underground passages of the former pleasure gardens.
Build in 18th century, the era of Sultan Hamengku Buwono I, by Raden Ronggo Prawirosentiko; the Water Castle served multiple functions, like a resting area, a workshop, a meditation area, a defense area or a hiding place.
Except that there is a complex of buildings like Pulau Cemeti and Sumur Gumuling, our guide mr. Yoga Efendi also mentioned the presence of tens of secret tunnels that were used to escape the royal family in case of danger. The story also mentions that men trying to solve the mystery several years ago have disappeared when entering the tunnels.
Mr. Yoga made our visit of this collection of stones worthwhile, there is definitely more appreciation of its functionality.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: This place consists of some large water tanks where the Sultan would bath and have fun. It is a huge complex but not maintained. There is graffiti all over the place and the authority are all interested in collecting the entrance fees. The gardens around this place is beautiful though. Can be skipped if time is a constraint. However as it is close to Prambanan Temples, a short trip can be planned.
Ticket 5k / pax. Opens from 9am-3:30pm daily。A local guide will follow you and explain what he understand to you after that he will ask you to give him some tips.

Taman Sari is one of the highlight when you do a visit in Yogyakarta. It is a nice hidden historical place surrounded by a nice, clean and serene village.
A must visit place !

Love that the place is a little run down but still nice. Still has that ancient feeling to it. Didn't really explore all the way because it started to rain, but the caretaker said that there is an underground mosque.

Saya biasa ke Tamansari jika sedang bosan dengan rutinitas. Memandang air kolam pemandian dari 'menara pengawas' yg biasa dipakai Sultan untuk melihat para putri mandi terasa sangat menyenangkan. Tempat ini cocok untuk menyendiri, berkontemplasi sejenak dari kebisingan kota.

To enjoy this historical place, please get yourself a guide. If you don’t, you will only see old buildings with rundown cracked walls, green bathing pools and some signs to indicate the rooms without any further descriptions. With a guide, he will describe you the history, the story, the purpose of this castle, and the intelligence of the King who built the place. I assure you, you will find it very interesting and will appreciate the place more. I highly recommend this place to visit in Yogyakarta although lots of walking but it was worth it.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Lieu méconnu et pourtant très intéressant à visiter...On remonte le temps et on s'imagine le faste qui devait régner dans ces lieux.

Review Text: This place is good for photos, however, it is tired and needs maintenance. The walls were not spared by vandals. If you are in Kraton already, it is worth visiting. By the way, the local will give you a tour but will ask for a fee afterwards. And will lead you to overpriced shops to buy batik and wayang.
御先祖が代々王様に仕えていたという（ホントか！？）近所のおじさんに案内してもらいました。タマンサリはもとより周辺の路地、地下道、バテック工房、等、小一時間案内してもらいました。それなりのチップは払いましたが何も知らずにただ見て回るよりは良いです。

Review Text: UGH, by far i felt cheated there, local will give you a tour and will ask for a fee. go on your own, dont miss the bathing place and there a small fee to be made, 300idr is okay. nothing much. pretty boring. forever under construction and repairs

The Water Castle - or Taman Sari is the only part of the over hyped Kraton worth visiting. It costs 7000rp to enter and is difficult to find. It is near the western gate down Jl. Taman. The rows of Bechak drivers will lead you in the right direction. The building is an unusual mix of European and Asian styles. There are many rumours whether it was the Dutch or Portuguese who built this in the 1700's. Some persistent guides may try to grab your attention while you are here, there is nothing in English but it is a pleasant enough place just to walk and relax. Its original purpose was a pleasure palace for the Sultan anyway - where he would select his concubines. The place shuts quite early in the afternoon.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
Planning for holiday can be tiring too although the excitement is there. I can’t recall how Yogjakarta came into our mind but somehow we choose the place and the planning begin. We have set our mind to visit Yogjakarta will not be complete without visiting Borobudur.  Another main attraction for our visit was Dowa Bag. During the planning and searching for the right tour agent and also within our budget, we were recommended by a friend to look at Pan Family Hotel website for accomodation. At the website of Pan Family there was a tour package for Yogjakarta run by Pusaka Tours. Taking a little bit of effort I contact Pusaka Tours personally and our relationship began.

Pusaka Tours and Travel

We are in a group of four and Pusaka Tours arranged our tour neatly and putting our request their priority. Since we found Pan Family through friends, we also found Manohara Resort through friends too.  Pusaka Tours make it possible for us to stay at Manohara and no hassle visiting Borobudur the next day. We have requested Pusaka to arrange our tour with priority of visiting Borobudur and Dowa. Upon confirming the details and getting the quotation, I found Pusaka Tours pricing are very reasonable and affordable together with their friendliness approach. To Merry and the family of Pusaka, my appreciation and gratitude for their dedication toward promoting Yogjakarta and taking good care of my mom during our stay .
We were met at the airport on 3rd April 2014 by Pusaka representative Mr Yoga Effendi who is our tour guide, Pak Miswan our driver and Pak Sulis (assisting us with our luggage, upon our arrival and during our departure). After brief introduction we were taken to our first stop for lunch, a boutique/restaurant called Sapthohoedoyo. At this boutique we are surrounded by arts since the owner is a renowned artist in Jogya. After the hearty and lovely lunch we visit the batik gallery adjacent to the restaurant and that begins our first day in Yogjakarta. 

The Tour Guide

Visiting places that we are not familiar with will be difficult without a guide. This is the reason we hire a tour agent and Pusaka Tours gave us a tour guide by the name of Yoga Effendi. From the moment he met us at the airport with his broad smile and smiling face, our chemistry developed. Our 4 days visit is full of knowledge and information as Mas Yoga is very proud about his country and especially his birthplace, Yogjakarta. He was a former teacher and taking up a job as tour guide because of his deep interest getting to know people and introduced Indonesia to the world. Since our package inclusive breakfast, lunch and dinner (BLD) we are not able to taste any local cuisine but nevertheless Yoga pointed to us what is local delicacies are. His good and detailed explanation about the history of Borodubur attracts one of the tourists beside us from Singapore and we get to know each other. We are lucky to have Mas Yoga Effendi as our guide.  He is very helpful, accommodative, informative and co-operative. His work is his passion and he is also a great photographer and a cuisine expert.

Places of Visit 

Our itinerary during our 4 days in Yogjakarta was very full. We visited The Prambanan Temple (an heritage recognise by Unesco and receiving Unesco funds for restoration which part of it destroyed during The Merapi eruption in 2010). Although we are not able to climb to one of the temple because of the on going repairs and restoration work being done, Prambanan is a must visit historical site. At Prambanan I’ve learnt about Hindu footing in the Java Islands and their belief. Around the area there are three main temples named Vishnu, Shiva and Brahma. This spot also kept history about half human bird named Garuda (a mystical bird in Hindu mythology). I assume from this name, the Indonesian gets the name of their airliner Garuda, since Garuda also is the symbol of the country.  At this site also kept the history of Ramayana. There is a theatre stage in Prambanan compound to performed Ramayana Ballet in the evening. My family and I missed the cultural show at Prambanan (The Ramayana Ballet) but we will not miss it again on our next visit. This historical site surrounded by beautiful garden and lawns, neatly kept and clean. As we exit the site of Prambanan, there are rows of shops selling souvenir of Yogjakarta and there are street sellers too who might lure you into buying their things (please be careful for not easily fall into buying).

Borobudur is another heritage in Yogjakarta and for not visiting Borobudur your trip to Yogjakarta will not be complete. We decided to view the sunrise on top of Borobudur. From words of friends too, we get to know about Princess Manohara Resort which part of Borobudur area. After getting a good bargain in lodging we stay a night in Princess Manohara and avoid getting up an hour early to travel to Borobudur from Yogjakarta town. (Note: sunrise in Yogjakarta is around 5.30 am). We climb the stairs of Borobudur at about 4.30am using the direct passage from the hotel. It is completely dark. Our light is only from the torch light given by the hotel to us. Being up of Borobudur is a breathtaking experience. The serene morning while waiting for the daylight was amazing. The stillness and quietness surrounded by mountains, tress and seeing “sleeping” Mount Merapi from the top gave you the feeling of calmness. This is also another historical site acknowledged by Unesco and many restoration works been done over the years. Borobudur has very high artistic value and the whole Borobudur explains of Buddha sitting on the lotus petals. One must know that enjoying the splendour of Borobudur just not climbing up the temple but will to see the sunrise or the sunset. It is most stunning when we are able to see the splash of morning sunlight against the stupas. My personal suggestion and opinion, if anyone wish to visit Borobudur, enjoy the scenic Princess Manohara entire estate and climb Borobudur in the early hours of next morning. Again I do hope and wish to get the experience of climbing Borobudur during sunset.

Our visit to The Sultanate Palace a living palace by the previous and current Sultan. It was very spacious and the servant (abdi dalem) activities. Many of them are around the palace to get the blessings. They meditate and meet each other within the compound. We miss the gamelan show/performance because it was a Friday. The palace is unique in design and architectural. Since the current Sultan does not have any sons the living quarters for them are left empty for long. 

We visited Taman Sari (Water Castle) and Kotagede (the witness of Islamic Kingdom of Mataram). We are very fortunate to allow entry at Kotagede which according to Mas Yoga they are not opened to public (tourist) to see the interior of the mosque. Tourists are only allowed to view from the exterior of the mosque.

Holiday without shopping will not be complete. We visited the silver industry and batik industry.  Since our main visit to Yogjakarta is Dowa, we are so happy when Mas Yoga and Pak Wan drop us there. My mom was not too good at that time since she had a fall a week before our departure and I thank Mas Yoga and Pak Wan who’s keeping her company all the time. We had a pit stop (I can’t recall the name) where rows of shop selling buah salak and I had the opportunity to have a glimpse of the tress along the road. Pak Wan stop the car and Mas Yoga and I have few pictures taken.

Not forgetting our sunset experience in Parangtritis beach, the famous beach among tourist in Yogjakarta and gained knowledge about Luwak Coffee (lu_a as pronounced by the Indonesian).  It is a home based industry and being exported by the owner himself. Without doubt the coffee is expensive but the scientific proven for health benefits is great advantage.

The Food

I am not able to describe details on the food but listed here are the restaurant where we had our lunch and dinner during our stay in Yogjakarta. The restaurants are: Pesta Perak Restaurant (Javanese Restaurant), Garlic Resto (Chinese Indonesian Food), Den Nanny Restaurant (Pusaka Tour), Iga Bakar Bali Resto.

At Den Nanny Restaurant I remember we had a grill fish served with traditional sambal. The fish is fresh and rare by the staff hotel of Pan Family and the pond is not far from our chalet. At Iga Bakar Bali Resto we are served with local cuisine Iga Sapi (grilled beef) and few other dishes. I’m really sorry for not able to recall the name of the food but it is very nice and worth trying.
My family and I were not too happy with Pesta Perak Restaurant (Javanese Restaurant) because of the choices of food served. It is buffet arrangement and their choices are limited.
We had a late lunch at Garlic Resto and it is much expected of any Chinese cuisine anywhere. 
Nevertheless the food choices are with us since we are not very fussy on food, as long as we are not hungry and starving. I decided to have meal arranged during our stay because I do not know Yogjakarta and their food outlet. Staying healthy during holiday is a high priority especially in a foreign land. 

Conclusion

We had a good time in Yogjakarta. We enjoyed our stay and are making plans for our next visit. There are many things to see, food to taste, things to buy and the friendliness, courtesy and their seriousness of making and promoting tourism to boost their economy is something I am proud about. My family and I will not miss the cultural show this time and will make cultural as our main agenda in the itinerary. If opportunity arises I will choose Pusaka Tours again, my heartfelt thanks to Pusaka Tours and the family (warga kerja) of Pusaka for their dedication and putting their best to fulfil customer needs. I do hope they will remain the same even though the staff will change in future
Faktor Penarik: Ketertarikan Budaya, Ketertarikan Fasilitas, Ketertarikan Suasana
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah, Merencanakan perjalanan

With its abundance of personal guides, ice cream sellers, and not much to see it is  hardly worth a visit. I have yet to see water in the bathing pools after many years of traveling to Yogja.

Review Text: This place near the palace , and i prefer visit this place than the palace , cause i think in front the palace its not beautiful , maybe they have to make little garden in front the palace , so for the moment water castle better for me to visit

I can only agree with other reviewers in that once you have visited all the temples in and around Yogya, then the only other thing viewing in the city is probably Tamansari. It is not an essential 'must-see' but it will pad out your stay here in Yogya. I loved the photogenic nature of the place, what with its mixture of Arabic and European architecture, which makes it quite unique among the places I have visited. I visited very early in the morning, though I am told it closes for lunch and doesn't re-open, so you had better factor this into your planned itinerary.

Sekiranya kita sudah mengunjungi Keraton Ngayogyakarto Hadiningrat, maka mampir berkunjung ke Tamansari adalah suatu kewajiban. Sebuah taman dangan sajian utama kolam air dibangun untuk para puteri keraton yang ingin beristirahat menenangkan jiwa di air yang bening dan tenang. Taman ini dilengkapi dengan terowongan bawah tanah yang tembus ke pasar Ngasem dan sumur Gumuling yang menurut ceritanya tembus ke laut Selatan.

Review Text:
This complex could be a really great visit, however, it badly needs cosmetic surgery to take it from its current dismal condition to reflect how I'm, sure it's creator envisenged it. 

There's plenty to see and explore, but unfortunately it's all unkempt and seemingly unloved. Go but don't expect to be amazed.
Was great to go see, much better than sultans palace. Interesting history & some great photo opportunities. Really reasonably priced, ok english speaking guide.

I like this bathing palace so much better than The Sultanante Palace itself! This bathing palace complex in including main bathing palace, underground tunnel and uderground mosque and the ruins of former recreational palace overlooking the densely populated village around the palace. This complex is unoubtedly unique in archetectural as it applied the combination of portuguese + javanese + arab architectural styles. Legend said that this palace was designed by a portuguese who was stranded in southern coast of Yogyakarta. As a punishment Sultan asked him to design a new bathing palace complex for Sultan's concubines. Anyway this bathing palace is no longer serves the royal family as it used to be, it is now open for public for tourism purpose only. This palace can be categorized as well preserved and restorated heritage building, eventhough the walls are covered with moss here and there. For me it is more beautiful and more well preserved than the main palace itself where the Royal Family still lives in there.

Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Nice for a short visit because it is situated in the Kraton. We didn't have to pay the entrance fee but were given a guide which we could not refuse. Although his English was quite difficult to understand we heard some interesting facts about the waterpalace. It seems to be closed in the afternoon.

Some ruins should stay ruined. Tamansari used to be a tumbled down palace whose nooks and crannies were occupied by families of batik artists. Visiting at night by lantern light was incredibly evocative. The restoration is pretty sterile. If they add plantings and make it more of a paradise garden, it has potential, but right now, it's a step in the wrong direction, IMHO.
Istana air ini cukup menarik untuk dikunjungi, kita bs melihat kolam taman air yg jernih tempat permandian putri2 raja jaman dahulu. Tapi tidak ada spot menarik lain yg ditawarkan selain itu.

I went to this water castle after seeing the Kraton; the palace. This was built around 1760 with the Portugese architecture and was used by a Sultan who had 30 wives.
It takes 30 minutes to get there if you walk from Malioboro Street. There are plenty of rickshaws offering rides to the palace and taman sari. I walked but it was so hot under the sun. 
The pool used by the wives seemed not that clean. However i liked the story behind it. At the entrance a guide followed me even before I asked. He explained to me about the history in brief and ended up in a Batik shop. I tipped him 10000 as it was just 10 minutes. The ticket price was around 1 dollar. I feel this place need renovation preserving the historic value. There is a settlement inside or adjoining the castle. Its strange.
Do not miss this place if you are in jogja. I would suggest for 1-2 hour slot in your schedule. I used a rickshaw on my way back for 15000 Idr. But I felt sad for the rider to be honest.
Enjoy your time in jogja.
Manjula

Review Text: Awal Februari 2014 lalu merupakan kunjungan kedua saya ke Taman Sari, Jogja. Sejak pertama kali datang, saya langsung jatuh hati pada tempat ini. Buat saya, aura historikal dan "mistis" sangat terasa. Pada kunjungan kedua ini, saya bersama pasangan. Tiket masuk hanya seharga 4rb rupiah. Kesalahan saya adalah membiarkan kami diikuti oleh tour guide lokal, padahal seharusnya tidak perlu karena kami berdua pernah kesana. Jika tidak ingin ditemani guide, kita bisa menolaknya secara halus dan tegas. Tapi lumayan deh waktu itu karena kami cuma berdua, bapak tour guide ini pun selalu menawarkan foto diberbagai tempat dan pengarah gaya plus fotografer yang lumayan bagus. Kami jadi punya beberapa foto layaknya foto pre wedding hehehe. Para tour guide ini biasanya adalah abdi dalem keraton. sebenarnya dengan memakai jasa mereka, kita sekaligus membantu mereka mencari nafkah dan rezeki, karena abdi dalem sekitar taman sari disini kebanyakan mencari nafkah dengan menjadi tour guide. Taman Sari ini terletak didalam pemukiman yang lumayan padat. Jika belum tahu, tidak menyangka ada istana air cantik ditengah pemukiman tersebut. Setelah berkeliling, jangan lupa untuk mengunjungi masjid bawah tanah yang terkenal dengan mimbar 5 arah mata angin.Sangat cantik dan unik kalau menurut saya. Letak mesjid ini harus melewati pemukiman abdi dalem melewati gang kecil. Sepanjang jalan, banyak rumah yang diubah menjadi workshop batik atau lukisan & kaligrafi.
A beautiful and quite place inside the city. You can find old pools and underground mosques. Not so many directional signs so it's easy to get lost inside.

Undoubtedly this was a magnificent complex in it's day but it is very dilapidated and well worth the investment of reconstruction. The architecture shows a strong Islamic influence particularly in the tunnels.
Interesting bit of history and architecture to see, we visited April 2014. It was a shame the pools aren't kept clean, there was algae up the walls and on the floor of the pools.
Iedereen spreekt over het Water Castle maar ik denk dat we op 10 minuten terug buiten waren.  Waarom ze hier met bussen naartoe komen, snappen we nog steeds niet?
ini wisata air yang katanya dulu adalah tempat pemandian raja, tapi menurut saya tidak ada yang menarik disini

After the disappointing Kraton, I was wondering if this would be any better. Oh yeah, A LOT better. Once you walk through the gates you are transported to another world, quiet, pink, watery and so restful and peaceful. While I was there it started to drizzle, but even that could not distract the other visitors or me from the tranquility of this place. It has NOT been disnified, some of the paint is peeling, and the pools are not immaculate. This only adds to the charm. The Water Castle looks old and dignified, and I spent the better part of 90 minutes just wandering around and sitting and taking photos. Rain or shine (the sun did eventually come out) time spent here will give you a sense of serenity and peace that is certainly lacking in so much of life.

Terletak tidak jauh dari alun-alun Yogyakarya, Taman Sari menawarkan destinasi wisata yang unik dengan menghadirkan istana air. Sangat cocok bagi kami yang melepas penat dari hiruk pikuk ibu kota. Sejak pintu masuk, ada beberapa tour guide yang menawarkan jasanya untuk menjelaskan tentang sejarah Taman Sari, dan tentunya membantu mengambilkan gambar bagi kami yang datang hanya berdua dari Jakarta.
Faktor Penarik: Ketertarikan Budaya, Ketertarikan Fasilitas, Ketertarikan Suasana
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
Это старая резиденция султана Джокьякарты, весьма интересное место. Найти его самим достаточно сложно, чем и пользуются местные горе-гиды. Они представляются местными жителями и радостно ведут  вас по окрестностям и магазинам. Так как цену они не называют да и гидами не представляются, платить или не платить- это ваше личное дело.
Бассейны  оказались на удивление фотогиеничными.
Kesan pertama saya kesana adalah, abdi dalem keraton itu kreatif kreatif! Banyak penjual lukisan dan barang barang lain disana. Agak sedikit mistis juga aih menurut saya. Hehehe

Kali ini perjalanan saya sampai di sebuah taman air di kompleks Kraton Jogjakarta. Jika anda memasuki kawasan ini dari arah pasar maka Anda akan bertemu dengan bangunan besar yang tidak beratap. Bangunan bergaya eropa ini merupakan tempat perjamuan istana, yang terbangun atas dua lantai. Sayangnya kita tidak bisa naik ke lantai atas mengingat bangunan sudah rapuh akibat tragedi gempa tahun 2006 silam. Jika anda bisa naik ke atas anda dapat menyaksikan pemandangan kota Jogja. Bahkan zaman dulu kata orang setempat jika kita menghadap ke selatan kita bisa menyaksikan laut kidul atau laut selatan dan jika kita menghadap ke utara kita bisa menyaksikan gunung merapi. 

Langkah kaki saya pindah ke bagian lain menyusuri kawasan pulau cemeti ini masuk ke dalam dan menjumpai sebuah terowongan yang menuju ke arah masjid. Terowongan ini istimewa karena berada di bawah air. Sebuah arsitektur dan perencanaan bangunan yang luar biasa waktu itu. Orang jaman dulu masih bisa mengatur bagaiman cahaya tetap masuk ke dalam terowongan meski lokasinya berada di bawah air, mereka dapat memperhitungkan keindahan arsitektur dan filosofi dari makna bangunan itu sendiri.

Saya kagum dengan rancangan bangunan masjid ini. Dirancang dengan bentuk melingkar di mana terdapat celah-celah jendela yang menghadap ke tengah bagian bangunan. Tengah bangunan merupakan sumur gemuling tempat ambil wudhu bagi jamaah. Bentuk bangunan memungkinkan suara imam pada saat memimpin sembahyang menjadi menggema dan terdengar oleh seluruh jamaah tanpa harus menggunakan pengeras suara. Masjid ini terdiri atas dua lantai dimana lantai atas untuk jamaah pria dan lantai bawah untuk jamaah wanita.

Beralih kecbagian lain tempat ini kita bisa menemukan dapur umum dan ruang makan. Di dapur umum ini terdapat sumur tua yang masih terdapat air di dalamnya. Banyak koin-koin yang dimasukkan di dalamnya. Entah ini tradisi yang biasa dilakukan orang-orang kebanyakan atau hanya sebuah simbol tertentu. Kemudian menuju kamar sultan, saya tertarik dengan model dipan yang dibangun dari batu bata dan semen kala itu. Sangat besar dan di bawahnya terdapat lubang untuk menempatkan bara api, tujuannya adalah untuk menghangatkan tempat tidur. Di bagian luar kamar Raja waktu itu adalah kebun bunga. Saya dapat membayangkan bagaimana indahnya tempat ini waktu itu. Layaknya sebuah cerita dongeng dari kerajaan yang termahsyur. 

Sekalipun anda masuk melalui pasar ngasem tetap saja Anda harus membeli tiket masuk, sangat terjangkau hanya IDR 3,000 dan tambahan IDR 1,000 jika anda membawa kamera. Banyak yang bisa kita ungkap dan ketahui atas warisan leluhur bangsa ini. Selamat berwisata budaya dan sejarah kawan.
Faktor Penarik: Ketertarikan Budaya, Ketertarikan Fasilitas, Ketertarikan Suasana
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Marlboro tickets only 5000 IDR don't know why ppl saying is more then that ! Good place with crystal clear water . Best to visit in afternoon open till 5 pm !

Review Text:
Taman Sari Yogyakarta atau Taman Sari Keraton Yogyakarta adalah situs bekas taman atau kebun istana Keraton Yogyakarta. Terletak tidak jauh dari kompleks Keraton Yogyakarta. Dari Keraton Yogyakarta ke Taman sari, butuh waktu kurang lebih hanya lima belas menit saja, jalan kaki. Sejarah Taman Sari Yogyakarta berawal dari pecahnya Kerajaan Mataram menjadi 2 kesultanan, yaitu Kesultanan Surakarta dan Kesultanan Yogyakarta. Gemericik air, keindahan arsitekturnya yang kuno, dan pemandangan yang menakjubkan membuat Taman Sari sangat mempesona. Kolam pemandian di area ini dibagi menjadi tiga yaitu Umbul Kawitan (kolam untuk putra-putri Raja), Umbul Pamuncar (kolam untuk para selir), dan Umbul Panguras (kolam untuk Raja). Pengunjung dapat menapaki anak tangga menuju lantai II Masjid Bawah Tanah Sumur Gumulung komplek Tamansari.
Tiket:
    Wisatawan Domestik: Rp 3.000
    Wisatawan Mancanegara: Rp 7.000
    Guide: nego (Rp 10.000 - Rp 20.000)
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Sangat disayangkan kebersihan lingkungan disekitar area wisata tsb kurang maksimal penanganannya, sehingga masih banyak/mudah diketemukan di mana2 misal bekas gelas/botol minuman air mineral ataupun bungkus rokok. Review Text: This place near the palace , just beside the palace, if you come from south place in prawirotaman area u can walk just around 15 minute, hidden but nice to visit
Not really impressed. After Merapi, we have some spare time. The Royal Palace was closed, so we came to Water Castle or Taman Sari.

Taman Sari (or Tamansari) Water Castle is about 500 meters from the Kraton palace. The castle used to be the royal garden of the sultanate. Built around 1750, the castle is believed to be an area for the former kings to rest, meditate, defence, and even to escape from the enemies. The castle is believed to be a place for the kings to accommodate their concubines.The entrance fee is RP 20,000 , with additional RP 1000 for camera. The castle is opened to visitors 9 am - 3:30 pm daily.

There are several elements that influence the architecture of the building complex of Taman Sari 's, including the influence of Hindu and Buddhist, Javanese and Islamic, Chinese, Portuguese and European style, can be seen from some parts of the building. 

But the problem is the maintenence. Nobody seems to take care of the place. 

it is actually the bathing place for the sultan and his cumbupines. Nowdays you find alot of old wodden residential building and most occupied by people. the place looks run down.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
if you come here you can expect unique architecture of old javanese royalties bathing place. 
the place is not so well maintained though. nothing much to explore here but it complement the visit to Kraton.

After having visited the temples around Yogya, the state of the baths at the water castles was very disappointing.  It is a beautiful place, with exceptional Portuguese architecture, but why is maintenance non-existent?  There are so many people sitting around, why are they not involved in keeping the place nice, rather than trying to hustle you to buy batiks and other-such??  We were very disappointed.

The Taman Sari comprises three separate swimming pools for the Sultan, the sultanas and concubines and the third for the princes and princesses. A three storey roomed structure separates the sultans pool from the other two and it is said that the sultan would ascend to the top of the divide to fling a handkerchief into the middle pool and whichever lucky lady managed to retrieve this would be invited to join him on his side. Rooms within the structure provide space for the preparation, including messages with scented oils of the lady for what usually followed. 

Overall a delightful short stop, if only for an insight into the lives of Javanese rulers of old. Visitors to the Taman Sari might also want to consider visiting the underground Mosque a short 15 minute walk away.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: This was a disappointing landmark to visit. There is too much hype & the reality leaves one disappointed. But they have a lovely emporium on premise - would advise visitors to shop here - good quality products at reasonable rates.

Once you enter the water village from the main road, you'll be walking around houses before you can find anything interesting. So if you can get a guide from the entrance, you'll be better off. 

1st - Visit the underground mosque which has Roman and Chinese influence. 
2nd - Walk over to the rubble remains of the "istana", or king's palace
3rd - Walk over to Tamansari, the water castle which housed the king's concubines. There are influences of Hindu, Buddhism and Islam in the architecture of Tamansari so keep your eyes peeled to spot each touch of religion. 

Accessible via public transport called "Halte" which is a bus system all around Jogja. Don't worry, these buses are clean and not dodgy.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Jika kita menyukai wisata sejarah dan mengagumi arsitektur kuno, ini adalah tempat wisata yang tepat. kita akan menemukan sebuah bangunan pemandian jaman kerajaan dulu. Kita akan terkagum-kagum dengan bangunan yang masih kokoh  berdiri dan bagaimana mereke memikirkan detail dan keindahan serta kemewahan kelas kerajaan. Mereka dijaman dulu pun sudah memikirkan sebuah tempat untuk spa dan merawat diri. Harga tiket masuk ketempat ini pun sangat murah, jika anda berkunjung ke Jogja jangan melewatkan tempat ini untuk dikunjungi karena tepat berada di kota satu kompleks dengan keraton.
Faktor Penarik: Ketertarikan Budaya, Ketertarikan Fasilitas, Ketertarikan Suasana
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: This was my favourite sight in Yogyakarta.  It was as impressive as I was expecting it to be.  I spent most of my time wanting to jump in as it looked so inviting!  The guide was probably very knowledgeable, but his accent was so strong that I was unable to understand anything he said (and I teach over here)!  However, he took some great photos!

Water palace is where the king of Yogyakarta used to live, it is a little dirty but still a nice place to go if you're ever in Yogyakarta. There was no fee when I went and no tour guide is required to enjoy

C'est une agréable petite visite. J'avais le guide de mon voyage mais je ne sais pas si ça vaut la peine d'en payer un pour une si courte visite. Ce n'est pas mal du tout et les petites ruelles aux alentours nous entrainent dans un dépaysement total et en toute sécurité.

Taman Sari is a huge complex. Other years we had visited the main water castle, the underground water tunnel, this time we visited the ruins above one of the water tunnels. Hopefully this section will be going into restoration sooner than later. I overheard from one of the tourist guides that it was the plan. It's a beautiful and meaningful place, but most local young tourists we saw who were there didn't respect much of the place. We didn't see anyone trashing the place, but it's unfortunate that people were throwing garbage as they wished. The old walls were also full of graffitis...
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: The city council and the Kraton should give more attention to the site since it's worth every history that city has. The site is left unattended and we can find rubbish in almost every corner of the site.  It really too bad!  But it still worth a visit to learn the story behind it existent.

Ke jogja saat iburan akhir tahun/liburan anak sekolah sungguh ramai sekali. Sungguh tidak efisien kalau menggunakan mobil keliling malioboro & kraton dan sekitarnya. 
Saya menyewa becak fasilitas hotel dengan harga 30rb. dari situ keliilng jogja salah satunya Taman sari. Setelah membayar tiket kita bertemu dengan jajaran tour guide. terserah anda untuk menggunakan atau tidak. Masuk ke pintu utama anda akan mencium bau yang khas. dan kemudian masuk ke dalam kompleks pemandian, disitu kita berfoto2 ria, dan kebelakang lagi ada bangunan kecil yg langsung bertetanggaan dengan rumah warga. 
Tidak terlalu lama disini karena memang kompleks taman sari tidak terlalu besar.
for sure a place you should visit while you are in Yogya. Explore the inner city of the kraton area and enjoy this jewel of old palace architecture.

The water castle is just adjacent of the Kraton and its worth a visit if you are already there. Entrance is only IDR2000 each person. There are many volunteers who acts as guides. Just tip them IDR10,000 for bringing you around. The castle grounds is old and fairly well maintained as could be expected. The castle is basically a place where the Sultan and his wife relaxes and swim. There is an underground mosque as well. Great for photography though

Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: I like it though not very big but just pool found.  It is a so relaxing environment after 10-15 minutes walk under the heat after visiting Kraton Yogyakarta.  Visitors here just chit chat with smile on their faces and take a rest at the pool side and stairs.  Don't miss to claim up the tower and a bird view of the pool.  Imagine you were the King to choose the beauty queen.  A happy moment here.

We walked about 10 mins to get here and at the end of it were not sure if it was worth it.  The idea that the Sultan had a tower from where he would watch and choose from lots of pretty women was novel . We felt that the structure itself is not that impressive.

I'm not sure if it was because it was high noon and the sun was at its hottest but the vision of this water park was truly an oasis!  The place was well kept and you have liberty to go all around to discover secret tunnels and rooms... allowing you to better imagine how beautiful the place was at its peak. Be careful of people approaching you to take you to or around the castle, they will always expect money in return so make sure its clear in the beginning.  Also, the small streets around the castle are beautiful so its worth your time to go around and get lost a bit.

Так получилось, что по пути в водный замок нас одолел местный "гид", который уверял, что он бесплатно нам все покажет, так как ему с нами по пути и ему просто хочется поделиться гордостью своего города с приезжими издалека туристами. Ни намеки, ни заявления прямым текстом, что он не получит ни рупии, его не смутили. Зря.
Этот товарищ показал нам много мест, которые мы сами бы не нашли никак. Виды с хорошим обзором, неплохие комментарии. Конечно он заводил нас каждые пятнадцать минут в "лавку моего дяди/брата/соседа, которые изготавливали куклы исключительно лично для султана", мы, разумеется, ничего не покупали. Нам не нужно было. Каждый раз мы объясняли ему, что мы бекпекеры и нам громоздкие куклы - как ежу футболка. Но впустую его бодрость исчезала не спеша. 
Сама водная крепость весьма симпатична, а фотографии так вообще прекрасные. Посетить стоит.

It's an old monument with a underground mosque. Nothing fascinating..just a long walk...The construction and story behind the mosque if you have a good guide is interesting. If you go to visit the Sultan Palace, this place is walking distance so might as well see it since you are there. But if you are hard pressed on time, it's ok to skip...

The pools looked dirty and not regularly cleaned. There was little water in them. It was disappointing to see almost every wall in the castle graffitied and the whole place looked poorly maintained. Considering there is an entry fee, it looks like nothing is spent on maintaining this historical site. Very disappointing.

The accient water castle and the tunell was impressive. You cant stop your brain to thinking what was the history behind the castle and tunnel. The escavation is wasnt completed, but this attraction still interesting

Most “monuments” in Asia seem to be one that can be spotted and enjoyed from the vehicles, this is one of them. You don’t need to stop by to have a view because this monument is a roundabout, so many vehicles pass by non stop.
If you want to buy Jogja bakpia, it's really delicious at BIBIR69, or if you want to go for a walk to Tugu Yogyakarta, where the atmosphere is really delicious, like at BIBIR 69

This 25m Pilar is located on a roundabout of a busy intersection about a kilometre north of jalan Malioboro. 

It was originally built in I755 by Sri Sultan Hamengkubuwono in the spirit of unity of the people. 

The covering photo is basically what you will see if you come to visit it. It’s not really approachable as it’s located in the middle of a busy roundabout. Locals seem to appreciate it anyway as there are a number of people who stop by here at night to get photos in front of the monument. 

The coffee store and cafe Kebon Ndalem is located on this roundabout and serves pretty decent coffee and Indonesian food if you wanted to take in the view.
Sinceramente nulla di che, un semplice monumento impossibile da fotografare o vedere perchè si trova in un incrocio super trafficato da cui parte la via Malioboro.

Tugu yg sekarang dipagar karena untuk melindungi dari ketidakramahan pengunjung yang sembarangan memperlakukan ini tugu, hiks. The locals called it Tugu Golong Gilig (Spirit of togetherness) with a hint of anti-colonialism during the founding of the Yogyakarta Kingdom. It represents the unity between the King and his people. After being destroyed by an earthquake in 1867, it was reconstructed in 1889 by the Dutch and renamed Tugu Pal Putih (White Pole).  The Dutch tried to erase the philosophy of togetherness between lay people and the king. The Indonesians have a tradition of university students to hug and kiss the monument after their graduation. All in all, it is the representation of Yogya and so it is worth a visit.

Tugu Pal Putih selesai dibangun oleh Sultan Hemengku Buwana ke VII pada tanggal 03 Oktober 1889 dengan pelaksana pembangunan  YPF Van Brussel Opzichter Waterstaat (warga negara Belanda).
Tinggi Tugu Pal Putih adalah  11.95 m dengan rincian :
1. Selasar 0.40 m
2. Kaki 1.70 m
3. Tubuh 3.75 m
4. Kepala 4.60 m
5. Kemuncak 1.5 m

Sampai saat ini Tugu Pal Putih masih berdiri dengan megah. Dan menjadi spot pengambilan gambar baik oleh wisatawan lokal maupun wisatawan mancanegara.

the monument have a great importance in Javanese cosmology as it marks the straight line between the realm of the spirits living in the south sea, the sultan palace and the kingdom of the spirits dwelling in the peak of Mount Merapi.

The monument itself is absolutely unremarkable. I lived in a hotel nearby and passed it like ten times a day without giving it a thought. There isn't a reason to travel to see the monument by itself unless you have some other plans in the neighbourhood. 
However, if you happen to be there, cross the road, and find the best coffee in Yogyakarta at a little street stall. Yes, it looks absolutely unremarkable as well, and it might even seem kind of dirty for some, but it's so worth it. They speak very very basic English, just enough to understand how you take your coffee and tell you the prices. Ask for kopi joss - it's coffee with coal - and get the unique experience. I like it with sugar, very sweet, but they offer milk as well. It doesn't only taste great, but it's also super-fun to watch how they make it, a piece of coal hissing in your glass. Take your coffee, and sit at one of the benches, or go sit right on the floor covered with straw mats and share it with a lazy cat trying to hide from the afternoon heat. It's perfect, and you'll come back for more, just as I did.

モニュメントのある「マリオボロ通り（Jalan Malioboro）」は、ジョグジャカルタの中心的な目抜通り。ジョグジャカルタ王国を収めていたスルタン家の住む王宮「クラトン」まで続く一本道で、観光客向けの露店がずらりと並んでいます。特別な行事の際にはたくさんの花で飾られたことから、サンスクリット語で「花飾り」を意味する「マリオボロ」と名付けられました。現在でも伝統的なアンドン(馬車)やベチャ（三輪人力車）が走り、昼夜を問わず賑わうメインストリートです。夕方になると「レセハン」と呼ばれる屋台が地面にゴザのようなマットを広げ、ナシゴレンやカレー、グドゥと呼ばれる伝統的なジャワ料理を地元の人たちに混ざって食べることができます。

Tugu Jogja or the Jogja Monument is the landmark that is closely linked to Yogyakarta. There is a tradition to hug and kiss this monument after finishing the study in a university.

Also when it was built it served to symbolize the unity of the Sultan and his subjects. After it's destruction in the 1860's the Dutch used the opportunity and gave it it's nowadays look thus trying to drive a wedge between the Sultan and his people. Didn't quite work out.

The Plaosan temple complex actually consists of two complexes, the Plaosan Lor temple with its twin main temples and the further Plaosan Kidul temple. As far as I understand, experts don't quite agree on whether the Lor and Kidul belong to one sanctuary. We came across the Candi (= temple) Plaosan Lor while cycling. Built in the 9th century on the initiative of a princess from the then ruling Sailendra Dynasty. The Plaosan Lor temples are located in the middle of an agricultural area with numerous rice fields etc., near the village of Busigan, in Central Java, not far from Yogyakarta. The Candi Plaosan Lor consists of two almost identical Buddhist main temples, one female, one male. These main temples were once surrounded by countless smaller temples, statues and stupas .. many have been decayed by the numerous eruptions of the Merapi and other volcanoes and the accompanying earthquakes. In the forecourt of the restored twin temples surrounded by some repaired outbuildings, there are large piles of stone, mostly with reliefs. This is material for repair of the other collapsed buildings. This rebuilding process will undoubtedly take many years. Curiously, this complex Plaosan Lor is a shrine for both Buddhists and Hindus. Bridal couples come here to beg for a prosperous marriage. In the event of fertility problems, one comes to beg help from the gods. When progeny is realized, one naturally comes to give thanks again for the divine assistance. A glance at the Candi Plaosan Lor makes you realize what a huge job it is to restore such a temple complex after centuries of decline.

Review Text:
The Plaosan Temple is a mere 6 mins drive away from the Prambahan Temple.

From its architecture, characteristic of its temple top is Hinduism, while the base is Buddhism, thus at first sight i cannot figure out whether Plaosan is a Buddhist or
Hindu Temple. 

But as the story unfold, as differences of religion and ideology cannot separate the love of a Hindu King and his Buddhist Queen, to support and strengthen one another,  this Temple is built to reflect their love which can be seen in the architecture of Plaosan Temple. Hence the physical structure of the temple is also a marriage & union of their individual belief/religion. 

The Plaosan Complex consists of 2 main temples surrounded by stone walls. Surrounding the stone walls are mostly ruins of the ancillary temples.  
The Temples are ornamented with decorations carved with beautiful details. 
The stairs up the temple has dragon head ornaments on its banister. 

Sadly about half the temple structures were damaged by the previous major earthquakes. Nevertheless, the Temple Complex is peaceful and quiet, Dwarapala statues can be seen standing, like guards on sentry duty.  

There were no any street peddlers touting or to telling us to  buy their products. Very peaceful , not crowded with spectacular view of the whole green land !!
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Therefore, my first impression of the temple was, it been started to build during the Hinduism period in Java and the templet completed build when the Buddhist teaching took over in Java.

However, after spoke to a local guy, I understand that this temple been purposely builded as combination of Hinduism and Buddish architecture.

Each temple has been diverted into 3 chambers which placed for God Shiwa, God Vishnu and God Brahma statues. In fact, there are 2 statues in each chamber, Buddha statues in Hinduism structure and vice versa.

If you plan to visit this beautiful temples during the dry season, bring along plenty of plain water, sunblock, UV protection lotion, sunglasses and hot or even umbrella. The weather is extremely hot during the dry season

Candi Plaosan, also known as the 'Plaosan Complex', is one of the Buddhist temples located in Bugisan village, Prambanan district, Klaten Regency, Central Java, Indonesia, about a kilometer to the northwest of the renowned Hindu PrambananTemple.
Candi Plaosan covers an area of 2,000 square meters with an elevation of 148 meters above sea level. The Dengok River is located nearby, about 200 meters away. Candi Plaosan is surrounded by paddy fields along with vegetation such as banana and corn.
Plaosan temple was built in the mid 9th century by Sri Kahulunnan or Pramodhawardhani, the daughter of Samaratungga, descendant of Sailendra Dynasty, and who was married to Rakai Pikatan in the Hindu tradition.
The Plaosan complex currently comprises two Buddhist temples, Plaosan Lor and Plaosan Kidul 
The inscriptions and images of Plaosan Lor and Kalasan have raised questions about the origins of complex and the relationships between the images found and the religious complexity of the area when the structures were created.
The temples are separated by a road; Plaosan Lor is located in the North and Plaosan Kidul in the South. Plaosan Lor consists of two main temples and an open area known as a mandapa. Both temples have an entrance, a gate, and the guardian statue known as Dwarapala. Plaosan Lor and Plaosan Kidul are considered to originally be one complex.

Prambanan and Borobudur are great but I do love this temple as well. The location is not that far from Prambanan and it is really amazing. If you ask me, I def. will tell you to go to this place.
On the way to Prambanan, Plaosan temple is a must-do. Nice place to take nice photos especially on shiny days.

Que dire de plus, que Magnifique. 
C'est vraiment fabuleux d'avoir pu conserver ce type de construction et de continuer à l'entretenir. 
A ne pas manquer.

Quand on évoque Yogyakarta, c'est Borobudur qui vient en tête en premier.
Or Prambanan n'est pas en reste, bien au contraire : magnifique site Hindou, facile à visiter avec de multiples angles pour de belles photos, et une superbe vue sur le volcan.
Ne pas manquer le coucher du soleil !

Ketika pertama kesini letak candi yang agak menjorok kekampung. Tetapi view ternyata cukup menarik. Dekat persawahan, saran kalau ingin lebih menarik berfoto dikala pagi dan sore hari akan lebih menarik.

Pour y aller de Yogyakarta, prenez un bus public (faisable et bon marché) au lieu de prendre un "tour"

Le tour se termine, comme pour le Borobodur, par un passage par les "souks". Au mois d'août, un festival de jazz a lieu à proximité, ce qui gâche le charme et l'authenticité.
definitely recomended on sunset, what a golden hour. Especially this time around when the weather is dry and nice

De nombreuses tours disséminées sur un sol poussiéreux et d'un accès difficile.Il y a des nombreuses marches très hautes a franchir pour accéder à l'intérieur. Mieux vaut ne pas avoir de problèmes de genoux...

Joli visite.
Un après midi bien passe dans l'histoire du passe.
une bonne demi heure de Yogyakarta ..

Review Text:

You should defenitely visit this tempel so jou can enjoin the silence and quietness.

Jika kemari pada siang hari, jangan lupa gunakan sun block dan topi, karena terik matahari berasa sekali. Disekitar candi banyak puing-puing batu yang bekas dibongkar para penggali harta. Sangat disayangkan sekali peninggalan budaya cantik ini dirusak karena keserakahan manusia. Di dalam candi ada arca Budha. Karena memang candi ini adalah candi Budhist. Karena cantiknya dan juga ada mitos bahwa pasangan yang ke candi ini maka hubungannya akan langgeng, candi ini sering dijadikan tempat untuk foto prewedding.
Make sure you visit this beautiful temple, not so many tourist so you can explore more, especially if you visit at Sunrise. So romantic.

Un must-see si vous passez par Yogyakarta. Bien plus impressionnant que Borobudur !
À faire pour le coucher de soleil absolument !

Facilement accessible en bus public depuis le centre ; facilement accessible via une voiture (application GrabCar ++) ou scooter. Parking pas cher.

pemandangan di sekitar nya juga bagus, fotonya dari sisi luar.

Another wonderful temple in the area, you should definitely visit if you are in the area or visiting other temples in the area.

Review Text: muy linda experiencia entre todos los templos que recorrí ese día, hay algunos que son más imponente que otros, pero todos exquisitos!

Main place is wonderful and very nice to visit. You can enter in each temple separately and find in each a sculpture of the local divinity. 

It is possible to take a small train to visit the rest of the « parc » but is not mandatory as the main temple is really the most worthy. Moreover, the train does not stop at the other, except a the small museum which is really not necessary to visit.

Film très intéressant à voir a l'entrée
Acces facile par Bus du centre ville

If you are interested in history and mythology, include this temple in your list of ‘things to do in Yogyakarta’. Candi Plaosan, also known as the ‘Plaosan Complex’, is one of the Buddhist temples located in Bugisan village, about a kilometer from the renowned Hindu Prambanan Temple. The Plaosan complex currently comprises two Buddhist temples, Plaosan Lor and Plaosan Kidul.

Today, only two statues of Bodhisattva seated on each sides of each rooms, flanked by an empty pedestal. Rows of exquisite carvings are found adorning the outer walls, with the majority of them being male. Smaller and less occurring carvings by the windows represent female figures.

IDR3000 per visit to the plaosan temple where there's much less people vs IDR337500 per visit to the prambanan temple complex with so many tourists, you do the math.
It's more or less the same within a much smaller complex, but you get to see 2 beautiful stupas, and right behind that the Merapi Mountain. Stunning.

Unique temple combining elements of Hindu & Buddha. Built in 10 century to compliment the marriage of a Hindu king & Buddha queen, a harmony of unity. The complex consists of twin main temple buildings to represent the male (king) and female (queen), surrounded by smaller temples as well as a pendopo area. We hire a guide to explain the history of this temple and gain real understanding about it and really appreciate it at the end. Eventhough not as majesty as Borobudur and Prambanan, this smaller yet unique temple worth a visit.

It was great to visit this temple. It's not nearly as busy as at the Prambanan and the entrance fee for foreigners is very low (3000 rupiah per person, whereas the Prambanan is 340000 per person). The temple is beautifully situated among the rice fields. There are plenty of places where you can buy souvenirs or something to drink. The temple itself is rather small but lovely to see. It's also fun that you can go inside, something that (as far as I can remember from 5 years ago) is not allowed at the Prambanan.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: A cause de la chaleur il est préférable de visiter le cite tôt le matin. 6 h c'est bon.  En en plus vous n' aurez pas a chercher le miment quand vous serez seule dans le cadre. Java est une île le plus peuplé d'Indonésie😜

Compared to the Borobudur temple, the entrance fees for this temple is cheap. We paid about IDR 3k/pax. This is just a small temple with very few tourists. Quite a lot of rubble from fallen temple structures. Nice to visit away from the crowds.
Get a grab and go! Very small entrance fee and no one was there. A real cool ruin to explore and read about on your phone while there.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
according to our guide, Candi Plaosan is supposedly worth visiting because unlike other temples, it's a combined temple of both Buddhism and Hinduism. But frankly speaking, as we've dropped by after visiting Borobudur and Prambanan, Plaosan just pales in comparison for us. And we couldn't really make out the distinctive difference (on the outside) between Plaosan (with both Buddhist and Hindu culture) and the other two temples. 
A good thing is that this temple is really quiet (there was only 1 lone traveller there when we arrived) and you can almost have the entire (small) complex to yourself if you're lucky. entrance fee is also only a fraction of that for borobudur and prambanan. However, it's really so small that we merely spent half a hour (max) over here.
masuk ke plaosan gratis dan tidak kalah indah jika kamu sedang tidak ada budget untuk ke prambanan, karena candi ini jaraknya hanya 1 km dari Prambanan

Prambanan fait partie de ces endroits emprunts d'un mysticisme  troublant. C'est grand, bien entretenu et on imagine aisément la splendeur et la grandeur de ce lieu à son apogée. Nous avions un guide francophone qui nous a bien aidé à comprendre la complexité de cette religion et à comprendre chaque bâtiment de ce magnifique temple

Lokasinya tak jauh dari kompleks Candi Prambanan, Sewu dan Bubrah. Secara administratif berada di Desa Bugisan yang masuk wilayah Klaten, Jawa Tengah. Plaosan terbagi dalam dua kelompok yakni Plaosan Lor (utara) dan Kidul (selatan). Keduanya sama-sama memiliki banyak candi perwara selain candi utama yang besar. Plaosan berdenah empat persegi panjang dan bertingkat seperti Candi Sari.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
Memang candi ini tidak sekondang Candi Prambanan maupun Candi Borobudur yang sudah kondang kaloka sak nuswantoro itu. Meski sama-sama dibangun pada masa Mataram Kuno. 

Menurutku candi di Klaten ini keren. Terutama filosofinya. Karena Candi ini adalah Simbol Kerukunan Beragama dan Cinta.

Sebab, Candi Plaosan adalah sebuah candi yang dibangun oleh Rakai Pikatan  (beragama Hindu) pada abad ke-9. Candi dengan arsitektur perpaduan Budha-Hindu ini diperuntukkan buat sang Prameswari, Sri Pramudyawardani (beragama Budha).

Juga simbol persatuan dua wangsa penguasa Mataram Kuno (Rakai Pikatan dari Wangsa Sanjaya, Pramodyawardani dari Wangsa Sailendra).
Très beau temple, mais un peu déçue par rapport à Borobudur. Par contre, beaucoup moins de monde. On peut louer des vélos ou une voiturette pour faire le parc et voir les autres temples.

Went with 4yrs and it was a good stop before going to Prambanan for sunset and after our 2hrs drive from Yogyakarta. Kid enjoyed running around and looking to the spiders and critters around the temple. It well kept and the site clean and probably managed.
 Worth visiting before going to the big temple.

Je conseille de prendre un guide à l'entrée,  il y a toujours une possibilité de trouver le guide qui vous expliquera le site, l'histoire, la découverte du site, les techniques employées, tous les curieux en auront pour leur argent. 150000rp pour 7 personnes + d'une heure..
un piccolo tempio con nulla di originale ma già che si è qui consiglio una visita perchè comunque è carino ne apprezzerete la semplicità

It's about a 10 min walk from the Prambanan temple complex. We went on a hot day and it is a fairly small temple which is thankfully not overrun with tourists. Much of it has undergone restoration, so it is smaller and relatively peaceful.
a combined of Hindu ad Buddha temple.the local called it as twin temple as well.  should be maintained to show the history of this place.

très belle surprise, j'ai même préféré à borobudur car le site est vaste et est composé de plusieurs monuments, dédiés tantôt à un dieu tantôt à un autre.. c'est splendide !
ouvre à 6h, coûte 337.000 par adulte.
allez y a l'ouverture pour être tranquilles, n'oubliez pas candi sewu (sur le même site et inclus dans le billet), puis prenez votre moto pour vous balader dans les rizières autour, vers la cascade sri getuch, c'est magique !

I went there after seeing Prambanan temple (I took a scooter there) - it's much smaller, parts of it are not really restored (which makes it interesting for me), there are much fewer tourists so the visit is more relaxed. I definitely recommend it!
When you visit Prambanan Temple, come early at the opening, because Sewu Temple is in the same area, same ticket and Plaosan Temple is 10 min drive from Prambanan but less people

One of the must see candi in Yogyakarta and it is spectacular.

Review Text:
Kenapa saya bilang Kemurahannya?

Plaosan Temple, also known as the 'Plaosan Complex', is one of the Buddhist temples located in Bugisan village, Prambanan district, Klaten Regency, Central Java, Indonesia, about a kilometer to the northwest of the renowned Hindu Prambanan Temple. Plaosan Temple is instagramable view and have many photo spot, also the history about the temple is really romantic. Recommended to visit.

Review Text:

Second, usually no crowd in here, so I found it more enjoyable.

Entrance is only IDR3000. It is so quiet and not many tourists know about this place. Thus it makes it so special because we can freely take photos and enjoy ourselves strolling at each corner at our own pace. Beautiful, big compound. Love it!

candi ini merupakan candi candi cantik yang ada di dekat candi prambanan,,candi ini merupakan peninggalan masa lampau dan cagar budaya, candi ini menyimpang keindahan tata arsitektur yang luar biasa rumit dan indah

Twee kleine tempels gelegen in de buurt van de Prambanan. Hoewel klein zijn deze 2 budistish tempels de moeite van een bezoek waard.nauwelijks toeristen.Het verhaal over de bouw is interessant en de meeste beelden zijn hoed intact

menarik sekali untuk mengunjungi tempat tempat bersejarah ini dengan tidak merusak dan mengambil barang barang yang ada di candi ini agar bisa bertahan sampai anak cucu kita nanti untuk selalu bangga akan INDONESIA

As we are Temple junkies  and selfie crazy this Temple was OK for us. Not large . Younger normal tourists may not be enamored with this place.
Temple agréable mais nous n'avons pas eu de chance car nous y sommes allé en fin de journée et l'éclairage n'était pas propice aux photos ! Balade agréable dans le temple et ses environs !

Moyen de s'y rendre en bus local pour pas cher avec le Transjoga (environ 3000rupiah/pers). Depuis le terminus du bus, il faut environ marcher 1km pour se rendre à l'entrée du site (le site est proche mais entouré de barrières à contourner). Il faut longer les grilles en allant dans la direction de la mosquée et ensuite tourner à gauche.
Ne ratez pas les magnifiques temples autours du Prambanan (entre autre candi sewu) qui sont également très beaux et surtout avec beaucoup moins de touristes.
Pour manger, un resto est présent sur le site et proposait ce jour là un buffet à 50 000rupiah/pers. Très bon marché donc et la nourriture proposée était bonne (nasi et mie goreng, sauce cacahouète, crudités, tempé, tofu, poulet frit,...) Eau comprise dans le prix.

Review Text:
Just 2.5 kilometres from Prambanan Temple is the beautiful Plaosan Lor and Kidul Temples.  While there is no denying Prambanan Temple is spectacular, we both preferred the beautiful Plasoan North Temple over Prambanan, this was partly due to having it all to ourselves with only a couple of other people visiting, as opposed to the heavy tourist traffic Prambanan receives, this made it more intimate and was definitely more peaceful.  We spent almost as long here as we did at Prambanan Temple.

The Buddhist Plaosan Temple Complex was built 9th century by Queen Pramodhawardhani, wife of Rikai Piatan who was responsible for Prambanan Temple.   The site is split into two, with Plaosan Lor (north) and Plaosan Kidul (south), the north section has more to see and the south section, just across the road less than 100 metres away is a lot smaller.  

The Plaosan North Temple consists of two temples with external bas-reliefs, while the interior has statues, bas-reliefs and niches.  The compound also has temple gates, stupas, shrines and wall.  Originally there were an additional 174 temples consisting of 58 small temples and 116 stupa, which have crumbled and now form a wall of rubble on the site.  The two temples each have two Dwarapala (temple guardian) statues facing each other which are very charming, despite their fierce looks and weapons.

The Plaosan South Temple is nowhere as impressive as its cousin across the road but still worth a quick look.  The main temples have long gone and there are only a handful of smaller temples left.

A donation is required and covers the visit to both Plaosan Lor and Plaosan Kidul and a book is also signed on entry.  

If in the area and you dismiss this site, you have truly missed out on an absolute treasure.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
This temple is simply stunning for two reasons: one, for the architecture itself, which is worth dropping by even though the temple is quite a detour away from the main touristy points, and second, the road that takes you to the temple is breathtaking. 
There are green rice fields on both sides, so if you're in a car or on a bike, you wouldn't know which way to look faster so that you see as much as possible. If you're in love with rice fields this is the perfect trip very picturesque and beautiful.

Par contre musique boumboum a fond, des tentes kitches partout, Un immense panneau publicitaire "Tupperware" juste devant le temple principal, aucune indication ou information pertinente et des daims/chevreuils parqués au fin de cette foire qui massacre Un site spirituel, culturel et religieux. Quel dommage!
