Untuk bangunan candi tidak begitu banyak, dikarenakan hanya reruntuhan candi yang bisa kita lihat. Tetapi tidak mengurangi rasa untuk berkunjung kesini. Banyak taman-taman yang apik dan bisa kita nikmati setelah lelah mengelilingi candi.

Kompleks Candi Ratu Boko cukup luas untuk dinikmati dalam waktu yang lama, ada beberapa lokasi yang terpisah dalam kompleks. Semua memiliki sejarah dan cerita yang menarik. Tidak pernah bosan meskipun sudah beberapa kali kesini.  Suasana pagi hari saat matahari terbit ataupun saat matahari terbenam disini sangatlah indah, apalagi saat bulan purnama.

Memotret untuk keperluan pribadi tidak masalah, tetapi untuk komersial harus mendapat ijin dan ada biaya lagi yang harus dikeluarkan.

the beautiful place to enjoy sunset and there are many spots to take sunset pics. you should go before 4 pm so you can go around first and save a spot to take sunset pics. Actually, there is a trip for prambanan temple and ratu boko, you can ask the information in prambanan and take the shuttle bus from prambanan.

Me and my wife deciding to go to Ratu Bokok and cancelled for Prambanan. I thought i it was mistakes but wowwww... It was nice seeing everyone from the top of temple. and also it was the great spot for photography (my wife told that)

Thanks Central Java Government for revitalize Ratu Bokok into the good one.

It's been so long that I planned to visit this place, but everytime I go to Jogja it's always being cancelled and most of the reasons are because the bad weather. Finally, in February 2014, my plan was succeeded. I finally visited this temple with my brother(cousin actually). Thank you so much for you brother for making my plans come true hahahaba :) :D Ratu Boko Temple is located on the top of the hills just south of Prambanan Temple. It's accessible and easily reached, especially by motorbike. At glance, the panorama from the temple is very beautiful. If it's sunny and the weather is good, we'll be able to see Prambanan Temple, Jogja-Solo Railway, Adi Sucipto Airport, ricefields, and houses above the hills. It's very beautiful. Talking about the temple, actually Ratu Boko Temple is very large. Sadly, visitors sometimes only visit until the gate or "gapura" and seldom take a look or walk around this area. Ratu Boko Temple is not only the gate itself, it still has a lot of things to see such as the bathing pool, the wall, the cave, etc. And i was so glad to be there with my cousin because he really knows Ratu Boko Temple well. He tokd me about the history, the places, and many more. It seemed like I didn't need to pay a tourguide at that time. The weather was good and very hot so don't forget to bring your own hat, drink, and handkerchief before visiting Ratu Boko Temple. The ticket price is Rp25.000,00. Sounds expensive right? But it's worthed because the temple is very precious and beautiful to be visited. You'll be amazed with the panorama and the temple itself. Don't forget to keep your attitude during visiting Ratu Boko Temple. A smart traveller is the one who respect the place they visit. Are you curious? Just come to Jogja and Ratu Boko.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
L unico vantaggio è la vista sulla valle ma non aspettatevi nulla di romantico.

Si vede il pranbanam ma mooooolto piccolo e per fare una foto avrete bisogno di uno zoom molto potente superiore al 200mm

Alla mattina e alla sera se limpido dalla terrazza si puo ammirare la sagoma del vulcano merapi.

Le rovine del palazzo nn sono molto interessanti se avete visto in giornata il pranbanan....

Positif:

Sunset yang sangat indah, pelajaran sejarah, explore hal hal baru yang jarang dikunjungi wisatawan

Negatif:

Karena luasnya tempat harus mempunyai stamina yang cukup :)
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Go there on a day that the locals are not coming. A couple of very interesting statues; On top of a mountain.

Been to Indonesia so many times and my first time up to see Ratu Boko - unbelievable. It was virtually deserted and lunch at the lookout was fantastic. I could have spent a whole day here meditating! Superb! It is a must see. Overwhelmed by the planning and placement of the structures.

Menikmati Keraton Ratu Boko dari depan sampai akhir sungguh mengagumkan, situs sejarah sungguh dijaga dan dirawat luar biasa. Pemandangannya keren, banyak gazebo untuk bersantai. Melewati Keraton Ratu Boko lewat hutan belakang subuh-subuh memberikan pengalaman yang luar biasa. Pertama berkunjung ke Keraton Ratu Boko malam Selasa, 30 Desember 2013. Gak bisa jalan ke area candinya, tapi bisa nyantae-nyantae dulu di Restonya.

ジョグジャカルタの景色が一望できます。
遺跡がある敷地もけっこう広く全てを見て回るには1時間以上かかると思います。

Two years ago, I've been here and feels so authentic. But, at the second visit, it still underconstruction, you cant capture anything. Rp25rb for Indonesian and Rp50rb for foreigners isnt worth at the time.
if you visit this temple better to visit in the afternoon waiting for sunset, you will have the fantastic view, and also you can try the restaurant too

Jujur ini adalah pertama kalinya saya mengunjungi kompleks Candi Ratu Boko setelah hampir 8 tahun tinggal di kota gudeg. Pemandangan indah disertai hawa yang sejuk sangat tepat untuk dinikmati bersama keluarga dan orang terdekat di sore hari. Sejenak saya membayangkan betapa bahagianya keluarga raja yang dahulu membangun kompleks candi ini dapat menikmati waktu di tempat se-spektakuler ini. Perfect!
need luck for a nice sunset, can be cloudy. nice small temple, try to combine with prambanan temple.

Main entrance fees USD13 per person for foreigner and included with drink. Place very quiet and not many people. Scenery very nice, clean but not many people visiting there.  The temple not very high. From there we can see Mt. Merapi.

If want to see sunset in Jojga, this would be the right place. But also make sure that weather favors your trip or else you may not enjoy if it rains. Going to this place would be better if you are going to take smaller cars since the  access road is quite small. Tour buses can stay at the bottom part and you need to walk up to see the sunset.

Saya ke Candi Ratu Boko ditempuh dengan bus sewaan  ke lokasi parkir dan dilanjutkan dengan bus kecil disediakan pengelola (ga tahu bayar atau engga) karena lokasi di puncak bukit. Candi sendiri masih dalam pemugaran, belum 'asik'. Hanya ada gapura2 Candi beberapa unit. karena malam, saya hanya bisa menangkap beberapa penunjuk arah, sedangkan lokasi yang disebut tidak terlihat karena tidak ada pencahayaan sama sekali. Hanya kebetulan kami ada acara yang diselenggarakan, pentas kisah Ramayana, sehingga acara menjadi menarik. Oh ya, dari Candi Boko ini, kita bisa melihat di bawah, kompelk Candi Prambanan yang terang bermandikan cahaya....

Had a end of course dinner celebration at Ratu Boko temple. Journey there from UMY took more than 1.5 hours. Had to change from a 40 seater to 15 seater to make the last trip up the temple.
The immediate thing that graps you when you enter is the night scenery. Was told you can see Mt Merapi from there. But in the night... well... you can only guess. 
Because there is'nt much lighting in the night sky, you can't really see much. So conclusion is that if you want to see the distance scenery, better go there in the day.
There was a good performance by a traditional ensemble of Javanese singers and musicians. Worth the visit if you are looking for a Javanese experience. The singers and musicians, beside being accomplished at their craft, were also very accommodating when we sat/knelt next to them to take pictures. 
At our dinner, we were told that the place where we were eating our dinner is actually not the temple perse. The temple is next door. Sigh!

lokasinya berada di kawasan wonosari, tak jauh dari candi prambanan. perlu usaha lebih untuk menanjak karena lokasinya berada di atas bukit. kawasan candi ratu boko sangat luas, bahkan hampir bisa disamakan dengan luas candi borobudur. lokasi ini cocok untuk anda yang menyukai fotografi.

1) Kata orang di Candi Ratu BOko ini mengeluarkan energi positif. Berhubung belum terbukti untuk saya jadi saya perlu pembuktian lain dengan cara yang lain.  Sore itu saya tergesa-gesa masuk ke area Candi Ratu Boko takut gelap. Ternyata di dalamnya banyak para fotografer sudah  stand by menunggu sunset. Wow ada terlihat Candi Prambanan yang cantik. Langit mulai memerah......waah semua menjadi luar biasa.  Areanya cenderung banyak yang datar, Seperti hal nya candi-candi yang lain tentunya ada gapura dan tangga-tangga. Tentu saja semua indah untuk diabadikan

2) Mungkin karena sudah sore, kamar kecil/toilet airnya kurang jadi repot

3) Apakah mungkin penerangan Candi Ratu Boko ditambah? Tentunya tanpa mengurangi keindahan jika diabadikan
Not much big building given that nobody knows what the original building is. The complimentary food and drink were good and nice view

menyempatkan diri untuk mampir di salah satu candi bersejarah di indonesia ini membuat kita kagum pada para pendahulu..tempatnya beberapa kilo meter dari candi prambanan, tiketnya dapat kita dapatkan di loket masuk candi prambanan itu sudah termasuk transportasinya.sepanjang jalan menuju candi boko yg agak masuk ke dalam perkampungan ini kita disuguhkan pemandangan sawah dan beberapa pemukiman warga.walaupun yg tersisa hanya gerbang yg megah dan lapangan yg luas, disini kita dapat merasakan kemegahan bangunan ini pada jamannya.Dan saya menyempatkan diri untuk foto prewedding dan hasilnya memuaskan.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
Jika anda ingin mengunjungi tempat klasik yang sangat menarik, eksotis dan romantis, jangan lewatkan untuk mengunjungi Candi Ratu Boko. Di sana paling sedikit ada 4 hal yang tak ternilai:
1. Indahnya pemandangan Yogya dengan candi Prambanan yang bisa dinikmati dari ketinggian, di tempat minum kopi di areal candi Ratu Boko.
2. Reruntuhan candi dan gerbang candi yang indah, bak panggung alamiah
3. Bekas pemandian keluarga raja yang eksotis dan unik
4. Pemandangan mata hari tenggelam (Sunset) yang sangat indah dan dramati.

Lokasi candi mudah dicapai, bahkan kita bisa membeli karcis terusan di candi Prambanan, dan kkita bisa naik shuttle bus ke Candi ratu Boko. Sore hari adalah waktu yang sangat tepat ke sana.

Candi ini juga menjadi salahs atu tempat foto favorit untuk Pre-Wedding

Rato boko is actually "keraton" (english: kingdom) so it's not same as other temples around Jogjakarta - Magelang, central Java Indonesia. But today, you will find lots of stones and leftover temples/building inside Ratu Boko.

You will need to walk quite far from ticket gate, yet the view was worth the walk. I went there just before sunset so the weather is not too hot. The gate keeper told me to went up and witnessing sunset on incineration stone (left side of Ratu Boko enterance stone). It was beautiful!   

While you here, i recommend you to explore the kingdom down to the backside. you'll find bathing pool of the anxcient prince & princess. Unlike other temples, this place is quit, peaceful yet relaxing. I would rather spent my time just to sit on the grass, feels the wind and listening to the bees and cricket sounds.

Ratu Boku is an ancient temple that has been around since 7/8AD. Rock ruins and remnants of old structures are spread across a large area of land at the top of a hill with panoramic views of Jogya and animals like goats and birds running around.

This is a good place to come for either sunrise or sunset and a group of restaurants and souvenir shops sit at the base of the temple to enjoy a meal afterwards or before. There are many stairs and uneven surfaces here, as well as a steep driveway, so do take that into consideration if you are traveling with someone unable or elderly.
Ticket (adult): 90k, dinner is included. Dinner just very simple but tasty something like fried rice + egg + tea ; Ticket (student): 81k, ONLY drinks is included。Opens from Mon-Sun 6am-5:30pm.
Peninggalan sejarah yang indah. Tempat wisata yang tidak terlalu ramai dibandingkan dengan Candi Prambanan. Pemandangan dari bukit yang sangat indah, hamparan rumput hijau.

Jarak 2.5km dari prambanan. Jika mengunjungi prambanan, bisa beli tiket kedua tempat sekaligus dan ada antar jemput ke ragunan. Saya lbh suka lari dari prambanan. Ketinggian 200m. Tidak banyak tersisa kecuali halaman depan yg sudah rapi dan indah, gerbang utama memperlihatkan kemegahan...kedalam ada lapangan halaman utama...pendopo utuh....cukup bagus...ujung keraton ada taman sari ...tempat permandian ratu...sayang belum dipugar. Taman utama istana juga indah...dan ada bberapa tmpat melihat pemandangan merapi dan prambanan. Sore hari halaman utama menjadi restoran dengan pemandangan menakjubkan.

Pergi sendirian ke Ratu Boko bisa dilakukan dengan menyewa kendaraan sendiri. Kira-kira berangkat dari tengah kota Yogya sekitar jam 5 pagi. Jangan terlalu pagi karena masih lumayan gelap. Kunjungan pagi terasa menyenangkan bagi anda yang menikmati pagi yang sunyi, karena baru penjaga dan pemelihara candi yang datang. Pemandangan sunrise di Ratu Boko tidak kalah menarik dengan suanana sunset, dengan sedikit eksperimen dijamin bisa mendapatkan spot menarik untuk foto.
BIG Temple with no shades, Walk till the end, theres much to see and FIND THE CAVE ;) good luck. its really hot there and there's food shops around there. NO SMOKING PLEASE

Candi Ratu Boko bisa dikatakan berada diatas tebing karena lokasinya berada diatas bukit. Saya berkunjung kesana menggunakan shuttle bis dari Candi Prambanan dengan membeli tiket paket Candi Prambana-Candi Ratu Boko. Kononterdapat pemandian dewa-dewi di area candi ini dengan sumur berisi air suci

Candi boko dekat dengan area prambanan. Candi nya sudah tidak tampak lagi. Hanya sisa-sisa candi yang terlihat. Area nya luas dan tempat yang indah. Apalagi untuk menikmati sunset. So romantic. Jangan lupa menonton pertunjukan tari atau drama di panggungnya. Bagus.

i have gone to borobudur and prambanan temple. but i can say that ratu boko has an amazing places. i can feel the atmosphere of past time when i go to ratu boko. i can feel that i'm not at jogja at present time, but someplace, sometime in past..

ratu boko also have stairs, but not too high, and its enough to make me loose my breath loll..
maybe if you wonder a temple that maintained like borobudur or prambanan, you will dissapointed.  one think i love when i go here, burn some incense and do a meditation near paseban.. 

dont worry if you thirsty, after you pay for entrance (under 50K IDR) they will give a mineral water. and also a restaurant near parking. the restaurant has a beautiful view. enjoy the sunset here..
Jika berkunjung ke kawasan Ratu Boko maka akan menarik manakala di waktu sore hari. Matahari yang akan tenggelam di ufuk barat menambah suasana kemegahan bangunan yang ada di kawasan ini.

This place is a total rip-off. The adult entrance fee is USD15 / 165.000 Rp (including one drink) which is ridiculous for an attraction with only one (badly renovated) small structure still standing. We were able to get in on a student ticket, which is still 77.000 Rp and not worth it (for example: the Water Palace in the kraton of Yogya is only 10.000Rp and much nicer). The view is nice but not really special. Save time and money and skip this place.
This former water palace is not too awe-inspiring in itself, with the gate being the only large standing structure. It's a good place for a sunset view of Prambanan on a clear day.

We visited Boko Temple at sunset and the view was magnificent. There is not a lot left of the temple but the admission price of 90,000 rupiah we thought was very reasonable as it included a very nice meal and a drink.

The temple is a placed on a big aerea.
In the past years they build a restorant to the view.
You can see as well as the Prambanan Temple as the Merapi vulcano when it is a clear day.

Menuurut legenda, candi Boko adalah tempat dimana Roro Jonggrang mengawasi pembangunan seribu candi sebagai syarat yang diberikan kepada Bandung Bondowoso jika ingin mempersuntingnya sebagai istri.
Dan memang benar, jika anda berdiri di tempat yang tepat, anda akan bisa melihaat Prambanan dengan jelas. Pemandangannya indah sekali. Hijaunya sawah sungguh menyegarkan.
Candi Boko saat ini sudah dikelola dengan sangat baik. Ini jika dibandingkan 7 tahun yang lalu ketika saya pertama kali kesana. Saya sarankan kepada anda untuk mengunjungi Boko pada saat sunrise atau sunset. Anda akan bersyukur bisa menikmati salah satu spot terindah di Indonesia.

Candi Ratu Boko termasuk salah satu candi yang kurang dikenal jika dibandingkan dengan saudaranya, Candi Prambanan atau Candi Sewu. Namun Candi Ratu Boko merupakan tempat yang komplit untuk melarikan diri dari hingar bingar kota sembari mengagumi arsitektur sejarah  dan menikmati senja yang cantik di sore hari. Beneran, senja di Ratu Boko luar biasa cantik! 

Untuk yang menyukai fotografi, Candi Ratu Boko merupakan tempat yang tepat untuk dieksplorasi. Jangan lewatkan mengambil gambar terbaik dari tiga gerbang utama yang epik itu! 

PS: Sayang beberapa beberapa bagian kurang begitu dirawat, seharusnya pemerintah serius memperhatikan perawatan dan fasilitas pendukung lain, karena Ratu Boko sangat potensial untuk dikembangkan seperti candi-candi lainnya di Jogja dan Jawa Tengah.

Sebenarnya ini tour sepaketan dengan Candi Prambanan. sangat sayang melewatkan Candi Ratu Boko jika sudah sampai di Prambanan.
Berbeda dengan candi-candi lain yang menjelang sore akan tutup, untuk Ratu Boko, datanglah menjelang senja. karena kita akan mendapatkan senja yang sangat cantik disini.
Selain mendapatkan wisata sejarah, kita juga akan dibuat tercengang dengan kerumitan dan kemegahand dari candi ini.
ada yang bilang sebenarnya Ratu Boko ini merupakan bekas istana kerajaan, tapi ada juga yang bilang ini merupakan asrama dari para brahmana menimba ilmu.
terlepas dari fungsinya terdahulu, Ratu Boko merupakan kompleks candi yang sangat cantik dan menawan
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
We had a great trip with our young kids to Yogyakarta and we were at Ratu Boko on 28th March 2013. We arrived at around 4pm local time and the entrance fees was R90,000 for adults and R50,000 for kids. The fees is inclusive of a snack and coffee/tea. But we told them we just want to view the sunset as we just had a late lunch but was told there is NO choice but to buy the package.
Earlier we failed to go to Merapi as there was a slight tremor and the weather was very cloudy. When we asked the Ratu Boko ticketing counter will we be able to view the sunset (that's the whole idea of this visit to this place) but was told around 5.30-6pm will be the sunset. We were concerned as there wasn't many tourist at the time and we thought, they will surely tell us if the weather does not permit us to view the sunset that day.
We happily walked up to the Ratu Boko temple and waited diligently until 5.45pm but by then we know we will not be seeing any sunset. We were obviously angry as the management should have advise us if the weather was not suitable to view the sunset.
We went to consult the office and enquired why we were not pre-advised before that and requested can we just come again tomorrow (which is a long distance from our hotel in Yogyakarta town) and just to view the sunset BUT was told to BUY another ticket tomorrow!
I demanded to speak to the manager but was told the manager is on off day and will not pick up his mobile phone even if they called. They were reluctant to give me the manager's contact number.
In a nutshell, I think this place is a total rip off especially to foreign tourist as we pay a different entrance fees and have NO choice but to buy with the drink and snack for about R100,000 for the whole family.
I would NOT RECOMMEND this place to any tourist to Ratu Boko because the temple is nothing compared to Prabanam and Borobudur and the only thing they sell is the sunset package which comes with hidden cost (drink and snack) to raise the entrance fees!
I complaint to my transport company and they promise to email the management on this matter but I would like the whole world to know what we were short changed of and be very careful because sad to say they just want your money even though I strongly believe they would know the weather that day will NOT able to see the sunset (I confirmed this with one of the guards when we sadly decend from the temple). 
I felt that they would at least let us decide and tell us the consequences that we MAY not be able to view the sunset due to the current weather,
Totally disappointed with Ratu Boko!

The Ratu Boko complex is unique and strategically located. This is good spot to take sunset. The complex, though not totally uncovered, provides an excellent glimpse of how the Javanese old kingdom used to be set up and thrive. Would be good if more research done and we can see the virtual kingdom looks like in the past.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Good location to catch the sunset. Temple is on to a hill so may not be suitable with walking problem.  Ticket price inclusive of a simple meal.
Странная штука, не тратьте деньги и время, единственное - прикольный вид на вулкан, но в нашу поездку небо было затянуто ... Лучше ехать на закате в 5-6 вечера ...

Pemandangan yang begitu indah, walaupun beberapa bagian dari candi ada yang kurang terawat, namun tetap saja keindahannya terjaga. warga sekitar yang ramah dan memberitahukan mengenai sejarah candi ini dengan jelas pun dapat melengkapi hiburan anda semua.

Awalnya ga ada niat untuk mengunjungi candi ratu boko karena saat itu sedang ingin berkunjung ke prambanan. Tapi saat membeli tiket masuk prambanan ditawari paket untuk sekalian mengunjungi candi ratu boko. Kesempatan itu saya iyakan karena memiliki waktu yang cukup banyak.

Jadi dari prambanan akan ada mobil sejenis "ELF" yang akan mengantarkan wisatawan untuk mengunjungi candi ratu boko. Saya pikir dekat, ternyata lumayan juga, jalannya naik turun. 
Saat baru  sampai hujan turun, cuaca menjadi sejuk setelah panas-panasan di prambanan. 
Tempat yang luas dan bersih menurut saya serta warisan yang harus dijaga.

dengan lokasi yang hanya berjarak sekitar 5 kilometer dari candi Prambanan, Candi Ratu Boko sangat layak untuk dikunjungi. Candi ini memiliki lingkungan yang bersih dan teduh dan beberapa guide yang siap membantu dan menemani para wisatawan untuk berbagi cerita mengenai sejarah candi ini.
Compared to Borobudur and Prambanan, admission fee of Ratu Boko is quite expensive since it has almost nothing left except the nice scenery from top of the hill.
the temple is situated on a hill, you can choose morning or afternoon to be able to capture the sunrise and sunset, very charming.

Banyak yang merekomendasikan tempat ini terutama untuk foto prewedding dan pemandangan sunsetnya.

Menurut saya, tempat ini tidak semegah candi Prambanan atau Borobudur. Yang anda bisa lihat hanya sebuah gerbang candi, tempat pembakaran sesajen, dan tempat mandi para putri. Dimana, ketiga tempat ini terpisah tanah lapang hijau yang sangat luas. Sehingga ketika anda memasuki gerbang, anda akan mendapati lahan hijau luas, dan beberapa meter di sblh timur dan baratnya anda dapat menemukan bebatuan yang merupakan tempat sesajen dan permandian putri.

Pemandangan sunsetnya? Hmm, saat saya ke sana, agak terutup awan. Menurut saya biasa saja, tidak spesial.
Menurut saya, tempat ini cocok dijadikan tempat piknik dan bersantai ria. Untuk wisata sejarah, nampaknya kurang tepat, karena tidak banyak yang bisa dilihat. Tempat ini menurut saya bersih dan sangat terawat.

Di dekat candi ada restaurant makan. Menurut saya kurang recommended. Tempat nya biasa saja. Menu makanannyapun biasa.
Mereka menyajikan steak dan masakan lokal. Yang saya rekomendasikan hanya mie godoknya saja. Untuk steak, harganya cukup mahal dan porsinya sangat kecil.

Terletak kurang lebih 30an menit dari Jogja, tempat ini sangat direkomendasikan untuk menikmati sunset. Dari sini anda akan bisa melihat candi prambanan dan pemandangan kota di bawahnya.
Areanya cukup bersih dengan fasilitas yg cukup lengkap semakin memanjakan anda menikmati pemandangan yg ada.
Area Candi ditutup setelah matahari terbenam (sekitar pukul 6) namun untuk area tamannya masih dibuka. Terdapat restoran apabila anda ingin langsung bersantap malam dgn pemandangan city view, rasa dan harganya masih cukup bagus menurut saya.

Pemandangan di Candi Ratu Boko ini sungguh sangat bagus, berada diatas bukit.
dan pada waktu saya ke sana, diadakan pentas sendratari ramayana dengan back ground pemandangan perbukitan.

tapi sayang jarak tempuh yang lumayan jauh dari Kota Jogja dan  keterbatasan alat transportasi yang menuju daerah wisata ini, sehingga apabila ingin mengunjungi harus merogoh kocek lebih dalam untuk sewa kendaraan.

Bagi saya pribadi, memasuki kawasan Candi Boko seperti masuk ke dalam sebuah kawasan yang lain daripada yang lain. Letak candi yang dibangun pada masa Wangsa Sailendra (Rakai Panangkaran) dari Kerajaan Medang (Mataram Hindu) berada di sebuah bukit yang cukup tinggi, bentuk bangunannya yang lain dari pakem bentuk candi yang selama ini kita kenal adalah keunggulan yang dimiliki oleh Candi Boko dan tidak dimiliki oleh candi-candi lain.
 Menurut situs Wikipedia Candi Boko sebenarnya bukanlah sebuah candi atau bangunan yang diperuntukkan untuk kegiatan keagamaan. Komplek ini diperkirakan merupakan sebuah komplek keraton lengkap dengan gerbang masuk, pendopo, tempat tinggal, kolam pemandian, hingga benteng dan parit kering untuk keperluan pertahanan.
 Saat yang paling tepat untuk mengunjungi kawasan Candi Boko adalah saat matahari terbit atau menjelang matahari terbenam. Saat matahari terbit, kita bisa menyaksikan sinar matahari pagi yang lembut menerobos bangunan dan gerbang-gerbang candi tersebut, seolah-olah kita dibawa ke suasana magis di abad ke-8 masehi. Saat matahari terbenam, kita juga akan dapat menyaksikan kelembutan sinar matahari serupa dari sisi barat.
 Kita juga dapat menyaksikan kemegahan Candi Prambanan, Gunung Merapi yang penuh misteri dan gemerlapnya kota Yogyakarta menjelang terbenamnya matahari dari ketinggian bukit dimana candi ini berada.

HOW TO GET THERE:

- Public Transport:
We went to Prambanan from Yogyakarta (a bit out of the city centre) by ourselves with local buses following Google Maps and I found quite easy to do it. We also made sure to ask locals in bus stops to confirm that was the best route. 
We took the bus 3B to “TJ Bandara Adisucipto” (station at the airport) and from there changed to bus 1A to “Terminal Prambanan”. The total cost for both buses was IDR 7,200 as stated on Google Maps. From the Terminal, you have to walk for 16 min.
The full trip took about 2 hours, even though Google was saying that would take a bit longer than that.

- Grab:
On the way back we decided to catch a Grab as it was pouring down rain and it cost about IDR 130,000 back into our accommodation.
Just be aware if you choose to go there by Grab, the driver might offer to wait for you to take you back into town. Take into consideration what’s best for you.

- DAMRI bus:
Just after we’ve been to Prambanan we found out that was a third option how to get there that we didn’t know about it.
The DAMRI buses/minivans run everyday in specific times leaving from “Bank Indonesia Yogyakarta” (located in Malioboro city centre). 
As the timetables are fixed and they don’t have many buses running, I would highly recommend you to go in their stand in person the day before and book your bus in advance, once you have bought your ticket to the Temple. Also double check how long the journey would take, as you don’t want to miss your ticket entrance time.
We ended up not using this option as we couldn’t find much information online, the website was a bit confusing and not translated to English, so I found the best option is to ask them in person.

I hope those tips are useful, I wish I knew them before going there :)

Review Text: Prambanan Temple is an incredible cultural and architectural gem! As a UNESCO World Heritage site, it offers stunning views of towering Hindu temples, intricately carved reliefs, and a rich history that takes you back centuries. I went to Prambanan temple for several times already but never failed me. This time I went there with my husband and my sister, even though me and my sister are Indonesian but we are living abroad and my husband also he is a foreigner, so when we visited Indonesia, we decided to go to Yogyakarta to see the beauty of Prambanan temple during sunset time and it is so beautiful. I do recommend to go there during sunset time before it's closing time so the weather is not so hot anymore.

An incredible temple complex on the outskirts of Yogyakarta. A great place to wander around; we came on a busy day, and most visitors went straight to the main complex (as we did), but after a while we strolled around the parkland, and we had most of the outlying temple structures to ourselves. Easily walkable - flat, good paths, and not that far really.

The temple complex is renowned for its exquisite bas-reliefs that adorn the walls of the temples. These intricate carvings depict scenes from Hindu epics, such as the Ramayana and the Mahabharata. The level of detail and artistry showcased in these reliefs is truly awe-inspiring. Visitors can spend hours exploring the intricate stories and symbolism etched into the stone.

Giant, dramatic stupas silhouetted against a stormy sky made for a very special visit even though we were soaked to the skin. Huge towers of grey with dozens of mini styles and some beautiful reliefs make this worth a visit whatever the weather.

The Candi Prambanan means Temple of the Many Priests. That already indicates the size of this large 9th century Hindu temple complex, located near Yogyakarta. The entire complex covers more than one square kilometer and is the largest Hindu temple complex in Asia after Anghor Wat, Cambodia. Prambanan consists of three large main temples, some 50 meters high, dedicated to Vishnu, Brahma and Shiva. Around these large temples there are many smaller, yet still substantial temples, dedicated to "lesser" Hindu gods, eg Nandi, the riding animal of Vishnu. Originally, the complex consisted of some 240 (!) temple buildings, grouped around the three main temples. The entire complex decayed over the centuries. In the 19th century, Candi Prambaran was discovered by the colonial administration. Or rather, heronded, because the locals knew the temple ruins well and used stones from them for the construction of their houses. It was not until the early 20th century that a serious restoration of the Prambanan was discussed, partly due to initiatives by the Dutch colonial administration. It was not until 1953 that the first main temple was rebuilt, the one dedicated to Vishnu. The two other main temples and a number of smaller temples have now been rebuilt and can be visited. The intention is to restore about 200 more temple buildings, the remains of which have been found. A challenge, because on average it takes one year to rebuild a temple about 20 meters high. Beautiful reliefs on the temples, beautiful statues in the great Vishnu temple .. Candi Prambanan is a historic wonder!

The Prambanan temple complex is the largest Hindu temple site in Indonesia and 2nd largest in South East Asia after Angkor Wat. This is the 2nd most popular tourist attraction in Central Java after Borobudur. Within the Prambanan temple complex, you will find Candi Roro Jonggrang(the Hindu temples), Candi Lumbung(a few small Buddhist temples), Candi Bubrah(a small Buddhist temple) and Candi Sewu(the 2nd largest Buddhist temple in the world after Borobudur!).

Candi Roro Jonggrang are the temples dedicated to the Trimurti of Hindu Gods: Brahma, Vishnu & Shiva. The largest temple structure in this entire complex is the Shiva temple that stands at 47 metres tall. Candi Sewu is the most notable of the Buddhist temples here, it is located 800 metres from Candi Roro Jonggrang and very few visitors bother to walk over to Candi Sewu. I recommend that you take the effort to visit Candi Sewu, as it is beautiful. A huge earthquake hit central Java in 2006 and damaged most of the small temple structures in Prambanan. Restoration works are still ongoing today.

For Prambanan, there are no limits to the daily number of visitors, no footwear restrictions and no time-limit restrictions for all visitors, unlike Borobudur. You can just walk-in to the ticketing office during operating hours(6.30am to 5pm, 6 days per week, closed on Mondays) and buy your tickets. Please allocate a big part of your day here, to carefully explore each and every temple that are still standing or that has been restored. DO NOT try to cram Borobudur AND Prambanan into 1 day, they are located very far apart and the traffic in Indonesia is insane!!!

Finally, I could visit Prambanan Temple again, this time from Solo using the Solo-Jogja commuter train and getting off at Brambanan station. It takes about 10-15 minutes to walk from Brambanan train station to the entrance of Prambanan Temple. The entrance ticket to Prambanan Temple is around Rp 50,000 for domestic visitors. These tickets can be purchased well in advance through online booking platforms like Traveloka or Tiket.com, so there's no need to queue when you arrive at Prambanan Temple; you can simply scan your ticket for entry.

This temple, famous for the legend of Roro Jonggrang and the Ramayana, always captivates tourists visiting Yogyakarta, especially those entering Jogja from the Solo direction. Travelers coming from Solo can take an intercity bus or the commuter train and get off at Brambanan station. Meanwhile, those coming from Yogyakarta city can take the commuter train and also get off at Brambanan station, or they can take the Trans Jogja bus and get off at Prambanan bus stop, then continue on foot for 10-15 minutes. Alternatively, they can use intercity buses or private/rented vehicles, providing plenty of transportation options.

In addition to the main Prambanan Temple, visitors can also explore several other temples within the Prambanan Temple Compounds, including Candi Bubrah, Candi Lumbung, and Candi Sewu. Exploring these temples can be done on foot or by renting a bicycle for Rp 20,000 per bicycle for 20-30 minutes.

For those carrying bags or belongings, it's advisable to store them at the luggage storage area before entering the temples and retrieve them after exploring the temples. This is for the visitors' convenience, as the temple area is vast and can be quite hot.

Caṇḍi Prambanan is the largest Hindu temple building in Indonesia which was built in the 9th century AD. This temple, which is also known as Rara Jonggrang, is dedicated to Trimurti, the three main Hindu gods, namely Brahma as the creator god, Vishnu as the preserver god, and Shiva as the destroyer god. Based on the Siwagrha inscription, the original name of this temple complex is Siwagrha (Sanskrit which means 'House of Shiva'), and indeed in the garbagriha (main room) of this temple there is a three meter high statue of Shiva Mahadewa, because the Syaiwa sect prioritizes the worship of the god Shiva in this temple.

My wife and I recently visited prambanan from Yogyakarta. Overall we had a really good time with our only gripe being the mistreatment of animals on site and the overcharging of foreigners. Here are a few tips for those planning a trip here. 

- The site is reportedly closed on Mondays. Same as Borobudur. I can’t find information about whether it’s just entrance into the temples that’s not allowed or the entrance gates are closed completely. Better not to risk it anyway. 

- Ticket price is 387500IR for foreigner or 50000IR for local. This is a similar pricing structure to Borobudur. There is a combination ticket available with Borobudur but I would advise against this as it only allows entry into Borobudur temple ground, not structure access (ie the ticket does not allow you to climb the temple). There is also a combination ticket available for prambanan and Ratu Boko - which is a ruined hindu palace located about 5km from prambanan. 

- Entry into prambanan complex actually provides entry to four temple structures. The first is roro Jonggrang which is the most famous prambanan complex featuring the 47m high candi shiva mahadeva. The other three are Candi lumbung, Candi bubrah and Candi sewu. Candi sewu is definitely worth visiting but the other two are not noteable. 

- To get between the above four temple areas you can hire bikes. Alternatively it’s a peaceful 30ish minute stroll. There is a cart available for the elderly. 

- The site is about 17km from Yogyakarta. You can get here using a private driver (500000 to 650000), a grab (81000 one way), a bus or apparently the train. I’ve attached the bus schedule to this review - the station is in front of the bank of Indonesia on the southern end of Jalan Malioboro. We personally got a grab for the above cost and then on the way out just asked one of the drivers waiting to match the grab fare. It took about 45 minutes to get here by car each way.

- I would get here early to avoid the crowds. I would also get here early as it gets very hot. Even by mid morning. The temples aren’t shaded and are made of rock.

- Due to the heat I would encourage bringing plenty of water, sunscreen and a hat.

- It took us about 3 hours to get through the site.

- There is a cafe on site selling drinks and ice cream. 

- You could technically combine this with Borobudur but it would be a long day and I wouldn’t want to visit either site in the heat of the afternoon.

- The grounds had a very disturbing animal display featuring deer and cassowaries. Being from northern Australia we know cassowaries should never be kept in small exposed cages like this and were quite disgusted by that.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
Prambanan was quiet when I visited due to a large storm. It's more popular with locals than Borobodur as it's a lot more affordable and doesn't have limited access. 
Prambanan is a couple of hours' drive from Borobodur, and a couple of hours drive from Yogyakarta. It's possible to see both in the same day but will require your own car/driver and good planning. It's worth paying for the services of a guide as they'll be able to tell you so much more about what you're seeing and the giant 3-dimensional jigsaw puzzle that is the process of reassembling the hundreds of temples at this site. There is a small museum near the ticket office and some signage closer to the temples, but it's limited. I really enjoyed visiting. Carry an umbrella, either for rain or sun, as it's a reasonable walk and there's no shelter.

Prambanan temple is an architectural marvel dating to the 9th century AD dedicated to the 3 principal deities of Hinduism- Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva. There are other deities such Ganesha, Durga,Nandi etc.

We were there very early - and that was a good thing, as there are a lot of visitors later!
The complex with the various temples is absolutely worth seeing!

It was a place that could be considered simple and magnificent among Hindu temples. It was composed of parts rather than a whole, with images of Hindu gods inside them. It's a point worth visiting. As usual, tourist-loving souvenir sellers will follow you at the exit.

prambanan temple is the second largest temple complex in SE Asia after angkor wat. there are several temples onsite, including the sewu temple, which is also worth a visit 

to get around, there are golf carts (200K IDR for 40 min ride). alternatively, you can walk or rent a bicycle. 

i recommend visiting towards the end of the day so that you can enjoy the sunset view. note however, you have to watch the sunset from the park grounds, instead of at the temple, as the closing time for the temple is earlier than sunset. 

the prambaman ramayana ballet performance is on every tue, thu, and sat. there is also another performance (different story line) on fri. all shows begin at 7:30 pm. i bought the ballet tickets in person  from the information center after entering the temple complex. just exchange the voucher for show tickets at the ballet performance center upon arrival
Faktor Penarik: Ketertarikan Budaya, Ketertarikan Fasilitas, Ketertarikan Suasana
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
My first time coming here. I was curious about the statue of Roro Jonggrang, but it turned out that the story was just a legend, what I found inside the temple was a statue of Lord Shiva.

Around the temple grounds there is lots of entertainment for children and families, such as massage machines and places to rent children's toys. There is live music too. The location is not that far from the center of Yogyakarta, but there are not many souvenir sellers here

The temple can be reached by a train from Yogyakarta and then a short walk. There are numerous buildings on the site - originally there were 250 - it must have been splendid when completed. Each stupa features a different Hindu God and the larger stupa are all interesting. Note that you can walk around the larger stupa with each offering a good view. Arguably better than Borborudur.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Another temple that you won't want to miss it. The ruins of the temples simply have character. If you enjoyed Ankor Wat, you will also enjoy Prambanan Temples. A place to visit at least once in your lifetime. You won't regret it!

Prambanan is an ancient Hindu temple that was built during the 9th or 10th century, and It features three main structures along with a number of small temple structures situated in an immaculate grounds area.   Prambanan is another Indonesian temple that has been designated by UNESCO as a world heritage site because of its historical significance.  The temples are lovely and nicely constructed.  It is definitely a worthwhile place to visit to see the temple and the immaculate grounds surrounding it.

Just 15 km from Yogyakarta is this site of remarkable beauty. A series of Hindu temples and ruins cover a rather large area. It is worth climbing the temples to enter the small cells where the statues of the deities are located. When there are a lot of people you have to adapt a little because the spaces are limited.

Prambanan is a complex of 240 Hindu temples dedicated to Shiva. The entire complex is spectacular, and the visit is well worth it. Just like Borobudur, they close the inner part of the compound for cleaning on Mondays, so if you go on a Monday, you won't be able to access a portion of the temples.

Not terrible. The second temple is beautiful, but the rest is crowded with people, and not that impressive. The price is much too high for tourists (400,000 IDR per person), it's a bit exaggerated for 2 not-so-great temples.
Locals may ask you for photos if you look foreign. Not disturbing but it can become a little intrusive.

In addition to Borobudur, another must-see in Yogyakarta is Prambanan.
For Prambanan,
I must describe it like this,
it is majestic but elegant.

Maybe I want to describe it in words,
maybe I want to express it in photos,
but I encourage everyone to go there in person,
to feel its beauty with their eyes and heart.

Many people may compare Angkor Wat with Prambanan,
but I don't like to make unnecessary comparisons when I travel.
Because the two tell the same story,
there will definitely be similarities to some extent,
but when it comes to the architectural style and the depiction of the characters,
there will definitely be differences.
In terms of scale,
although it cannot be compared with Angkor Wat,
the 240 intact buildings in Prambanan during its heyday are amazing enough.
In the final analysis,
there is no need for comparison,
because the existence of these monuments is enough to be admired.

🎫＞
Tickets: 387.5K

🕑＞
Opening hours: 6:30-17:00

💡＞
TIPS: Prambanan is not very big and can be seen in about two hours. It is suitable for an afternoon visit. If you are short on time, you can visit Borobudur in the morning and Prambanan in the afternoon.
There is a large lawn at the exit. It is very photogenic to sit under the tree and take pictures.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Prambanan Temple tourist destination, a tourist spot with a beautiful tropical plant area and the work of the country's children in the form of a very beautiful temple complex from several centuries ago, really amazing 👍
This was even better than Borobudur! Especially if you Visit it during sunset! It's a masterpiece of Hindu culture! Worth your time!

The intricate carvings, the towering spires, and the rich historical aura make it a true architectural marvel. Exploring the complex felt like delving into a captivating storybook of Indonesian mythology and Hindu culture. The sunset backdrop against the temple's silhouette created a magical atmosphere that felt straight out of a dream. What struck me most was the sense of reverence that hangs in the air, even amidst the buzzing crowds. Standing there, surrounded by centuries-old stone structures, I couldn't help but marvel at the craftsmanship and artistry of ancient civilizations. Prambanan is more than a tourist site; it's a tangible link to Indonesia's glorious past, and visiting it was a humbling and unforgettable experience.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
spacious complex, luckily it's easy to get lost. nice staff, you can climb up the temple. 
a small bottle of water is available at the entrance for the price of the ticket. 
I was there quite late in the afternoon, which looked quite beautiful with the low sun.

Nice and beautiful temple complex to visit. An hour or two is enough for you. We were towards the end of the day, so that the sunset could work its magic on the whole. There are also many local people/children who want to have their picture taken with you.

Surely his closeness to Borodubur has harmed him, almost undervaluing him.
In my opinion it is at its level, despite being less visited and considered almost of a lower category.
Although it is true that it is less exploited.
The ticket is purchased on the same website, but here they do not give you a guided tour, you see it on your own, unless you hire a guide at the entrance.
It is a wonderful Hindu temple complex from the 10th century.
In the area there are other temples, such as Sewu, some of which are even Buddhist.
It is usually packed with school visits.
In my opinion, it is essential to buy a combined ticket and visit both. The rest of the temples in the complex are hardly visited, the walk is worth it and practically alone.
There is no dress code and the entrance is much more accessible than Borodubur, requiring less planning.
Being only 18km from Yogyakarta, it can be reached more easily. There is a public bus, as well as taxis and local drivers. Some tourists venture to go by motorcycle.
You can also book excursions combining the two.
In Yogyakarta there are many local agencies on Sosrowijayan Street, which starts from Maliboro, the main street.
Faktor Penarik: Ketertarikan Budaya, Ketertarikan Fasilitas, Ketertarikan Suasana
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: This is the largest Hindu temple of ancient Java.   Mid-9th century the  river was moved to construct  it.  A major earthquake in the 16th century and again in 2006 the Yogyakarta earthquake  destroyed a great majority of the structures.  35 temples have been put back together of the original 240  One of the the criteria for reconstruction is that 75% of the original stone still exists in order to qualify to put them back together.  There are 2 main areas which can be walked or driven between.  It is a very interesting area.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
Beautiful temple complex. You can walk around there for 2 hours. It is also possible to rent a bicycle or tandem to cycle around, or to be driven around in a golf cart.
A visit to Prambanan can easily be combined with a visit to Merapi volcano and Borobudur in one day
Faktor Penarik: Ketertarikan Budaya, Ketertarikan Fasilitas, Ketertarikan Suasana

Review Text:
Not incredible. Everything is done to make you want to go there.
You won't break a duck's 3 legs on site.
A large park with 4 temples ok….. animals in cages….
2 peacocks 🦚 locked in 3m2, not even space to spread their tails. Similar to abuse.
Super expensive, 25 euro pp
Fantastic Hindu temple, the reconstruction after the earthquake was exemplary, mystical place, a must for Java. The reliefs are fantastic
It’s a must see for anyone heading to Jogjakarta. It’s the largest Hindu temple complex outside of India. Be awed by the beautiful cravings and the magnificent towered structures of the temple.

The area itself is quite nice, and the temples as well, but the entrance fee is way overpriced. I cannot understand who thought that was a fair price. I entered because it is once in a lifetime, I would not go again.

Really interesting and intricate architecture, and the complex has four 'bundles' of temples, of varying sizes. The reconstruction is still underway, so it is very interesting to see the fully constructed temples next to the semi-complete parts. Bit pricey (we paid 750K IDR for two people) but imo worth it. 

The architecture is not like anything I've seen before. 

It's really vast and the ground is pale and dry, so in the summer I recommend sunscreen and a hat. 

Smooth experience from start to end, and the staff were all really lovely and helpful.
Faktor Penarik: Ketertarikan Budaya, Ketertarikan Fasilitas, Ketertarikan Suasana
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
Another must-visit place in Jogja. The ticket price for locals is 50k/pax and 375k/pax for foreigners. The temple is well kept and they have started conducting prayers at this temple. 

Now they control the visitors going up the temple, so expect some queue waiting for your turn. Might be due to safety reasons. They close at 5 pm. Good place to take a lot o f photos.

We included this in our itinerary for Yogyakarta and our entry fee was sorted out by our tour guide. We did not use a tour guide inside - there really is no need. The temples themselves are quite impressive, and it’s nice walking between each one. There were quite a lot of people even in the late afternoon, but nevertheless it didn’t feel too crowded. It makes for some great photos. The exit is quite long winded and it takes a while to get back to the car park, so bear this in mind if you’re on time constraints.

Magnificent temple. This complex comprises several different temples. In Prambanan complex, there are a few temples. Then we took a shuttle to Sewe temple, was given 15 minutes to look around. 
Sewu temple was another magnificent temple. On the way to Sewu, we passed several different smaller temple

The site consists of several temples, of which the Prambanan is the largest. Very beautiful and still in quite good condition. The nice thing about this temple (compared to Angkor Wat and Borobudur) is that you can go inside. Not very big and there is only 1 statue per temple. If you take a tour with a guide, you will easily spend 1.5 to 2 hours.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Awesome - been hoping to visit for ages and it lived up and exceeded expectations. Well worth visiting - about 30 mins north of central Yogyakarta.

Meget imponerende tempel kompleks, som er fint restaureret på en måde, hvor man virkelig kan fornemme stedets storhed, samtidig med at det er tydeligt, hvilke sten er nye og hvilke er oprindelige. 
Vores guide gav os et fint indblik i de hinduistiske guder og stedets symbolik - bestemt værd at betale de 150k for at få ham med rundt. Efter endt rundvisning kunne vi blive så længe vi ville og slå et sving i parken og få nogle flotte billeder og en is!

Impressionnant cet ensemble de 220 temples shivaistes construits au 9eme siècle. 

Tout comme son voisin de borododur, ce site indouiste est impressionnant et vertical en hauteur. 

Sur les fresques, nous voyons l'histoire de d'une princesse qui a tout fait pour éviter le mariage avec le démon. 

Il a dans le temple principal, il y a une statue de cette princesse.
Il y a également des statuts de Shiva et Ganesh.

Un incontournable à visiter sur Java
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Très beau site mais attention fermé le lundi. Cela ne vous empêchera pas de faire le tour du site principal et d’ensuite voir et entrer sur les 3 autres sites de moindre importance. La visite du musée est également possible. Côté tarif, 362,500 roupies pour 1 adulte et 217,500 pour 1 étudiant. Tarif normal même si vous ne pouvez pas aller physiquement sur le site principal. Pour y aller, nous avons pris le train au départ de Yogyakarta. 3 stations et vous êtes arrivés, ensuite 1 km à pieds À/R en train, 8€ pour 3.

Borobudur e Prambanan sono i due siti che valgono il viaggio . Il prezzo per gli  stranieri è alto ma ne vale la pena , anche perché i due siti sono splendidi . Dovete però FARE ATTENZIONE alle nuove regole di accesso post Covid  , che le guide non scrivono, l’accesso al sito è sempre consentito ma il Lunedì il tempio è chiuso per manutenzione. Per salire nei templi si deve aspettare  il propio turno , se c’è molta gente , per contingentare gli accessi , dovuto all’alto volume di turisti (sopratutto indonesiani) .
Il sito comprende altri templi magnifici , che molti turisti non considerano , ma ne vale la pena , semmai prendete  il golf car che è accessibilissimo per scoprirli tutti con calma . 
Vi consiglio un giorno Prambanan e un giorno Borobudur , anche perché fa caldo e rischiate di non goderveli appieno in una sola giornata ! 
Quindi ricordate fate il biglietto prima su internet , e il LUNEDÌ ricordatevi che i siti sono chiusi per pulizia e manutenzione.
Faktor Penarik: Ketertarikan Budaya, Ketertarikan Fasilitas, Ketertarikan Suasana
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: This is definitely worth visiting. No way to visit it during sunrise unfortunately. However I can recommend visiting the ballet at night. They do ask a lot but it’s definitely worth it. Beautiful temples and well maintained till the extent possible.
Setelah saya mengunjungi salah satu tempat wisata yg ada d Jogja salah satux adalah Candi Prambanan yg sangat Indah dan Bersejarah,d sana tempatx Bersih dan banyak candi-candi yang tertata rapi...

Imperdible templo en Jawa, es muy fácil de visitar y muy interesante.
Evitar las horas de muchos visitantes y de calor. Muy recomendable
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
Visiting Temple Prambanan was an extraordinary journey that transported me back in time to an era of rich cultural heritage and architectural brilliance. This UNESCO World Heritage Site, located in Yogyakarta, Indonesia, stands as a testament to the artistic mastery of the ancient Javanese civilization.

From the moment I laid my eyes on the towering spires of Temple Prambanan, I was awestruck. The sheer magnitude of the complex and the intricate details carved into every stone were a sight to behold. As I approached the temple grounds, I was greeted by a serene atmosphere, and the gentle sound of flowing water from nearby fountains added to the sense of tranquility.

The main complex of Prambanan consists of several towering temples dedicated to Hindu deities. Each temple boasts stunning architectural features, with meticulously carved reliefs and statues depicting tales from ancient Hindu epics. The grandeur of the main temple, dedicated to Lord Shiva, commands attention with its soaring height and intricate carvings that tell captivating stories of gods, demons, and heroes.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: I would reccomend going around the afternoon, it's the best time to go to these sort of places for me. The view and experience was excellent, I took some pretty nice pictures there. There weren't too many people there so that wasn't an issue aswell.

Really enjoyed this - more to see than Borobodur and not so crowded (in fact much less crowded than the guidebook had led us to expect.) And an easy walk to the extra temples at the other end of the site where it was much quieter. Lots of beautiful carvings and great views across the site. It is quite costly by Indonesian standards but worth it and as others have said there is lots of maintenance work to support.

We travelled there from Malioboro in Yogyakarta on bus 1a which seems to run about every 10 minutes. Technically you are meant to have a prepaid card but the drivers were flexible in taking cash - just don't expect any change! It's 3.6k rupiahs each so take some small notes. And don't be alarmed if they make you get off at the airport - you just have to switch buses but not pay again.

We tried and failed to also get to Kraton Katu Boko - there is a shuttle bus if you buy the combined ticket with Prambanan but when got there they told us it had finished, so check the details. We didn't have the combined ticket (as we'd bought the combined Prambanan-Borobudur ticket) and couldn't either get a Bluebird or persuade/communicate clearly enough with an autorickshaw driver to take us.

Overall really recommend!

Ensemble de plus de 200 temples construit au IX siècle, à proximité de Yogyakarta. À l'intérieur du temple principal, on trouve des scènes de combats entre le Bien et le Mal... et bien sûr, des représentations de Brahma, Shiva, Vishnu, Ganesh ....... Le soir on peut assister à un spectacle de danse ramayana

Pemandangan candi Yang Sangat Indah
Suka sekali Dengan Suasananya disini.
Orang orangnya ramah ramah.
Magnifique endroit, avec un étonnant mélange de temples hindous et bouddhistes. Cadre verdoyant et calme, attention au soleil. Accessible par train (commuter line) en unë vingtaine de minutes.

Candi Prambanan adalah candi Hindu terbesar di Indonesia asia. Di bangun pada abad ke 9 sebelum Masehi. Candi Prambanan terletak di 2 provinsi. Satu sisi milik propinsi Yogyakarta dan sisi yang lain milik propinsi Jawa Tengah. Terdapat beberapa candi di area candi Prambanan yang menggambarkan lambang trimurti pada agama Hindu yaitu dewa Siwa, dewa Brahma dan dewa Wishnu juga beberapa candi yang menggambarkan alat transportasi para dewa tersebut.

I loved my experience here. I got there as soon as it opened and was able to freely walk around these beautiful temples and enjoy the moment. A beautiful, peaceful place that is well maintained and cared for. Thank you for my time here.

This temple complex is easy to get to from Yogyakarta on the 1b bus from Malioboro. You may have to change bus at the airport but you don't have to pay your 3.6k rp again. From the bus terminal it's a 15min walk to the entrance.

You can currently go in the temples and are free to wonder around the grounds at your leisure. Don't miss the other 3 temples in the grounds particularly Candi Sewu (typically the furthest away but still easy walking distance).

It was expensive for a foreigner at 362,500rp per person, but I guess there is a lot of restoration needed after the last earthquake.  I cant help but feel there will be another long before the restoration is complete. You can get a double ticket with Borobudur for a small saving, but they have to be used on consecutive days, but we visited on a Sunday and have learnt never to visit anywhere in Indonesia on a Monday, it will probably be closed. We found it difficult to be clear but we think we were told the grounds to both Prambanan and Borobudur are open on Mondays but there is no access to the temples.

Prambanan is incredible.  It's one of two very large Temple Complexes within an Archeological park.  Its about a 2.5 kilometer walk around the entire park, and you'll see other temples in this beautifully landscaped and perfectly preserved setting.  the foliage is part of the experience.  Really beautiful!  I took a taxi from Yogyakarta the 16 kilometers or so to Pramadan in the late afternoon, spent the night in a small hotel across the street from the entrance area to the park.  Got up at 6:00 to get to the ticket office at 6:30 a.m. when they open, and was ready to get into the Temple complex at 7:00 a.m.  I was the only person in Prambanan for the first half hour!  Magical.  I then walked to Sewu Temple (Buddhist, and awesome,) and continued walking around the park visiting the smaller temples in the park.  I avoided almost all people at all times.   Just lucky!   This is not a sunrise temple, so first thing in the morning is your best bet.   And its cooler.   Enjoy.  It's worth every cent.  It was just under $25.00 to get in.

История и восторги-это прекрасно, но есть особенности о которых должен знать каждый самостоятельный турист при планировании путешествия, но почему-то этой информации нет или на неё мало обращают внимание.
Комплекс закрыт внутри для посещения в понедельник (это официальная информация, полученная в центральном офисе по продаже билетов). Наш гид сказал, что открыт во вторник и в пятницу, тут ничего подтвердить не могу.
Местных туристов привозят на автобусах, в основном это школьники, которым эти достопримечательности на фиг не нужны, они проходят строем и всё.
На территории проводятся фестивали (мы застали подготовку к рок!!! фестивалю-это жесть). Тоже было бы неплохо узнать заранее.
В принципе, нам всё понравилось именно потому, что туристов было мало,  вида из-за забора каменного было достаточно. На закате мы были вдвоем (!). Закрывают ворота в 17:30, но можно фотографировать через них, тоже отличные кадры. 
Совет: если увидите большую группу местных туристов, берите правее и идите к дальним башням. Они открыты даже в дни, когда всё закрыто, людей там нет вообще, а виды просто обалденные.

Better than Borobudur in my humble opinion still super expensive but there are more temples to visit e.g. Candi Sewu and you can now enter the temples which is good, also if you look at all non-Indonesian don't be suprised if people ask for photos . I didn't realise I was famous in Indonesia.

Went there today on 1st of March. Wanting to let everyone know that the temples are re opened to visitors walking up and inside the temples. Not sure of the past reviews that visitors weren’t allowed. We didn’t have that problem. We went during mid week on Wednesday about 10 in the morning, it was busy with school children. We were approved by different groups of school kids asking to speak to us with a set of questions. It was a way of learning for them to speak to an English speaker. Some of the kids were nervous, so please be kind. Engage with them and support their enthusiasm. This, itself, is an experience to engage with local kids and have a bit of fun. 

I didn’t mind paying the “tourist price” to visit Prambanan. It wasn’t much considering the money will be used in the restoration of the many structures that were damaged in the 2006 earthquake. You can see many of the ruins just walking around, especially at Candi Sewu. Don’t miss Candi Sewu. It is worth spending my money and time at Prambanan. Glad that I went to Prambanan instead of Borobudur on this trip. Reason is that Borobudur is still closed to visitors going up the temple when I checked with the tourist information centre and they don’t even know when it will reopen. So, skip Borobudur and go to Prambanan.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
The Prambanan temple complex is probably one of the most well maintained temple sites in Central Java. The main site, Candi Prambanan, contains 3 huge temples that are dedicated to Hindu Holy Trinity (Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva) . The temples are being rebuilt after the 2006 earthquake in Bantul and you will encounter sites that still have stones lying around. 

The complex itself contains several temples like Candi Sewu (a Buddhist temple) and other temples that are being rebuilt or have been recently discovered.

The parking place is big and also has an EV charging station. The street vendors are contained in the souvenir area

For a better experience and to give you context of the site, it is recommended to hire a guide which costs around IDR 150k. The guide will give background stories of the site, maybe some anecdotes here and there, but all in all you won't be just looking at stones.

If you are looking for a place with a view and have a good lunch and/or dinner, head to Abhiyagiri restaurant located at the Sumber Watu Heritage resort (advisable to use/rent a car)
Faktor Penarik: Ketertarikan Budaya, Ketertarikan Fasilitas, Ketertarikan Suasana
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
I have just returned from Prambanan Temple (10 Feb, 2023) and want to clear up some confusion which seems to be swirling around the internet. You absolutely can enter the temple and walk all over it as I just did it an hour ago (with about a million school kids, but to be expected). It is expensive to get in owing to the vast cost associated with restoring this place from the ground up. And considering how inexpensive everything else is in Yogja, it balances it. 

As for getting there is was a simple 125,000 from the centre of town to the temple, and there are cabs waiting outside. If you want a guide they are around, but even if you don't know your basic stories of Rama, Ganesha, etc it is pretty easy to to read up about the symbolism beforehand so you don't really need a guide.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
Боробудур, лежащий в нескольких десятках километров к западу, безусловно, в мире боле знаменит, чем Прамбанан. Но этот храм, созданный примерно в то же самое время, что и соперник, не менее интересен. Посетить оба грандиозных сооружения можно за один день даже при неспешном движении местного транспорта и проблемах с пробками. Билет берите лучше сразу на два храма. Это можно сделать в кассе  при входе в любой из них. 

             Прамбанан  виден издалека. Высоченное сооружение. Вокруг храма создана большая зеленая парковая зона. В эту зону входит еще два небольших храма, Бубра и Люмбунг,  и знаменитый храм Севу.  От Прамбанана  до Севу   больше километра. Времени, чтобы неспешно все обойти и рассмотреть, нужно зарезервировать примерно  часа два. Если воспользоваться услугами электрокара, то получиться быстрее. Здесь я встретил много групп местных школьников и взрослых людей. На стоянке стояли минимум пятнадцать туристических  автобусов. Ценят собственную историю индонезийцы. 

          Я на территории храма был в этот момент, скорее всего, единственным европеоидом, человеком аномального белого, даже после трехнедельного загара, для Индонезии  цвета кожи.  Прохода местные парни и девчата мне  не   давали. Отовсюду слышалось «Хэлло!!!». Пришлось несколько раз сфотографироваться  с ребятами. Даже немного поговорили. У некоторых пацанов понятны английские слова.  Прамбанан несколько напоминает некоторые храмы Ангкора, в том числе и самый известный Ангкор-Ват. Форма подобная. Много скульптурных изображений. Правда, монументальности чуть меньше.  Обязательно изучите историю этих мест, прежде, чем ехать сюда. Тогда точно интересно будет. Может кого-то в скульптурах и узнаете)).
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

We enjoyed our time at the temples. It was very hot which can't be helped but the ruins were stunning. The price is very steep ($25USDpp) but we spent 3 hours here. You are not allowed to take in outside food and drink. We were fortunate the bag checker didn't take our snacks off us and requested that we just didn't eat them at the temple (we had a whole day out planned, so we has quite a few snacks in our bag). They give you 1 bottle of water with your ticket.  The only place selling food is the restaurant located near the exit. However when you exit the temple there are heaps of food stalls.

This temple is situated in a large complex of other sites. The Prambanan temple is Indonesia’s largest Hindu site, built in the late 9th century. The main compound consists of 3 temples dedicated to Shiva, Vishnu and Brahma. At the time of our visit, no one was allowed to enter or climb the temples and they could only be viewed from the grounds.

Be sure to walk (or rent a bike) to the other minor Buddhist temples in the complex. Candi Lumbung, Candi Bubrah and Candi Sewu are spread out over 1km and in my opinion Candi Sewu (the furthest away) is the most impressive of the three.

There is also a small museum and deer feeding area to enjoy.

One could spend 2-3 hours exploring the complex. It is possible to do Borobudur in the morning and Prambanan in the afternoon. We purchased a combination Borobudur-Prambanan ticket for IDR 652.500. Overall we had a great experience and, would highly recommend a visit to Prambanan.

Review Text:
Prambanan Temples date back to the 10th century and are one of the largest Hindu temples. The temples are dedicated to the Trimurti (Lord Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva).

It is fascinating to see how something so massive and detailed could be built 1000 years ago. The epic Ramayana and various Hindu deities are engraved on the walls.  We can also notice temples dedicated to the animal companions of Trimurti.  Inside the compound, the temples have similar architecture with different carvings and hundreds of shrines. The ruins around the temple also suggest that the monument has indeed been exposed to a number of natural and man-made catastrophes over the years. The ruins may be from other temples or may just be evidence of past civilization in the area.

The Prambanan Temple Compounds serve as a testament to the cutting-edge stone construction technology and architecture used in the ninth century. It also represents religious coexistence and peace during the period.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

👕What is the best outfit?
Casual is the suitable outfit. 

Opening hours
6 am - 5 pm daily
