Review Text:
Many reviews already exist about the impressive art, architecture, and history of this great place.  To reiterate: go see it!  It exceeded our expectations despite our previous experiences with Angkor and many other temples across SE Asia.

This review is more about the nuts and bolts of the visit.  

About getting there: there is a much cheaper and less confined way to visit than booking a tour.  You can take the 1A TransJogya bus from the airport that runs every 20 minutes and costs just 3.5k IDR per person each way.  Takes about 30 min and plenty of friendly people will help you if you need directions.  The Prambanan bus stop is just south of the park so you will need to walk ~1km to the entrance on the eastern edge of the park to gain entry.

About getting in: 'park' is open 6AM-5:15PM and includes Prambanan, Lumbung & Bubrah, and Sewu (not entirely sure why some of these have their own listing on TripAdvisor).  Sure, the ticket is somewhat expensive for foreigners (325k IDR as of May 2017) but do note that there is a combo ticket available for entry in Borobudur the following day (590k IDR) and they do accept credit card.  Also note that there is a dedicated ticket booth for international visitors west of the normal booth.  Additionally, I read elsewhere that the ticket is one entry/exit only but this isn't the case--for example we walked to Plaosan temple and were able to get back in using our same-day ticket.  Plan on arriving earlier rather than later to avoid the crowds and the heat.

About the park itself: the park is large but is not on the scale of Angkor so walking to each site is doable.  There is indeed a free shuttle for tourists that stops at several points around the park.  If you take it, use it to ride from the park road north of Prambanan to Sewu and back; otherwise the 1km walk is a piece of cake.  Guides are available for hire inside the park.  

For picture takers: the temples are mostly oriented to the east so pictures will come out better in the morning before 11am.  If you are interested in the intricate carvings, the least weathered ones (most recently restored ones?) seem to be on the eastern and southern edges of the temples.  There is also a neat little perch (treehouse?) on the park road north of Prambanan that has a nice angle of the main temples.  

Happy visiting!
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Es muy bonito. Algo que hay que ver. Pero nos pareció abusivo el precio. 
Es una pesadilla continua las mujeres de los puestos de fuera del templo. No pararon de atosigarnos tanto para sacarnos fotos con ellas, como para que les comprásemos algo.

Beberapa kali ke jogja, tapi baru kesampaian ke candi Prambanan kali ini. dan sayang sekali di bulan April, pertunjukan sendratari Rama Shinta sedang tidak ada pertunjukan di bulan April kemarin. This place is an amazing experience but make sure you have a guide with you to give you the necessary background. Otherwise you will loose most of the magic.

It is definitely beautiful and visually impressive but the building method and cultural significance, in conjunction with learning about the hindu practices is what will make your visit great.
Bulan April, Candi Prambanan menjadi tempat penyelengaraan lomba marathon sehingga menjadikan kawasan ini bukan hanya sebagai tempat wisata budaya juga menjadi tempat wisata olahraga.

This temple is near to the heart of Yogyakarta. The yard is wide and quite dense. But right around the temple there are no shade plants so if it is summer season, it will feel very hot. Especially when the wind blowing, then the sand dust will make eyes sore. We should use sunglasses and bring umbrellas to anticipate. But if you do not carry an umbrella, there are many local people offering umbrella rentals. At the front of the temple we can see some of the ruins of temples caused by earthquakes. If we heading to the exit of the temple we will pass the stalls of souvenir shopping and food. Many food choices and souvenirs typical of Yogyakarta are sold there. The entrance fee to the temple is quite expensive, cost of IDR 30,000 for adults. But it is worth the magical of history we've seen.

Review Text:
The sheer number of temples here is very impressive!  Even tough only the large, main temples have been rebuilt, the scale of this site is impressive, and the archeological "rubble" of the smaller temples points to a long hard project to rebuild all temples, that have been destroyed by earthquake.

The large temples are beautiful with lovely carvings, and the whole site feels very special.  We were there towards late afternoon, and the photographers in our group were loving the light!
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: How marvelous and grand these temples would have been ...the ruins tells the story. The place is heavily priced to visit in but worth it if interested in past. A big part of temple is still lying as ruins and should be assembled back.

They seem to rise the entry fee from month to month. For the ridiculous overpriced 25€ for Prambanan only and about 33€ incl. Borobodur (plus a surcharge of about 10€ for sunrise/sunset visits plus transports) you get very little. The provided information boards are of bad qualitity and are in Bahasa Indonesia only. They don't even have handouts available. So you need a guide and luck to catch a good one.

For those that havn't been to South East Asian temples yet, Prambanan might be a place to visit. But for those who have been it possibly might be just another temple - even if they are very interested in temples.

Apart from that Prambanan is smaller than most imagine. A 60-90 min vist will do for most visitors. I went there in the morning and still it was too crowded for it's size to enjoy or to catch anything close to a special and memorable moment.

If you're on a low budget better save your bucks.

The entire temple complex is amazing and the temples are far bigger and more majestic than I had expected. The level of detail is beautiful! I would highly recommend it as a place to visit not just if you're in the area but I would go out of my way to come here again. 

Unfortunately while in the temple complex I lost my wallet, I am unsure if I misplaced it or left my bag unattended at any time. 

The staff at Prambanan were exceptionally helpful. Three ladies helped me to re trace my steps through the temples looking for my wallet, the information desk team made a loudspeaker announcement and took my contact details. 
In addition as I was travelling alone and I had taken the local bus 1A from Yogyakarta to Prambanan I had no cash for the return journey. The temple staff were so helpful they alerted their manager who was able to assist me in getting back to Yogyakarta. 

It's rare that you meet such a sympathetic and helpful team of people and they are a credit to Prambanan.
Faktor Penarik: Ketertarikan Budaya, Ketertarikan Fasilitas, Ketertarikan Suasana
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: I don't know why, but I was under the impression I would see some little ruins of what was once great Hindu temples and to my surprise, I got way more that I expected !! Prambanan is monumental and impressive, a smaller scale of what you would see in Angkor. If it wasn't for that unfortunate earthquake, most of the surrounding temples would still be standing today. Three main temples, each dedicated to one of the Hindu Trinity with additional temples for their corresponding vehicles are the highlight of the visit. The temples are adorned with bas-reliefs from the Ramayana. Similar to Angkor, it can only instill awe in the visitor, as you are completely amazed by the perfection of the construction.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Punkt obowiązkowy do zobaczenia. Dużo turystów. Przepiękne, choć odrobinę zniszczone. My byliśmy w ramach zorganizowanego wyjazdu zakupionego przez internet 2 dni wcześniej.
Een van de mooiste oude tempelcomplexen die ik gezien heb. Zeer groot qua oppervlakte. Lokale gids gaf veel uitleg over de historie.

Komplex chrámů Prambanan stojí za vidění vstupné je dražší, jelikož chrám patří k dědictví UNESCO. Doporučuji návštěvu v pracovních dnech a raději hned z rána. O víkendech zde bývá velmi rušno, což narušuje majestátnost a ubíjí atmosféru tohoto místa. Nezapomeňte se projít celým parkem chrámů Prambanan a objevit tak další dva chrámy, které se nacházení poblíž.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: A wonderful Hindu temple of the Trimurti (Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva) and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. I would suggest taking a guide from the ticket counter to really understand the details of this place. The place is good during the morning or late evening as the sun get really hot and there is not much shade in the main premise. The architecture and the carvings are amazing.
Faktor Penarik: Ketertarikan Budaya, Ketertarikan Fasilitas, Ketertarikan Suasana

Review Text: It was a huge temple complex with tall, enormous temples. They had dark, windy space inside the temple that you could enter and see the statues put inside them. Better go with guide since you could know the function of all the temple and distinguish them under their guidance. They were constantly under restoration since there were always a temple under maintenance during all my visit there and there were nuemrous rock on the other side of the park. On the other side of the complex, they had deer conservation camp and several kidrides. They also offer packages to go to Ratu Boko by shuttle.
Faktor Penarik: Ketertarikan Budaya, Ketertarikan Fasilitas, Ketertarikan Suasana
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
If you are making a visit to Yogyakarta, do visit Prambanan Temple. 

One of the few temples in the world which has a Brahma Statue.
Salah satu tempat wajib nih kalau lagi di Jogja. Mudah di capai dengan transportasi umum baik dari Jogja maupun Solo. Bisa menggunakan transjogja atau naik bus dari Solo.
kami sekeluarga senang melihat cagar budaya ini, pemandangan ok, tapi sayangnya kurang tertata rapih banyak timbunan batu mungkin sedang di renovasi

Love it. Words can't describe how I actually felt when I reached the entrance of the temple. 
This place can be reached by local bus. Just make sure you get on the right bus and get off at the right station. It's on the opposite road of the bus station. Do not get cheated by the locals waiting at the bus station, they will tell you Prambanan temple is very far from the bus station. In actual fact, it's only about 5 mins walk. If you are not sure about the location, there's a bank near the bus station, I went there for clarification and to get rid of those locals.
Beautiful stone carving and very intricate design. Come after 2pm or it will be too hot.  Good place to walk around since they have a park also.

Menikmati Candi disaat pagi menjadi lebih berkesan, suasana pagi yang sejuk, kicau burung dan matahari yang hangat.

Jika langit cerah, Gunung Merapi aka nampak di sebelah utara.

Прамбанан - это несколько храмов, сосредоточенных на большой территории. Самые популярные это комплекс Лара Джонронг, три храма, посвященных Вишну, Шиве и Брахме, рядом с ними маленькие храмы их ездовых животных. Сами храмы красивые, резьба, барельефы, архитектура сооружений, в храмы можно зайти, они не действующие, обувь снимать не надо. Людей много, но на территории мусор не разбросан, чисто, провести пару-другую часов неспешно осматривая храмы будет приятным времяпрепровождением.

Our group had Ullen Sentalu as the next destination to visit so we rushed through Prambanan, visiting only one major temple and minor temples. These temples had already been restored and there were fewer people than in Borobudur so we were able to climb the steep steps and enter the temples. Very heavy atmosphere inside, which left me with a heaviness of spirit. The carvings and statues are beautiful, impressive, even awe-inducing. Surrounding the restored temples are several hills of blocks and stones that have yet to be reconstructed. I regret not having spared more time to visit the other temples in the complex. The entrance fee is steep and it would have been better if we spared enough time--a day perhaps--to explore the whole complex. A visit to Prambanan should be in every visitor's itinerary.
This place is really maintained very well, lots of public facilities provided. If we see the building of the temple and the carvings of the arcana, only one word is utterly "amazing".
One of the best maintained historical building in Indonesia. Bringing us back to hundreds of years ago when civilization has reached a high level of sophistication.
Candi ini masih terlihat megah dgn taman yg bersih..namun sayang udah banyak yg rusak..buat photo2 lumayan keren...wow...wow..melihatnya

If you have visited Angkor Watt in Siem Reap, then you could skip visiting this temple. 
It is very similar to Angkor Watt collection.The area around the temple is quite large, and this could be a nice half-day trip out of Joga.I should mention that the foreigners pay 10 times higher fees than the locals, so make sure you bring extra cash.

Tempanya di Candi Prambanan, untuk pemandangannya gak usah di ragukan tiket masuknya juga murah sekitar Rp. 35.000.
cocok untuk mengenal Indonesia lebih dekat lagi.
cocok untuk bersantai sambil melihat pemandangan
cocok untuk berfoto, apalagi prawedding.
Berjalan jalan melihat berbagai candi yang besar dan indah. Banyak spot untuk berfoto bersama teman atau keluarga. Disarankan menggunakan sun block saat cuaca panas terik
Increible. Les recomiendo pagar el guia de  de la puerta, si no no van a entender nada y se van a perder lo mejor. La entrada sale 18 uss. Medio cara pero lo vale
berwisata ke sini seakan kembali ke masa lampau, banyak hal yang kita lihat dari sekitar candi ini. Sangat menarik bila berkunjung bersama teman atau keluarga.

World class architectural/religious/cultural attraction.
Unlike Borobudur which is a much smaller and less impressive "copy" of Cambodia's Angkor Wat (but still very much worth seeing) we hadn't seen a temple of this style before. The size is impressive, as are the reliefs which are mostly still in very good condition.
The grounds are also very pleasant.
Entry in rupiah. "Foreigner" price the equivalent of under $AU45 for two.
Faktor Penarik: Ketertarikan Budaya, Ketertarikan Fasilitas, Ketertarikan Suasana
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: It was historical place you should come to when you visit Yogyakarta, Indonesia. The best time to visit for seeing sunset.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
Wer Tempelanlagen interessant findet, ist hier wohl richtig. Als Nicht-Kenner war es zwar eine beeindruckende Erfahrung, mehr aber auch nicht. Der Preis für internationale Touristen (mit Studentenrabatt - Ausweis erforderlich!) ist mit 117k IDR meiner Meinung nach viel zu hoch. Locals zahlen weitaus weniger! Die ganze Anlage ist gut geeignet für einen angenehmen Spaziergang und zum entspannen, wenn da nicht die vielen Einheimischen Touristen wären. Diese ermöglichen leider keine Entspannung, da diese permanent und penetrant versuchen mit einem Fotos vor den Tempelanlagen zu schießen, was nach 10 Minuten anstrengend wird in der sengenden Hitze. 
Man sollte als nicht allzu viel von dem Tempel erwarten.

Firstly - absolutely spend the extra IDR 100,000 to get a local tour guide (official ones are available at the ticket desk). The temples are unbelievably impressive even without the guide, but there's so much history about these, and loads of interesting stories - not to mention they know where to point out to look up for the bats inside the various temples!
If you don't want to splash for a guide, then at least take a torch, as there are some cool engravings on the inside of the temples.
Also - worthwhile getting the joint ticket with Borabodur.
We turned up around 10am and it wasn't too busy - nowhere near as busy as Borabodur which we'd left around 8am.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
Diese alte Tempelanlage, die UNESCO Kulturerbe ist, haben wir nachmittags, nach Borobudur besucht und auch diese, ist wirklich sehr beeindruckend!
Es lohnt sich definitiv beide Temple miteinander zu kombinieren und es ist absolut machbar, beide an einem Tag stressfrei zu besuchen!
Nach einem heftigen Erdbeben, sind die kleinen Tempel im Umfeld zwar komplett zerstört aber die Haupttempel stehen noch an Ort und Stelle und außen herum, wird fleißig wieder aufgebaut. Ich kann diesen Ausflug nur jedem empfehlen, der kulturell und geschichtlich interessiert ist.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
Erg mooi erfgoed.
Wij hadden een leuke gids
Alleen erg druk. 
je kan er super leuk fietsen in de omgeving. 
Aanrader.

The temple complex covers a space bigger than that one of Borobudur with about ten temple of different sizes. A couple of them can be entered by steep stairways and shows reliefs and statues (nothing illuminated and therefore in relative darkness). Therefore for us the complex itself was more impressive than the single temple buildings.

We were accompanied by a guide but got the feeling with a good guide book and preparation for the visit you can do it on your own.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Amazing temple. Magnificent structures. Incredible sight of history and religion. Had very fun photos taken by Indonesians.

ボロブドゥールとはまた全然違う良さがある。シルエットや造形の美しさだとプランバナンの方が印象深い。
とても美しい寺院だった。
友人がボロブドゥールのみ見て帰ると言っていたが、空港にも近いので、短時間でもいいから必ず見た方が良い！と念押ししたくなる場所。
ここをゆっくり見たかったので、ジョクジャの滞在は個人でフリーで予定した。プランバナン園内にあるレンタサイクルで、丸一日かけてのんびりとめぐった。
可能であれば、ロロ・ジョングラン以外の寺院（ほぼ修復中）も見ると良いと思う。
マリオボロからのアクセスはバスとバイタクなどを使ったが、タクシーがオススメ。メーターもちゃんとしているし、バイタク（値切りにもよるが）とたいして変わらなかった。暑いし埃っぽいので、クーラーも効いた車で移動するのがオススメ。
4/14に行ってきました。遠くから見たシルエットでは、アンコールワットに似てる印象でしたが土台部分が繋がっていない、角張った創りと思っていたのとは違う感じでした。壁のレリーフや内部の石像は、見事でした。石の遺跡好きにはたまらない寺院でした。

The temple themselves are quite few though very tall and magnificent in terms of design. I suggest you see the Ramayana show with the Prambanan Temple as the background especially on a full moon. Its one of the best show/sites to see in Indonesia.

The Prambanan temple is part of a much larger complex of temples with a real mix of Hindu and Buddhist architecture.

It was 'found' after abandonment and has been partly reconstructed. The scale is huge and it's wonderful to be able to walk in and around all the temples. Be aware inside some of them you may need a small torch to appreciate the interior statues. 

Go to the museum at the back of the complex (near the Sewu temple) for an insight on the reconstruction works - English subtitles.

On route out, tourists are shepherded through the markets so if this isn't your thing just grin and bear it :-)
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
Situated 30 min away from Jogjakarta airport and fee for foreigners is around 250,000 IDR but it's worth.  
You can have Temple run (only the background) / Indiana John experience here. things for sell here are really expensive and you can bargain for more than half of the price.

Only one word for prambanan, fantastic!! Ticket entrance is cheap,but bit expensive for foreigner, but for the ticket price still make sense.
Would be better visit in the morning,cause the weather will be more hotter at noon.

Build in 9 century. Is a Siwa temple. God of distraction in Hindu. 
The most beautiful Hindu temple .. The best come to watch sunset between the temple. 

There are 3 main temple. Wisnu, Brahma and Siwa. The biggest one is Siwa.

Review Text: The temple's architecture has similarities with those of Siem Reap and Ayutthaya.  But of course the details are very different.  It is a hindu temple.  There are many things to see every corner of the temple for those who like ancient architecture and history.  Recommend with a tour guide

Amazing architects of building in Yogyakarta, about 45 minutes from Malioboro, very recomended for photograph in afternoon and You'll get the unlimited photos from many views. It's good if you bring your best camera and quiet enough about 4-6pm. But the ticket sales open up to 5pm.

O por do sol é maravilhoso.
Muito fácil de chegar de onibus (1A) da Malioboro. Algumas "tours" não incluem guia. Então melhor ir por sua conta e contratar um guia lá por 75/80 Rp.

Incredible view of this temple at sunset. They close it at 6, they will tell you they don't do sunset but actually you can see the sunset because nobosy kicks you out. The architecture is impressive, the temple is massive, the biggest hindu temple in Indonesia ( as I read), is a hindu Temple built in honour to Shiva in the 8th century.
Is ome of the most beautiful temple I've seen and is realy worth it to be seen.

Though not as popular and impressive as Borobudur, still worth a visit. You could buy a Prambanan-Borobudur or Prambanan-Ratu Boko package. From Malioboro, Trans Jogja bus 1A will bring you to Prambanan Temple. Just alight at the terminal station and walk about 15 minutes to the ticket booth.

This Hindu temple is a must-see in the proximity of Jogjakarta. Although it suffered from the many earthquakes over the centuries, it is still in a good shape. For Rp 100k, you can have a guide for groups of max 4 persons. These can tell you much about the stories behind the stone carvings and the statues. It gives you a good insight in the Hindu religion and brings things to life. Else you would wander around the temple a bit clueless. ...

At the exit of the temple, you can take a golf cart for Rp 20k per person that drives you around the complex, including the 3 buddhist temples and drops you at the exit. Be aware that this is not a hop-on hop-off system. The Buddhist temples themselves are in poor shape and being reconstructed. The statues are taken out for safe-keeping and placed back after the restoration is done.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
Candi Prambanan (temple) , is a well known ancient Hindu Temple in Indonesia built during the 9th century. It is one of the largest Hindu temple architecture in Southeast Asia.Temple was destroyed and rebuilt to its past glory by Dutch and UNESCO help. Good job done.  Three main temples  of God with 3 temples for their vehicle in front of it and Ganesha temple.   The three gods, Creator (Brahma), Preserver (Vishnu) and also the Destroyer (Shiva).  
We were supprised about how well preserved the site is,.  There is nothing much to see inside except a statue of God or its vehicle but  complex as whole we found magnificent and attractive. My request, instead of paying for a guide at the front entrance,  go to Candu Pranbanan and you will be approached by some students from local tourism school. They perform a free tour in order to practice their English. Give them a tip at the end of their tour presentation.
 Best time to visit is evening as you can visit temple as well as famous Ramayana ballet. Make sure you enter before 5 pm as entry closes by that time. We booked it around 3 am before we started for Sewu Temple. We couldn't get front seat. So it is recommended to book by phone call.
We enjoyed the complex and Ramayana ballet.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Yo arrendé una moto y me fui por las mías a este bello lugar, conocer sus ruinas fue muy divertido, vallan con tiempo, para que disfruten el lugar y no se pierdan la danza que se hace en la noche a un costado del templo.

Lovely site, less expansive than Borobodur, much more accessible. The temples themselves are beautiful, the insides are... not much to speak of. A bare room with one statue in (in the largest of the temples there are four rooms = 4 statues) But the atmosphere and the ambience... FInd a place to sit and just enjoy the atmosphere - I'd recommend going late in the afternoon, not to many people and the added beautiful light of a beginning sunset. I do believe there were more pictures taken of my son than the temple (he is also VERY cute) but it did become a little bit too much for me (though I am a very relaxed mother) but stranger holding my 1,5 year old despite him screaming, just to take a picture... I didn't like that very much, but on the other hand they were nice and just facsinated by a little blonde boy that size who for the most part took it in his stride,,, And asking is difficult if you barely speak english... Beautiful place, and don't forget to visit ratu boko especially before sunset. Very rcmndd. amazing place.

we can take Trans jogja to this place and from the last stop we can walk to the temple around 15 minutes. large place make us feel like at ancient place.we can buy full ticket and they will arrange to the other temple with mini bus..... amazing place!!!

Java island is famous for its multi-complex cultural civilization. It was realized from the many sites important heritage site that became physical evidence that we can find today. One is the temple. One very famous temple is Prambanan temple has hundreds lined the surrounding temples. At every step we pass around the temples as if recounting to us the atmosphere of the past life of the ancestors of Java. I'm sure every visit there will feel at home made.
Happy Nice Trip Brother

Review Text: Very beautiful site with its 3 gods temple! We met 3 young trainee who offered their guide in change of practising their own English and tourist guide skills. Very nice girls!!! Lot of beautiful stories and tales to know. The temples are beautiful and worth to visit as well as knowing the history and tales inscriptions.

The Prambanan temple complex is the largest Hindu temple  of ancient Java. Though the compound is slightly smaller than Borobudur, but yet need to walk a lot and much to see too. Very beautiful and magnificent old temples in the compound. Contains a lot of religious sculptures. Though we were there in the late afternoon with the hot sun high up, the view was still fantastic. A must visit tourist site under UNESCO World Heritage. You can get wide selection of  souvenirs at the exit path. Here the hawkers are more relaxed and won't chase after you as like those at Borobudur.

Review Text: Prambanan is a vast Buddhist temple complex dating to the 9th century. The inner compound is compelling, and looks like a pre-cursor to Angkor Wat in Cambodia, as much of the style is so similar. There are huge numbers if relief panels depicting the Ramaynana legend. We really needed our expert guide with us to really understand what we were seeing.

遺跡のすばらしさをさらに知るにはガイドを付ける事をおススメします。
それぞれの遺跡や中にある石像、壁の彫刻の意味等を教えてもらえるのでより一層楽しむ事ができます。（ガイド料はRp100000程度）
公園が広く、気温も高いので日除けと水分は準備しておいた方が良いです。

Nice landscape. Very old temples. TIR near the Temples. 20 000 rp pro person.
Entrence Prambanan and Borobudur, 2 adults - 832 000 rp (the ticket for Prambanan for Indonesien people is 20 000 rp).
 The tickets for the temples are available 2 days. Gid 100 000 rp. The mini train (kereta) in Pranbanan area is included. 
You can take a public bus with AC for 7 000 rp two ways. 
I had a very nice day there.
This is a huge monumental temple what contains a lot of different sculptures. Very nice park near the temple and market with souvenirs. Nice to visit it, however, the price is too much.

When we finished climbing up & down the temples and need to go to the exit gate, it's very helpful to ride the golf car provided. With 20K for one person, we got an electric golf car with no sound, no pollution, and a knowledgeable driver with many stories about the temple. The driver also suggest us to stop, taking picture or going into interesting spots. 
It's very recommended !

Review Text:
What an amazing temple complex! Similarity with Angkor Wat from far view, perhaps caused of Buddhist influence (Wiki said its Hindu Temple), I'm not so sure. 

You will love it if you like ancient building!

tempat nya unik, menarik dan penuh dengan sejarah. wisata nya yg memiliki lokasi yg sangat luas dan asri sehingga sangat nyaman untuk dikunjungi. Di bagian samping dari arah pintu masuk, terdapat pasar sebagai pusat oleh2. Makanan dan pakaian disana sangatlah murah, dan masih bisa untuk di-nego. Sehingga cocok untuk rombongan sekolah ataupun keluarga yg ingin mendapatkan oleh2 yg banyak untuk para kerabatnya.

Review Text: The original temples were very old. How ever, most of them were destroyed in earthquake and have been reconstructed.

These temples have been assiduously restored over the decades first by the Dutch and then by the Indonesian government with assistance from international bodies like UNESCO. They've all done a terrific job. Walking here takes you back to the time when the area had a Hindu kingdom and was Very well connected to nearby kingdoms like those in India. It is said that the architect was first sent to study architecture at Nalanda University in India and then return to oversee the construction of these temples. They're all dedicated to Hindu gods and have ancient idols that are masterpieces of stone craft. There's a lot of detail in the stone carving all over. Beautiful.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
Candi ini sangat kental dengan nilai sejarah. Cerita tentang cinta Bandung Bondowoso kepada Roro Jonggrang. Mengisahkan betapa cinta bisa menggerakkan seseorang melakukan apapun untuk orang yang dikasihinya. Dan Bandung Bondowoso membuktikannya dengan membangun candi ini. Candi ini merupakan candi Hindu. Terdiri dari 240 candi (16 candi utama di dalam pagar pembatas dan 224 di luar pagar). Candi utama masih relatif utuh, sedangkan 224 candi lainnya tidak (seperti bekas reruntuhan jaman dulu).
Candi ini sudah dirawat dengan cukup baik. Area komplek candi terlihat bersih dan hanya ada sampah daun kering, karena area ini memang banyak ditumbuhi pohon - pohon. Sarana penunjang pun cukup lengkap, seperti lahan parkir, mushola, toilet, dan lain - lain.  Di sekitar komplek juga ada kios - kios penjual oleh - oleh atau souvenir. Bagi yang laper setelah capek keliling - keliling dan foto - foto, bisa mengisi perut di tempat - tempat makan yang tersedia di area pintu keluar komplek candi (sebelum menuju area parkir).

Candi Prambanan atau Candi Roro Jonggrang dikenal sebagai bukti cinta Bandung Bondowoso untuk Roro Jonggrang. Candi Prambanan merupakan Candi Hindu terbesar di Asia Tenggara. Di dalam candi terdapat relief yang mengisahkan tentang epos Hindu seperti kisah Ramayana dan Krishnayana. Candi yang terletak di perbatasan Kota Klaten dan Propinsi Yogyakarta ini sangatlah indah dan sarat dengan nilai-nilai sejarah.

Candi Prambanan atau yang lebih dikenal dengan kisahnya Roro Jonggrang adalah komplek candi Hindu terbesar di Indonesia bahkan Asia Tenggara. Candi ini dipersembahkan untuk Trimurti yaitu tiga dewa utama Hindu,  yaitu Brahma sebagai Dewa Pencipta,  Wishnu sebagai Dewa Pemelihara dan Siwa sebagai Dewa Pemusnah. 

Tiap hari khususnya hari libur yang menginjungi Candi Prambanan ini luar biasa apalagi kebersihan di area Candi sangat bersih dan banyak fasilitas lain diantaranya kuliner,  hasil kerajinan, hasil UKM seperti pakaian dan lain lain. 

Fasilitas lain tempat parkir yang luas baik yang menggunakan sepeda motor,  Mobil Pribadi atau Mobil Umum akan aman di tempat parkir sehingga para wisatawan bisa menikmati secara leluasa indahnya Candi Prambanan.

Jika anda seorang muslim jangan khawatir karena di area candi juga ada masjid yang lumayan besar dan bersih sehingga nyaman dalam kita beribadah kepada Allah SWT. 

Sungguh betapa pendahulu kita sudah mempunyai kemampuan yang luar biasa kita tinggal menikmati dan memelihara sehingga bisa terjaga selamanya.
Faktor Penarik: Ketertarikan Budaya, Ketertarikan Fasilitas, Ketertarikan Suasana

Review Text: A few of my friends and I visited this site in March 2017. We were supprised about how well preserved the site is, even though there are several apparently destroyed buildings. These were apparently destroyed by varuous earthquakes. There is a project in place to rebuild the destroyed structures. Instead of paying for a guide at the front entrance,  go to Candu Pranbanan and you will probably be approached by sime students if the local tourism school. They perform a free tour in order to practice their English. Give them a tip at the end of their tour presentation.

Review Text: Visited this place at opening time (6am) which I would recommend as the place gets packed by 8 and sun is quite hot by then. The site is kept very clean and well managed. Temples are stunning. Reliefs throughout depict the story of the Ramayana, the Hindu epic tale of Rama and Sita. Guide most definitely needed to get the best out of these -as someone who teaches Hinduism and thought I knew the story very well from celebrating many Diwali's, I was surprised to learn many new things! The reliefs themselves are very detailed and incredible. The statues of deities inside the temples are very well preserved and wonderful to see a statue of Brahma as this is quite rare. Beautiful place, MUST visit!

从日惹市区到普兰班南大约开始不到一小时。在售票处可以拿游览图，有中文的。不得不说这个景点的门票，还是很贵的，大概20美金一个人。这里是印尼目前现存的规模最大的印度教寺庙群，是爪哇印度教建筑代表，也是世界遗产之一。普兰班南包括外部庭院包括224座寺庙遗迹，内部庭院则包括8座较小的寺庙和8座主神庙。游客还是很多的，大部分都是当地人。普兰巴南的建造时间比吴哥现存的大部分印度教寺庙都要早，吴哥现存最古老的印度教寺庙神牛寺和巴空寺是因陀罗跋摩一世在位时期所建，它们的修建时间都比普兰巴南晚了20多年，这足可见到普兰巴南的历史悠久性和重要性。“普兰巴南的八座主神庙分别供奉了印度教的三大主神：湿婆、梵天、毗湿奴以及他们的坐骑。印度教是以梵天、湿婆、毗湿奴三大神为中心的众神结构体系，他们的妻子、儿子都作为神灵存在，且都有各种各样的化身。湿婆是印度教的毁灭之神，也是创造和转化之神，他的坐骑是神牛南迪，妻子是雪山神女。湿婆终年在喜马拉雅山上的吉婆娑山修炼苦行，通过最严格的苦行和最彻底的沉思，获得最深奥的知识和神奇力量。他还创造了刚柔两种舞蹈，被誉为舞王。他是妖魔鬼怪的统帅，据说他有极大的降魔能力，额上的第三只眼能喷毁灭一切的神火，曾烧毁三座妖魔城市和引诱他的爱神。印度教认为“毁灭”有“再生”的含义，故表示生殖能力的男性生殖器——林伽是他创造力的象征。”
三座主神庙都有回廊，在回廊的墙壁上布满了叙事浅浮雕，但是跟婆罗浮屠相比，其数量要少得多，最大的湿婆神庙也只有72块浅浮雕，这些浅浮雕的故事都来源于印度教的史诗《罗摩衍那》。
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Setelah lebaran idul fitri kami sekeluarga mengunjungi Candi Prambanan. Tempatnya sangat menarik terutama bagi isteri dan anak-anak saya. I am in awe of the temples throughout the area. Such detail and story telling. This temple is the largest Hindu temple. It is always a good idea to research prior to going to the temple to get some knowledge of its story. I had a tour guide who was able to give all the details.

Been here 15 years ago. But this time I much more enjoyed it. Though many of the sculptures been damaged by the rain and the weather but the statues inside the temples still intact. Outside the temples there is market where you can buy something to bring home. There is archery game too. It had deers too.. 

This place had a storytale. 

A long time ago there was a man that love a woman. He wanted to marry her, but she didn't want to. Then she asked the man to built 1000 statues in 1 night. 

It was almost morning when the man finished the 999 statues, the woman felt so desperate than she asked the roosters to crow to deceive the man. Hearing the crow he stopped and felt so angry. But after knowing that the woman deceived her, he mad and made the lady into a stone and made her the 1000th statue.

Review Text:
Explored the entire complex and enjoyed almost everything. The remaining intact temples, including Candi Shiva (the main temple), had very impressive architecture, carvings, statues, etc. A guide on the site helped explain to me how the temples were built (apparently with no nails or mortar; the blocks were carved so they fit together like jigsaw pieces, which I thought was incredible), and also described the meaning behind the various statues. When I was done exploring the main area and taking pictures I walked north to the ruins of a few more temples, including a huge field of ruins around Candi Sewu, another important temple on the complex. 

The site was big enough and had enough interesting temples and sights that it was definitely worth visiting. I did have a complaint that it was hard to get across the complex, as it was a hot day and it's a surprisingly long distance between Candi Shiva and Candi Sewu (there was some kind of shuttle, but it wasn't clear where it went and if it stopped at other temple ruins as it moved around the property). There's also a huge compound of stalls at the exit that I had to navigate through in order to actually leave, which was annoying. The on-site museum was also hard to find and get into; the entrance was not well labeled. But these are small things.

All in all, I recommend visiting Prambanan to people in the Yogyakarta area.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
Prambanan is a 9th-century Hindu Temple complex and it is one of the two largest Hindu sites in Indonesia (the other being Besakih, in Bali).  Prambanan immediately overwhelmed my visual senses.  The pointed architecture of these buildings and the sheer size are quite impressive from any angle. The tallest temple is equivalent to a 14-floor building.  

I went on an overcast afternoon and the weather was cool and windy.  (Fortunately, the rain started only as we were beginning to leave the site).  The number of tourists here seemed much smaller than at Borobudur, which I went to the next morning.

As a foreigner, the price for admission is significantly higher than for Indonesian citizens so make sure to get the combo ticket for 420,000 rupiah ($32 usd) if you plan to visit both Borobudur and Prambanan. A single ticket to Prambanan costs $18 (240,000 Rp) while a single to Borobudur is $20 (260,000 Rp).

This 9th century Hindu temple complex was built just after the Borobudur Buddhist temple and was similarly abandoned a few centuries later when the royal court moved to eastern Java. The structures are very vertical in design and suffered major collapse in the 1600's during an earthquake. Over the last 150 years, they've been gradually pieced back together, a process which continues. This World Heritage site is now an imposing presence on the flat plain east of Jogjakarta and well worth a visit.
Hire a local guide at the entrance - there's an office for this. We learned much more than we had through guidebooks. The complex takes a couple of hours to see and is a short drive from the airport, so it's ideal as a last stop before departure if you have an afternoon flight. Don't try to do this and Borobudur in a day - too much driving.
A must see if you're in this area. We thoroughly enjoyed our visit.

Take your time to visit these and the other temples at the complex.

I recommend reading up before going or getting a guide there to get your money's worth.

Be sure to buy the Prambanan & Borobudur combo ticket.

Ada Tur Gaet yang siap mengantar dan menjelaskan dari masing-masing bangunan candi tersebut. Lingkungan sekitar candi sangat nyaman, asri dan bersih dengan pemandangan alam pegunungan yang Indah dengan udara yang sangat sejuk, ada kendara mobil golf dan kereta wisata yang disediakan dan siap mengantar untuk berkelliling di lingkungan sekitar candi prambanan setelah selesai berkeliling candi maka begitu pintu keluar terdapat pasar oleh-oleh dan sauvenir dan kuliner. Review Text:
My fifth visit and Candi Prambanan still got me stunned as always before. 

I came very early with an expectation that I can have the temple all mine for a bit. Had to wait until the ticket office open at 6.15am - supposedly at 6am! Grrr. There were some groups of people already queuing behind me.

It was nice to enjoy the temple when not many other visitors around but that wasn't last long. More crowd were pouring in at 7AM.

On the way out I saw an archery field, bicycle rental, electric train, a restaurant and a museum. All were not open yet. I also saw deers and a cassowary bird.

Had breakfast at one of the warungs (not recommended unless you're really starving) and went through the souvenir market. It was around 8:30AM, only few shops that were already open. Bought many snacks and nice souvenirs with good price after bargaining.

There are more than five buildings there, should be more than ten as a lot of buildings were ruined (you can still see hundreds of huge stones piled up there). Inside the largest and tallest building, you will find god shiva statue. There is a deer park on your way to the exit, and you can buy vegetable to feed them, cost IDR 2.000 per bunch.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Candi Prambanan adalah candi Hindu yang terkenal dengan cerita legenda Roro Jonggrang nya. Kita akan menemukan cerita di reliefnya. Candi ini sangat megah dan menawan, wajib dikunjungi!

These temples are not as impressive as the Borobudur temples in my opinion, but they are still a must see. The entire complex is quite large with many temples to explore. The largest of them stands tall above the others, and is a great place for photographs.

This is one of the great cultural sites of the world, just in the shadow of the Borobudur.

Do *not* visit Prambanan on the same day as Borobudur.  It is both too similar and too different; memories and impressions will blur.  If you are only a short visit, choose one (probably still Borobudur), wait for your next one for the second temple.

Do not wear high heels or anything but flat shoes, sneakers etc.  Prambanan is as a site quite big, asphalty and so on, and the temples themselves are unforgiving.

This also makes the place really hot; water, sunscreen, hat or even parasol are musts.  Non-sunny days are really the best, and early-morning visits are a great idea.

Don't skip the non-core temples, especially the one farthest away in the compound, unless you have a problem walking - the latter is quite far, and it's not a nice road.

The little train is allegedly free for holders of the (much more expensive) international tickets; find out whether this is so once you're there, it would be quite handy.

There is no nice restaurant or cafeteria on the temple grounds; if  you're a regular-meal person, plan to eat before or after (there are nice places in the area, including soto restaurants in the rice paddies).

The market at the end, the inside touts etc. are not a problem; you can say "no thanks" if you want or just walk by (and if you can't do that, you should probably stay home).  Prices are actually okay, but for many international visitors, the hard sell is offputting.  (I wonder why Indonesian merchants don't get that they will sell more to Western tourists if they let them first look at their items in peace.)  

Find Roy E. Jordaan's "In Praise of Prambanan" by Googling if you are really interested in the temple compound - it's downloadable for free and an excellent collection of scholarly essays.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text: Went on a hot sunny day, but it is suitable weather for taking nice pictures. Your visit to Yogyakarta will be incomplete if you did not go to Prambanan, as well as Borobudur.

There is quite a lot of walking, so make sure you wear flat shoes and bring a hat, and umbrella.  Not too crowded to walk to the further temples, so don't miss them.
The history of the temple is also intriguing and you can hire a guide for about $10 per hour, which is worthwhile.
It would be wonderful to come and see the ballet here, but limited to dry season.
Close to Jogya, so easy for a day trip, allow 2- 3 hours.  Unfortunately you have to exit via all the shops, which is a bit annoying, other wise the site is clean and has reasonable toilet facilities.

Prambanan Temple located near the Yogyakarta airport is a UNESCO World heritage site that is a must visit for all tourists to this city. The group of temple was built about 1200 years ago and is a reminder of the great influence that the Hindu culture of India had in South-East Asia starting from first century AD. The temple was built in 9th century by the kings of Hindu Sanjaya Dynesty. The temple complex is essentially devoted to Shiva but has temples for Brahma and Vishnu also. One has to climb a rather steep stone staircase to reach the temple. Main Shiva Temple has a hight of about 150 ft and has statues of Lord Shiva in a Shiva-Linga-Yoni format, as also the statues of Lord Ganesha and Devi Durga. The temple on its external walls has full story of Ramayana depicted in stone engravings. The temple was destroyed a couple of times (In the year 1006 and latest being in the year 2006) due to earth quakes (there is a live volcano nearby) and was rebuild, most recently by Dutch archeologists. Indonesia had been under the Dutch rule and still has a strong connection with Netherland. The temple has initially been built by putting inter-locking stone blocks together in a Lago like fashion without using any cement like adhesive. When the temple fell apart and stones scattered all over due to earth quake, rebuilding the temple was like solving a jig-saw puzzle of placing stones back again in the original order. The work is not complete as a huge number of stone blocks are still lying scattered all around waiting to be placed in form again. Nevertheless, the temples already re-constructed are very impressive. Hindus and Buddhists made up the bulk of ancient Indonesian population that later converted to Islam. Except in Bali that is about 80% Hindu population, rest of Indonesia is predominantly Muslim now. The Hindu Prambanan temple though very impressive and a great tourist attraction, is not an active temple anymore. No regular religious ceremonies and rituals are held on the site now. In that sense, the Prambanan temple is an extinguished and empty temple. There is a huge handicraft and garment market strategically placed at the end of the visit so all visitors pass through it after seeing the temple.  The temple site is a good hour and a half drive from the center of the city and is well preserved and managed. Entrance fee to the temple for foreigners is rather steep at about Rs. 300,000 Indonesian rupiah (for natives the fee is 30,000 rupiah). One can however buy a combo entrance ticket for this temple and the equally important and contemporary Buddhist temple “Borobudur” (about 2 hours drive away) and save about 100,000 rupiah. Both places may be covered in one day. One should keep about 2 hours for visit to this important site. Keep a water bottle and an umbrella / hat as the place can be hot and humid.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

I went here directly from the airport by bus (trans jogja 1A, bus fare 3,500rp). Make sure the bus is going to Prambanan, NOT coming from Prambanan. The bus stop is about 800m from the temple entrance. There's free luggage storage from 9:30am-5pm near the ticket booth for locals. Ticket booth for foreigners is inside a building and the price is 243,000rp, you can also hire a guide for 100,000rp if you want to appreciate Prambanan more. Lots of stores that sell food/water/souvenirs near the entrance. If it's hot out, I suggest you buy water before entering the temple grounds. You'll be climbing a lot of steep stairs so wear comfy footwear. Place is crowded during weekends especially in the late afternoon with lots of locals also visiting. I left around 4pm and it wasn't a long wait before the bus going back to city arrived. If you're going to Ratu Boku, there's a free shuttle for that. You can also buy combined temple entrance ticket (Prambanan+Ratu Boku, or Prambanan+Borobudur) that's cheaper but must be used within 2 days.

Additional info: If you're planning on going to Borobudur from Prambanan via bus, ride 1A to the airport, then 3A to Condong Catur, then 2A to Terminal Jombor. Total travel time takes less than an hour depending on traffic, and you only have to pay 3,500rp once from Prambanan to Jombor, just don't exit the bus stop. From Terminal Jombor, ride the bus to Borobudur Terminal (fare 25,000rp). Guy at the terminal told me that the last bus going to Borobudur is at 3pm.

Review Text: walaupun panas dimalam hari, tapi keliatan indah waktu malam hari, yang pasti Candi Prambanan adalah cagar budaya yang harus sama-sama kita jaga

We paid 150,000 to get there by taxi. Foreigners then must pay 225000 IDR (about the equivalent of $17 USD) admission. We then hired an official guide next to the ticket office for 100000 IDR. The guide was very good, but we found the site to be kind of dull, especially if you've been to other similar temples such as Wat Arun and Angkor Wat. It was also very crowded (we went during a long weekend, so it may be a lot less crowded during a weekday). It seemed like at least 50 tour buses were there. 

Our tour only lasted 40 minutes. It's not a very large temple. We then decided to save some money on the way back by taking the A1 bus for 3500 IDR back into town. Big mistake. The station is about a 15 minute walk from the exit. It seemed to take about 40 minutes to wait for the bus, even though they are supposed to come every 20 minutes. The buses are crowded. We were lucky to get a seat. At least it was air-conditioned! There were many stops, so about 1 1/2 hours later, we finally got off on Malioboro Street. The whole journey back took 2 1/2 hours, whereas the taxi ride would only have taken 1 hour max. 

It's a good idea to have your taxi driver wait for you, as we didn't see anything but bike carriages and motorbike taxis at the exit. For us, the whole experience was skippable. I would have preferred to spend the day reading a book by the pool. Borobudur was much nicer.

Review Text:
The main site of the Prambanan complex is located inside a large, landscaped park. The complex is open daily from 6AM to 6PM. Try to visit early as it gets really hot in the afternoon. 
Entry costs for Indonesians are less than $4, while foreigners are charged a fixed tourist rate of Rp 252,000 There is also a combination ticket with Borobudur which is worth the saving if you are visiting both. There is a separate entrance for foreigners with a much shorter queue. Entry ticket also entitles you to complimentary tea/coffee/water. A sarong is provided upon entry - should your clothes not cover enough to be respectable.

Guides can be hired at the ticket office for about US$8 (75,000 rp) and as this is a complex monument, a guide is a very good idea.

The structures have been heavily damaged by previous volcanic eruptions and earthquakes ... but it seems like ongoing Unesco World Herritage Site programmes are trying to restore what they can.

Worth a visit, it's one of the Yogya must see sights.

We went on a combined trip Borobudur + Prambanan. We booked transport at our hotel for IDR 140,000. The combined ticket for both sites costed IDR 420,000 - that's a price for foreigners as Indonesians pay IDR 50,000 (sic!).

Borobudur was first and to Prambanan we got around 10am. Hindu temple compund that's one of the largest Hindu sites in South East Asia. It is characterised by tall and pointed architecture - typical for Hindu architecture. Similarly to Borobudur it's dating back to 9th century, was later abandoned and rediscovered in 19th century. Main temple is dedicated to Shiva, others to Brahma and Vishnu, among others. Reliefs present stories from Hindu epics. The remains of some other temples that were not reconstructed yet are gathered nearby. Prambanan is a great piece of history - not far behind Borobudur.

Review Text: インドネシアに旅行するまではこのような素晴らしい遺跡があることは知りませんでしたがこの遺跡はカンボジアのアンコールワットに匹敵する素晴らしい遺跡と思います。ジョグジャカルタ街中からバスで40分くらいのところにあります。ボロブドゥールとあわせて１日でめぐることも可能ですが、それではもったいないので時間が許すなら時間をかけてみるのが良いと思います。

Die Prambanan Tempelanlage besteht aus der großen hinduistischen Tempelanlage Prambanan und drei weiteren kleinen buddhistischen Tempelanlagen. Was der Borobudur für den Buddhismus, ist der Prambanan für den Hinduismus. Beide Anlagen sind ungefähr gleich alt. Und auch der Prambanan ist seit 1991 auf der Liste des Weltkulturerbe der UNESCO. Die Prambanan-Tempelanlage besteht aus acht Haupttempeln und über 250 weiteren kleinen Tempeln bzw. Schreinen. Charakteristisch und immer wieder in allen Variationen abgebildet sind die drei großen Haupttempel für Shiva, Vishnu und Brahma.
Меня больше всего впечатлило это место.Это необъяснимо. Поражает размах комплекса и сама  древняя архитектура.  Рекомендую взять зонтик от солнца.

El templo esta muy bien, cerca del aeropuerto.  Valor entrada 230 mil Rupias.  Si compras el paquete de entrada para Borobudur te ahorras $5 dólares. Es valido por dos días. 
Gran espacio verde bien cuidado y organizado. Te dan café y agua gratis por la entrada. Pídelo ya que no lo ofrecen. Una muy buena experiencia.  Ahh prepárate para ser la estrella del lugar todos los locales querrán fotografiarse contigo.

Я очень давно мечтала попасть сюда и когда попала, понимала что меня так тянуло сюда.... такой мощной энергетики место, что аж слезы наернулись от невероятной красоты и колоссальности. Вход сейчас стоит 238 тыс рупий, но вы не пожалеете. Лучше Сэкономить на дороге к этому храму , но побывать в нем стоит однозначно. Храмовый комплекс состоит из нескольких пирамидальных храмов. Прамбанан – место с невероятной энергетикой. Три основных храма – Брахме, Шиве и Вишну, находятся в окружении святилищ поменьше. Напротив каждого храма – еще три поменьше, со священными животными богов. Напомню, что в индуизме Шива – разрушитель и тот, кто забирает жизнь. Брахма – создатель. А Вишну – тот, кто отвечает и помогает нам при жизни. Напомним, что на Яве был очень развит Шиваизм, поэтому храм Шиве находится в центре и поражает размерами. В храме остались еще несколько статуй, одна из них статуя бога Ганеши, которая поразила меня больше всего. в полной темноте, он приветсвует гостя спокойным взглядом сидя в позе лотоса, оторвать глаз от него невозможно, он такой грозный и безмятежный что просто стоишь перед ним как ребенок и дух захватывает... Это просто нечто. На территории действует бесплатный музей , где собраны статуи богов разных размеров , которые принесли сюда после того, как храм был разрушен землятрясением в 2006 году. все что уцелело можно увидеть в этом музее. По вопросам как доехать. Прошу вас не берите тур в гостиницах которые предлагают вас доставить туда за бешенные деньги. Проще всего взять такси по городу, которое обойдется вам около 15 000 рупий ( чуть больше доллара) и доехать до остановки автобуса 1А, который едет прямехонько в Прамбанан и стоит 3500 рупий. Так вы доберетесь туда за 20 000 рупий самое большее, в то время как отели предлагают довезти вас туда и обратно за 500 000 рупий за машину.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah

Review Text:
Candi Prambanan is a Hindu temple complex dating from the 9th century. It was originally constructed as a Hindu rival to Buddhist Borobudur. Like Borobudur, Prambanan fell into disrepair over the centuries until restoration began under Dutch rule in the 1930s. What stands now is the restored version of the original but only part of that restoration due to the devastating effects of the 2006 earthquake.

There are separate entrances to the complex for Indonesians and foreigners. The foreigner price is the somewhat odd IDR252k.

The park itself contains the temples as the main attraction but is a pleasant green area in its own right. The walk around the park is a rare piece of well-manicured greenery. The complex contains the main temples as well as a couple of smaller temples, a children's play area, a small free museum depicting the temple and its reconstruction, and a cafe.

The main temples are the key attraction. They are huge and beautiful. It is quite awe-inspiring to walk around them or to walk up their steps and see the statues in the dark. Statues of various Hindu gods welcome those who travel up the 20 or so steps. The temples have four sides with each side having a god statue. In the dark with the statue it is quite a spiritual experience. While Borobudur is the legendary location in this region, Prambanan is certainly impressive in its own right and to some eyes is more attractive.

The damage from the 2006 earthquake is clearly visible. There are piles and piles of stones laid on top of each other which presumably used to be part of temple structures. Incredible to think what it must have looked like just a decade ago and a reminder of how special it is to have such a huge site from more than a millennium of antiquity.

Prambanan is a special place and well worth a visit to see such an incredible Hindu complex from so long ago.
Faktor Pendorong: Keinginan untuk belajar, Keinginan untuk menjelajah
